new_roles.title: SVP, Environment, Safety, Health & Quality (ESHQ)
new_roles.description:
**Description**
Title: SVP, Environment, Safety, Health & Quality (ESHQ)
 
 
Department: EPC Business Unit
 
 
Location: Houston, TX
 
 
Supervisor: COO
 
 
FLSA Status: Exempt
 
 
Position Status: Permanent, Full-time
 
 
Work Status: Hybrid
 
 
SVP, ENVIRONMENT, SAFETY, HEALTH & QUALITY (ESHQ)
 
 
Hanwha Qcells USA Corp (Qcells USA), headquartered in Houston, TX, specializes in providing utility-scale modules, solar photovoltaic (PV), and battery energy storage systems (BESS) project development, along with Engineering, Procurement, and Construction (EPC) services for solar and BESS projects nationwide. Qcells USA delivers comprehensive turnkey solutions encompassing the entire utility-scale project lifecycle. By choosing Qcells USA for turnkey solutions, customers can reduce uncertainty and risk, leading to enhanced investment returns and contributing to a more sustainable future.
 
 
Qcells USA’s complete turnkey solutions seamlessly integrate the expertise of our Development, Module, and EPC teams, while ensuring close coordination with other vital internal groups such as Project Finance, Systems Integration, and Legal. This collaborative approach ensures that Qcells USA projects deliver exceptional value and performance. With several multi-billion-dollar investments, Qcells is pioneering the establishment of the only complete module supply chain in the U.S., including the expansion of our Georgia module manufacturing facility, which stands as the largest in the Western Hemisphere.
 
 
As an integral part of the global Qcells brand, Qcells USA benefits from a legacy of excellence in photovoltaic manufacturing. Qcells is renowned worldwide for its high-performance, superior-quality solar cells and modules. With dual headquarters in Seoul, South Korea (Global Executive HQ) and Thalheim, Germany (Technology & Innovation HQ), Qcells operates under the umbrella of Hanwha Group, a FORTUNE Global 500 company and one of the top 8 business conglomerates in South Korea.
 
 
**Summary**
The SVP, Environment, Safety, Health & Quality (ESHQ) provides senior executive leadership over all environmental, safety, health, and quality programs across Qcells USA's EPC construction operations. This role is accountable for developing and executing the company's integrated ESHQ strategy, driving a zero-incident safety culture, embedding construction quality excellence into every phase of project delivery, ensuring regulatory compliance, and managing ESHQ performance across active utility-scale solar PV and BESS project sites nationwide.
 
 
Working in close partnership with EPC project leadership, site teams, subcontractors, and corporate stakeholders, the SVP, ESHQ sets the enterprise standard for environmental stewardship, occupational health, construction safety, and quality management. This role serves as the primary ESHQ authority for the EPC business, owns the company's Quality Management System (QMS), and represents Qcells USA with regulatory agencies, clients, certification bodies, and industry organizations. This position reports to the COO, or another management personnel that the CEO of the Company may designate. This position is hybrid, based out of our Houston, TX office, requiring up to 4 days per week in the office. Standard working hours are Monday through Friday, from 8:00am to 5:00pm or 9:00am to 6:00pm local time. This position is expected to travel up to 40%.
 
 
Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the United States. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa at this time.
 
 
**Essential Job Function & Responsibilities**

* Define and lead the integrated ESHQ strategy for Qcells USA's EPC business, aligning programs with corporate goals, project requirements, client expectations, and regulatory standards across the ESH and Quality functions
* Build, develop, and manage a high-performing ESHQ organization including site safety managers, environmental coordinators, industrial hygienists, quality managers, and QA/QC engineers across multiple active projects
* Establish and enforce ESHQ policies, standards, and integrated management systems including ISO 45001 (Safety), ISO 14001 (Environmental), ISO 9001 (Quality), OSHA, and EPA requirements applicable to utility-scale solar and BESS construction
* Drive a proactive zero-incident safety culture through leadership engagement, hazard recognition programs, behavioral safety initiatives, and accountability frameworks embedded across all project sites and subcontractor workforces
* Oversee incident investigation processes; ensure root cause analyses are thorough, corrective actions are implemented, and lessons learned are shared across the project portfolio and incorporated into future planning
* Lead emergency preparedness and crisis response planning for site-level incidents; serve as executive escalation point for serious incidents, regulatory actions, or significant near-misses
* Monitor and ensure compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local environmental, safety, and health regulations across all project sites and corporate operations
* Manage environmental permitting, compliance monitoring, stormwater and spill prevention plans, and environmental impact mitigation programs for EPC projects from NTP through construction completion
* Manage relationships with OSHA, EPA, and state regulatory agencies; lead responses to inspections, citations, and enforcement actions with urgency and thoroughness
* Own and continuously improve Qcells USA's Quality Management System (QMS), ensuring it is documented, implemented, audited, and certified in accordance with ISO 9001 and applicable client and contractual quality requirements
* Oversee the development, issuance, and field implementation of Construction Quality Management Plans (CQMPs), Inspection and Test Plans (ITPs), and quality specifications for all EPC projects
* Manage the non-conformance report (NCR) process across the portfolio, ensuring timely identification, documentation, disposition, and systemic corrective action to prevent recurrence
* Lead quality audits of Qcells USA's construction operations and subcontractor quality programs; drive corrective action plans and track closure to ensure sustained compliance
* Partner with Engineering, Procurement, and Construction teams to integrate quality requirements at the design, procurement, and field execution stages, minimizing rework and defect costs
* Oversee construction punchlist management and systems turnover quality processes, ensuring projects are handed over to owners with complete documentation and no outstanding quality deficiencies
* Develop and maintain ESHQ metrics, KPIs, and reporting frameworks across both safety and quality dimensions; present integrated performance data and strategic updates to executive leadership and the Board
* Partner with EPC project managers and construction managers to integrate ESHQ requirements into project planning, scheduling, and execution from bid phase through close-out
* Oversee ESHQ orientation, training programs, and competency assessments for craft workers, site supervisors, and subcontractor personnel covering safety, environmental, and quality topics
* Support client ESHQ audits, pre-qualification requirements, and quality reporting obligations across the EPC project portfolio
* Develop and manage the ESHQ department budget, including staffing, equipment, training, certifications, and third-party services
* Represent Qcells USA in industry associations, safety councils, quality forums, and regulatory proceedings to advance ESHQ best practices in the renewable energy construction sector
* Regular attendance, in accordance with company's attendance policy and supervisory assignment, is an essential job duty requirement for this position
* Perform other duties and special projects, as assigned by Management

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Occupational Safety & Health, Environmental Science, Engineering, Quality Management, or a related field; advanced degree preferred
* Minimum of 18 years of progressive ESHQ leadership experience, with at least 7 years in a senior or executive role with accountability across both ESH and Quality functions
* Demonstrated experience leading integrated ESHQ programs in large-scale construction, EPC, energy, or infrastructure environments; utility-scale solar or BESS construction experience strongly preferred
* Deep knowledge of OSHA construction standards (29 CFR 1926), EPA regulations, NFPA 70E, and applicable state safety and environmental requirements
* Proven expertise in Quality Management Systems including ISO 9001 implementation, internal auditing, NCR management, and construction QA/QC program leadership on utility-scale EPC projects
* Experience with integrated management system frameworks (ISO 45001, ISO 14001, ISO 9001) and leading third-party certification or surveillance audits
* Proven ability to build and lead geographically dispersed ESHQ teams across multiple concurrent project sites
* Certified Safety Professional (CSP), Certified Quality Manager (CQM), or equivalent professional certification required or strongly preferred; CIH a plus
* Strong executive presence with the ability to influence project leadership, subcontractors, clients, and field personnel at all levels of the organization
* Experience managing regulatory relationships and leading responses to OSHA inspections, EPA audits, client quality audits, or state agency enforcement actions
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills; ability to present complex ESHQ performance data and strategy to executive leadership, clients, and certification bodies
* Strong organizational and program management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities across a fast-paced, growing construction portfolio

EXAMPLES OF PHYSICAL DEMANDS
 
 

* Stationary Position: frequently remains stationary up to 90% of the time and sitting up to 8 hours in a day
* Move/Traverse: infrequently bend, stand, stoop and/or walk
* Carry Weight: infrequently carry weight and/or lift objects (light to heavy) weighing up to 10 pounds
* Hearing and Speech: frequently communicates with the ability to hear and talk on a regular basis with employees, coworkers, and all personnel matters; must be able to exchange accurate information in these situations
* Sight: frequent use of sight to detect images on computer, office documents, and office objects near and far
* Climb: occasionally ascends/descends on stairway to get to office upper and lower floors
* Travel: up to 40% as needed

EXAMPLES OF WORK ENVIRONMENT
 
 

* Regular professional, office business setting
* Noise level ranges from low to moderate (if in office setting)
* Noise level ranges from moderate to high (if on construction worksite)
* Under the Office Mobilization Plan (OMP) policy, the role may transition to an onsite or hybrid arrangement, as determined by business needs and the Head of Department

Hanwha Qcells is proud to be an at-will Equal Opportunity Employer and prohibits discrimination against race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender perception or identity, national origin, age, marital status, pregnancy, citizenship, disability, protected veteran status and any other classification protected by applicable federal, state or local law. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation and training.
 
 
It is important to note that the job descriptions provided by Qcells USA Corp are not intended to be comprehensive lists of all duties, responsibilities, or qualifications associated with the positions. Duties and responsibilities may change at any time with or without notice, reflecting our dynamic and evolving work environment.
 
 
We are committed to the full inclusion of all qualified individuals. As part of this commitment, Hanwha Qcells will provide reasonable accommodations to all qualified individuals with disabilities to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and/or to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodations at hr-usa@qcells.com.

new_roles.title: Vice President of Operations, Piston Interiors
new_roles.description:
The Vice President of Operations at Piston Interiors is a key member of the executive leadership team, reporting directly to the President. This role provides enterprise-level leadership for Piston Interiors operations across the United States and Mexico and has direct responsibility for multi-plant manufacturing execution across five manufacturing facilities in northern Mexico and two distribution centers along the Texas border, supporting a workforce of more than 7,000 employees. The VP of Operations leads Manufacturing, Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, and launch execution; drives Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost, Productivity, Profitability, and Customer Performance; and builds a culture of disciplined continuous improvement, leadership accountability, and reliable execution. Candidate must be located in Acuna, Mexico or Metro-Detroit, United States to be considered for this position. Relocation will be considered.
 
 
**Responsibilities**
**Strategic Operations Leadership**

* Serve as the senior-most Operations executive for Piston Int eriors, setting enterprise direction across U.S. and Mexico

operations and maintaining direct accountability for manufacturing and distribution performance across all locations.
 
 

* Establish a clear manufacturing approach and translate business strategy into annual operating plans, budgets, capital

priorities, capacity decisions, and measurable operating objectives.
 
 

* Advise the President and executive leadership team on operating performance, customer commitments, risk, growth

readiness, resource requirements, and strategic opportunities.
 
 
**Multi-Site Operations & Performance Accountability**

* Lead plant and distribution-center execution across Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost, labor efficiency, schedule

attainment, scrap, premium freight, inventory, throughput, and profitability.
 
 

* Establish consistent daily, weekly, and monthly management cadence, visual controls, performance measures,

escalation routines, and corrective-action discipline across the operating network.
 
 

* Ensure safe working conditions, regulatory and legal compliance, ethical conduct, operational continuity, and reliable

delivery of customer commitments.
 
 
**Piston Production System (PPS), Lean & Continuous Improvement**

* Lead the cultural and process transformation from maximizing production-minute utilization to a disciplined focus on

productivity, efficiency, quality, flow, profitability, and sustainable performance.
 
 

* Deploy and sustain the Piston Production System, including standard work, visual management, tiered accountability,

structured problem solving, root-cause analysis, waste elimination, and continuous improvement.
 
 

* Use operational data and technology to improve labor utilization, first-pass yield, scrap, downtime, throughput,

process capability, and decision quality.
 
 
**Financial Performance & Resource Optimization**

* Own operating performance against profit-and-loss, cash, working-capital, productivity, cost-reduction, and annual

operating-plan commitments.
 
 

* Plan and manage direct and indirect labor, operating budgets, capital, equipment, facilities, inventory, logistics, and

other resources in alignment with financial objectives.
 
 

* Partner with Finance to understand cost drivers, program and customer profitability, forecast accuracy, capital returns,

and the financial impact of operating decisions.
 
 
**Supply Chain, Capacity & Cross-Border Operations**

* Provide executive oversight for production planning, materials, purchasing, logistics, distribution, supplier

performance, capacity, inventory, and business continuity.
 
 

* Optimize manufacturing and distribution capacity across the United States and Mexico while ensuring compliance with

applicable IMMEX, customs, import/export, USMCA, labor, and regulatory requirements.
 
 
**Growth, Engineering & Launch Excellence**

* Partner with Sales, Engineering, Program Management, Quality, Finance, and Supply Chain to secure and launch new

business with disciplined manufacturability, capacity, cost, capital, quality, and resource assumptions.
 
 

* Lead integrated launch readiness and execution, protecting existing operations while meeting customer timing,

delivery, quality, and profitability expectations.
 
 
**Organization & Talent Leadership**

* Review and optimize the operations organization structure, leadership capability, spans of control, role clarity, and

succession depth required to support current performance and future growth.
 
 

* Build, coach, and hold accountable a cohesive, high-performing multi-plant leadership team; align goal setting,

performance, development, and succession practices with the ONE PISTON Talent Cycle.
 
 
**Culture, Customer & Stakeholder Leadership**

* Inspire a culture of winning, disciplined execution, continuous improvement, trust, and collaboration while maintaining

an organizational climate that prioritizes safety, dignity, pride, satisfaction, and well-being at work.
 
 

* Build credibility with customers, employees, executive leaders, suppliers, and community stakeholders through

transparent communication, predictable results, ethical leadership, and decisive action.
 
 
**Qualifications**
**Education / Experience / Skills & Abilities**

* Bachelor’s degree required in Engineering, Operations Management, Supply Chain, Business, or a related field;

Master’s degree or MBA preferred.
 
 

* 15+ years of progressive manufacturing and operations leadership experience within automotive manufacturing,

including significant multi-site responsibility and leadership through other leaders.
 
 

* Automotive Tier 1 supplier experience required, with direct accountability for manufacturing, quality, industrial

engineering, supply chain, program/launch execution, customer delivery, and plant financial performance.
 
 

* Demonstrated profit-and-loss leadership, including budgeting, forecasting, labor management, working capital, capital

planning, cost reduction, and profitability improvement.
 
 

* Proven success implementing lean manufacturing, continuous improvement, daily management systems, and plant or

network turnaround initiatives.
 
 

* Significant experience leading U.S.-Mexico cross-border manufacturing operations; experience within an IMMEX

maquiladora environment strongly preferred.
 
 

* Experience in automotive interiors, cut-and-sew, seat trim, visors, leather/vinyl processing, or other labor-intensive

manufacturing strongly preferred.
 
 

* Bilingual proficiency in English and Spanish required.
* Strong business acumen, analytical capability, technical manufacturing knowledge, and the ability to communicate,

influence, negotiate, and build trust across all organizational levels and stakeholders.

new_roles.title: Vice President, Quality
new_roles.description:
**About LeonaBio:**
LeonaBio, Inc., headquartered in the Seattle, Washington area, is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing novel therapeutics for high unmet medical needs, including treatment-resistant metastatic breast cancer and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). Our lead programs, lasofoxifene and brelgometon, are novel small-molecule therapies with the potential to address devastating diseases where current treatment options are limited or ineffective. We are committed to scientific excellence and patient-centered innovation as we advance meaningful new therapies for patients.
 
 
**Position Summary**
LeonaBio is seeking an experienced, hands-on Vice President, Quality to lead the company's Quality function through the transition from late-stage clinical development to regulatory approval, commercial launch, and lifecycle management. This executive will be responsible for designing, implementing, and scaling a phase-appropriate Quality Management System and Quality Risk Management framework that meets global regulatory requirements, reflects the company's size and stage, and supports commercial operations.
 
 
The ideal candidate has direct leadership experience in a biotechnology company developing and commercializing small-molecule products, with a demonstrated track record of building or materially transforming Quality systems and governance. This individual will integrate product quality, patient, compliance, supply, vendor, inspection, and commercialization risks into enterprise decision-making and provide clear, risk-based guidance to executive leadership and the Board. The Vice President, Quality will foster a practical culture of quality that supports timely business decisions, inspection readiness, reliable product supply, and sustainable commercial operations.
 
 
**Responsibilities**

* Serve as the executive leader for LeonaBio's Quality function, providing strategic direction across quality systems, clinical development, manufacturing, and regulatory compliance.
* Develop and execute a scalable, phase-appropriate Quality strategy that supports late-stage clinical development, regulatory submissions, commercial readiness, and lifecycle management.
* Own the architecture, implementation, effectiveness, and scaling of the company's pharmaceutical Quality Management System (QMS) and Quality Risk Management (QRM) framework, ensuring inspection readiness and alignment with a lean, outsourced operating model.
* Ensure compliance with applicable global GxP requirements, including GMP, GCP, and GVP, while maintaining a pragmatic, risk-based approach to Quality. Lead inspection readiness, audits, quality governance, and timely resolution of observations.
* Establish and oversee the Quality governance model for CMOs, CDMOs, CROs, contract laboratories, suppliers, and other GxP partners, including qualification, quality agreements, audits, performance monitoring, risk escalation, change control, investigations, validation, and supply continuity.
* Provide Quality leadership across small-molecule drug substance and drug product development, technology transfer, process validation and PPQ, analytical methods, stability, specifications, packaging, commercial launch, and post-approval lifecycle management.
* Build and develop a high-performing Quality organization, including leadership of the Senior Director of Quality Assurance, while fostering accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in a scientific discipline required; advanced degree (MS, PhD, PharmD, or equivalent) preferred.
* 15+ years of progressive Quality experience in biotechnology or pharmaceutical companies, including significant leadership responsibility in lean, resource-constrained environments.
* Demonstrated experience leading Quality strategy through late-stage clinical development, regulatory submissions, and commercial readiness, including first product launches, with direct small-molecule experience; recent small-molecule experience preferred.
* Deep knowledge and practical application of FDA, EMA, ICH, GMP, GCP, and GVP requirements, including ICH Q9(R1) and ICH Q10 principles.
* Demonstrated experience personally designing, implementing, or materially transforming pharmaceutical QMS and QRM frameworks in organizations without mature commercial Quality systems.
* Experience leading FDA and international regulatory inspections and interacting with global health authorities.
* Experience overseeing Quality in an outsourced development and manufacturing model, including CMOs, CDMOs, CROs, and other GxP vendors.
* Proven ability to build and scale Quality organizations, lead through influence, and provide clear, risk-based recommendations to executive leadership and Boards.
* Occasional domestic travel required; international travel may be required

**Benefits & Perks**
We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support our employees and their families, including:
 
 

* Medical, dental, and vision coverage: Leona covers 100% of employee premiums and 80% of dependent premiums (Premera Blue Cross PPO, Delta Dental, VSP)
* 401(k) with employer match: immediate eligibility, with Leona matching 100% of employee contributions up to 4% of salary
* Generous PTO: 25 days accrued annually, plus 11 paid holidays and a company-wide closure the last week of December
* Life & disability coverage: Basic Life, AD&D, Short-Term and Long-Term Disability fully paid by Leona, with voluntary options available
* Flexible Spending Accounts: Health and Dependent Care FSA options
* Professional development: up to $6,000 annually reimbursed for job-relevant, manager-approved education

**Compensation**
The base salary range for this position is $320,000-$350,000. This role may be eligible for an annual bonus and equity, in addition to our full benefits package outlined above. Actual compensation will be determined based on factors including relevant experience, skill set, education, and internal pay equity.
 
 
LeonaBio is an equal opportunity employer and does not unlawfully discriminate against employees or applicants for employment on the basis of an individual's race, color, religion, creed, sex, national origin, age, disability, marital status, veteran status or any other status protected by applicable law. This policy applies to all terms, conditions and privileges of employment, including recruitment, hiring, placement, compensation, promotion, discipline and termination.

new_roles.title: Vice President of Quality
new_roles.description:
**Vice President Quality**

**Global Product Distribution Quality**

**The Opportunity**

Our client is a leading global medical technology company looking to appoint a hands-on VP Global Product Distribution Quality. Reporting directly to the SVP of Corporate Quality, you will be responsible for developing and implementing business strategies to effectively manage all global product distribution quality. In this role, you will lead the global product distribution quality organization and processes, holding quality management accountability for all captive and outsourced distribution centres across every entity worldwide.

This is a genuine turnaround and organizational design mandate, rather than a caretaker or step-up role. You will step in to stabilize day-to-day operations, manage significant FDA and global regulatory scrutiny, and reshape the commercial quality infrastructure into a world-class function. For a seasoned executive who enjoys building progressive systems at scale, there is a clear path to expanded enterprise responsibility within 6 to 20 months.

**Key Responsibilities**

* **Global Distribution Governance:**
 Own quality management systems/compliance performance across captive/3PL distribution centres globally - alongside full P&L, budget, and headcount accountability for the function.
* **Turnaround & Future-State Design:**
 Audit current teams, workflows, and systems to close compliance gaps, restructuring the global commercial quality organization into a streamlined, best-in-class model.
* **FDA & Global Regulatory Execution:**
 Act as the single accountable global executive for all distribution-related regulatory inspections, audit responses, and direct agency communications, including intensive FDA engagement.
* **Quality Systems & Digital Traceability:**
 Direct the IT partnership to optimize warehouse management systems (WMS), end-to-end product traceability, inventory controls, and nonconforming product containment.
* **Enterprise Leadership:**
 Serve as the global subject matter expert for distribution quality and contribute to enterprise-wide quality strategy as a senior member of the Global Corporate Quality leadership team.

**Candidate Profile**

* **Sitting or Recent Med-Tech VP:**
 Minimum 10 years of global organizational leadership at the Vice President level within medical devices, capital equipment, or adjacent life sciences—ready to deliver impact from day one.
* **Post-Manufacturing & 3PL Mastery:**
 Deep operational expertise in commercial, supply chain, and global distribution quality across multi-site networks (upstream supplier quality into manufacturing is out of scope).
* **Proven Remediation Track Record:**
 Demonstrated success leading quality turnarounds, organizational redesigns, and systemic remediation under active FDA scrutiny.
* **Global Trade & Customs Compliance:**
 Hands-on command of international medical device regulations, import/export laws, embargoes, import bans, and regional market-entry barriers.
* **Academic Foundation:**
 Bachelor of Science in a medical or applied science discipline

**What Sets You Apart**

You lead from the front with high energy and a clear appetite for complex turnarounds. You combine sharp analytical rigor with executive presence, enabling you to influence across commercial, supply chain, and regulatory stakeholders while building high-performing global teams.

Stord is The Consumer Experience Company, powering seamless checkout through delivery for today's leading brands. Stord is rapidly growing and is on track to double our revenue in the next 18 months. To meet and exceed this target, Stord is strategically scaling teams across the entire company, and seeking energetic experts to help us achieve our mission.
 
 
By combining comprehensive commerce-enablement technology with high-volume fulfillment services, Stord provides brands a platform to compete with retail giants. Stord manages over $10 billion of commerce annually through its fulfillment, warehousing, transportation, and operator-built software suite including OMS, Pre- and Post-Purchase, and WMS platforms. Stord is leveling the playing field for all brands to deliver the best consumer experience at scale.
 
 
With Stord, brands can increase cart conversion, improve unit economics, and drive sustained customer loyalty. Stord’s end-to-end commerce solutions combine best-in-class omnichannel fulfillment and shipping with leading technology to ensure fast shipping, reliable delivery promises, easy access to more channels, and improved margins on every order.
 
 
Hundreds of leading DTC and B2B companies like AG1, True Classic, Native, Seed Health, quip, goodr, Sundays for Dogs, and more trust Stord to deliver industry-leading consumer experiences on every order. Stord is headquartered in Atlanta with facilities across the United States, Canada, and Europe. Stord is backed by top-tier investors including Kleiner Perkins, Franklin Templeton, Founders Fund, Strike Capital, Baillie Gifford, and Salesforce Ventures.
 
 
**About The Role**
Stord is looking for a Vice President of Quality to build and lead the quality function across our fulfillment network.
 
 
This leader will own the systems, standards, and operating mechanisms that ensure inventory is accurate, processes are followed, and every order moves through our network the way it was designed to. The mandate spans the full lifecycle of inventory inside our buildings from inbound receipt and putaway through picking, packing, sorting, and outbound shipment.
 
 
This is an independent quality function. While our Operations teams are responsible for delivering volume efficiently, the VP of Quality is responsible for ensuring we never achieve speed, growth, or cost improvements by compromising inventory integrity or execution quality.
 
 
This leader should be an inventory and fulfillment quality expert at heart — someone who understands how inventory moves through a complex fulfillment operation, knows where process breakdowns create downstream failures, and is relentless about identifying and eliminating root causes.
 
 
**What You'll Own**
**Inventory Health & Accuracy**

* Own inventory health and accuracy across Stord's fulfillment network.
* Establish the standards, controls, and operating mechanisms required to maintain book-to-floor and floor-to-book inventory integrity.
* Own cycle counting, inventory reconciliation, adjustment governance, and inventory variance reduction.
* Build mechanisms to identify inventory defects early and systematically eliminate their root causes.
* Establish network-level metrics and reporting that make inventory health visible and actionable.

**Fulfillment Process Quality**

* Own process adherence across inbound, receiving, putaway, picking, packing, sorting, and outbound operations.
* Define the critical quality controls for each process path and ensure sites consistently execute against them.
* Build audit mechanisms that identify process drift before it becomes a customer or inventory issue.
* Partner with Operations, Product, Engineering, and Data to eliminate systemic sources of defects.
* Develop a clear view of transaction volume, exception rates, and defect rates by process path to identify where quality is breaking down.

**Lot Control & Regulatory Compliance**

* Own lot, expiration-date, and inventory-attribute accuracy across applicable customers and facilities.
* Establish controls for FIFO, FEFO, lot traceability, recalls, quarantine, and other regulated inventory requirements.
* Ensure Stord's operating processes meet applicable customer, regulatory, and contractual quality requirements.
* Build a quality organization capable of supporting increasingly complex and regulated categories as Stord grows.

**Continuous Improvement**

* Build a rigorous root-cause and corrective-action discipline across the fulfillment network.
* Turn recurring defects into permanent process, system, or training improvements rather than repeatedly solving individual incidents.
* Identify network-wide trends and deploy standardized improvements across sites.
* Partner with Product and Engineering to ensure recurring operational defects inform the technology roadmap.
* Create a culture where defects are surfaced quickly, investigated objectively, and permanently resolved.

**Quality Organization**

* Build and lead Stord's network Quality and Inventory Control organization.
* Establish clear ownership and accountability between Quality and Operations.
* Develop site and regional quality leaders capable of independently auditing operational performance.
* Serve as the executive escalation point when inventory integrity, regulatory compliance, or fulfillment quality is at risk.
* Maintain an independent point of view and be willing to stop, challenge, or redesign processes when quality standards are not being met.

**What We're Looking For**
We are looking for someone who has spent their career inside
**large, complex fulfillment or distribution operations**
and understands inventory at a level most operators do not.
 
 
**The Ideal Candidate**

* Has 12+ years of experience across fulfillment quality, inventory control, operational excellence, distribution, or supply chain operations, including significant leadership experience.
* Has led quality or inventory control across a multi-site fulfillment or distribution network.
* Comes from a scaled 3PL, retailer, e-commerce fulfillment network, food distribution company, or similarly complex physical operation.
* Is deeply fluent in inventory control, WMS-driven processes, cycle counting, reconciliation, lot control, and inventory accuracy.
* Understands the mechanics of inbound, putaway, pick, pack, sort, and outbound processes — and how defects in one process create downstream failures elsewhere.
* Has built quality systems based on data, audits, root-cause analysis, corrective actions, and measurable defect reduction.
* Is comfortable challenging Operations leadership when execution does not meet the required standard.
* Has operated in environments where quality and compliance cannot be traded for throughput or cost.
* Ideally brings experience from food, grocery, pharmaceutical, healthcare, or another environment with rigorous lot, expiration, traceability, or regulatory requirements.
* Can operate strategically at the executive level while still being willing to go onto the warehouse floor, trace an inventory discrepancy through a WMS, and understand exactly where a process failed.

new_roles.title: Vice President Quality Control
new_roles.description:
**This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, which manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Vice President, Quality Control based in the United States.**
The Vice President, Quality Control will provide strategic leadership for a global laboratory network supporting clinical development and commercial manufacturing programs. Reporting to the Chief Quality Officer, this executive will define and implement an enterprise-wide Quality Control strategy, ensuring scientific excellence, regulatory compliance, reliable data, and timely product release. The role oversees a broad range of laboratory operations across multiple sites and product modalities, while driving standardization, digital transformation, and operational performance. Working closely with senior executives, strategic clients, and regulatory authorities, the successful candidate will influence investment decisions, strengthen inspection readiness, and protect continuity of supply. This is an opportunity to shape a high-performing global organization and make a meaningful contribution to product quality and patient safety.
 
 
Accountabilities
 
 

* Define and execute the global Quality Control strategy, operating model, and multi-year roadmap across sites, product modalities, and development stages. Establish consistent enterprise standards, governance structures, and decision-making responsibilities while accommodating justified site-specific requirements.
* Provide executive oversight of end-to-end Quality Control operations, including analytical, biochemical, biological, microbiological, raw-material, in-process, release, and stability testing, as well as environmental and utility monitoring. Ensure laboratory capacity, priorities, and execution support program milestones, product disposition, client commitments, and uninterrupted supply.
* Govern the analytical method lifecycle from early development through transfer, qualification, validation, comparability, continued performance verification, and retirement. Ensure testing strategies and specifications evolve appropriately throughout clinical development, process performance qualification, product launch, and commercial supply.
* Establish global expectations for current good manufacturing practice, applicable good laboratory practice principles, data governance and integrity, laboratory investigations, out-of-specification and out-of-trend management, corrective and preventive action effectiveness, change control, and audit readiness. Lead enterprise-level regulatory inspection strategies and responses to critical client audits.
* Drive the global laboratory digital and technology roadmap, including laboratory information management systems, electronic laboratory notebooks, laboratory execution systems, chromatography data systems, automation, advanced analytics, and instrument connectivity. Sponsor validated technology deployment, master-data governance, cybersecurity, and adoption to improve accuracy, efficiency, and cycle times.
* Lead enterprise capacity planning, capital investment prioritization, make-versus-buy decisions, laboratory footprint strategy, and oversight of external testing partners. Align resources and contingency plans with demand forecasts, technology transfers, new product introductions, and network resilience requirements.
* Establish enterprise performance metrics and management reviews covering testing and release timelines, lead times, invalid results, out-of-specification and out-of-trend rates, investigation cycle times, corrective and preventive action effectiveness, stability execution, method performance, cost, and productivity. Promote risk-based decision-making, Lean practices, and cross-site learning.
* Act as the senior Quality Control representative for strategic clients, regulatory authorities, and executive governance. Translate complex technical and compliance risks into clear business implications, negotiate scientifically sound solutions, and ensure commitments are realistic and consistently delivered.
* Build and lead a global organization through senior leaders. Develop organizational capabilities, succession plans, technical career paths, and communities of practice while fostering scientific rigor, transparency, accountability, inclusion, and proactive risk management.
* Lead escalations and coordinated responses to significant Quality Control events, laboratory constraints, data-integrity concerns, assay failures, method or specification issues, and testing disruptions. Make or recommend risk-based decisions regarding testing strategies, product impact, remediation, and continuity of supply.
* Perform additional responsibilities in support of the broader Global Quality strategy and organizational objectives.

**Requirements**

* Bachelor's degree in Chemistry, Biochemistry, Biology, Microbiology, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Engineering, or a related scientific discipline, with at least 15 years of progressive Quality Control experience in the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO) sector; alternatively, a Master's degree with at least 10 years of relevant experience.
* At least 10 years of people-management experience, including a minimum of five years leading senior leaders with responsibility for multiple laboratories, sites, or functional areas.
* Demonstrated leadership of Quality Control operations across clinical development and commercial manufacturing, including analytical method transfer, qualification and validation, release and stability testing, microbiology, and environmental and utility monitoring.
* Proven experience managing global regulatory inspections and client audits, as well as complex out-of-specification, out-of-trend, data-integrity, and laboratory-compliance matters.
* Experience overseeing budgets, capital investment portfolios, headcount, laboratory capacity, external testing partners, and enterprise transformation initiatives within a complex, matrixed global organization.
* Strong executive communication, stakeholder-management, and client-facing skills, with the ability to communicate complex scientific and regulatory matters clearly and influence strategic decisions.
* An advanced scientific degree and/or a Master of Business Administration is preferred.
* Global leadership experience within a CDMO supporting biologics, vaccines, advanced therapies, or sterile manufacturing is highly desirable.
* Experience scaling Quality Control capabilities from clinical development through process performance qualification, product launch, and sustained commercial supply is an advantage.
* Working knowledge of relevant regulatory authorities, standards, and guidance, including the US Food and Drug Administration, European Medicines Agency, Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency, and Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency.
* Familiarity with International Council for Harmonisation guidelines Q2, Q5, Q6, Q9, Q10, and Q14; United States Pharmacopeia; European Pharmacopoeia; Japanese Pharmacopoeia; Title 21 of the Code of Federal Regulations Parts 210, 211, and 11; European Union Good Manufacturing Practice Annexes 1 and 11; and applicable data-integrity expectations.
* Experience implementing global laboratory information management systems and laboratory digitalization and automation initiatives is preferred.
* Professional credentials from the American Society for Quality, along with Lean, Six Sigma, or equivalent quality and operational excellence training, are valued.

**Benefits**

* Annual salary range of $272,000–$325,000, with compensation determined by work location and relevant knowledge, skills, and experience.
* Medical, dental, vision, and prescription drug coverage.
* Health Savings Account option with company contributions.
* Industry-leading 401(k) savings plan.
* Insurance coverage and employee assistance programs.
* Wellness incentives designed to support overall health and well-being.
* Paid vacation, sick leave, and company holidays.
* A supportive environment that encourages personal and professional development.
* Global scope, with the role supporting sites worldwide. Compensation and benefits are governed by the location designated as the employee's home site.

to ensure your application is reviewed quickly, objectively, and fairly against the role's core requirements. Our system identifies the top-fitting candidates, and this shortlist is then shared directly with the hiring company. The final decision and next steps (interviews, assessments) are managed by their internal team.
 
 
We appreciate your interest and wish you the best!
 
 
Why Apply Through Jobgether?

By submitting your application, you acknowledge that Jobgether will process your personal data to evaluate your candidacy and share relevant information with the hiring employer. This processing is based on legitimate interest and pre-contractual measures under applicable data protection laws (including GDPR). You may exercise your rights (access, rectification, erasure, objection) at any time.
 
 
We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. new_roles.title: VP Operations
new_roles.description:
Daubert Chemical Company is seeking a Vice President of Operations at our specialty chemical plant near Midway airport. The VP leads the functional areas of chemical production, customer service, supply chain, engineering, maintenance and reliability, and EHS. The VP of Operations is a member of the executive team reporting to the CEO, and is accountable for achieving safe, reliable, efficient, and cost-effective operations while consistently meeting product quality standards, customer commitments, and regulatory requirements. This leader will establish clear performance and behavioral expectations, execute with the appropriate sense of urgency, develop organizational capabilities, and drive accountability across all operational functions.
 
 
The successful candidate will balance day-to-day operational execution with long-term strategic planning, continuous improvement and corrective action programs, ensuring that plant equipment, processes, systems, and people are positioned to support business growth and operational excellence.
 
 
This position requires a hands-on, visible leader who demonstrates sound judgment, urgency, follow-up, disciplined problem-solving, and a commitment to improvement and resolution of issues via a methodical corrective action program. The VP of Operations must effectively lead through others, collaborate across departments, and develop sustainable solutions that improve safety, productivity, reliability, product quality, waste reduction, and regulatory compliance.
 
 
**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES**
include, but not limited to the following.
 
 

* Lead, coach, and develop a team of functional managers and operational leaders, establishing clear responsibilities, performance standards, and accountability. Build leadership capability at all levels through coaching, performance feedback, succession planning, and professional development
* Evaluate organizational structure, staffing levels, technical competencies, and resource requirements to ensure effective operational support
* Lead operational decision-making with a strong sense of urgency, appropriate prioritization, and consideration of safety, quality, cost, and customer impact
* Develop and manage departmental operating budgets, control expenditures, evaluate variances, and identify opportunities to improve financial performance
* Collaborate with Sales, R&D, IT, Procurement, Quality, Finance, and other functions to align operational capabilities with business requirements
* Provide leadership to production management to optimize plant capacity, equipment utilization, labor resources, product mix, and material availability
* Develop and ensure execution of a long-range capital investment plan; provide strategic leadership and oversight of plant engineering, equipment performance, reliability initiatives, and capital improvement projects that align with business priorities and integrate safety and environmental considerations
* Direct the team in the development and effectiveness of preventive, predictive, and corrective maintenance programs
* Provide executive oversight of EHS programs and ensure compliance with applicable OSHA, EPA, state, local, and other regulatory requirements
* Support effective safety inspections, regulatory audits, incident investigations, corrective actions, and ongoing risk-reduction initiatives
* Champion the use of structured problem-solving, root cause analysis, 5S, and other appropriate improvement methodologies
* Foster a culture of respect, teamwork, ownership, continuous learning, and personal accountability.
* Demonstrate and reinforce the company's Core Values: Reliable, Improving, Fair, and Caring

**Supervisory Responsibilities**
Directly manages functional leaders. Performs managerial responsibilities in accordance with the organization's policies and applicable laws, such as recruitment, selection, training, goals, performance expectations and accountability, compensation management.
 
 
**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related technical discipline required; Chemical Engineering strongly preferred. MBA preferred.
* Minimum of 10 years of progressive manufacturing and operations leadership experience, including at least five years leading managers and multiple operational functions
* Significant leadership experience in specialty chemical manufacturing, batch processing, or a comparable process manufacturing environment strongly preferred
* Demonstrated responsibility for managing and improving cost optimization with a multi-million-dollar operational budget in manufacturing operations, engineering, maintenance, equipment reliability, capital projects, and resource allocation
* Experience in a regulated manufacturing environment with strong safety, environmental, and process compliance requirements.
* Proven experience developing and executing operational improvement initiatives with measurable business results
* Experience leading cross-functional teams and managing competing operational priorities in a manufacturing plant
* Support change management and transactional integrity within the new ERP, Microsoft Dynamics - D365
* Expertise in methodologies like Lean or Six Sigma to streamline plant throughput and reduce waste
* Exhibits solid judgement along with decision making skills
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills as well as interpersonal, analytical and presentation skills.
* Must read, speak and write English fluently.
* Strong attention to detail with solid organizational and planning skills
* High degree of professional integrity, ethics and confidentiality.
* Ability to learn company ERP. Requires advances proficiency with MS Office suite i.e. Outlook, Excel, PowerPoint, SharePoint, etc.

**Compensation & Benefits**

* Base salary range $209,000-235,000, plus management incentive bonus plan
* BCBS of Illinois Medical & Dental. Vision Service Plan.
* 401(k) Savings Plan + generous company match
* Paid time off with 11 annual Holidays
* Disability, Family, & Military Leave
* Life Insurance, Identity Protection, and more!

Relocation assistance is not available. Must be authorized to work in the U.S.
 
 
Daubert Chemical Company is an Equal Opportunity Employer: Disability/Veteran.
 
 
Powered by JazzHR

new_roles.title: Vice President of Quality
new_roles.description:
VP of Quality – Structural Steel & Bridge Fabrication

**Confidential Fabricator**

The cost of poor quality rarely sits in one department.

Production loses hours to repairs.

Project managers spend time chasing answers.

Shipping loses its window.

And the customer remembers who had to explain the delay.

That’s when quality becomes a leadership issue.

A large-scale structural steel and bridge fabricator is hiring a
**VP of Quality**
to set the quality strategy and make it work across engineering, fabrication and project delivery.

You’ll set expectations with department leaders, use data on rework and audit findings to decide where to act first, and build a quality team that can support the business as it grows.

You’ll need the technical credibility to challenge a welding or inspection decision and the judgment to know when a recurring issue calls for investment, a process change or clearer ownership.

**What they’re looking for**

* Senior quality leadership in structural steel, bridge fabrication or comparable heavy welded fabrication
* Experience owning a quality management system and leading quality managers or inspection teams
* Strong knowledge of AWS D1.1, AWS D1.5 and AISC certification requirements
* Evidence of measurable improvements in rework, delivery performance or customer outcomes
* Confidence representing the business with customers, auditors and third-party inspectors

**Why it’s worth a conversation**

* Executive influence over how quality decisions are made across the business
* State-of-the-art facility: 2000+ tonnes a month
* Complex steel and bridge work where those decisions have a real impact on cost and delivery
* Scope to shape the quality team, systems and standards as the business grows

If you’ve changed how a fabrication business manages quality, I’d like to hear what you changed and what improved.

**Apply on LinkedIn or message me directly for a confidential conversation.**

new_roles.title: Vice President of Operations
new_roles.description:
**SEDIVER**

Sediver is a global leader in overhead line insulator technology, with decades of proven excellence in research, engineering, manufacturing, and field performance. With millions of insulators operating worldwide, Sediver is recognized for unmatched technical expertise, product reliability, and continuous innovation. As an industry pioneer, Sediver is actively shaping the future of more resilient, efficient, and reliable transmission and distribution networks.

With 6 commercial offices (China, France, Italy, Brazil, USA and Canada) and 4 production facilities in Italy, USA, Czech and China, the Group is highly international.

Sediver USA is in a period of sustained growth, with expanding demand across the U.S. and broader Americas grid modernization market. This trajectory creates a meaningful opportunity for Operations to scale capacity, professionalize systems, and shape the manufacturing footprint that will support the next decade of expansion.

**Position Summary:**

The Vice President of Operations is a senior executive leader accountable for setting and executing the operational strategy for Sediver USA and, in partnership with the President and Group COO, contributing to the broader Americas operational agenda. The role oversees the West Memphis, Arkansas manufacturing site — a 24/7 facility with end-to-end responsibility for production, quality, supply chain, and logistics.

This is a thought-partner role to the President of Sediver USA: the company is looking for a leader who can think beyond day-to-day plant execution and help shape how Operations enables Sediver’s long-term growth in the Americas.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**Operations & Manufacturing Leadership**

new_roles.description:
We are partnering with a leading global prestige beauty and skincare company to identify a
**Vice President of Quality**
to lead its North American Quality organization.

This is a high-impact executive leadership opportunity for a commercially minded quality professional who can connect quality, regulatory compliance, manufacturing excellence, and business performance within a complex, global organization.

The successful candidate will oversee Quality across North American manufacturing and distribution operations, providing leadership to a network of internal manufacturing operations and external manufacturing partners across multiple continents.

**About The Opportunity**

Reporting into senior global leadership, the Vice President of Quality will lead an organization of approximately 100 professionals, with four Directors reporting directly into the role.

The scope encompasses contract manufacturing quality, factory quality (QA, QC, laboratories, and Quality Management Systems), and quality assurance across North America, while providing technical quality leadership and guidance to teams in Canada and Brazil.

**Key Responsibilities**

* **Lead the North American Quality organization:**
 Provide strategic direction and leadership across manufacturing, quality assurance, quality control, laboratories, and quality systems.
* **Act as the business voice of Quality:**
 Partner with commercial, brand, manufacturing, and executive stakeholders to translate quality and regulatory requirements into sound business decisions.
* **Drive regulatory and compliance excellence:**
 Ensure alignment between global quality standards and US regulatory requirements, particularly FDA OTC regulations and Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP).
* **Oversee contract manufacturing quality:**
 Provide quality leadership and oversight across a network of approximately 30–40 contract manufacturing partners, including key strategic suppliers.
* **Strengthen organizational capabilities:**
 Develop a technically strong team, promote greater autonomy, build leadership capabilities, and establish succession depth.
* **Partner with manufacturing leadership:**
 Work closely with plant and operational leaders to balance quality expectations with production demands, providing constructive challenge and driving continuous improvement.
* **Lead through influence:**
 Build strong relationships across a global, multicultural, and matrixed organization, including teams and stakeholders outside of the direct reporting structure.
* **Prepare the organization for future growth:**
 Build the organizational structure, capabilities, and relationships necessary to support a potentially broader international Quality remit.

**Ideal Candidate Profile**

* Extensive leadership experience in Quality within beauty, personal care, consumer health, or complex consumer goods manufacturing environments.
* Strong hands-on experience with
 **FDA OTC regulations and GMP requirements**
 .
* Proven experience leading large, multi-layered Quality organizations and developing senior leadership teams.
* Experience overseeing contract manufacturers, external manufacturing partners, and complex supplier networks.
* Strong understanding of manufacturing quality, QA, QC, laboratory operations, and Quality Management Systems.
* Commercially oriented leadership approach, with the ability to translate technical and regulatory considerations into practical business decisions.
* Demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders and operate effectively within global, matrixed organizations.
* Experience balancing quality standards, operational performance, and business priorities.
* Conversational French is considered a strong advantage.

new_roles.title: Vice President of Quality
new_roles.description:
**Vice President of Quality**

**Growing Engineering & Advanced Manufacturing Business**

**Connecticut**

An exciting opportunity has arisen for an experienced Vice President of Quality to join a growing, established engineering and manufacturing business.

This is a key leadership appointment, offering the opportunity to shape and develop the quality function, drive operational excellence and embed a proactive culture of quality across the organisation.

The business is continuing to grow and invest in its manufacturing capabilities, making this an important role in ensuring that quality systems, processes and standards evolve in line with its ambitions.

We are particularly interested in hearing from individuals with a background in precision engineering, aerospace or advanced manufacturing, where quality, technical accuracy and process control are fundamental to business performance.

**The Opportunity**

Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, you will take overall responsibility for the strategic direction and operational delivery of the Quality function.

A key priority will be to move quality beyond a reactive, inspection-led approach, working closely with Engineering, Manufacturing, Production and Supply Chain to identify the root causes of issues, implement sustainable corrective actions and prevent recurrence.

You will play a highly visible, cross-functional role, influencing how the business operates and ensuring quality is embedded at every stage of the manufacturing process.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead and develop the Quality function, establishing a clear strategy, measurable objectives and a culture of continuous improvement.
* Drive a proactive approach to Quality Assurance, focusing on identifying the underlying causes of process and product issues rather than simply addressing the symptoms.
* Work collaboratively with Engineering, Manufacturing, Production and Supply Chain to improve process capability, product consistency and operational performance.
* Lead root cause analysis, corrective and preventative action (CAPA) and structured problem-solving initiatives.
* Oversee the Quality Management System, ensuring robust processes, compliance and readiness for internal, external and customer audits.
* Develop and monitor quality KPIs, using data and trend analysis to identify opportunities for improvement and drive accountability.
* Take ownership of supplier quality, working with key suppliers to improve standards, resolve issues and strengthen supply chain performance.
* Partner with Engineering on new product introduction, design changes and manufacturing process improvements.
* Develop, coach and lead a capable quality team, building technical expertise and accountability throughout the function.
* Work closely with the senior leadership team to ensure quality initiatives support wider business objectives, customer satisfaction and continued growth.

**The Ideal Candidate**

We are looking for a commercially aware and technically credible Quality leader who can operate strategically while remaining close enough to the manufacturing operation to understand where and why issues occur.

**You will ideally bring:**

* Significant senior-level Quality leadership experience within a precision engineering, aerospace, advanced manufacturing or similarly demanding engineering environment.
* A strong background in Quality Assurance, Quality Management Systems and manufacturing process control.
* Proven experience of leading root cause analysis and driving effective, lasting corrective actions across complex manufacturing processes.
* The ability to work cross-functionally, influencing Engineering, Operations, Production and Supply Chain teams to improve quality performance.
* A good understanding of machining, manufacturing processes, materials and engineering specifications.
* Experience with continuous improvement methodologies, statistical process control and quality performance metrics.
* Experience managing customer and supplier quality, audits and regulatory or industry compliance requirements.
* Strong leadership and communication skills, with the ability to develop teams and influence at all levels of an organisation.
* A relevant engineering or science degree, alongside substantial Quality Management experience, would be advantageous.

**POSITION SUMMARY**
The Head of Global Quality Strategic Initiatives is responsible for defining, leading and executing enterprise-wide initiatives that strengthen TransMedics’ global quality management system (QMS), enhance regulatory compliance, improve product quality and patient safety, and advance operational excellence across the product lifecycle.
 
 
Partnering closely with executive leadership and cross-functional teams, this leader translates business priorities into measurable quality outcomes. The role drives complex transformation programs, anticipates emerging quality and regulatory risks, and establishes the processes, governance and metrics needed to support growth while maintaining high standards of safety, effectiveness and compliance.
 
 
The successful candidate combines deep medical device quality and regulatory expertise with strategic vision, strong business acumen and exceptional program leadership, with the ability to influence at every level of a global organization.
 
 
**Responsibilities**
This position is responsible for, but not limited to, the following:
 
 

* Develop and execute a multi-year global quality roadmap aligned with business priorities, regulatory expectations and patient safety. Identify systemic issues and emerging risks, prioritize transformation initiatives, and integrate quality priorities into business planning, product development and growth.
* Lead a portfolio of cross-functional quality programs with clear scope, milestones, resources, accountability and measurable outcomes. Establish executive steering committees, decision rights and escalation paths; resolve barriers, recommend investment priorities and track business impact and sustained results.
* Improve and harmonize the global QMS in line with FDA QMSR (21 CFR Part 820), ISO 13485, EU MDR and other applicable requirements. Strengthen process ownership, management review and effectiveness monitoring while accommodating regional requirements and local operating needs.
* Oversee improvement programs spanning document and records management, design and manufacturing controls, risk management, supplier quality, nonconformance, corrective and preventive action (CAPA), change control and post-market processes.
* Partner with Regulatory Affairs and site Quality leaders to assess regulatory changes and lead enterprise remediation programs addressing audit findings, regulatory observations and emerging risks. Support FDA inspections and external audits, resolve root causes, and embed sustainable inspection readiness.
* Define enterprise quality KPIs and key risk indicators covering CAPA effectiveness, complaints, nonconformances, audit findings, suppliers and product quality. Build consistent dashboards and executive reporting that improve visibility into risks, trends and program progress.
* Sponsor electronic QMS, quality data integration, advanced analytics and appropriate AI-enabled initiatives within applicable validation, privacy, security and regulatory controls. Promote data integrity, traceability and evidence-based decisions.
* Partner with functional leaders to strengthen product risk management, complaint handling, adverse event reporting, field action assessment and post-market monitoring from development and design transfer through manufacturing and post-market surveillance. Lead analysis of recurring issues and systemic failure modes to improve detection, containment and prevention.
* Apply Lean, Six Sigma and risk-based problem-solving to reduce rework, scrap, variation and the cost of poor quality while protecting compliance and patient safety. Partner with Manufacturing, Engineering, Supply Chain and site leaders to improve process capability and supplier performance, replicate best practices and measure benefits.
* Advise the Chief Regulatory Officer and executive leadership on quality priorities, systemic risks and transformation opportunities; communicate with the Board as appropriate. Influence priorities and resource decisions, mentor quality and program leaders, and lead training and change management that build accountability, transparency and lasting quality ownership.
* Collaborate with IT/Digital, Finance, Human Resources and other internal partners, and engage regulatory authorities, notified and certification bodies, external auditors, strategic suppliers, consultants and industry organizations as needed.
* Success will be measured by on-time transformation milestones; stronger QMS effectiveness and consistency; fewer recurring issues, overdue corrective actions and repeat audit findings; sustained inspection readiness; and measurable improvements in product quality, complaint trends, supplier performance and cost of poor quality.
* Perform other TransMedics tasks and duties as assigned.

**Management Responsibilities**
Convene and lead cross-functional teams, establish program governance, and develop and mentor quality and program leaders within the approved mandate, budget and governance structure. Direct-report responsibilities are to be confirmed. Formal authority for regulatory decisions, product disposition, quality approvals and regulatory reporting remains with the accountable functions under company procedures.
 
 
**PHYSICAL ATTRIBUTES**
This is an on-site role in Andover or Somerville, MA, with approximately 10–20% travel. Additional essential physical requirements, if applicable, are to be confirmed.
 
 
**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Life Sciences, Quality, Regulatory Affairs or a related technical discipline.
* 15+ years of progressive experience in medical devices, combination products or another highly regulated healthcare industry, including significant leadership experience in Quality, Regulatory Affairs, quality transformation or enterprise program management.
* Proven success leading complex quality improvement, remediation or organizational change programs across business units, manufacturing sites and geographies, translating strategy into executable plans and measurable, sustainable results.
* Strong knowledge of FDA medical device requirements, including QMSR, and working knowledge of ISO 13485, ISO 14971, EU MDR and applicable global medical device frameworks.
* Hands-on experience with CAPA, nonconformances, complaints, design controls, supplier quality, change management, audits, remediation and post-market surveillance; understanding of root cause analysis, process validation, manufacturing controls and QMS effectiveness.
* Familiarity with electronic QMS platforms, quality data analytics and computerized system validation or assurance (CSV/CSA) principles.
* Ability to influence senior executives and stakeholders in a global matrix organization, communicate complex issues clearly, and drive decisions without relying on direct authority.
* Demonstrated strategic thinking, analytical problem-solving, change leadership and talent development, with sound risk-based judgment, integrity and accountability for product quality, patient safety and regulatory compliance.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Advanced degree in Engineering, Life Sciences, Business Administration or a related field.
* Professional certifications in quality (ASQ CQE or CMQ/OE), regulatory affairs (RAC), program management (PMP), Lean Six Sigma or change management.
* Experience with MasterControl.

As part of our long-term growth plans, TransMedics is excited to announce our plan to relocate our headquarters (HQ) to Somerville, MA by 2028. We chose this location because we believe it is a place where innovation will thrive. Our new state-of-the-art headquarters is designed to support collaboration, creativity, and discovery. We believe this will be a place where we can continue to do things few thought possible in organ transplantation to help patients.
*Specific timing and role impact may vary.*
TransMedics, Inc. is a commercial-stage medical technology company transforming organ transplant therapy for patients worldwide. Our mission is to help save more patients’ lives by increasing access to viable donor organs for those who are awaiting an organ transplant. To accomplish this mission, we partner closely with transplant stakeholders worldwide and help expand their access to healthy donor organs, while delivering the highest quality technology, service, clinical care and outcomes.
 
 
Driven by a passion for improving patient care, we make the impossible possible and keep our employees at the center of everything we do. Together, we strive to enhance the quality of life for transplant recipients and their families, fostering hope and healing in the journey toward better health.
 
 
**Maximize your potential at TransMedics, Inc.**
www.TransMedics.com
 
 
TransMedics is committed to equitable and transparent compensation. The expected base salary range for this role is $232,800-$331,350, which represents the company’s current good-faith estimate of compensation for this position. Actual salary will depend on factors such as, but not limited to, candidate experience, qualifications, skills, and the specific work location. This role may also be eligible for bonuses, equity, and a comprehensive benefits package (medical, dental, vision, retirement savings, paid time off, and wellness resources). We comply with all U.S. pay transparency laws and do not request or consider salary history.
 
 
**Employee Benefit**
Medical with Health Reimbursement Account through Blue Cross/Blue Shield of MA
 
 
Dental
 
 
Vision
 
 
Healthcare Flexible Spending Account
 
 
Dependent Care Flexible Spending Account
 
 
Short Term Disability
 
 
Long Term Disability
 
 
401K Plan
 
 
Pet insurance
 
 
Employee Stock Purchase Plan
 
 
TransMedics is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, marital status, age, disability or protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

new_roles.title: SVP Quality Systems - 2718
new_roles.description:
An established regenerative medicine company with a commercial wound care portfolio and a biologic advancing through FDA licensure. The SVP, Quality Systems will lead the entire quality organization, owning commercial manufacturing quality and a major remediation program for the biologic manufacturing operation. This is a rebuilding role: finalize the remediation plan, restructure and grow the team, and strengthen the quality system with lean resources at first. A rare chance for a seasoned biologics quality leader to make a visible, company-defining impact, with a path for upward mobility.
 
 
**You'll Love This Opportunity Because**

* Two substantial mandates at once: lead biologic remediation through licensure and oversee complex commercial manufacturing.
* Direct exposure to the executive team and board, reporting to a COO who gives department heads real independence.
* A technology- and patient-focused culture at an established leader in regenerative medicine.

**The Ideal Candidate Will Have**

* Senior biologics or biopharma quality executive who has brought a product through BLA and led commercial product quality.
* Has led a company through a pre-license inspection, warning letter, or comparable remediation, with strong FDA working relationships.
* A culture builder who can rebuild a team and deliver with lean resources, not someone looking for a steady-state role.
* Based in Greater Boston and ready to be on site every day.
* Cell therapy experience is a plus but not required.
