new_roles.title: Director, Operations
new_roles.description:
**Company Overview**
**Nikkiso Clean Energy & Industrial Gases**
is a leading provider of cryogenic pumps, heat exchangers, process systems, services, and solutions for the LNG and industrial gases industry. We are a subsidiary of Nikkiso Company Ltd, a leading industrial manufacturer headquartered in Tokyo, Japan, with over $1.5 B in annual revenue, 8000 + employees worldwide, and publicly traded on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
 
 
**Nikkiso ACD**
is an engineering and manufacturing company specializing in machinery designed to operate at cryogenic temperatures as low as – 420 degrees Fahrenheit, the boiling point of Liquid hydrogen. For over 50 years, Nikkiso ACD has specialized in centrifugal and reciprocating pumps as well as turbines for air separation. Nikkiso ACD has the most diversified product line in the industry covering nearly every application requiring pumps or turboexpanders.
 
 
**Job Overview**
The Director, Operations is responsible for overseeing all aspects of the manufacturing process. This role will develop and implement strategies that optimize the efficiency and effectiveness of the manufacturing operations to ensure the delivery of high-quality products on time and within budget.
 
 
**Responsibilities**

* Develop and implement operational strategies that improve the efficiency, productivity, and profitability of the manufacturing operations for cryogenic pumps
* Ensure that manufacturing operations comply with all relevant safety and environmental regulations
* Develop and manage the annual manufacturing budget and monitor and control expenses to ensure that they remain within budgetary constraints
* Identify and implement process improvements that increase efficiency, reduce costs, and enhance product quality while reducing product cost and increase margins
* Manage and develop a large team of manufacturing professionals, providing coaching and mentoring to enable them to reach their full potential
* Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including engineering, design, and sales, to ensure that products meet customer requirements
* Maintain positive relationships with key stakeholders, including suppliers, customers, and outsourced manufacturing partners
* Develop and implement consistent processes and best practice strategies, policies, procedures, and goals
* Work cross-functionally with product manager, product development, engineering and project management teams to ensure company goals are met and the necessary support to deliver on time is provided
* Lead the effort in identification, recruiting, interviewing, onboarding, training, and ongoing engagement of high-performance team members
* Monitor and analyze key performance indicators for manufacturing such as safety, quality, delivery, cost, cash and, people
* Address escalated customer issues with speed and urgency, orchestrating resources across the company as appropriate
* Identify and remove obstacles to delivering products consistently on time with the right quality

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's or Master’s degree in Engineering, Supply Chain, or Operations Management, or related field or equivalent work experience
* Minimum of 10 years of experience in a manufacturing leadership role, preferably in the rotating equipment industry
* Extensive knowledge in manufacturing that are consistent with pump products, and how they are manufactured for the cryogenic industry preferred
* Proven track record of developing and implementing operational strategies that improve efficiency, productivity, and profitability
* Experience managing budgets and controlling expenses for operations
* Strong understanding of regulatory requirements and environmental and safety regulations
* Extensive knowledge in lean manufacturing
* Strong knowledge of quality control systems and procedures
* Hands-on experience working with global manufacturing operations
* Broad knowledge of multi-functional and multi-site teams working in a global environment
* Broad knowledge working with cryogenic industries
* Hands-on experience with Problem Solving / Six Sigma
* Project Planning / Project Management experience is preferred
* Ability to communicate effectively with senior management
* Proficient in Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook
* Progressive experience in roles leading manufacturing operations
* High adaptability and flexibility, including the ability to manage deadline pressure, ambiguity, and change
* Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to connect with and positively influence leadership at all levels of the organization
* Self-motivated with extremely strong sense of urgency-act as a change agent in the organization
* Demonstrates excellence in interpersonal skills - verbal and written communication, self-starter, positive make-it-happen attitude, team player
* Able to travel domestically and internationally as needed

**Supervisory Responsibility**
Reports to Director, Operations and manages and develops a team of manufacturing professionals, providing coaching and mentoring to enable them to reach their full potential.
 
 
**Work Environment**
This job operates in both a professional office environment and a manufacturing/production environment. Commitment to safety is essential. This role routinely uses standard office equipment such as laptop computers, photocopiers, and smartphones.
 
 
**Physical Demands**
While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to talk or hear. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision and ability to adjust focus. This would require the ability to lift files, open filing cabinets and bend or stand on a stool as necessary.
 
 
**Other Duties**
Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice.
 
 
**Salary Range:**
$150,000 - $200,000 per year.
 
 
**EEOC Statement**
Nikkiso CE&IG is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or protected veteran status and will not be discriminated against on the basis of disability. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

new_roles.title: Director, Plant Operations
new_roles.description:
Welcome to CTI Foods, where quality, service, and people are at the heart of everything we do. We are a leading food manufacturing company, dedicated to providing our customers with the best possible products and our employees with a rewarding career.
 
 
At CTI, we passionately believe that people are our #1 ingredient. We provide a positive and supportive work environment, opportunities for growth and advancement, and a competitive compensation package. We value our employees' contributions and strive to create a culture of respect, teamwork, and excellence.
 
 
Whether you're interested in a career in production, quality control, or management, we have a variety of opportunities available. We believe that our success is a result of our focus on quality, service, and people, and we look forward to continuing to serve our customers and employees with excellence.
 
 
If you're looking for a rewarding career in the food manufacturing industry, look no further than CTI Foods! Join our team and become a part of a company that values quality, service, and people.
 
 
**Job Overview**
To lead and direct production and maintenance functions for the respective location, while supporting and adhering to the efforts of safety, food safety, supply chain, human resources, and commercialization, in order to meet location’s business objectives as established by the Senior Leadership Team.
 
 
**Responsibilities**

* Direct daily operations while maintaining compliance to quality and regulatory standards.
* Execute all plans and initiatives as directed by safety, supply chain, food safety, HR and other cross functional areas.
* Achieve all location KPIs.
* Achieve budget for all operating costs including manufacturing, maintenance, and labor.
* Champion and model the CTI culture and the necessary mindsets to (3Fs) to deliver optimal results.
* Actively participate and engage with other plant leaders for best practice sharing and replication for areas such as network optimization and asset efficiency.
* Lead continuous improvement efforts around plant performance, people and processes to execute on current goals and to prepare for future growth.
* Lead team by effectively utilizing CTI’s Operating Principles.
* Attract, hire and lead the supervisory teams throughout the location, ensuring that all team members are knowledgeable with operating processes and procedures.
* Ability to develop the maintenance department into a pro-active / asset life management model.
* Identify, study and determine the processing equipment that best meets production needs from a product quality and productivity standpoint.
* Play a key role on major CAPEX project budgeting and large project management to ensure timely completion and on budget.
* Define and model the overall facility capacity to have an overall understanding of bottlenecks and limitations.
* Knowledge of USDA-FSIS regulations and ability to work with USDA inspectors on an ongoing basis to ensure compliance to all USDA regulations and HACCP and SQF requirements.
* Knowledge of other regulatory requirements, including OSHA and EPA/DNR. OSHA experience covering worker safety in a protein processing environment as well as ammonia-based refrigeration. EPA/DNR as it pertains to plant discharges either by air or water.
* Maintains continuity among work teams by documenting and communicating actions, irregularities, and continuing needs.
* Any other duties as assigned.

**Qualifications**
What we need from you:
 
 

* Minimum of 10 years of operations management experience, food manufacturing preferred. Bachelor’s degree in Business, Food Science, Engineering, or related field preferred.
* Ability to apply understanding to carry out instructions furnished in written, oral or diagram form.
* Track record of strong performance as a senior operations manager with demonstrated operations and management talent and a desire to participate in a team environment.
* Demonstrated experience in organizational and process improvement, ideally with using Lean, Kaizen, and Six Sigma concepts.
* Long term and short-term planning skills.
* Budget development and presentation skills.
* Ability to effectively analyze and evaluate new equipment and new processes and assign a value for reduced labor, yield improvement, or quality improvement.
* Negotiating strategy and skills, for dealing with vendors, union, or government personnel.
* Must be able to adapt to and become an advocate of the company mission and vision statements.
* Team member who will quickly earn and maintain the personal and professional respect of people inside and outside the Company.
* Articulate and effective communicator with the ability to influence others through the employment of sound judgment.
* Maintains professional demeanor, high standards of integrity, honesty, loyalty, and ethical values.

What you'll receive from us:
 
 

* Salary within the range of $160,000 - $175,000, depending on experience\*
* Unlimited PTO\*
* Medical, Dental, & Vision Insurance
* Company Paid Life Insurance
* Telehealth Services
* 401K Matching
* FSA & HSA available
* EAP and wellbeing support
* Tuition reimbursement program available
* The estimate displayed represents the typical salary range of candidates hired. Factors that may be used to determine your actual salary may include your specific skills, how many years of experience you have and comparison to other employees already in this role. Most candidates will start in the bottom half of the range. Unlimited PTO requests are subject to approval and is subject to the current business needs of CTI Foods.

new_roles.title: Director of Operations | OKC
new_roles.description:
**General Description:**

The Director of Operations is a strategic leader who oversees the entire production lifecycle. This role is responsible for optimizing production schedules to meet customer delivery requirements and maximizing the company’s productive capacity. A key function is process management, which involves constantly analyzing and refining workflows to improve efficiency, reduce waste, and enhance product quality. The director is also crucial to ensure customer satisfaction by guaranteeing that products are delivered on time and meet quality standards. The Director of Operations ensures that all operational components work together seamlessly to achieve business goals.

**Essential Functions:**

* Production & Process Management: Oversee the entire production process, ensuring all production schedules meet customer delivery requirements and maximize the company's productive capacity.
* Blueprint & Specification Interpretation: Read and interpret blueprints, customer purchase orders, and process specifications to guide production activities.
* Cross-Functional Collaboration: Serve as the primary point of contact for internal communication, collaborating with the Quality, Production, and Engineering Departments to address Non-Conformance Reports (NCRs) and ensure accuracy.
* Quality System & Audits: Develop a deep understanding of the company's quality system to effectively participate in customer quality audits and sales visits.
* Customer & Scheduling Coordination: Partner with Customer Service to prioritize jobs and adjust production schedules based on customer urgency.
* Process Improvement: Establish, document, and continuously improve production processes and schedules to meet release dates and enhance overall efficiency.
* Inventory Management: Manage and maintain optimal inventory levels to support production needs without creating excess stock.

**Competencies:**

* Leadership & Team Management: Ability to lead and manage a diverse team, fostering a collaborative and productive work environment.
* Operational & Technical Expertise: A strong understanding of manufacturing processes, including plating, grinding, and HVOF, with the ability to schedule work across various centers.
* Problem-Solving & Analysis: Skilled in identifying issues, analyzing root causes, and implementing effective solutions to improve operations.
* Communication: Excellent verbal and written communication skills for interfacing with internal teams and external customers.
* Organizational & Time Management: Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines effectively.
* Ethical Conduct: Upholds high ethical standards in all business practices.
* Technical Proficiency: Computer literate with the ability to use standard office software and specialized production systems.

**Supervisory Responsibility:**

**This position is responsible for managing all shop employees, including performance management and assisting with hiring needs.**

**Required Education:**

**5-10 years of experience in production operations, including managing employees, implementing processes, and purchasing. Proven experience in production and process improvement.**

**Experience:**

**A degree in a related field is preferred but not required with sufficient experience.**

**Work Environment:**

**This role operates in both a professional office environment and on the production floor.**

**Physical Demands:**

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job.

·        Mobility and Lifting: This role requires frequent movement and the ability to lift and move objects. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 10 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds. The job may also require occasional sitting, climbing, balancing, stooping, kneeling, crouching, or crawling.

·        Vision: Specific vision requirements include close vision for reading documents and labels, distance vision, and the ability to distinguish colors, as well as peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus. A minimum of 20/20 vision with or without corrective lenses is required.

·        Safety Equipment: The employee must be physically able to safely utilize, and wear required PPE, such as a dust mask, steel-toe footwear, and safety glasses.

·        The role requires the ability to remain in a stationary position for extended periods.

**Position Type/Expected Hours of Work:**

**This is a full-time position with an expected work schedule of Monday through Friday, 7:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.**

**Travel:**
No travel is expected for this position.

**Other Duties:**

Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

\*\*\*Must be able to undergo a drug screening

new_roles.title: Director of Manufacturing Operations (low-vol/high-mix, multi-dept oversight exp. req. / Mesquite)
new_roles.description:
**Director of Manufacturing Operations (low-volume, high-mix or complex assembly req.)**

**Location: East Dallas, near Mesquite, TX**

**Salary: $200,000 - $250,000+ (DOE) + Performance-based Bonus + Benefits**

**Benefits: Medical, Dental, Vision, Holidays, PTO, Equity Shares**

**Job Type: Full-Time | On-site**

**Typical Hours: Monday-Friday; 40-45 hours/week**

**Start Date: ASAP**

**Sponsorship is not available**

**Relocation assistance available**

**Director of Manufacturing Operations Description**

Our client in the manufacturing industry is looking for a Director of Manufacturing Operations to join their team in East Dallas, near Mesquite, TX. This newly created role will lead approximately 40 employees across production, supply chain, inventory, quality, and continuous improvement, through three direct report managers. You will build the operating systems needed to support continued growth, with an emphasis on improving production flow, standardizing work, strengthening material availability, and reducing order-to-ship lead times. The operation is low-volume, high-mix, and highly customized, making experience applying lean principles in complex manufacturing environments critical. Our client is looking for a manufacturing leader who has led multiple functions and personally delivered measurable improvements from batch production toward flow. This is an opportunity to build and improve an operating system while leading a growing manufacturing organization in a high-demand market.

**Director of Manufacturing Operations Responsibilities**

• Lead production, supply chain, inventory, quality, and facilities

• Develop production flow, capacity, scheduling, and standard work systems

• Reduce order-to-ship lead times and improve on-time delivery

• Build material replenishment, point-of-use, and inventory systems

• Improve supplier performance, sourcing, material availability, and lead times

• Move quality controls upstream to reduce defects reaching final testing

• Establish daily management and structured problem-solving systems

• Lead lean improvements across low-volume, high-mix production

• Develop operations leaders and an approximately 40-person team

• Build capacity to support growth without proportional labor or space increases

**Director of Manufacturing Operations Qualifications**

• 10+ years of manufacturing operations experience required

• 5+ years leading multiple manufacturing departments, including production, required

• Low-volume, high-mix or complex assembly experience required

• Experience leading production flow improvements or measurable lead-time reduction required

• Experience implementing and sustaining lean management practices in manufacturing required

• Experience scaling production capacity or output required

• Manufacturing ERP proficiency required

new_roles.description:
**Application Close Date**
Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed.
 
 
At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!
 
 
This role is part of Blue Origin Operations, which is comprised of Integrated Supply Chain, Test Operations, Safety, Quality, and Mission Assurance. This includes Manufacturing and Supply Chain support across all Blue Origin facilities.
 
 
**About Blue Origin**
We are a team of collaborators, doers, and problem-solvers who are relentlessly committed to a culture of safety. These positions will directly impact the history of space exploration and will require your commitment and detailed attention towards safe and repeatable spaceflight. Join us in lowering the cost of access to space and enabling Blue Origin's vision of millions of people living and working in space to benefit Earth.
 
 
We are looking for senior leaders to apply their technical expertise, leadership skills, and commitment to quality to positively impact safe human spaceflight. Passion for our mission and vision is required.
 
 
**About This Opportunity**
Blue Origin is actively building its senior manufacturing and operations leadership team across multiple sites. We are seeking experienced Directors and Senior Directors with a strong aerospace background to lead high-performing teams in support of rocket engine and spacecraft production programs.
 
 
By expressing interest in this opportunity, you will be considered for current and future openings aligned to your experience and location preference. Roles span the following functional areas:
 
 
**Manufacturing**
 
 
Provides senior leadership across production operations including assembly, machine shop, heat treat, welding, and component fabrication for space systems and propulsion programs. Accountable for establishing and maintaining process controls, driving production efficiency, and ensuring safe, repeatable spaceflight hardware delivery at all stages of the product lifecycle.
 
 
**Test**
Provides leadership across test operations supporting engine, component, and system-level testing. Accountable for ensuring test processes are executed safely, efficiently, and in alignment with program requirements. Drives continuous improvement in test throughput, first-time quality, and the feedback loop between test results and production processes.
 
 
**Fabrication**
Provides leadership across fabrication operations including machining, welding, composites, additive manufacturing, cleaning, and post-processing of flight hardware. Accountable for the development, qualification, and continuous improvement of fabrication processes and capabilities that meet the demanding quality and schedule requirements of space and propulsion programs.
 
 
**Integration**
 
 
Provides leadership across integration operations supporting the assembly and verification of complex space systems, launch vehicles, and propulsion hardware. Accountable for coordinating cross-functional teams to ensure the safe, on-time integration of hardware in alignment with engineering requirements, mission assurance standards, and program milestones.
 
 
**Key Responsibilities**
Leaders across these functional areas are expected to:
 
 

* Lead and develop teams of Managers, Senior Managers, and Directors driving manufacturing and operations execution across space and propulsion programs
* Champion a culture of safety, quality, and continuous improvement across all functional teams
* Own departmental KPIs, budgets, staffing plans, and capital project portfolios
* Partner with Program Management, Site Leadership, and cross-functional stakeholders to meet production schedules and customer expectations
* Drive process definition, development, deployment, and improvement initiatives including Lean Manufacturing and root cause analysis
* Collaborate with engineering teams to advance Design for Manufacturability principles and accelerate the transition from development to production
* Implement and mature production frameworks that support world-class manufacturing capabilities
* Communicate and enforce mission assurance and safety principles throughout the organization
* Recruit, develop, coach, and mentor talent at all levels of the organization

**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Manufacturing, Industrial, Aerospace, or Electrical Engineering, or equivalent experience
* 15 or more years of progressive experience in aerospace manufacturing or a closely related industry, such as launch vehicles, aircraft, spacecraft systems, or defense
* 5 or more years in a senior leadership role managing managers and large, cross-functional teams
* Demonstrated experience leading manufacturing and operations teams in fast-paced, complex environments
* Proven ability to manage budgets, schedules, and capital projects at a department or program level
* Strong quality mindset with expertise in root cause analysis and corrective action methodologies
* Experience with process definition, development, deployment, measurement, and continuous improvement
* Effective communicator across all levels of an organization, including executive leadership
* Must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Master's degree, MBA, or advanced degree in a relevant engineering or business field
* Prior experience in aerospace environments supporting space hardware, rocket propulsion, or other mission-critical, high-value components
* Familiarity with Lean Manufacturing, the Toyota Production System, or Six Sigma; Black Belt certification preferred
* Experience transitioning manufacturing capabilities from development and prototyping into full-rate production
* Knowledge of fabrication processes including machining, welding, composites, additive manufacturing, cleaning, and non-destructive testing
* Experience with facility activation, new production line startup, or multi-site manufacturing operations
* Proficiency with MRP/ERP, PLM, and Manufacturing Execution Systems

**Base Pay Range For**
WA applicants is $203,165.00 - $284,430.30
 
 
**Other Site Ranges May Differ**
**Culture Statement**
Don’t meet all desired requirements? Studies have shown that some people are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single desired qualification. At Blue Origin, we are dedicated to building an authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every desired qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.
 
 
**Export Control Regulations**
Applicants for employment at Blue Origin must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e. current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.
 
 
**Background Check**

* Required for all positions: Blue’s Standard Background Check
* Required for Certain Job Profiles: Defense Biometric Identification System (DBIDS) background check if at any time the role requires one to be on a military installation
* Required for Certain Job Profiles: Drivers who operate Commercial Motor Vehicles with a Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW), Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) or combination of power unit and trailer that meets or exceeds 10,001 lbs. and/or transports placardable amounts of hazardous materials by ground in any vehicle on a public road while in commerce, may be subject to additional Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations including: Driver Qualification Files, Medical Certification (obtained before onboarding), Road Test, Hours of Service, Drug and Alcohol Testing, vehicle inspection requirements, CDL requirements (if applicable) and hazardous materials transportation/shipping training.
* Required for certain Job Profiles: Ability to obtain and maintain Merchant Mariner Credential, which includes pre-employment and random drug testing as well as DOT physical

**Benefits**

* Benefits include: Medical, dental, vision, basic and supplemental life insurance, paid parental leave, short and long-term disability, 401(k) with a company match of up to 5%, and an Education Support Program.
* Stock Options for all regular employees (working at least 20 hours/week)
* Paid Time Off: Up to four (4) weeks per year based on weekly scheduled hours, and up to 14 company-paid holidays.
* Dependent on role type and job level, employees may be eligible for benefits and bonuses based on the company's intent to reward individual contributions and enable them to share in the company's results, or other factors at the company's sole discretion. Bonus amounts and eligibility are not guaranteed and subject to change and cancellation. Please check with your recruiter for more details.

**Equal Employment Opportunity**
Blue Origin is proud to be an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer and is committed to attracting, retaining, and developing a highly qualified and dedicated work force. Blue Origin hires and promotes people on the basis of their qualifications, performance, and abilities. We support the establishment and maintenance of a workplace that fosters trust, equality, and teamwork. We provide all qualified applicants for employment and employees with equal opportunities for hire, promotion, and other terms and conditions of employment, regardless of their race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin/ethnicity, age, physical or mental disability, genetic factors, military/veteran status, or any other status or characteristic protected by federal, state, and/or local law. Blue Origin will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with applicable federal, state, and local laws, including the Washington Fair Chance Act, the California Fair Chance Act, the Los Angeles Fair Chance in Hiring Ordinance, and other applicable laws. For more information on “Know Your Rights,” please see here.
 
 
**Affirmative Action and Disability Accommodation**
Applicants wishing to receive information on Blue Origin’s Affirmative Action Plans, or applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation in order to participate in the application and/or interview process, please contact us at EEOCompliance@blueorigin.com. Please note this is a publicly managed inbox. Please do not include any personal medical information in your request.

new_roles.title: Director of Operations
new_roles.description:
**Director of Operations**

The Director of Operations is responsible for directing all aspects of manufacturing, scheduling and maintenance/engineering functions to maximize Company profits and customer satisfaction. The Director of Ops is responsible for achieving the business objectives of the Company within the budgetary, safety and productivity parameters established by the President and CEO.

**Responsibilities**

* Champions customer care in the production plant by interacting with customers and providing technical production support during all stages of the relationship from quotation and job planning to the permanent resolution of customer quality problems.
* In collaboration with the President and CEO, establishes an annual operating and capital budget for the manufacturing, scheduling and maintenance/engineering departments and manages all costs within these budgetary limits.
* In collaboration with the President and CEO, establishes annual improvement goals for manufacturing key measures, utilizing Lean Manufacturing as primary driver to accomplish goals.
* Directly responsible for maximizing profitability and driving cost out of the production and customer service process.
* Directly responsible for operating the plant in a manner that protects the health and safety of all employees, contractors, visitors, etc. and ensures compliance with the environmental laws and regulations interpreted to be applicable by the Safety Director.
* Interacts with customers and provides support during all stages of the relationship from quotation and job planning to resolution of customer quality problems.
* Responsible for supporting positive working relationship with local labor union through in depth understanding of the labor contract, fair and consistent implementation of its terms and respectful and timely response to labor relations issues.
* Completes special projects as assigned by the President and CEO.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s Degree in an Engineering, Technical or Business discipline preferred
* 10+ years of progressively more responsible positions in a manufacturing setting including experience in production, customer support, leadership, and supervisory functions
* 3-5+ years of experience within a plant leadership capacity
* Prior experience within a metal casting/foundry; gray/ductile iron preferred

new_roles.description:
**Hyve Company Overview**
Hyve Solutions transforms complex engineering challenges into production reality for technology innovators building AI, cloud, and connected infrastructure. As a US-based manufacturing partner, the company rapidly delivers fast, agile execution through dep technical partnerships and co-innovation, and supply chain clarity. Hyve’s integrated ODM, CM, and SI capabilities eliminate vendor complexity while accelerating time-to-market with single-partner accountability from design through scale. The company co-innovates with deep engineering expertise, treating customer success as its own while building tomorrow's digital infrastructure.
 
 
**Director, Manufacturing**
**Location: Las Vegas, Nevada Reports directly to the Vice President of Manufacturing**
**Responsibilities**

* Strategy: Develop and execute a manufacturing strategy aligned with Hyve's mission and values. Continuously refine and optimize processes for maximum efficiency at the primary location and across other manufacturing sites.
* Customer engagement: Serve as a direct interface with customer business, technical and operations teams.
* Planning and delivery: Build production plans, schedules and budgets that meet demand while maintaining world-class lean manufacturing and quality standards. Ensure on time, cost-effective delivery.
* Quality: Implement and maintain rigorous quality controls throughout the manufacturing process. Align to quality standards and monitor adherence to guarantee product excellence.
* Supply chain: Partner closely with customer and factory planning teams and 3PL teams to ensure reliable continuity of supply that supports production needs.
* Cost management: Control manufacturing costs by finding savings opportunities and managing headcount and budgets effectively.
* Compliance and safety: Stay current on industry regulations, safety standards and environmental requirements. Ensure full compliance with manufacturing operations.
* Continuous improvement: Drive initiatives that improve efficiency, quality and sustainability, apply lean principles and new technologies where they fit.
* Risk management: Identify and mitigate manufacturing risks to keep the operation resilient and adaptable.
* People leadership: Lead, develop and retain a multi-level manufacturing organization, building a strong bench of leaders.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, Manufacturing or a related field.
* 15+ years of experience in manufacturing, sustaining, or product, process or design engineering. Experience with data infrastructure products, from peripherals through L10 or higher, is preferred.
* Strong knowledge of NPI and manufacturing processes, quality management, and rapid factory transitions and production ramps.
* 10+ years of interaction with customers and internal executives at peer and senior levels.
* Proven record and formal training in team management, leadership and talent development.
* Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
* Strong, data-driven problem-solving skills, including DOE, DFMEA and DFx.
* Familiarity with industry-standard manufacturing tools, shop floor control systems (MES) and operational metrics.
* A passion for environmental sustainability and commitment to Hyve's

What’s in it for you
 
 
Benefit Insurance
 
 

* Flexible Spending Account (FSA)
* Health Savings Account (HSA)
* Mental Health Care
* 401K with match
* Paid Holidays, Vacation & Sick Days
* Tuition Reimbursement
* Perks at Work

new_roles.title: Director of Operations - Industrial - Durham, North Carolina
new_roles.description:
As a Director Of Operations, you will guide Engineering & Manufacturing operations for an Industrial Manufacturing company. You will set operational direction and coordinate priorities that help the business deliver its manufacturing goals. You will be both a strategic and operational leader who is hands-on with the team and communicates strongly with executives.

**Client Details**

My client is a well-established manufacturer serving highly regulated industries where quality, precision, and operational excellence are critical. The organization has built a strong reputation for engineering innovation and customer service and is investing in continued growth, operational improvements, and long-term scalability.

This is a highly visible leadership opportunity for an experienced manufacturing executive to work closely with senior leadership and play a key role in driving business performance. The company offers a collaborative environment where leaders are empowered to make decisions, improve processes, develop teams, and influence company-wide strategy.

**Description**

Reporting directly into the President, you will be responsible for the following:

* Lead all day-to-day plant operations, ensuring safety, quality, delivery, and productivity targets are achieved.
* Promote and strengthen a proactive safety culture across the facility.
* Develop and execute operational strategies that support revenue growth, profitability, and overall business objectives.
* Manage manufacturing, production, inventory, and operational resources to maximize efficiency and customer satisfaction.
* Establish, communicate, and monitor KPIs to drive accountability and continuous improvement.
* Partner with Environmental Health & Safety and Human Resources teams to maintain compliance and support organizational objectives.
* Drive Lean Manufacturing and 5S initiatives throughout the facility.
* Oversee inventory management and collaborate with finance teams on operational performance initiatives.
* Maintain compliance with quality and industry standards including ISO and AS9100 requirements.
* Interface with customers and represent operational capabilities during key business interactions.
* Lead, mentor, and develop management teams while fostering a culture of integrity, accountability, and collaboration.
* Support major business initiatives, including future facility expansion and relocation efforts.

**Profile**

A successful Director Of Operations should have:

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering required; MBA or advanced degree preferred.
* 15+ years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience with direct plant management responsibility.
* Strong background within precision manufacturing, machining, CNC fabrication, or machine shop environments.
* Experience leading operations within aerospace, defense, or other highly regulated manufacturing industries.
* Demonstrated success implementing Lean Manufacturing principles and continuous improvement initiatives; Lean Six Sigma BlackBelt preferred.
* Proven track record of driving operational excellence, productivity improvements, and financial performance.
* Experience leading strategic projects, organizational change, and complex operational initiatives.
* Strong leadership skills with the ability to motivate, mentor, and develop high-performing teams.
* Excellent communication and executive presentation skills.
* Proficiency with ERP/MRP systems and manufacturing performance management tools.
* Experience supporting facility expansion, consolidation, or relocation projects is highly desirable.

**Job Offer**

* Competitive compensation.
* Comprehensive benefits plan.
* 401K with company match.
* Executive leadership position with direct exposure to senior leadership and company strategy.
* Significant influence over plant operations, business performance, and future growth initiatives.
* Opportunity to lead continuous improvement and operational transformation efforts.
* High-impact role overseeing a complex manufacturing environment serving demanding end markets.
* Strong platform for career advancement within a growing and innovative manufacturing organization.
* Collaborative culture focused on safety, operational excellence, integrity, and leadership development.
* Ability to make meaningful contributions to company growth, profitability, and long-term success.

*MPI does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, marital status, or based on an individual's status in any group or class protected by applicable federal, state or local law. MPI encourages applications from minorities, women, the disabled, protected veterans and all other qualified applicants.*

new_roles.title: Director of Integrated Fab Manufacturing
new_roles.description:
**Bold Thinking. World Changing.**
At SkyWater, our ingenuity helps improve lives around the world by manufacturing U.S. made semiconductors that are essential ingredients of modern life. Automotive safety enhancements, life-saving medical devices, consumer electronics and American security require semiconductors. Working in our Minnesota headquarters, Florida, or Texas location — employees join together to improve the world.
 
 
**Explore what’s possible.**
Joining our U.S. - based team means contributing to and learning about the commercialization of some of the most exciting technologies the world has ever seen. We are turning “science fiction” into everyday reality through technologies such as superconducting, 3D integrated circuits or computer chips, carbon nanotubes, photonic logic devices, micro electro-mechanical systems and other emerging device topologies. We manufacture products for aerospace and defense, medical, automotive, consumer and industrial markets, to name a few. Our customers include emerging leaders who rely on our intellectual property security and quality manufacturing services.
 
 
**Step into the future.**
SkyWater’s values of Integrity, Excellence, Collaboration, Empowerment and Growth Mindset guide us to cultivate an empowered, learning environment. We also invest in developing highly skilled, dedicated employees — and employees who are entering the workforce for the first time, from the military, and a variety of educational backgrounds.
 
 
**Are you bold thinking?**
Find your place on our team and help us change the world!
 
 
**Primary Objective**
Join an innovative semiconductor manufacturing organization at the forefront of advanced technology and manufacturing excellence. The Director of Integrated Fab Manufacturing owns the operational, financial, and strategic leadership of the Bloomington fabrication facility, including the Advanced Technology Services (ATS) Process Engineering Technician team. This role ensures the factory achieves world-class safety, quality, output, cycle time, and cost performance while directing a 24/7 organization and partnering across engineering, planning, and quality teams to meet all customer and business commitments.
 
 
In this role, you will be responsible for the end-to-end operational execution, strategic planning, budgetary ownership, and leadership to ensure safe, reliable, and efficient semiconductor manufacturing. You will be responsible for driving absolute excellence across safety, quality, output, cost optimization, and ensuring smooth production flow to consistently meet internal and external customer quality and on-time delivery (OTD) commitments, and fab velocity metrics / key performance indicators (KPIs).
 
 
The successful candidate will own the organizational design and talent strategy for their organization, serving as a role model and lead a highly matrixed organization consisting of the Manufacturing team, Process Engineering Technicians group, and Flow Engineers. This role is expected to partner closely with Program Managers, Technical Leads, Wafer Planning, Manufacturing, Equipment Engineering, Quality, and Technology Development teams to improve operational performance, resolve manufacturing constraints, and deliver business objectives. This leader will play a critical role in transforming factory capabilities to meet strict customer commitments and flexible demand by influencing long-range capacity and setting standards for the MN fab operations organization.
 
 
**Major Areas Of Accountability**

* Operations Leadership: Lead the daily and long-term operational execution in the fab, as well as the ATS technician and flow engineer teams to meet all production starts, output targets, yield expectations, cycle time goals, and quality standards, including setting clear priorities for the organization. Direct, develop, and coach the 24/7 operations teams—including Production, ATS Process Engineering Technicians, and Flow Engineers—to ensure capability, accountability, and organizational readiness.
* Team Leadership: Lead, develop, and empower the Production team, Process Engineering Technicians and Flow Engineers to provide effective manufacturing support, maintain production continuity, and resolve process and workflow issues
* Budgetary Responsibility: Own the fab operating budget, including labor, materials, maintenance, and operational spending; drive cost-reduction initiatives and evaluate capital investments using ROI-based decision-making.
* Wafer Planning and Customer Delivery: Partner with Wafer Planning and Program Management to align schedules, capacity, and customer priorities; identify delivery risks and oversee recovery plans to maintain on time delivery (OTD) performance.
* Manufacturing Performance: Partner with Industrial Engineers, and drive continuous improvement in throughput, cycle time, WIP management, yield, quality, equipment availability, and manufacturing cost using data-driven decision-making and structured problem-solving.
* Cross-Functional Collaboration: Coordinate with Manufacturing, Process Engineering, Equipment Engineering, Quality, and Technology Development to resolve production constraints, improve equipment readiness, and maintain stable manufacturing operations.
* Operational Excellence: Establish and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs), including customer OTD, cycle time, throughput, equipment availability, and quality. Promote standardization, disciplined execution, effective escalation, and continuous improvement.
* Talent Development: Build a high-performing organization through coaching, accountability, collaboration, and development of technical and operational talent. Responsible for the organizational design and talent strategy of these teams, with a focus on cultivating and retaining key talent, developing future leaders and preparing current leaders for the next level role.

**Required Qualifications**- Education: Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, Physics, or related technical discipline.
- Experience: Minimum 12 years in semiconductor manufacturing or operations; minimum 5+ years leading fab operations in a senior manager or director capacity within a 24/7 manufacturing environment.
- Skills:

* Demonstrated ability to improve manufacturing performance (throughput, cycle time, yield, cost, and customer delivery).
* Expertise in wafer planning, WIP management, or production scheduling.
* Strong capability in statistical process control (SPC), structured problem-solving, and data-driven decision-making.
* Demonstrated leadership with large technical teams, with an ability to communicate and collaborate cross-functionally, delivering results in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
* Proven track record of managing a 24/7 manufacturing organization and guiding cross-functional teams through technical tool or yield crises.
* Citizenship: US Citizen required.

**Physical Requirements**

* Ability to enter the cleanroom in full PPE to provide technical and operational support.
* Ability to navigate multi-level fab environments, including prolonged walking and standing when needed.

*The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job.*
**Preferred Qualifications**

* Education: Master’s or PhD in a relevant technical discipline.
* Experience: Deep knowledge of advanced Complimentary Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor (CMOS) nodes, fab toolsets (Lithography, Etch, Diffusion, Thin Films, Chemical Mechanical Polish, Metrology, Metals), and factory automation systems.
* Skills: Experience driving major manufacturing transformations, automation or digitization initiatives, or large-scale capacity improvements.

**The annual salary range for this role is $159440 - $239,160. Pay offered is based on many factors, including, but not limited to, the job-related experience, skills, education, and credentials of each candidate.**
SkyWater offers an exciting environment where the brightest semiconductor minds come together to achieve exceptional results. We offer competitive salary and an opportunity to participate in incentive plans as well as other employee financial benefits, including 401k match, and life insurance.
 
 
Additionally, SkyWater offers a comprehensive benefits package which promotes a healthy life. This includes benefit eligibility day one, medical, dental, mental health benefits, vision, legal planning, short- and long-term disability, paid time off, paid holidays, an on-site fitness facility, and an on-site self-serve market.
 
 
SkyWater complies with federal and state disability laws and makes reasonable accommodations for applicants and employees with disabilities unless doing so would cause an undue hardship. Alternative methods of applying for employment are available to individuals unable to submit an application through this site because of a disability. To request reasonable accommodations, to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and/or to receive other benefits and privileges of employment, please contact Human Resources at 952-851-5200 or Recruiting@SkyWatertechnology.com.
 
 
**EOE, including disability/vets**
We will never ask applicants to pay fees, purchase equipment or gift cards, or provide financial information before a formal offer of employment has been accepted. If you receive a suspicious communication claiming to represent our company, please verify its authenticity by contacting our recruitment team at recruiting@skywatertechnology.com before responding.

new_roles.title: Director of Operations
new_roles.description:
**Position Summary**
The Director of Operations is responsible for leading Hughes-Treitler operations to achieve business objectives related to safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, and customer satisfaction. This hands-on leadership role provides strategic and day-to-day direction for manufacturing, materials, and operational excellence while ensuring the organization has the talent, capacity, processes, and resources required to support current demand and business growth. The Director establishes operating plans, drives accountability, builds organizational capability, and leads continuous improvement initiatives that improve performance, expand capacity, control costs, and strengthen customer responsiveness.
 
 
**Supervisory Responsibilties**

* The position has direct reports but must be able to work in partnership with Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain and Production in support of the departmental objectives.

**Duties And Responsibilities**

* Lead and develop Operations teams to effectively support day-to-day execution, strategic business objectives, customer requirements, and growth plans.
* Establish operating strategies, objectives, budgets, capital requirements, material plans, labor requirements, and organizational priorities aligned with customer and business needs.
* Ensure the organization is structured and staffed with the talent, resources, and capabilities needed to meet customer quality, technical, delivery, and turnaround-time expectations.
* Partner with business leadership to achieve key performance indicators, including safety, quality, on-time delivery, throughput, backlog reduction, customer lead time, productivity, labor utilization, cost, and profitability.
* Lead the development and execution of the site Lean and Operational Excellence roadmap, using Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, 5S, TPM, SIOP and daily management practices to improve flow, yield, cycle time, productivity, and cost performance.
* Establish and monitor operating standards, performance metrics, and management routines that drive accountability, timely problem-solving, and sustained results.
* Drive capacity planning and expansion initiatives, including capital equipment, automation, facility, tooling, staffing, and process investments required to support business growth.
* Manage operating expenses and capital investments in accordance with approved budgets; identify and execute cost-reduction and productivity opportunities.
* Ensure effective planning and control of materials, inventory, suppliers, production schedules, and labor resources to support quality, cost, and delivery commitments.
* Collaborate with Quality, Engineering, Sales, Finance, and other cross-functional partners to resolve operational issues, support new product introductions, strengthen manufacturability, and meet customer requirements.
* Provide leadership for robust root cause analysis, corrective actions, and continuous improvement activities related to safety, quality, delivery, cost, and customer performance.
* Participate in the development and execution of the business strategy and translate strategic priorities into actionable operating plans and measurable objectives.
* Support commercial and customer-facing activities, including operational reviews, pricing and capacity analyses, customer visits, and performance presentations.
* Recruit, develop, coach, and retain operations talent through performance management, career development, succession planning, cross-training, and ongoing capability building.
* Foster a culture of accountability, employee engagement, collaboration, innovation, safety, and continuous improvement across the organization.
* Author annual performance reviews and develop continuing education and advancement paths for entire department.
* Demonstrate the ability and willingness to use AI tools appropriately to improve productivity, decision-making, work quality, and cost performance, including identifying suitable use cases and critically evaluating AI-generated outputs.

**Required Skills And Abilities**

* Strong leadership, project management, analytical, problem-solving, and cross-functional collaboration skills.
* Demonstrated success leading manufacturing operations and continuous improvement initiatives in a complex manufacturing environment.
* Proficiency with Lean, Six Sigma, 5S, Kaizen, TPM, and other continuous improvement methodologies.
* Ability to establish performance metrics, analyze operating data, prioritize competing demands, and drive accountability for results.
* Proven ability to lead change, manage multiple complex initiatives, and meet critical deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
* Exceptional interpersonal, written, verbal, and presentation skills, with the ability to build effective work relationships.
* Strong customer orientation and demonstrated ability to balance customer requirements with operational, financial, and organizational priorities.
* Ability to work effectively under pressure, exercise sound judgment, and maintain a hands-on leadership presence across the operation.
* Proficiency with enterprise resource planning and manufacturing systems; experience with SIOP or related planning processes preferred.
* Demonstrated history of successful change management and implementation of operational excellence improvements.
* Strong interpersonal, leadership and organizational skills and the ability to communicate with all levels of the organization from the production floor to the executive office.
* Willingness to work a flexible schedule and travel as needed to support business requirements.

**Education And Experience**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Supply Chain, Business, or another related technical discipline required; MBA or other relevant advanced degree preferred.
* Minimum of 10 years of progressive manufacturing operations leadership experience in a low-volume/high-mix, build-to-order, or engineered-products environment; experience in aerospace, defense, metal-forming, precision machining, brazing, welding, or another highly regulated industry preferred.
* Demonstrated experience leading salaried and hourly employees.
* Demonstrated experience leading Lean Manufacturing, Operational Excellence, and continuous improvement programs with measurable results.
* Demonstrated experience driving operational planning, capital and capacity expansion, production and materials management, cost optimization, organizational improvements, and customer-facing operational reviews.

**Other**

* Due to the nature of Hughes-Treitler's programs and products, applicants must have the legal right to work in the US and additionally must be legally authorized to access export-controlled information and source code.

**Compensation**
Employee Type: Salaried
 
 
Currency: USD
 
 
Salary Minimum: 200,000
 
 
Salary Maximum: 225,000
 
 
Incentive: No
 
 
Disclaimer: Where a specific pay range is noted, it is a good faith estimate at the time of this posting. The actual salary offered will be based on experience, skills, qualifications, market / business considerations, and geographic location.

**Job Description**
**Director Operations for Drug Product**
Do you aspire to secure a critical role in the production of biologics-based medicines? Are you excited to lead dynamic teams in a state-of-the-art facility that brings transformative biotech treatments to patients globally? We invite you to become a part of our journey as the Director Operations for Drug Product. This role offers you the chance to contribute to the site's development and wield technical leadership to ensure successful GMP manufacturing.
 
 
**Principle Roles & Responsibilities / Accountabilities**

* The Director, Operations – Drug Product plays a critical part in strategic project realization of the Wilmington Biotech facility, a new hi-potent facility in our company's Biologic manufacturing network, ensuring that site’s mission and objectives are effectively achieved, consistent with our company's requirements to ensure compliance, safety and reliable supply to our customers.
* As a key member of the Site Leadership Team, you'll have the opportunity to shape site and organizational strategies, overseeing drug product manufacturing for commercial and new product introductions.
* Be part of facility start-up to manufacture high-potent products, eg antibody drug conjugates (ADCs)
* You will work collaboratively with cross-functional teams to streamline technology transfers and commercial approvals, meanwhile nurturing and empowering your operations team.
* You'll get to foster a culture of continuous learning and improvement, leading or supporting various site functional and cross-functional structures for departmental alignment.
* Tackling resource constraints and needs, you will champion operational and technical excellence for efficient production and implement Lean principles for process optimization.
* Upholding our Manufacturing Division Quality Management System (QMS) requirements, you will manage relevant quality topics, and ensure permanent inspection readiness.
* You will oversee financial forecasts and workload for departmental cost improvements, aligning with capital and expense targets while contributing to sustainability and cost reduction initiatives.
* You will have the chance to leverage digital tools for operational efficiency and informed decision-making, keeping pace with emerging digital technologies relevant to manufacturing processes.
* You will be accountable for achieving onsite Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), monitoring and striving to improve performance metrics related to hiring, uptime, training, change controls, investigations, CAPAs, yield, volume, production cadence, operational availability, and more.

**Qualification And Experience**
**Required Experience and Skills:**

* A degree or equivalent in Engineering, Science, Technical, or other relevant fields: Bachelor’s degree + 12 years industry experience Or Masters + 10 years Or PhD + 8 years
* 6 or more years demonstrated leadership ability and experience managing, coaching, and mentoring high-performing cross function teams.
* Demonstrated experience in a biotech/vaccines/pharma manufacturing site, project, or other relevant roles, specifically drug product sterile manufacturing.
* Demonstrated experience in manufacturing clinical and commercial products.
* Understanding of cGMP requirements for commercial high-potent ADC manufacturing of drug product

**Preferred Experience And Skills**

* Sterile manufacturing leadership & operations, with preferred multi-product experience.
* A leader who inspires, coaches, and fosters a high-performance organizational culture.
* A continuous learner who cultivates a culture of ongoing development within your team.
* An innovative thinker with excellent decision-making and problem-solving skills.
* Experienced in leading highly effective cross-functional teams with a passion for shaping the future of our organization.
* Capable of influencing and building relationships across organizational layers, as well as externally with partners.

new_roles.description:
**it’s what’s inside that counts**
**\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_**
There’s more to CMC than our products and the buildings, structures, and roads they go into. At CMC, it’s the people inside our recycling centers, fabrication plants, manufacturing facilities, steel mills and offices that make us who we are as a company. Our success comes from finding, retaining, and supporting the highest quality talent by offering:
 
 

* Day 1 Benefits Coverage with low cost Medical, Vision, Dental
* Day 1 Paid-time Off and Vacation
* 4.5% Company Match 401(k) plan
* $500 Annual Company-paid Lifestyle Benefit
* Competitive Compensation and Bonuses
* Company-paid Life and Disability Insurance
* Employee Stock Purchase Plan
* Training and Advancement Opportunities

**Why This Job**
CMC provides an excellent opportunity to learn the steel, construction reinforcement and ground stabilization industries and to grow in your career. Whether you will spend your day brainstorming in an office cubicle, operating a crane, running manufacturing equipment or troubleshooting technical obstacles, at CMC, you’ll get the training and support from your team that you need to excel in your role and reach your full potential.
 
 
**What You'll Do**

* Lead in a professional manner toward achieving company performance goals with emphasis on safety, quality and all company standards
* Direct all activities of the Area including accounting, shipping, receiving, operations, safety and environmental
* Champion and ensure adherence to CMC’s Guiding Principles, Code of Conduct, Culture, and policies and procedures
* Must be able to establish operational goals, both financial and non-financial, with clear work plans, and hold management staff accountable
* Responsible for the planning of budgets, company assets, labor forecasts and capital expenditures for short-term and long-range production
* Collaborate with different departments to ensure successful accomplishments of company goals
* Develop and lead a Safety Culture that is consistent with CMC standards
* Control inventory dollars and tons by meeting inventory turn standards set forth by the company
* Provides guidance and direction to staff including hiring, disciplinary action, staff development, goal formulation and performance review
* Ensures compliance with employment laws and regulations, minimizing the company's exposure to adverse outcomes of complaints, litigation, audits and inspections

**What You'll Need**

* Must be able to maintain and be familiar with safety and environmental concerns
* Past successful experience in operations, marketing, sales in a metal recycling facility or other related industry a strong plus
* Must be able to control budgeted labor and overtime costs; as well as, maintain fiscal responsibility for all departments' budgets
* Understands and executes CMC accounting policies, RONA, Working Capital, Operating Profit, and Business strategies.
* Extensive knowledge of all areas of operations
* Preferred familiarity with material handling equipment and how to properly maintain (maintenance programs) and repair equipment
* Must collaborate and develop strong relationships with people to ensure successful accomplishments of plant and regional goals
* Ability to make sure all employees are trained and well prepared to carry out their daily tasks to ensure everyone's safety
* Able to clearly communicate expectations, issues and feedback
* Must be able to problem solve in all areas of plant
* Proficiency with computer operating systems, to include Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) required
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills; ability to communicate up, down, and across the business

**Your Education**

* High School Diploma or GED required
* Bachelor's Degree strongly preferred

We are CMC, a Fortune 500® company at the leading edge of our industry. Our construction reinforcement and steel products have supported construction projects and structures around the world. The secret to our success? We’ve built our legacy by assembling a team of innovators and doers to tackle some of the most challenging construction reinforcement problems facing our world for more than 100 years — and we’re just getting started.
 
 
If you’re ready to join a team working to make our industry more sustainable, support the bridges, roadways, buildings and infrastructure that connects our communities, and do meaningful work, you’re ready to join CMC. Apply today and start moving your career — and our world — forward. Let's build a better world!
 
 
*CMC is committed to providing equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, age, physical or mental disability, national origin, citizenship, military or veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity and/or expression, genetic information, or other status protected by federal, state or local law.*

new_roles.title: Plant Manager
new_roles.description:
**Job Description**
**Summary:**
The Plant Manager is responsible for the day-to-day operations of the entire manufacturing facility including safety, quality, efficiencies and meeting customer expectations. This includes driving strategic plans that ensure that production goals are met in the most cost-effective manner delivering expected financial results.
 
 
**Responsibilities**

* Ensures that the facility provides the highest quality products produced in the most efficient manner within budgeted costs. Implements systems to effectively manage production schedules properly supporting the business.
* Leads the effort and drives Lean Manufacturing tools and techniques fostering continuous improvement within the facility.
* Acts in a proactive fashion regarding problem resolution.
* Manages profit and loss for the facility and drives Plant performance and reviews KPIs regularly (Daily, weekly and monthly).
* Leads the overall strategic planning efforts for the location which include cost reduction initiatives, capital planning and resources as well as in other areas.
* Manages the overall safety, quality, scheduling, production, shipping, maintenance and other administrative functions for the facility.
* Leads the effort in maintaining a safe, clean and efficient operation working within all company guidelines and local/state/federal regulations.
* Strives to improve the plant’s safety accident record year over year in creating a positive safety culture for all employees. Conducts safety walks of the facility on a weekly basis.
* Conducts talent reviews. Trains, develops and motivates staff in an effort to optimize the workforce. Delivers performance reviews and any feedback to the team as needed.
* Conducts weekly staff meetings which focus on key operative measurements.
* Schedules and conducts plant communication meetings for all employees.
* Interfaces with customers and suppliers. Visits both as necessary.
* Works as necessary to establish positive community relationships.
* Performs other duties as assigned.

**Requirements**

* Minimum of a high school diploma. Bachelor's or Master’s Degree in Engineering, Operations or Business Management preferred
* Minimum of 7-10 years of experience in operations, maintenance, engineering and/or process Improvement roles including managing teams of people
* Previous experience working in a Lean environment.
* Six Sigma Green or Black Belt Certification a plus
* Proven experience and record of successes in a high-speed manufacturing environment. Experience with plastic injection molding environment, and metal processing/metal forming strong preferred
* Experience in a commercial role with direct customer contact
* Minimum of 5 years of experience with process development and business process design.
* Experience managing to the ISO or equivalent quality standards
* Experience implementing and/or managing to an Operating System (example: the Toyota Production Systems)
* Bilingual English/Spanish a plus, but not required

**About Us**
Do you want to work with people who are dedicated to innovation and making the world a better place? Do you want to build a career with a company that provides opportunities for growth and development?
 
 
Mauser Packaging Solutions is that company.
 
 
Our mission is to help our customers achieve better sustainability with their packaging. And we do that by giving our people the opportunity to do important work, solve interesting problems and be part of a diverse, forward-looking team.
 
 
At Mauser Packaging Solutions, you can be proud to work for a company that’s always striving to innovate and serve customers better—and help them be better stewards of the environment.
 
 
Whether you’re a seasoned professional—or just beginning your career—there’s a place where you can help make a difference at Mauser Packaging Solutions. Join us!
 
 
Mauser Packaging Solutions is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, protected veteran status, or disability status.

new_roles.description:
Job ID: 530934
 
 
Ash Grove is a CRH company with a legacy dating back to 1882. We combine technical expertise, safety and customer-focused solutions to deliver reliable performance for our customers. We manufacture and supply high-performance, advanced cementitious materials for the most demanding construction and infrastructure needs. With more than 2,000 people across 60 locations in the United States and Canada, we support a wide range of applications, from major infrastructure projects to the development and refurbishment of residential and non-residential buildings that support everyday life, from highways and bridges to schools and commercial buildings.
 
 
To learn more about us go to www.ashgrove.com
 
 
**Job Summary**
The Plant Manager plans, coordinates, and supervises the production operations, hazardous waste fuel program, maintenance activities, quality and safety programs, and other related functions involved in plant operations. This position incorporates directives provided by corporate management into policies and procedures to maintain standards and schedules. The position exercises direct or indirect supervision over a large number of employees.
 
 
**Job Location**

* This role will work out of our plant in Midlothian, TX.

**Job Responsibilities**

* Promote and follow all plant safety guidelines.
* Conducts meetings with plant staff personnel to communicate, coordinate and discuss plant operations.
* Monitors, inspects, and reviews all plant activities.
* Ensures production schedule corresponds with sales forecasts.
* Assists in investigating customer and quality problems and concerns.
* Meets with government agencies and community groups concerning plant activities to ensure compliance with environmental regulations, policies, and standards.
* Prepares regular reports regarding plant production operations.
* Attends Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA) training for waste-derived fuel activities.
* Promotes effective job performance through motivation, goals, and providing feedback.
* Promotes the safety program, compliance with safety standards, and participates in safety meetings.
* Establishes plant standards, short-term goals, and long-term strategic plans for production, maintenance, and improvements.
* Discusses new products, equipment, and ideas with staff and vendors.
* Analyzes plant costs and explore methods to improve productivity cost-effectively.
* Uses technology to develop a continuous improvement plan for the plant.
* Troubleshoots various problems and performance barriers.

**Job Requirements**

* Ability to read, write, and understand warning labels, instructions, signs, etc.
* Minimum 4 Year - Bachelors Degree in engineering, chemistry, natural sciences, business administration, or closely related field.
* Professional Engineer (PE) preferred
* Ability to develop and deliver effective presentations
* Ability to make decisions and solve problems with high attention to detail and accuracy
* Ability to make sound independent judgments regularly
* Ability to effectively coach and deliver constructive feedback
* Ability to inspire and develop staff
* Proficient in effective negotiation skills in business and construction contracts
* Proficient in Microsoft Office365
* Ability to effectively use computers for general word processing, spreadsheets, presentations, e-mail, internet, and customized company programs.
* Ability to communicate the company's vision into actionable goals and contributions for plant personnel.
* Ability to network with industry professionals, consultants, vendors, suppliers, regulators, and the community.
* Knowledge of safety and environmental health regulations.
* Knowledge of cement chemistry, physical testing, and concrete performance.
* Knowledge of various systems for cement manufacturing (crushing, grinding, pyro processing, chemistry).
* Ability to work from general policies and procedures.
* Ability to refer to supervisor when clarification or interpretation of the organizational policy

**What CRH Offers You**

* Highly competitive base pay
* Comprehensive medical, dental and disability benefits programs
* Group retirement savings program
* Health and wellness programs
* An inclusive culture that values opportunity for growth, development, and internal promotion

**About CRH**
CRH has a long and proud heritage. We are a collection of hundreds of family businesses, regional companies and large enterprises that together form the CRH family. CRH operates in a decentralized, diversified structure that allows you to work in a small company environment while having the career opportunities of a large international organization.
 
 
If you’re up for a rewarding challenge, we invite you to take the first step and apply today! Once you click apply now, you will be brought to our official employment application. Please complete your online profile and it will be sent to the hiring manager. Our system allows you to view and track your status 24 hours a day. Thank you for your interest!
 
 
Ash Grove Cement, a CRH Company, is an Affirmative Action and Equal Opportunity Employer.
 
 
EOE/Vet/Disability
 
 
CRH is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, status as a protected veteran or any other characteristic protected under applicable federal, state, or local law.
