new_roles.title: Director, Manufacturing Engineering
new_roles.description:
L3Harris is dedicated to recruiting and developing high-performing talent who are passionate about what they do. Our employees are unified in a shared dedication to our customers’ mission and quest for professional growth. L3Harris provides an inclusive, engaging environment designed to empower employees and promote work-life success. Fundamental to our culture is an unwavering focus on values, dedication to our communities, and commitment to excellence in everything we do.
 
 
L3Harris is the Trusted Disruptor in defense tech. With customers’ mission-critical needs always in mind, our employees deliver end-to-end technology solutions connecting the space, air, land, sea and cyber domains in the interest of national security.
 
 
***Job Title: Director, Manufacturing Engineering***
***Job Code: 47622***
***Job Location: Camden, AR***
***Job Schedule: 4/10: Employees work 10 hour days, 4 days a week***
**Job Description:**
The Manufacturing Engineering Director in Camden, Arkansas will plan, organize and technically direct the manufacturing engineering activities and staff. Enable Operations to execute all programs in a safe and efficient manner, and ensuring the achievement of quality, cost and delivery schedule objectives. This position reports to the Senior Director Operations and Site Management. Our Camden, AR site is at $600M+ revenue and produces a diverse portfolio of highly engineered products for aerospace and defense applications. The individual will be responsible for implementing a disciplined operating system in line with the enterprise while improving the operating effectiveness of the site and leading an organization of over 190 people.
 
 
**Essential Functions:**

* 50% - Direct and lead technical team: Analyze, evaluate and determine appropriate solutions for manufacturing technical problems encountered in the application of manufacturing methods, facilities and processes. Apply engineering procedures, provide technical direction, create and apply work instructions and tooling for the factory floor. Participate in program and site corrective action boards and be a key member in customer escape and non-conformance investigations; develop direct cause, root cause and mistake proof corrective actions, as well as separation criteria when required. Ensure proper deployment of resources to achieve cost effective results in support of site and business unit deliverables. Direct the installation of Electronic Work Instructions (Platform is DELMIA) across the site and all product lines. Strict oversight of the Job Safety Analysis and Process Safety Management programs at the site.
* 15% - Administrative management: Ensure a safe work environment and remain in compliance to federal and local regulations. Develop long range technical and administrative plans, goals and strategies.
* 15% - Customer interface: Establish priorities to meet the needs of the customer and the organization with a dedication to support the manufacturing shop floor. Represent the organization as a prime internal and customer contact on manufacturing technical operations.
* 20% - Strategy and Continuous Improvement: Lead the sites Advanced Product Quality Planning (APQP) program. Drive operational

excellence throughout the organization and create a metrics driven, highly accountable mindset within the organization.
 
 

* Ability to obtain a US secret security clearance.

**Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's Degree with a minimum of 15 years prior relevant experience. Graduate Degree with a minimum of 13 years prior relevant experience. In lieu of a degree, minimum of 19 years of prior relevant experience.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Demonstrated supervisory and leadership skills, including planning, organizing and directing activities; developing talent; and collaborating across business units and functional teams to achieve site objectives.
* Strong understanding of business development, program management, engineering, finance, operations and process control, with the ability to engage effectively with plant-floor teams, customers and executives.
* Experience in aerospace and/or general industrial sectors, including multiple years in a leadership capacity, with program management, engineering leadership and experience with inert, energetic and propellant materials.
* High-energy, results-driven leader with a disciplined work ethic, a bias for action and a continuous improvement mindset. Able to drive commitments to closure, elevate performance and lead organizational change in a demanding environment with lean staffing.
* Ability to satisfy federal government requirements for access to government information.

L3Harris Technologies is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. L3Harris is committed to treating all employees and applicants for employment with respect and dignity and maintaining a workplace that is free from unlawful discrimination. All applicants will be considered for employment without regard to race, color, religion, age, national origin, ancestry, ethnicity, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding or other related medical conditions), gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, veteran status, disability, genetic information, citizenship status, characteristic or membership in any other group protected by federal, state or local laws. L3Harris maintains a drug-free workplace and performs pre-employment substance abuse testing and background checks, where permitted by law.
 
 
Please be aware many of our positions require the ability to obtain a security clearance. Security clearances may only be granted to U.S. citizens. In addition, applicants who accept a conditional offer of employment may be subject to government security investigation(s) and must meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information.
 
 
By submitting your resume for this position, you understand and agree that L3Harris Technologies may share your resume, as well as any other related personal information or documentation you provide, with its subsidiaries and affiliated companies for the purpose of considering you for other available positions.
 
 
L3Harris Technologies is an E-Verify Employer. Please click here for the E-Verify Poster in English or Spanish. For information regarding your Right To Work, please click here for English or Spanish.

new_roles.title: Senior Manager of Operations
new_roles.description:
**Senior Manager of Operations - Austin, TX**

**DESCRIPTION:**

We’re seeking a hands-on Sr. Operations Manager with experience scaling silicon-based products in a semiconductor company. This player-coach role owns the operational path from foundry and wafer production through test, backend processing, and manufacturing. You’ll qualify and manage manufacturing vendors, establish and strengthen quality-control measures, and drive consistent quality, yield, cost, and delivery as production grows.

Experience with RFID inlay production is especially relevant.

**What you’ll do:**

* Own foundry relationships from negotiation through production execution, and scale wafer level production.
* Manage wafer-test facility relationships; evaluate and qualify test partners, and select test equipment to optimize cost, quality, and throughput.
* Lead test development, wafer backend operations, yield improvement, reliability, and failure analysis.
* Qualify and manage manufacturing vendors, including overseeing end-to-end inlay production and its ramp to volume.
* Establish and improve quality-control measures, operating procedures, and RMA processes.
* Monitor supplier quality, conduct supply-chain audits, and resolve manufacturing, quality, and delivery issues.
* Establish and improve ERP/MRP processes, WIP tracking, inventory planning, and production controls.
* Develop cost models, negotiate contracts, and drive improvements in cost, quality, and delivery.
* Manage one direct report and coordinate work across four internal engineers and executive stakeholders, including the CEO.

**What you’ll bring:**

* BSEE or equivalent practical experience.
* 7–10 years of operations, manufacturing, or related experience in a semiconductor company.
* Experience with RFID inlay manufacturing is a plus.
* Hands-on experience with silicon-based products and semiconductor manufacturing operations.
* Experience scaling products from wafer fabrication and test through backend processing and volume production.
* Experience working with foundries, wafer-test facilities, and manufacturing vendors.
* Familiarity with yield optimization, reliability, quality assurance, supplier audits, failure analysis, ERP/MRP systems, WIP tracking, and inventory planning.
* Strong communication, coordination, and negotiation skills, with a practical, roll-up-your sleeves approach.

new_roles.title: Senior Manager, Site Reliability Engineering & Operations
new_roles.description:
We’re building a world of health around every individual — shaping a more connected, convenient and compassionate health experience. At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. Join us and be part of something bigger – helping to simplify health care one person, one family and one community at a time.
 
 
**Position Summary**
The
**Senior Manager, Site Reliability Engineering & Operations**
is a highly visible leadership role within the Member & Client Services Engineering (MCSE) organization at CVS Health. This position is responsible for ensuring the reliability, availability, performance, and operational excellence of business-critical platforms that support millions of members, customer service operations, clinical services, and enterprise applications. In this role, you will lead the strategy and execution of Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), production operations, observability, incident management, and operational automation across a complex technology ecosystem. You will partner closely with engineering, infrastructure, architecture, and managed service providers to deliver highly reliable, scalable, and resilient technology solutions that support CVS Health's mission.
 
 
The ideal candidate is a strong technical leader with experience driving reliability engineering practices, operational excellence, and continuous improvement in large-scale enterprise environments. You will play a key role in advancing modern SRE capabilities, including AI-driven operations (AIOps), observability, automation, and proactive service reliability initiatives. As a people leader, you will build and develop high-performing teams, influence strategic technology decisions, and foster a culture of accountability, innovation, and continuous learning. This role requires a passion for solving complex operational challenges, improving customer experiences, and driving measurable business outcomes through technology excellence.
 
 
**Key Responsibilities**

* Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) Leadership
* Execute and advance the enterprise SRE strategy, including Service Level Objectives (SLOs), Service Level Indicators (SLIs), error budgets, and reliability roadmaps.
* Establish reliability standards and best practices across applications, APIs, data platforms, and emerging AI-powered solutions.
* Champion a culture of reliability, operational excellence, and continuous improvement across engineering teams.
* Drive platform resiliency, scalability, performance, and risk mitigation initiatives.

**AI-Driven Operations (AIOps) & Automation**

* Lead the adoption of AIOps capabilities to improve proactive issue detection, predictive analytics, and operational efficiency.
* Implement AI-assisted incident management, automated remediation, self-healing capabilities, and standardized operational runbooks.
* Partner with AI and platform engineering teams to integrate machine learning and generative AI technologies into operational workflows.

**Observability & Monitoring**

* Define and lead the enterprise observability strategy across metrics, logs, traces, and user experience monitoring.
* Drive standardization and adoption of observability platforms such as Datadog, Dynatrace, Splunk, Grafana, Prometheus, and OpenTelemetry.
* Deliver actionable insights, dashboards, and executive reporting related to platform health, availability, performance, and reliability metrics.

**Incident Management & Operational Excellence**

* Lead enterprise incident response, escalation management, and post-incident reviews.
* Reduce Mean Time to Detect (MTTD), Mean Time to Restore (MTTR), and recurring incidents through automation and preventive engineering practices.
* Establish operational readiness standards, on-call processes, and service management best practices.
* Drive root-cause analysis, problem management, and long-term service stability initiatives.

**Leadership & Talent Development**

* Build, mentor, and lead high-performing global SRE and operations teams.
* Develop career growth frameworks, skill development programs, and technical leadership capabilities.
* Foster a culture of collaboration, accountability, innovation, and continuous learning.
* Partner with stakeholders across technology and business organizations to align reliability priorities with business objectives.

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or equivalent work experience required, one additional year of experience is required for each year of college not attained.
* 10+ or more years of production support or service delivery experience.
* Experience working with a managed services vendor.
* ITIL Qualified & Expert knowledge of ITIL disciplines.
* Experience of managing 3rd parties and 3rd party delivered services.
* Service Management or Support in a large-scale and diverse environment of incident management, escalation procedures and related disciplines.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* High degree of self-motivation to work in a fast-paced dynamic environment.
* Strong communication skills are required to facilitate meetings with both technical and business audiences, often across multiple functional departments.
* Demonstrated understanding of various technologies (Java/J2EE, .Net, MQ, Mainframe, Telephony systems etc.)
* Experience with major database management systems, e.g. DB2, Oracle, and SQL Server.
* Experience creatively debugging complex system problems spanning entire hosting stack (application, server, communication channels, networking components, etc), resulting in problem determination and restoration through thorough research and fact finding.
* Be able to exhibit decisiveness and good judgment, even in ambiguous circumstances.
* Experience supporting both proprietary and vendor developed or supported applications.
* Demonstrated successful completion of technical projects.
* Demonstrated proficiency working on all phases of SDLC.
* Able to exhibit decisiveness and good judgment, even in ambiguous circumstances.

**Education**

* Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or equivalent work experience required, one additional year of experience is required for each year of college not attained.
* ITIL certified

**Pay Range**
**The Typical Pay Range For This Role Is**
$106,605.00 - $213,210.00
 
 
This pay range represents the base hourly rate or base annual full-time salary for all positions in the job grade within which this position falls. The actual base salary offer will depend on a variety of factors including experience, education, geography and other relevant factors. This position is eligible for a CVS Health bonus, commission or short-term incentive program in addition to the base pay range listed above. This position also includes an award target in the company’s equity award program.
 
 
Our people fuel our future. Our teams reflect the customers, patients, members and communities we serve and we are committed to fostering a workplace where every colleague feels valued and that they belong.
 
 
**Great Benefits For Great People**
We take pride in offering a comprehensive and competitive mix of pay and benefits that reflects our commitment to our colleagues and their families.
 
 
This full‑time position is eligible for a comprehensive benefits package designed to support the physical, emotional, and financial well‑being of colleagues and their families. The benefits for this position include medical, dental, and vision coverage, paid time off, retirement savings options, wellness programs, and other resources, based on eligibility.
 
 
Additional details about available benefits are provided during the application process and on Benefits Moments.
 
 
We anticipate the application window for this opening will close on: 11/30/2026
 
 
Qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment in accordance with all federal, state and local laws.

new_roles.title: Senior Manager - Biomanufacturing, Manufacturing Technical Operations
new_roles.description:
**About Site**
Catalent’s Madison, Wisconsin site is a state‑of‑the‑art biologics development and manufacturing facility supporting customers from research through early‑ and mid‑stage clinical production. Located at 726 Heartland Trail in Madison, the approximately 102,700‑square‑foot GMP facility specializes in mammalian cell line engineering, drug substance biomanufacturing, and biopharmaceutical development, utilizing flexible single‑use systems to enable rapid scale‑up and customization. The site is home to Catalent’s proprietary GPEx® and GPEx® Lightning technologies, which are used to generate high‑yielding mammalian cell lines for biologic therapies, and supports production scales ranging from 50 to 4,000 liters for clinical manufacturing. Following a $45 million expansion announced in 2025, the Madison site has significantly increased capacity, added new equipment, and created approximately 200 highly skilled biohealth jobs, further strengthening its role within Catalent’s global biologics network and Wisconsin’s growing life sciences ecosystem.
 
 
**Position Summary**
We have an opportunity for a Senior Manager - Biomanufacturing, Manufacturing Technical Operations to join our team. This role leads the Manufacturing Technical Operations organization, including Manufacturing Engineering, Manufacturing Compliance, Deviation Investigation, and Manufacturing Training. The position ensures safe, compliant, and reliable biomanufacturing operations while driving continuous improvement and technical excellence. The successful candidate will help strengthen workforce capability, reduce operational risk, and ensure sustainable preventive solutions across manufacturing operations.
 
 
Shift: Monday - Friday 8:00AM - 5:00PM
 
 
Location: Madison, WI
 
 
100% Onsite
 
 
**The Role**

* Lead, coach, develop, and evaluate leaders and technical professionals supporting Manufacturing Engineering, Compliance, Deviation Investigation, and Training.
* Establish clear goals, role accountabilities, performance expectations, succession plans, and development strategies for the organization.
* Provide organizational ownership for Manufacturing-based engineering support and technical response to process, equipment, materials, automation, documentation, and execution issues.
* Establish and govern a structured Rapid Response Team process that defines the problem, operational impact, containment, technical resources, decision ownership, recovery plan, communications, and escalation pathway.
* Provide leadership and oversight for Manufacturing deviation investigations, including investigation quality, aging, cycle time, right-first-time approval, and recurring-event reduction.
* Ensure investigations are fact-based and clearly distinguish event description, product and process impact, root cause, contributing factors, correction, corrective action, and preventive action.
* Establish Manufacturing Technical Operations as a key owner and contributor to process readiness, including batch production record review, dry runs, equipment readiness, material availability, qualification status, and execution-risk review.
* Ensure new equipment is transitioned into routine use with defined operational ownership, procedures, training, spare parts, maintenance, and troubleshooting strategies.
* Establish an integrated performance-management system using measures such as recurrence, recovery time, repeat failures, downtime, deviation aging, investigation right-first-time performance, corrective and preventive action aging and effectiveness, qualification progress, equipment reliability, open risks, and project delivery.
* Use performance data to establish priorities, allocate resources, escalate risk, and hold leaders accountable for outcomes.

**The Candidate**
**Minimum Requirements**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Biotechnology, Biological Sciences, Biochemistry, or another relevant scientific or technical discipline required.
* Ten (10) or more years of relevant manufacturing, engineering, technical operations, Manufacturing Science and Technology, Quality, or related experience.
* Five (5) or more years of progressive leadership experience, including responsibility for technical professionals, people leaders, or manufacturing-support organizations.
* Demonstrated experience leading complex technical problem solving and operational recovery in a Good Manufacturing Practice manufacturing environment.
* Demonstrated experience with deviation investigations, corrective and preventive actions, change control, root-cause analysis, inspection readiness, and quality risk management.
* Advanced understanding of current Good Manufacturing Practice biopharmaceutical manufacturing, including upstream, downstream, solution-preparation, equipment, and support systems.
* Demonstrable leadership experience at Catalent (including but not limited to participation in Catalent‑sponsored leadership programs such as Next Generation Global Leaders, GOLD, LEAD Now, General Manager Excellence, and GROW) may be considered in place of external experience.

**Preferred Skills & Background**

* Advanced degree preferred.
* Experience in Good Manufacturing Practice biopharmaceutical manufacturing.

**Why You Should Join Catalent**

* Defined career path and annual performance review and feedback process.
* Diverse, inclusive culture.
* Potential for career growth on an expanding team within an organization dedicated to preserving and bettering lives.
* Competitive paid time off plus 8 paid holidays.
* Community engagement and green initiatives.
* Medical, dental, and vision benefits effective day one of employment.
* Tuition reimbursement.

**Catalent offers rewarding opportunities to further your career!**
Join the global drug development and delivery leader and help us bring over 7,000 life-saving and life-enhancing products to patients around the world. Catalent is an exciting and growing international company where employees work directly with pharma, biopharma and consumer health companies of all sizes to advance new medicines from early development to clinical trials and to the market. Catalent produces more than 70 billion doses per year, and each one will be used by someone who is counting on us. Join us in making a difference.
 
 
personal initiative. dynamic pace. meaningful work.
 
 
Visit Catalent Careers to explore career opportunities.
 
 
Catalent is an Equal Opportunity Employer, including disability and veterans.
 
 
If you require reasonable accommodation for any part of the application or hiring process due to a disability, you may submit your request by sending an email, and confirming your request for an accommodation and include the job number, title and location to DisabilityAccommodations@catalent.com. This option is reserved for individuals who require accommodation due to a disability. Information received will be processed by a U.S. Catalent employee and then routed to a local recruiter who will provide assistance to ensure appropriate consideration in the application or hiring process.

Resumes submitted to any Catalent employee by a third party agency and/or search firm without a valid written & signed search agreement, will become the sole property of Catalent. No fee will be paid if a candidate is hired for this position as a result of an unsolicited agency or search firm referral. Thank you.
 
 
Important Security Notice to U.S. Job Seekers:
 
 
Catalent NEVER asks candidates to provide any type of payment, bank details, photocopies of identification, social security number or other highly sensitive personal information during the offer process, and we NEVER do so via email or social media. If you receive any such request, DO NOT respond— it is a fraudulent request. Please forward such requests to spam@catalent.com for us to investigate with local authorities.
 
 
California Job Seekers can find our California Job Applicant Notice HERE.

Applicants for employment in Massachusetts may include in their employment history any verified work performed on a volunteer basis.

It is unlawful in Massachusetts to require or administer a lie detector test as a condition of employment or continued employment. An employer who violates this law may be subject to criminal penalties and civil liability. Consistent with Massachusetts law, Catalent does not require or administer lie detector tests as a condition of employment or continued employment.

new_roles.description:
**Work Schedule**
Standard (Mon-Fri)
 
 
**Environmental Conditions**
Adherence to all Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) Safety Standards
 
 
As part of the Thermo Fisher Scientific team, you’ll discover meaningful work that makes a positive impact on a global scale. Join our colleagues in bringing our Mission to life every single day to enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer. We provide our global teams with the resources needed to achieve individual career goals while helping to take science a step beyond by developing solutions for some of the world’s toughest challenges, like protecting the environment, making sure our food is safe or helping find cures for cancer.
 
 
DESCRIPTION:
 
 
As a Sr. Manager, Manufacturing Engineering at Thermo Fisher Scientific, you will guide and support engineering teams to drive operational excellence and innovation across our manufacturing facilities. You will provide strategic direction and technical leadership for manufacturing processes, automation initiatives, and continuous improvement projects while ensuring compliance with quality and regulatory requirements. Working collaboratively with cross-functional teams, you'll optimize production efficiency, implement new technologies, and deliver solutions that enable our mission of making the world healthier, cleaner and safer.
 
 
REQUIREMENTS:
 
 

* Advanced Degree plus 6 years of experience, or Bachelor's Degree plus 8 years of experience in regulated manufacturing environments (pharmaceutical, medical device, or related industries)
* Preferred Fields of Study: Engineering (Mechanical, Electrical, Manufacturing, Chemical) or related technical field. Strong focus on Automation required.
* Industry certifications in Six Sigma, PMP, or related areas are beneficial
* 5+ years of leadership experience managing technical teams and facilitating organizational change
* Demonstrated success implementing automation, digitalization and continuous improvement initiatives
* Strong understanding of cGMP, ISO standards and regulatory compliance requirements
* Experience with new product introductions, technology transfers and process validation
* Expertise in lean manufacturing principles, Six Sigma methodology and practical process improvements (PPI)
* Demonstrated ability to develop and execute strategic plans aligned with business objectives
* Strong project management skills and experience leading complex, cross-functional initiatives
* Excellent analytical and problem-solving capabilities with data-driven decision making
* Strong communication and interpersonal skills to engage stakeholders at all levels
* Proficiency with manufacturing systems, automation platforms and quality tools
* Ability to manage multiple priorities effectively
* Experience with capital project planning, budgeting and resource allocation
* Relocation: Relocation assistance is not available for this position.
* Work Authorization: Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States without current or future employer-sponsored work authorization.
* Pre-Employment Screening: Employment is contingent upon successful completion of all applicable pre-employment requirements, including a background check and drug screening, in accordance with company policy and applicable law.

**Compensation And Benefits**
The salary range estimated for this position based in New Jersey is $155,100.00–$232,650.00.
 
 
This position may also be eligible to receive a variable annual bonus based on company, team, and/or individual performance results in accordance with company policy. We offer a comprehensive Total Rewards package that our U.S. colleagues and their families can count on, which includes:
 
 

* A choice of national medical and dental plans, and a national vision plan, including health incentive programs
* Employee assistance and family support programs, including commuter benefits and tuition reimbursement
* At least 120 hours paid time off (PTO), 10 paid holidays annually, paid parental leave (3 weeks for bonding and 8 weeks for caregiver leave), accident and life insurance, and short- and long-term disability in accordance with company policy
* Retirement and savings programs, such as our competitive 401(k) U.S. retirement savings plan
* Employees’ Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP) offers eligible colleagues the opportunity to purchase company stock at a discount

For more information on our benefits, please visit: https://jobs.thermofisher.com/global/en/total-rewards

new_roles.title: Senior Manager, Manufacturing Engineering
new_roles.description:
******Relocation assistance is available for this position.******
**Who We Are**
Stored Energy Systems (SENS) is an award-winning manufacturer of premium quality power conversion products located in Longmont, CO. In business for over 50 years, SENS is the market leader with a proven track record of providing highly reliable battery chargers, DC power systems, and related products to industrial markets. For more information on our company please see our web site at www.sens-usa.com .
 
 
**View the SENS Product Catalog**
**Summary**
SENS is seeking a manufacturing engineering leader to help build and scale the organization, processes, and technical capabilities required for our next stage of growth. Supporting the expansion of existing manufacturing operations and establishing new operations at our Broomfield Systems manufacturing factory, this leader will establish the manufacturing engineering strategy, develop a multidisciplinary team, and translate business growth plans into manufacturing capacity and reliable production processes for our fastest-growing products.
 
 
This role leads manufacturing engineering, industrialization, tooling, test systems, automation, and technical production support for our systems products, with a strong emphasis on configure-to-order assembly manufacturing. Working closely with Production, Design Engineering, Quality, Safety, and Supply Chain, the Senior Manager will establish clear priorities, strengthen new product and production transfer readiness, and deliver measurable improvements in productivity, quality, cost, and equipment reliability.
 
 
A successful candidate will combine organizational leadership with practical technical judgment, building a team that can support daily production while executing the improvements and investments needed to scale.
 
 
**Responsibilities**

* Help to build and develop the manufacturing engineering organization. Assess current capabilities, define the team structure and staffing plan, recruit talent, and develop engineers and technical leaders to support SENS’s growth.
* Establish performance measures and execution discipline. Set departmental goals, review project and operational performance, communicate risks and resource needs, and hold the team accountable for measurable improvements in manufacturing readiness, capacity, productivity, and equipment reliability.
* Establish and execute the manufacturing engineering roadmap. Translate business growth, product plans, and production requirements into prioritized initiatives for manufacturing capacity, processes, tooling, test systems, automation, and equipment reliability.
* Lead manufacturing readiness for new products and production transfers. Partner with Design Engineering, Production, Quality, and Planning & Fulfillment to establish readiness criteria and ensure processes, equipment, tooling, test capability, documentation, and training are in place before production release.
* Develop scalable manufacturing processes and standards. Establish consistent methods for process development, validation, work instructions, engineering changes, and production controls across manufacturing locations while accommodating product-specific requirements.
* Expand manufacturing capacity and improve productivity. Lead engineering efforts in capacity analysis, line balancing, factory layout, workflow, cycle-time reduction, and constraint elimination to support production demand and improve labor efficiency.
* Provide reliable technical support to Production. Establish clear support coverage, escalation processes, and problem-solving practices that resolve production issues promptly and prevent recurrence while maintaining progress on strategic projects.
* Guide manufacturing technology development. Lead technical specialists responsible for manufacturing test systems, production software, tooling, and automation. Prioritize investments based on safety, quality, capacity, reliability, and financial return.
* Improve production equipment reliability. Establish equipment ownership, maintenance strategies, critical spare requirements, and preventive and predictive maintenance practices in partnership with Production and technical support teams.
* Manage projects, capital investments, and departmental resources. Develop business cases, budgets, schedules, and resource plans; oversee implementation and production acceptance; and verify that projects deliver their expected operational and financial benefits.
* Partner with Design Engineering on manufacturability. Incorporate manufacturing feedback early in product development and engineering changes to improve assembly, testability, quality, serviceability, and cost.
* Drive safe processes and sustained quality improvement. Partner with EHS and Quality to incorporate risk assessment, error prevention, root cause analysis, and corrective action into manufacturing processes and equipment changes.
* Oversee the development and maintenance of manufacturing processes, work instructions, test procedures, tooling, fixtures, automation systems, and production software solutions.
* Be directly accountable for engineering project delivery, manufacturing readiness, equipment reliability, and validated improvement benefits, while sharing accountability with Production and Quality for labor efficiency and first-pass yield (FPY).

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or a related technical discipline, or an additional 4 years of manufacturing engineering experience.
* Eight or more years of experience in manufacturing engineering, production engineering, industrialization, or a related technical manufacturing role.
* Three or more years of experience directly leading engineering or technical teams, including setting priorities, developing employees, allocating resources, and managing performance.
* Demonstrated success improving manufacturing performance, with measurable results in productivity, capacity, quality, cost, or equipment reliability.
* Experience developing and improving manufacturing processes, tooling, fixtures, work instructions, and production controls, including introducing new or revised products into production.
* Ability to lead engineers and technical specialists across manufacturing processes, test systems, automation, and production support, using sound technical judgment to evaluate solutions and resolve issues.
* Practical application of Lean Manufacturing and structured problem-solving methods, including root cause analysis and corrective action.
* Experience leading cross-functional projects with Production, Design Engineering, Quality, Safety, and Supply Chain, balancing daily production needs with longer-term improvement priorities.
* Experience planning and executing manufacturing improvement or capital equipment projects, including defining scope, schedules, resource requirements, and expected business results.
* Strong communication and organizational skills, with the ability to translate business objectives into clear team priorities and communicate progress, risks, and decisions.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience in manufacturing of configure-to-order (CTO) and engineered-to-order (ETO) electrical systems such as switchgear, switchboard, etc.
* Experience with manufacturing software development, automated test systems, and data acquisition platforms.
* Experience using ERP systems such as SyteLine for BOM management, item masters, engineering changes, and manufacturing planning.
* Lean Six Sigma Green Belt, Black Belt, or equivalent certification.
* Experience managing departmental budgets and capital equipment projects from business case through production acceptance.

**Location:**
Longmont, CO
 
 
**Base Compensation:**
$120,000 - $175,000 is the projected annual base salary range for this role and will be determined on the candidate’s overall qualifications and experience.
 
 
****Bonus:**
This position is eligible for an annual bonus based on individual and company performance.**
**Closing Date:**
December 15th. While we expect to keep the position open through this date, the posting may be extended or closed early based on applicant volume and hiring needs.
 
 
**Onsite Perks**

* Free gym with 24/7 access
* Free Electric Vehicle charging
* Breakfast and Lunch Café
* After hours Grab & Go snacks
* Basketball court
* Walking paths

**Benefits**

* Paid Time Off
* Paid holidays
* Medical insurance
* Dental insurance
* Vision insurance
* Short-term and long-term disability
* Life insurance
* 401(k) plan with immediate vesting
* Employee referral program
* Tuition reimbursement
* Professional development

At SENS, our culture is rooted in a set of core values that reflect who we are and how we work. In a recent 2025 poll, our employees identified the values that best define us: “Innovative”, “Respectful”, “Inviting”, “Flexible”, “Collaborative”, and “Growth Driven”. Our team describes us as a dynamic, forward-thinking company where everyone has the opportunity to thrive.
 
 
We pride ourselves on being an equal opportunity employer, fully dedicated to fostering inclusion and diversity. We welcome all applicants, regardless of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other legally protected characteristic.
 
 
We hope you're interested in making a difference with us. Even if you don't feel that you meet every qualification listed in this job description, we still encourage you to apply.

new_roles.title: Director, NPI Program Management & Manufacturing Launch
new_roles.description:
If you’re looking for a special place to build or grow your career, you’ve found it. Whether you’re an experienced professional, a recent college graduate or somewhere in between, IDEX is a place where you can apply your existing skills and learn new ones in an environment where you can make an impact.
 
 
With interesting opportunities in engineering, marketing, sales, supply chain, operations, HR, finance, and more across more than 40 diverse businesses (https://www.idexcorp.com/our-businesses/business-segments/) around the globe, chances are, we have something special for you.
 
 
**LOCATION:**
Remote with Travel
 
 
US Valve is growing rapidly, driven by critical customer demand in data center and other high-growth markets, creating increasingly complex new product development programs with multiple manufacturing paths. The Director, NPI Program Management & Manufacturing Launch will build and lead the function responsible for taking these programs from business case through stable production, whether manufactured at US Valve, at sister IDEX business units, through external supply chain partners, or through a hybrid model. The role ensures that product design, manufacturing processes, suppliers, supply chain, quality systems, and commercial launch mature together against one integrated plan.
 
 
This leader is the single point of accountability for integrated NPI execution and owns end-to-end program results, including schedule, budget, quality, supplier readiness, manufacturing readiness, launch readiness, and ramp performance. The role organizes Product Management, Engineering, Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, Sourcing, Sales, Finance, BU partners, and external suppliers under one plan. The Director ensures APQP and launch deliverables, including PPAP, PFMEA, DFMEA, control plans, MSA, capability studies, and first article inspections, are completed on time and to standard. Success isn't design release; it is demonstrating that the full value stream can repeatedly meet customer demand with the required quality, cost, and delivery performance.
 
 
The right leader is a builder and results driver with the technical and operational credibility to walk the factory floor, challenge supplier capacity, identify manufacturing constraints, and lead cross-functional recovery. This person establishes the PMO, sets objective gate criteria and metrics, holds functional leaders and partners accountable without direct authority, challenges unrealistic plans, and leads recovery when programs fall behind. The leader will model IDEX values of trust, team, and excellence and build a high-performing team that scales with the business.
 
 
**Key Responsibilities**
***Build and Lead the Function***

* Build and lead the Program Management Office (PMO), including organizational structure, staffing plan, talent development, and succession for program and launch managers.
* Establish standard NPD governance—stage-gate/tollgate process, templates, operating cadence, and decision rights—aligned with the IDEX Operating Model.
* Define objective gate-exit criteria and recommend Go, Conditional Go, Hold, or Re-scope decisions based on demonstrated evidence.
* Own the NPD and launch portfolio; prioritize programs using 80/20 principles and align resources to the highest-value customer and growth opportunities.
* Lead executive-level business case, tollgate, and launch-readiness reviews, driving clear decisions on scope, investment, timing, and manufacturing path.

***IDEX Connected Growth and Cross-BU Leadership***

* Drive programs across multiple sister IDEX business units, leveraging IDEX connected growth strategies to share capacity, technology, capabilities, and supply chain.
* Organize and align BU partners, supply chain partners, and internal manufacturing teams into a single integrated execution plan for each program.
* Maintain one integrated critical path and one objective program status across product, supplier, tooling, manufacturing, quality, material, and customer workstreams.
* Lead make, buy, partner, intercompany, and contract manufacturing strategies, including location, capacity, Capex, tooling, staffing, and timing.
* Establish cross-BU agreements, roles, and communication cadences that ensure clear accountability for deliverables across sites and partners.
* Partner with Product Management, Engineering, Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, Sales, and Finance to align program strategy with BU and IDEX growth objectives.

***Quality Management and Launch Readiness Across Supply Chain Partners***

* Drive quality management across multiple supply chain partners, sister BUs, and internal sites to ensure consistent standards from development through production.
* Ensure APQP and product launch deliverables are completed on time and to standard, including PPAP, PFMEA, DFMEA, control plans, process flow diagrams, MSA, capability studies, and first article inspections.
* Partner with Quality and Supply Chain to qualify, develop, and audit suppliers and contract manufacturers, and drive corrective actions to closure.
* Lead launch-readiness and production-readiness gates, ensuring no program advances without required quality, validation, and capacity evidence.
* Separate product validation from production-rate validation; require evidence that the complete value stream can repeatedly achieve required volume, yield, quality, and delivery performance.
* Drive post-launch stabilization, ensuring yield, quality, and delivery targets are met before handoff to steady-state operations.

***Advanced Manufacturing and Capacity***

* Identify and drive advanced manufacturing processes, automation, and technologies needed to meet critical customer demand and scale production.
* Drive readiness of critical processes including welding and joining, filtration media and filter manufacturing, precision machining, assembly, automation, and production test.
* Lead capacity planning and implementation of new processes, including equipment selection, CapEx justification, facility changes, validation, and ramp plans.
* Partner with equipment providers, consultants, and IDEX sites to accelerate process development and transfer best practices.
* Champion design for manufacturability, lean, and continuous improvement in all new product introductions.
* Ensure process qualification, fixtures, tooling, controls, operator readiness, capacity, and rate trials are incorporated before design freeze and production release.

***Metrics, Visibility, and Results***

* Define and own program and launch KPIs, dashboards, and reporting that provide clear leadership visibility across BUs and partners.
* Identify risks early—schedule, resource, quality, sourcing, cost, capacity, and production readiness—and drive countermeasures and recovery plans.
* Challenge unrealistic timelines, resource assumptions, and commitments; escalate decisions and support needs to executive leadership.
* Deliver regular executive updates on portfolio status, risks, decisions, and results.
* Travel domestically and internationally up to 25% to support program execution, supplier engagement, site coordination, customer needs, and equipment-provider activities.
* Perform other related duties and support additional program, PMO, or business needs as assigned.

**Key Performance Metrics**

* On-time milestone and launch attainment across the NPD portfolio.
* PPAP on-time completion and first-pass approval rate across internal sites, sister BUs, and supply chain partners.
* PFMEA, DFMEA, and control plan completion prior to required gates.
* Launch quality, including first-pass yield, PPM, and escapes at launch and 90 days post-launch.
* Ramp-to-rate performance, including time to target capacity and on-time delivery to customers.
* Critical manufacturing process readiness, including qualification and demonstrated capability for welding/joining, filtration manufacturing, machining, assembly, and test as applicable.
* Program budget, Capex, and product cost performance versus business case.
* Supplier and partner quality and delivery performance on launch programs.
* New product and IDEX-connected growth revenue enabled.
* PMO team capability, staffing, and retention.

**Qualifications**

* Proven leader who has built and scaled a PMO, NPD launch, or program management function in a manufacturing environment.
* undefined
* Deep experience with APQP and product launch deliverables, including PPAP, PFMEA, DFMEA, control plans, and production part qualification.
* Track record driving quality and launch execution across multiple supply chain partners, contract manufacturers, and internal sites.
* Experience identifying and implementing advanced manufacturing processes, automation, and capacity expansions to meet demanding customer ramps.
* undefined
* Demonstrated success leading across multiple business units in a matrixed organization; multi-BU or IDEX experience preferred.
* Strong business acumen in make-versus-buy, multi-site manufacturing, CapEx, tooling, cost, capacity, and risk decisions.
* Builds metrics, dashboards, and operating cadence that drive accountability and measurable results.
* Influential leader able to align executives, BU partners, and suppliers, and hold owners accountable without direct authority.
* Strong executive communicator who turns complex program information into clear decisions and actions.
* Experience with welding/joining, filtration, pneumatics, fluid handling, pumps, compressors, blowers, valves, electromechanical products, precision manufacturing, data center, thermal management, or engineered industrial components preferred.
* Lean, Six Sigma, or PMP certification preferred; working knowledge of the IDEX Operating Model and 80/20 a plus.
* Proficient with project management tools, dashboards, and Microsoft Office applications.

**Education And/Or Experience**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, business, operations, supply chain, or a related field required; MBA or advanced degree preferred.
* 10+ years of program management, NPD, manufacturing launch, quality, or operations experience, including 5+ years leading teams, with experience in industrialization, supplier development, site transfers, and multi-site manufacturing.

**Physical Demands**

* While performing the duties of the job, the employee is required to move around and be still, use hands to finger, handle or feel objects, tools, or controls; reach with hands and arms; talk and hear.
* Employee will occasionally lift up to 35 lbs.
* Specific vision abilities required by the job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.

The compensation range for this position is $158,600.00 - $237,800.00, depending on experience. This position may be eligible for performance based bonus plan.
 
 
**Benefits Package**
Our comprehensive U.S. benefit offerings include: Health benefits, 401(k) retirement savings program with company match, PTO, and more. More information on our benefits and rewards can be found on our career page: https://www.idexcorp.com/careers/our-benefits-and-rewards/

With interesting opportunities in engineering, marketing, sales, supply chain, operations, HR, finance, and more across more than 40 diverse businesses (https://www.idexcorp.com/our-businesses/business-segments/) around the globe, chances are, we have something special for you.
 
 
**LOCATION:**
Remote with Travel
 
 
US Valve is growing rapidly, driven by critical customer demand in data center and other high-growth markets, creating increasingly complex new product development programs with multiple manufacturing paths. The Director, NPI Program Management & Manufacturing Launch will build and lead the function responsible for taking these programs from business case through stable production, whether manufactured at US Valve, at sister IDEX business units, through external supply chain partners, or through a hybrid model. The role ensures that product design, manufacturing processes, suppliers, supply chain, quality systems, and commercial launch mature together against one integrated plan.
 
 
This leader is the single point of accountability for integrated NPI execution and owns end-to-end program results, including schedule, budget, quality, supplier readiness, manufacturing readiness, launch readiness, and ramp performance. The role organizes Product Management, Engineering, Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, Sourcing, Sales, Finance, BU partners, and external suppliers under one plan. The Director ensures APQP and launch deliverables, including PPAP, PFMEA, DFMEA, control plans, MSA, capability studies, and first article inspections, are completed on time and to standard. Success isn't design release; it is demonstrating that the full value stream can repeatedly meet customer demand with the required quality, cost, and delivery performance.
 
 
The right leader is a builder and results driver with the technical and operational credibility to walk the factory floor, challenge supplier capacity, identify manufacturing constraints, and lead cross-functional recovery. This person establishes the PMO, sets objective gate criteria and metrics, holds functional leaders and partners accountable without direct authority, challenges unrealistic plans, and leads recovery when programs fall behind. The leader will model IDEX values of trust, team, and excellence and build a high-performing team that scales with the business.
 
 
**Key Responsibilities**
***Build and Lead the Function***

* Build and lead the Program Management Office (PMO), including organizational structure, staffing plan, talent development, and succession for program and launch managers.
* Establish standard NPD governance—stage-gate/tollgate process, templates, operating cadence, and decision rights—aligned with the IDEX Operating Model.
* Define objective gate-exit criteria and recommend Go, Conditional Go, Hold, or Re-scope decisions based on demonstrated evidence.
* Own the NPD and launch portfolio; prioritize programs using 80/20 principles and align resources to the highest-value customer and growth opportunities.
* Lead executive-level business case, tollgate, and launch-readiness reviews, driving clear decisions on scope, investment, timing, and manufacturing path.

***IDEX Connected Growth and Cross-BU Leadership***

* Drive programs across multiple sister IDEX business units, leveraging IDEX connected growth strategies to share capacity, technology, capabilities, and supply chain.
* Organize and align BU partners, supply chain partners, and internal manufacturing teams into a single integrated execution plan for each program.
* Maintain one integrated critical path and one objective program status across product, supplier, tooling, manufacturing, quality, material, and customer workstreams.
* Lead make, buy, partner, intercompany, and contract manufacturing strategies, including location, capacity, Capex, tooling, staffing, and timing.
* Establish cross-BU agreements, roles, and communication cadences that ensure clear accountability for deliverables across sites and partners.
* Partner with Product Management, Engineering, Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, Sales, and Finance to align program strategy with BU and IDEX growth objectives.

***Quality Management and Launch Readiness Across Supply Chain Partners***

* Drive quality management across multiple supply chain partners, sister BUs, and internal sites to ensure consistent standards from development through production.
* Ensure APQP and product launch deliverables are completed on time and to standard, including PPAP, PFMEA, DFMEA, control plans, process flow diagrams, MSA, capability studies, and first article inspections.
* Partner with Quality and Supply Chain to qualify, develop, and audit suppliers and contract manufacturers, and drive corrective actions to closure.
* Lead launch-readiness and production-readiness gates, ensuring no program advances without required quality, validation, and capacity evidence.
* Separate product validation from production-rate validation; require evidence that the complete value stream can repeatedly achieve required volume, yield, quality, and delivery performance.
* Drive post-launch stabilization, ensuring yield, quality, and delivery targets are met before handoff to steady-state operations.

***Advanced Manufacturing and Capacity***

* Identify and drive advanced manufacturing processes, automation, and technologies needed to meet critical customer demand and scale production.
* Drive readiness of critical processes including welding and joining, filtration media and filter manufacturing, precision machining, assembly, automation, and production test.
* Lead capacity planning and implementation of new processes, including equipment selection, CapEx justification, facility changes, validation, and ramp plans.
* Partner with equipment providers, consultants, and IDEX sites to accelerate process development and transfer best practices.
* Champion design for manufacturability, lean, and continuous improvement in all new product introductions.
* Ensure process qualification, fixtures, tooling, controls, operator readiness, capacity, and rate trials are incorporated before design freeze and production release.

***Metrics, Visibility, and Results***

* Define and own program and launch KPIs, dashboards, and reporting that provide clear leadership visibility across BUs and partners.
* Identify risks early—schedule, resource, quality, sourcing, cost, capacity, and production readiness—and drive countermeasures and recovery plans.
* Challenge unrealistic timelines, resource assumptions, and commitments; escalate decisions and support needs to executive leadership.
* Deliver regular executive updates on portfolio status, risks, decisions, and results.
* Travel domestically and internationally up to 25% to support program execution, supplier engagement, site coordination, customer needs, and equipment-provider activities.
* Perform other related duties and support additional program, PMO, or business needs as assigned.

**Key Performance Metrics**

* On-time milestone and launch attainment across the NPD portfolio.
* PPAP on-time completion and first-pass approval rate across internal sites, sister BUs, and supply chain partners.
* PFMEA, DFMEA, and control plan completion prior to required gates.
* Launch quality, including first-pass yield, PPM, and escapes at launch and 90 days post-launch.
* Ramp-to-rate performance, including time to target capacity and on-time delivery to customers.
* Critical manufacturing process readiness, including qualification and demonstrated capability for welding/joining, filtration manufacturing, machining, assembly, and test as applicable.
* Program budget, Capex, and product cost performance versus business case.
* Supplier and partner quality and delivery performance on launch programs.
* New product and IDEX-connected growth revenue enabled.
* PMO team capability, staffing, and retention.

**Qualifications**

* Proven leader who has built and scaled a PMO, NPD launch, or program management function in a manufacturing environment.
* undefined
* Deep experience with APQP and product launch deliverables, including PPAP, PFMEA, DFMEA, control plans, and production part qualification.
* Track record driving quality and launch execution across multiple supply chain partners, contract manufacturers, and internal sites.
* Experience identifying and implementing advanced manufacturing processes, automation, and capacity expansions to meet demanding customer ramps.
* undefined
* Demonstrated success leading across multiple business units in a matrixed organization; multi-BU or IDEX experience preferred.
* Strong business acumen in make-versus-buy, multi-site manufacturing, CapEx, tooling, cost, capacity, and risk decisions.
* Builds metrics, dashboards, and operating cadence that drive accountability and measurable results.
* Influential leader able to align executives, BU partners, and suppliers, and hold owners accountable without direct authority.
* Strong executive communicator who turns complex program information into clear decisions and actions.
* Experience with welding/joining, filtration, pneumatics, fluid handling, pumps, compressors, blowers, valves, electromechanical products, precision manufacturing, data center, thermal management, or engineered industrial components preferred.
* Lean, Six Sigma, or PMP certification preferred; working knowledge of the IDEX Operating Model and 80/20 a plus.
* Proficient with project management tools, dashboards, and Microsoft Office applications.

**Education And/Or Experience**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, business, operations, supply chain, or a related field required; MBA or advanced degree preferred.
* 10+ years of program management, NPD, manufacturing launch, quality, or operations experience, including 5+ years leading teams, with experience in industrialization, supplier development, site transfers, and multi-site manufacturing.

**Physical Demands**

* While performing the duties of the job, the employee is required to move around and be still, use hands to finger, handle or feel objects, tools, or controls; reach with hands and arms; talk and hear.
* Employee will occasionally lift up to 35 lbs.
* Specific vision abilities required by the job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.

new_roles.description:
**Job Description**
Be part of the global Integrated Supply Chain (ISC) Engineering leadership team driving factory improvements, product improvements for producibility and cost savings, manufacturing technology implementation, and new product development for Honeywell Aerospace.
 
 
We are hiring a Sr Director to lead the global ISC Advanced Manufacturing Engineering (AME) team for New Product Introduction (NPI) supporting programs across the Aerospace portfolio.
 
 
In this role, you will leverage your extensive product development experience and leadership skills. You will drive continuous improvement to develop new products, processes, and standards in support of the organization's business strategies with a direct impact on development program success. You will develop strategy, hold teams accountable and deliver high impact business results.
 
 
**Responsibilities**

* Deliver NPI program objectives including product producibility, design-to-cost (DTC) targets, production readiness, and customer quality.
* Operate as a change agent to embed producibility into our core design processes.
* Build Employee Engagement and Skills through the development of standard work, clear roles and responsibilities, and effective training programs.
* Design and develop Management Operating Systems to ensure effective team operations, driving results to program and department objectives.
* Work closely with the SBU engineering team, Program Management, and ISC leaders to build cross-organizational alignment

**Qualifications**
**YOU MUST HAVE**

* Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution in a technical discipline such as the sciences, technology, engineering or mathematics
* 8 years of experience in New Product Development
* Knowledge of manufacturing processes
* Experience working with suppliers on technical issues
* Track record of managing multiple projects with demonstrated results on a macro scale
* Experience leading a team with direct line reporting responsibility
* Abitlity to travel 30%

**Us Person Requirements**
Due to compliance with U.S. export control laws and regulations, candidate must be a U.S. Person, which is defined as, a U.S. citizen, a U.S. permanent resident, or have protected status in the U.S. under asylum or refugee status or have the ability to obtain an export authorization.
 
 
**WE VALUE**

* Advanced degree in engineering or business
* Exceptional data analysis and communication skills
* Willingness to raise standards each year to drive organizational excellence
* Ability to make sound and timely judgments in ambiguous environment
* Ability to convey subtle or complex messages clearly, as appropriate for the topic and audience.
* Diverse and global teaming and collaboration
* Balance between demand and capacity when establishing priorities for the organization.

**For Mn Candidates**
The annual base salary range for this position is $238,000-$297,000. Please note that this salary information serves as a general guideline. Honeywell considers various factors when extending an offer, including but not limited to the scope and responsibilities of the position, the candidate's work experience, education and training, key skills, as well as market and business considerations.
 
 
This position is incentive eligible.
 
 
**Benefits**
Beyond a performance-driven salary, you'll work alongside dedicated experts on technology that's advancing aviation. As a Honeywell Aerospace employee, you're eligible for a comprehensive benefits package that includes:
 
 

* Employer-subsidized medical, dental, vision and life insurance
* Short-term and long-term disability coverage
* 401(k) match, flexible spending accounts and health savings accounts
* Employee assistance program and educational assistance
* Parental leave and 12 paid holidays
* Paid time off for vacation, personal and sick time

Explore your benefits: https://honeywellaerospacebenefits.com/
 
 
**POSTING TIMELINE**
The application period for the job is estimated to be 40 days from the job posting date; however, this may be shortened or extended depending on business needs and the availability of qualified candidates.
 
 
Join a company that's reintroducing itself to the aviation community we've helped advance for more than a century. At
**Honeywell Aerospace**
(NASDAQ: HONA), we're launching as an independent, publicly traded aerospace and defense company built on a legacy of operational excellence and mission-focused execution.
 
 
Our new brand identity pairs that heritage with real momentum, as we build technology that helps pilots navigate with confidence, aircraft operate more efficiently, and operators stay ahead of change. With our systems on board 90% of the world's aircraft, your work here has reach that's rare to find anywhere else.
 
 
Focusing on our customers, investing in innovation, and building a culture of accountability and performance is how we're shaping what comes next.
 
 
Every horizon. Every mission. Every day.
 
 
Honeywell Aerospace Products And Services Are Found On Aircraft Across Commercial Aviation, Defense And Space. We Operate Through Three Business Areas
 
 
Electronic Solutions develops the avionics, navigation systems, sensors and electromagnetic defense technology on board 90% of the world's aircraft
 
 
Engines & Power Systems provides the propulsion, auxiliary power and electrical systems that keep those aircraft flying
 
 
Control Systems supplies the thermal and motion control systems that support takeoff, landing and the safety of everyone on board
 
 
With approximately 58,000 employees worldwide and net sales of $17.4B in 2025, we are also advancing systems for autonomous and supersonic platforms — bringing the same focus on safety and efficiency to the next era of flight. Explore our businesses: https://www.honeywellaerospace.com

new_roles.title: Director of Quality
new_roles.description:
Signia Aerospace is a global, integrated provider of high-performance systems and specialized components for the aerospace industry. Signia designs, manufactures, and services a wide range of products, that include mission equipment, thermal management systems, engine technology, and propellers. The Signia brands are leaders in their respective markets and provide a compelling value proposition to both aerospace and defense OEMs and end-users.

**Position Overview**

Onboard Systems Hoist & Winch, located in Anaheim, CA is one of the world’s leading providers of Search & Rescue (SAR) and Human External Cargo (HEC) advanced mission equipment for civil, commercial, and military helicopters.

The Director of Quality is a key leadership position reporting directly to the General Manager (GM), responsible for establishing and executing the company's overall quality strategy. This role provides strategic direction and oversight of the Quality function, ensuring the effectiveness of the Quality Management System (QMS), compliance with AS9100 and applicable regulatory and customer requirements, and continuous improvement across all business operations. As the designated FAA Part 145 Accountable Manager, the Director has authority over all Part 145 repair-station operations, ensures personnel follow applicable FAA regulations, and serves as the primary contact with the FAA. The Director also partners with executive and operational leadership to drive quality performance, manage organizational risk, and foster a company-wide culture of quality and accountability.

**Location:** Anaheim, CA (on-site)

**Schedule:** Monday - Friday

**Pay:** $180,000 - $225,000, plus bonus eligibility

**What You’ll Do**

**1. Quality Management System Leadership**

* Establish quality strategy, policies, and measurable objectives aligned with the company's business goals.
* Own and administer the company-wide Quality Management System in accordance with AS9100 (which incorporates ISO 9001) and applicable customer and regulatory requirements, including FAA and, where applicable, EASA requirements.
* Oversee the FAA Part 145 repair-station quality control system, including the Repair Station Manual, Quality Control Manual, Operations Specifications, and documented inspection and return-to-service controls.
* Ensure the QMS is effective, scalable, consistently deployed across the business, and aligned with the company's growth and product roadmap
* Lead continuous improvement and operational excellence initiatives to optimize quality processes, procedures, documentation, and controls.
* Manage document control and maintain accurate, controlled quality procedures, process documentation, and compliance records.

**2. Compliance & Customer Support**

* Serve as the primary point of contact for external audits, including AS9100 certification audits, customer audits, and regulatory assessments.
* Prepare the organization for audits and lead audit responses, corrective actions, and follow-up activities to verify effective closure.
* Build and maintain credibility and trust with executive stakeholders, aerospace OEM customers, auditors, regulatory officials, and relevant industry partners.
* Ensure ongoing compliance with applicable standards, customer requirements, and contractual quality clauses.
* Oversee incoming, in-process, and final manufacturing inspections, including first article inspection (FAI) activities to AS9102 when required by contract or approved procedures, while maintaining distinct FAA Part 145 maintenance-inspection and return-to-service controls.

**3. Quality Assurance**

* Ensure timely containment and investigation of quality issues using methods such as A3, 8D, and 5 Whys, with documented root cause and corrective action (RCCA).
* Support Manufacturing, Engineering, and Supply Chain teams with timely quality guidance and issue resolution.
* Establish quality KPIs and targets, monitor trends, and report performance and improvement plans to the GM and leadership team.
* Use data-driven insights to improve customer satisfaction, compliance, and product consistency; reduce defects and cost of poor quality (COPQ); and verify corrective-action effectiveness.
* Identify, assess, and mitigate product safety, airworthiness, quality, and compliance risks; escalate significant issues to leadership and track mitigation actions to closure.
* Establish clear escalation pathways for nonconforming product and airworthiness concerns; prevent unauthorized product release and ensure release decisions remain with appropriately authorized personnel.
* Lead internal audits and management reviews to ensure ongoing system effectiveness.
* Provide technical leadership and ensure team competency in precision metrology and geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T).
* Lead a risk-based supplier quality program covering supplier qualification, performance monitoring, audits, and supplier corrective-action follow-up.

**4. Cross-functional Collaboration and Team Leadership**

* Partner closely with Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, and Program teams to embed quality into design, production, and supplier processes.
* Support new product introduction (NPI) with quality planning, risk assessments, and validation activities.
* Lead and develop the Quality team through clear objectives, coaching, performance management, leadership development, and succession planning.
* Promote a proactive quality culture across the organization through training, mentorship, and leadership by example.

**Who You Are**

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in engineering, quality, manufacturing, or a related discipline.
* 7+ years of aerospace quality experience, including senior leadership responsibilities and significant responsibility for AS9100-based quality systems.
* Deep working knowledge of aerospace quality principles and requirements.
* Experience working with major aerospace OEMs and their quality expectations.
* Demonstrated experience leading internal, customer, and third-party certification or regulatory audits.
* Strong attention to detail and a commitment to accuracy, discipline, and compliance.
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to influence across functions and communicate effectively with customers, auditors, and executive leadership.
* Proven ability to lead and develop a small, high-impact Quality team.
* Demonstrated ability to lead continuous improvement and operational excellence initiatives.
* Working knowledge of 14 CFR Parts 21, 43, and 145, including the distinction between production airworthiness approvals and maintenance return to service, and applicable FAA Form 8130-3 issuance and signatory-authorization requirements.
* Experience with FAA-certificated Part 145 repair-station requirements, including regulatory interface and oversight of inspection and return-to-service controls.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Basic understanding of metallurgy and material certification review.
* AS9100 lead auditor training or equivalent demonstrated experience leading aerospace QMS audits.
* Background supporting NPI, supplier quality, and manufacturing quality operations.
* An advanced degree in a related discipline.
* ASQ or other relevant quality certifications, such as CQE or CQA.

**What’s In It for You**

* Competitive salary with annual bonus eligibility.
* Benefits package including medical, dental, vision, life, and disability coverage.
* Paid time off and holidays.
* 401(k) plan with employer contribution matching.
* In addition to offering competitive wages and benefits, Onboard Systems offers the opportunity to increase future earnings tied to growth in company performance. We recognize employee contributions toward growing the business through our Growth Participation Unit (GPU) program. GPUs are tied directly to company growth and reward all eligible employees with cash when the business grows over time.

*All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, religion, national origin, disability, veteran status, age, marital status, pregnancy, genetic information, or other legally protected status*

new_roles.description:
**Become a part of our caring community**
=========================================

Humana is committed to helping people achieve their best health by delivering innovative technology solutions that enable exceptional member and provider experiences.
 
 
The Director, Segment Quality Engineering is a strategic technology leader responsible for advancing quality engineering practices across a defined portion of Humana’s technology portfolio. Reporting to the AVP, Quality Engineering – Segment, this role will lead teams responsible for delivery quality, test automation, release readiness, and continuous improvement across multiple product and application teams.
 
 
This leader will work closely with Product, Engineering, Architecture, Platform, DevOps, and enterprise quality partners to embed quality throughout the software development lifecycle and improve release confidence, delivery speed, and production stability.

**Responsibilities**

 

* Lead quality engineering strategy and execution across a defined portfolio, domain, or segment.
* Lead and develop quality engineering managers, leads, engineers, and SDETs; drive organization design, talent growth, and team performance.
* Establish portfolio quality goals, KPIs, and governance to improve delivery quality, release readiness, and production stability.
* Embed built-in quality across planning, design, development, testing, and deployment.
* Oversee test strategy and execution across functional, integration, end-to-end, regression, and release validation.
* Own portfolio-level quality risk management, including defect trends, release concerns, environment issues, and cross-team dependencies.
* Drive automation-first practices and integrate quality signals, validation, and gates into CI/CD pipelines.
* Lead adoption of AI-enabled quality engineering capabilities and promote innovative practices that improve speed, coverage, and reliability.
* Sponsor modernization of quality frameworks, tooling, and test approaches for APIs, distributed systems, and cloud-native platforms.
* Oversee non-functional quality practices, including performance, resiliency, operational readiness, and security validation.
* Use metrics and production insights to drive continuous improvement, maturity, and investment priorities.
* Partner with segment and enterprise stakeholders to align execution with broader quality engineering strategy, standards, and reference architecture direction.
* Ensure responsible adoption of AI and compliance with applicable security, privacy, regulatory, and operational standards.

**Use your skills to make an impact**
=====================================

**Required Qualifications**

 

* Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience.
* 10+ years of experience in software engineering, quality engineering, testing, or related technical disciplines.
* 5+ years of leadership experience managing quality engineering, test automation, or software delivery teams in large enterprise environments.
