new_roles.title: Director of Operations (PCNY - Queens)
new_roles.description:
**ABOUT US:** 
With a dedication to our people and our products, The Honickman Companies® are collectively one of the largest independent beverage employers in the country. Our Pepsi business includes distribution for brands like Pepsi-Cola, Starbucks, Lipton Teas, Gatorade, Evian and more, throughout the 5 Borough’s, Long Island, Westchester and Pennsauken NJ. If you are excited to work with some of the biggest brands in the world, in the biggest brand market in the world, come see what we have to offer. a passionate, self-motivated, and detail-oriented team player who is committed to the success of our customers. You will focus on growing and developing existing clients, as well as generating new business by identifying, implementing and executing new strategies.
 
 
**SUMMARY:** 
Leads the day-to-day operations of a large-scale beverage manufacturing facility, with overall accountability for Production, Quality, Maintenance, Shipping, Receiving and Warehousing. Establishes operating priorities and develops leaders and teams to deliver safe, high-quality, cost-effective and efficient production. Applies practical business judgment, disciplined execution and continuous improvement through the Honickman Management Operating System to improve plant performance and support the Company’s business strategy.
 
 
**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:** 

* Provides visible, hands-on leadership and direction for all plant operations, including Production, Quality, Maintenance, Shipping, Receiving and Warehousing.
* Establishes clear operating priorities, performance expectations and accountability; aligns staffing, resources and production plans with customer and business requirements.
* Ensures production schedules are achieved while meeting safety, food safety, quality, efficiency, cost and customer service expectations.
* Monitors and acts upon key performance indicators, including safety performance, schedule attainment, production efficiency, equipment utilization, downtime, waste, labor productivity, inventory accuracy and service levels.
* Identifies operating constraints and performance gaps; leads root cause analysis, corrective actions and practical solutions that improve throughput, reliability and execution.
* Ensures manufacturing processes, standard operating procedures and controls are documented, consistently followed and improved as business needs evolve.
* Partners with Quality leadership to maintain effective food safety, sanitation, preventive control and quality systems and to resolve customer complaints, audit findings and corrective actions promptly.
* Provides leadership and oversight for preventive and predictive maintenance, work-order execution and equipment reliability; aligns maintenance priorities with production requirements and long-term asset needs.
* Supports capital planning and execution, including equipment upgrades, facility improvements and other investments that improve safety, capacity, reliability or cost performance.
* Oversees warehouse, inventory control, shipping and receiving operations to ensure accurate inventory, efficient material flow, appropriate space utilization and timely customer shipments.
* Drives practical, results-oriented continuous improvement through the Honickman Management Operating System; ensures initiatives produce measurable gains in safety, quality, productivity, waste, cost and equipment effectiveness.
* Develops and manages operating plans and budgets; controls labor, overtime, waste, operating expense and other key financial measures while balancing service and production needs.
* Leads, develops and holds department managers and supervisors accountable; builds leadership capability, cross-functional collaboration and a strong succession pipeline.
* Builds a culture of teamwork, communication, employee engagement and ownership by maintaining a regular presence on the plant floor and engaging employees at all levels.
* Establishes productive relationships with employees and union representatives; ensures consistent application of Company policies, procedures and applicable collective bargaining agreements and addresses employee relations matters promptly and professionally.
* Promotes a proactive safety culture and ensures compliance with applicable OSHA, environmental, food safety, regulatory and customer requirements; directs timely incident investigations and corrective actions.
* Provides accurate and timely operating reports, communicates plant performance and risks, and recommends actions needed to achieve business objectives.
* Performs other related duties as required and assigned

**KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS:** 
The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
 

* Comprehensive knowledge of large-scale manufacturing operations, production planning, equipment reliability, quality systems, food safety, warehousing, distribution and inventory controls.
* Strong business and financial acumen, including the ability to develop operating plans, manage budgets and labor costs, interpret performance data and translate findings into action.
* Practical knowledge of continuous improvement, root cause analysis, standard work and performance management; ability to implement solutions that deliver measurable operational results.
* Demonstrated ability to lead a complex operation through multiple levels of management and to establish priorities, accountability and disciplined execution across functions.
* Working knowledge of OSHA, environmental and food-manufacturing regulatory requirements and the ability to maintain effective safety, quality and compliance systems.
* Proven ability to lead and develop managers and supervisors, engage a diverse hourly workforce and build effective labor-management relationships in a union environment.
* Excellent judgment, problem-solving, organizational and follow-up skills; able to manage competing priorities and make timely decisions in a fast-paced operation.
* Effective oral, written and presentation skills, with the ability to communicate expectations, performance, risks and recommendations to employees, leaders and senior management.
* Strong computer skills, including Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook; familiarity with manufacturing, maintenance, warehouse and performance-reporting systems.

**EDUCATION AND WORK EXPERIENCE:** 

* Bachelor’s degree in Business, Engineering, Operations Management or a related field preferred; equivalent manufacturing leadership experience will be considered.
* Minimum 10 years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience, including prior overall responsibility as a plant, site or operations leader for a large, complex manufacturing facility.
* Prior responsibility for multiple functions, including Production, Quality, Maintenance and Warehouse/Distribution operations, with demonstrated success improving plant performance.
* Beverage manufacturing experience strongly preferred; significant food manufacturing experience will also be considered.
* Experience leading a unionized manufacturing workforce strongly preferred.
* Experience managing operating budgets, labor costs, productivity, equipment reliability, quality, safety and overall plant performance required.
* Any equivalent combination of education, experience and training that provides the required knowledge, skills and abilities.

**PHYSICAL DEMANDS / WORK ENVIRONMENT / TRAVEL:** 

* Manufacturing, warehouse and office environments; regular presence on the production floor is required.
* Must be able to work around moving equipment, elevated noise levels, temperature variation and other conditions typical of a beverage manufacturing facility, with required personal protective equipment.
* Ability to move throughout the facility and occasionally lift, push or pull up to 50 pounds.
* Ability to work a flexible schedule and respond to operational needs outside normal business hours; limited travel may be required.

**COMPENSATION RANGE:** 
Potential earning is from $190,000.00 - $215,000.00 annually
 
 
The statements herein are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by employees and are not to be construed as an exhaustive list of responsibilities, duties, and skills required by personnel so classified. Furthermore, they do not establish a contract for employment and are subject to change at the discretion of the company.
 
 

* We do not provide application status due to overwhelming volume. If your skills meet our needs, we will contact you to move forward in the process.\*

\*\*EOE without regard to race, color, religion, creed, affectional or sexual orientation or sex, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, genetics, veteran status, gender, gender identity, citizenship status, marital status, VEVRAA Federal Contractor.\*\*
 
\*\*\*If you have a disability and you need an accommodation to apply, please contact us at hiring@hongrp.com

new_roles.title: Plant Director
new_roles.description:
**Accelerate the possible by joining a winning Amcor team that’s transforming the packaging industry and improving lives around the world.**
============================================================================================================================================

At Amcor, we unpack possibility through our innovative and responsible packaging to provide solutions that benefit our customers, our people and our planet. More than 10,000 consumers worldwide encounter our products every second and rely on us for safe access to food, medicine and other goods. We value their trust by making safety our guiding principle. It’s our core value and integral to how we do business.

Beyond this core principle, our shared values and behaviors unite us as we work together to elevate customers, shape lives and protect the future. We champion our customers and help them succeed. We play to win – adapting quickly in an everchanging world – and make smart choices to safeguard our business, our communities and the people we serve for generations to come. And we invest in our world-class team, empowering our colleagues to unpack their potential, because we believe when our people grow, so does our business.

To learn more about playing for Team Amcor, visit www.amcor.com I LinkedIn I Glassdoor I Facebook I YouTube

**Job Description**
===================

To manage and lead overall plant operations ensuring the achievement of plant targets for Safety, Quality, Service and Cost. This will be executed through providing strong leadership to the plant team and managing the systems, equipment, people and materials according to the established policies, procedures, specifications, and customer requirements. This individual reports directly to the Director-Manufacturing. The Plant Lead Team members will report directly to the Plant Manager (typically 6-10 direct reports) Scope for this Plant Manager role is a medium to large-sized facility with typically greater than 300 employees and mid to high-level complexity.

**WHAT YOU GET TO DO**

* Leads and drives plant safety culture and puts safety first in all responsibilities.
* Leads identification of opportunities and problem areas for targeted improvement by creating, reviewing and monitoring data or reports that show performance to KPI's. (specifically, safety, quality, waste, and productivity)
* Oversees all aspects of human capital planning & management for the facility, including HC goal setting, improvement targets for KPI's, salary planning, performance management.
* Attract, hire, develop direct reports and create strong succession plans
* Ensure compliance with department safety, product safety, fire protection, Company polices/procedures, and housekeeping programs.
* Ensures effective, timely and well-developed communications for all product associates.
* Manage process control initiatives by ensuring manufacturing SOP's exist, and that they are sufficient for quality, safety, and process control.
* Leads plant budgeting processes
* Ensures execution of plant Cap-Ex
* Lead and ensure growth of CI culture by providing resources, participating in teams, and leading teams as necessary.
* Ensures facility compliance with local, state and federal regulatory agencies.
* Drives employee engagement action planning for the facility
* Leads communication to all plant associates regarding business needs and results
* Leads efforts at Best Practice sharing with other facilities
* Meets safety targets and drives a safety culture and environment to send every employee home everyday without injury.
* Meets or exceeds plant business plan and KPI’s.
* Delivers on established budget.
* Best Practices leadership
* Effective, cost-efficient planning and utilization of manpower, materials and machinery.
* Strong Human Capital planning, development and management for the facility.
* Drives High Performance Culture
* Plant talent to deliver on plan

 **WHAT WE VALUE**
* Strong financial acumen
* Results Orientation / Delivers on Plan
* Team Leadership
* Develops Organizational Capability
* Strategic Orientation / Enterprise Thinker
* Collaboration & Influence
* Change Leadership
* Facility Business Acumen/Market Knowledge

**WHAT WE WANT FROM YOU**

* A Bachelor’s degree in engineering, business administration, or related field
* 10+ years of relevant experience in a production environment
* Demonstrated passion for safety
* 7+ years of leadership experience, preferably in flexible packaging
* Lives Amcor Values and leads by example
* Proven ability to lead and drive continuous improvement
* Strong Customer Service mindset
* Strong written and verbal communication skills
* Demonstrated knowledge of BNA customers and plant capabilities
* Demonstrated understanding of drivers of plant results, including ability to interpret financial results
* Demonstrated CI knowledge, Six Sigma Black Belt certification strongly preferred

**Our Expectations**
====================

We expect our people to be guided by The Amcor Way and demonstrate our Values every day to enable the business to win. We are winning when:

* Our people are engaged and developing as part of a high-performing Amcor team
* Our customers grow and prosper from Amcor’s quality, service, and innovation
* Our investors benefit from Amcor’s consistent growth and superior returns
* The environment is better off because of Amcor’s leadership and products

**Equal Opportunity** **Employer/Minorities/Females/Disabled/Veterans/Sexual** **Orientation/Gender Identity**
==============================================================================================================

Amcor is an Equal Opportunity Employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

If you would like more information about your EEO rights as an applicant under the law, please click on the *"Know Your Rights: Workplace Discrimination is Illegal" Poster*. If, because of a medical condition or disability, you need a reasonable accommodation for any part of the employment process, please call 224-313-7000 and let us know the nature of your request and your contact information.

**E-Verify**
============

We verify the identity and employment authorization of individuals hired for employment in the United States.

**Compensation**
================

The starting salary for this position is expected to be between $176,100 to $242,100 depending on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Base pay information is based on national averages and a geographic differential may be applied based on work location. Position may also be eligible for Amcor’s Management Incentive Plan / Sales Incentive Plan, which is an annual bonus program based on business and individual performance, as well as medical coverage and other health and welfare benefits. The salary range provided reflects the anticipated starting salary base pay for this role at the time of this posting and does not necessarily reflect full earning potential over the course of employment. This range is applicable to positions performed in jurisdictions with pay transparency requirements, including CA, CO, CT, HI, IL, MD, MA, MN, NV, NJ, NY, RI, VT, WA, Washington DC, as well as remote roles that may be performed in these locations. Compensation for roles performed outside of these jurisdictions may vary. The Company reserves the right to modify this range at any time.

**Benefits**
============

When you join Amcor, you will have access to a comprehensive benefits and compensation package that includes:

* Medical, dental and vision plans
* Flexible time off, starting at 80 hours paid time per year for full-time salaried employees
* Company-paid holidays starting at 8 days per year and may vary by location
* Wellbeing program & Employee Assistance Program
* Health Savings Account/Flexible Spending Account
* Life insurance, AD&D, short-term & long-term disability, and voluntary benefits
* Paid Parental Leave
* Retirement Savings Plan with company match
* Tuition Reimbursement (dependent upon approval)
* Discretionary annual bonus program (initial eligibility dependent upon hire date)

new_roles.title: Director of Integrated Fab Manufacturing
new_roles.description:
Bold Thinking. World Changing. At SkyWater, our ingenuity helps improve lives around the world by manufacturing U.S. made semiconductors that are essential ingredients of modern life. Automotive safety enhancements, life-saving medical devices, consumer electronics and American security require semiconductors. Working in our Minnesota headquarters, Florida, or Texas location — employees join together to improve the world.
 
 
Explore what’s possible. Joining our U.S. - based team means contributing to and learning about the commercialization of some of the most exciting technologies the world has ever seen. We are turning “science fiction” into everyday reality through technologies such as superconducting, 3D integrated circuits or computer chips, carbon nanotubes, photonic logic devices, micro electro-mechanical systems and other emerging device topologies. We manufacture products for aerospace and defense, medical, automotive, consumer and industrial markets, to name a few. Our customers include emerging leaders who rely on our intellectual property security and quality manufacturing services.
 
 
Step into the future. SkyWater’s values of Integrity, Excellence, Collaboration, Empowerment and Growth Mindset guide us to cultivate an empowered, learning environment. We also invest in developing highly skilled, dedicated employees — and employees who are entering the workforce for the first time, from the military, and a variety of educational backgrounds.
 
 
Are you bold thinking? Find your place on our team and help us change the world!
 
 
**Primary Objective:** 
Join an innovative semiconductor manufacturing organization at the forefront of advanced technology and manufacturing excellence. The Director of Integrated Fab Manufacturing owns the operational, financial, and strategic leadership of the Bloomington fabrication facility, including the Advanced Technology Services (ATS) Process Engineering Technician team. This role ensures the factory achieves world-class safety, quality, output, cycle time, and cost performance while directing a 24/7 organization and partnering across engineering, planning, and quality teams to meet all customer and business commitments.
 
In this role, you will be responsible for the end-to-end operational execution, strategic planning, budgetary ownership, and leadership to ensure safe, reliable, and efficient semiconductor manufacturing. You will be responsible for driving absolute excellence across safety, quality, output, cost optimization, and ensuring smooth production flow to consistently meet internal and external customer quality and on-time delivery (OTD) commitments, and fab velocity metrics / key performance indicators (KPIs).
 
The successful candidate will own the organizational design and talent strategy for their organization, serving as a role model and lead a highly matrixed organization consisting of the Manufacturing team, Process Engineering Technicians group, and Flow Engineers. This role is expected to partner closely with Program Managers, Technical Leads, Wafer Planning, Manufacturing, Equipment Engineering, Quality, and Technology Development teams to improve operational performance, resolve manufacturing constraints, and deliver business objectives. This leader will play a critical role in transforming factory capabilities to meet strict customer commitments and flexible demand by influencing long-range capacity and setting standards for the MN fab operations organization.
 
 
**Major Areas of Accountability:** 

* Operations Leadership: Lead the daily and long-term operational execution in the fab, as well as the ATS technician and flow engineer teams to meet all production starts, output targets, yield expectations, cycle time goals, and quality standards, including setting clear priorities for the organization. Direct, develop, and coach the 24/7 operations teams—including Production, ATS Process Engineering Technicians, and Flow Engineers—to ensure capability, accountability, and organizational readiness.
* Team Leadership: Lead, develop, and empower the Production team, Process Engineering Technicians and Flow Engineers to provide effective manufacturing support, maintain production continuity, and resolve process and workflow issues
* Budgetary Responsibility: Own the fab operating budget, including labor, materials, maintenance, and operational spending; drive cost-reduction initiatives and evaluate capital investments using ROI-based decision-making.
* Wafer Planning and Customer Delivery: Partner with Wafer Planning and Program Management to align schedules, capacity, and customer priorities; identify delivery risks and oversee recovery plans to maintain on time delivery (OTD) performance.
* Manufacturing Performance: Partner with Industrial Engineers, and drive continuous improvement in throughput, cycle time, WIP management, yield, quality, equipment availability, and manufacturing cost using data-driven decision-making and structured problem-solving.
* Cross-Functional Collaboration: Coordinate with Manufacturing, Process Engineering, Equipment Engineering, Quality, and Technology Development to resolve production constraints, improve equipment readiness, and maintain stable manufacturing operations.
* Operational Excellence: Establish and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs), including customer OTD, cycle time, throughput, equipment availability, and quality. Promote standardization, disciplined execution, effective escalation, and continuous improvement.
* Talent Development: Build a high-performing organization through coaching, accountability, collaboration, and development of technical and operational talent. Responsible for the organizational design and talent strategy of these teams, with a focus on cultivating and retaining key talent, developing future leaders and preparing current leaders for the next level role.

**Required Qualifications:** 

* Education: Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, Physics, or related technical discipline.
* Experience: Minimum 12 years in semiconductor manufacturing or operations; minimum 5+ years leading fab operations in a senior manager or director capacity within a 24/7 manufacturing environment.
* Skills:
* Demonstrated ability to improve manufacturing performance (throughput, cycle time, yield, cost, and customer delivery).
* Expertise in wafer planning, WIP management, or production scheduling.
* Strong capability in statistical process control (SPC), structured problem-solving, and data-driven decision-making.
* Demonstrated leadership with large technical teams, with an ability to communicate and collaborate cross-functionally, delivering results in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
* Proven track record of managing a 24/7 manufacturing organization and guiding cross-functional teams through technical tool or yield crises.
* Citizenship: US Citizen required.

**Physical Requirements:** 

* Ability to enter the cleanroom in full PPE to provide technical and operational support.
* Ability to navigate multi-level fab environments, including prolonged walking and standing when needed.

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job.
 
 
**Preferred Qualifications:** 

* Education: Master’s or PhD in a relevant technical discipline.
* Experience: Deep knowledge of advanced Complimentary Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor (CMOS) nodes, fab toolsets (Lithography, Etch, Diffusion, Thin Films, Chemical Mechanical Polish, Metrology, Metals), and factory automation systems.
* Skills: Experience driving major manufacturing transformations, automation or digitization initiatives, or large-scale capacity improvements.

The annual salary range for this role is $159440 - $239,160. Pay offered is based on many factors, including, but not limited to, the job-related experience, skills, education, and credentials of each candidate.
 
 
SkyWater offers an exciting environment where the brightest semiconductor minds come together to achieve exceptional results. We offer competitive salary and an opportunity to participate in incentive plans as well as other employee financial benefits, including 401k match, and life insurance.
 
Additionally, SkyWater offers a comprehensive benefits package which promotes a healthy life. This includes benefit eligibility day one, medical, dental, mental health benefits, vision, legal planning, short- and long-term disability, paid time off, paid holidays, an on-site fitness facility, and an on-site self-serve market.
 
SkyWater complies with federal and state disability laws and makes reasonable accommodations for applicants and employees with disabilities unless doing so would cause an undue hardship. Alternative methods of applying for employment are available to individuals unable to submit an application through this site because of a disability. To request reasonable accommodations, to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and/or to receive other benefits and privileges of employment, please contact Human Resources at 952-851-5200 or Recruiting@SkyWatertechnology.com.
 
EOE, including disability/vets
 
We will never ask applicants to pay fees, purchase equipment or gift cards, or provide financial information before a formal offer of employment has been accepted. If you receive a suspicious communication claiming to represent our company, please verify its authenticity by contacting our recruitment team at recruiting@skywatertechnology.com before responding.

new_roles.title: Senior Director, Merchandise Manufacturing & Sourcing
new_roles.description:
**Job Description:**
====================

NOTE: This role is based in New York City and encourages a minimum of two days per week in the SoHo office. Some roles or teams may require additional in-office attendance if the essential functions of the role require it.

THE OPPORTUNITY

The Senior Director, Merchandise Manufacturing & Strategic Sourcing is a key global leadership role responsible for the strategic sourcing, manufacturing, commercialization, and production execution of Scholastic's merchandise portfolio supporting Book Fairs, Book Clubs, Trade Publishing, Discovery Fairs, and future consumer product initiatives.

Reporting directly to the SVP Manufacturing who is responsible for Global Supply Chain and Procurement, this position serves as the critical bridge between Product Development, Editorial, Design, Category Management, Publishing, and global manufacturing partners.

This leader partners with internal stakeholders from the earliest stages of product ideation, providing expertise in product engineering, sourcing strategy, manufacturing capabilities, material selection, cost optimization, and production feasibility. The objective is to transform creative concepts into high-quality, innovative products that deliver exceptional customer experiences while achieving aggressive cost, quality, and speed-to-market objectives.

The role oversees a global sourcing portfolio exceeding $200 million annually and leads an international team of approximately 12 professionals located across the United States and India. The position may be based in the United States, China, or India and requires extensive collaboration with domestic and international suppliers and manufacturing partners.

RESPONSIBILITIES

**Product Development, Ideation & Publishing Partnership**

* Serve as a strategic partner to Publishing, Editorial, Design, Category Management, Book Fairs, Book Clubs, Trade, and other stakeholders to translate creative concepts and intellectual property into compelling, manufacturable products.
* Engage early in product ideation, bringing manufacturing and sourcing expertise to decisions around materials, formats, construction, packaging, features, price points, and production methods.
* Proactively introduce new product concepts, materials, manufacturing capabilities, and supplier innovations that expand Scholastic's product opportunities.
* Partner throughout the development cycle from concept, specification, prototyping, sampling, and costing through pproval and production.
* Challenge and improve concepts where appropriate to enhance consumer appeal, quality, manufacturability, sustainability, speed, and cost.

**Consumer Products & Sourcing Strategy**

* Lead development of the sourcing and manufacturing strategy supporting Scholastic's expanding consumer-products and merchandise initiatives.
* Partner with business and publishing leadership to identify new product categories and opportunities across Book Fairs, Discovery Fairs, retail, e-commerce, licensing, and other emerging channels.
* Develop category sourcing strategies addressing manufacturing regions, supplier capabilities, cost, lead times, minimum quantities, tooling, quality, and supply-chain risk.
* Build a proactive pipeline of product ideas and manufacturing capabilities that can be regularly presented to internal stakeholders.
* Maintain awareness of consumer trends, emerging categories, materials, and manufacturing technologies and translate those insights into actionable product opportunities.

**Global Vendor Development & Innovation**

* Proactively identify and develop innovative manufacturers and product-development partners, particularly those offering engineering expertise, rapid prototyping, unique materials, creative capabilities, and new manufacturing technologies.
* Develop suppliers that can function as extensions of Scholastic's product-development organization, proactively bringing forward new concepts and capabilities.
* Continuously evaluate the supplier portfolio to improve competitiveness, increase speed, diversify supply, reduce risk, and enable entry into new categories.

**Global Sourcing, Cost & Operational Leadership**

* Develop and execute a comprehensive global sourcing strategy supporting more than $200 million in annual product expense.
* Establish sourcing roadmaps and supplier-diversification strategies that anticipate future business requirements and reduce dependency on individual suppliers or regions.
* Ensure products consistently meet expectations for quality, safety, regulatory compliance, sustainability, cost, and on-time delivery.

**Supplier Engagement & Global Travel**

* Maintain direct senior-level engagement with strategic manufacturing partners and regularly visit supplier facilities to evaluate capabilities, innovation, quality, capacity, and operational performance.
* Significant international travel is expected, with consistent travel to Asia, particularly China and India, as well as other global sourcing markets as required.
* Use supplier visits as product-development and innovation opportunities to identify new materials, manufacturing processes, capabilities, and product concepts for Scholastic.
* Participate in relevant trade shows, sourcing events, and supplier innovation sessions to identify emerging capabilities and potential partners.

**Organizational Leadership**

* Lead and develop a global organization of approximately 12 professionals across the United States and India.
* Build a culture combining sourcing discipline with creativity, product knowledge, commercial thinking, and an entrepreneurial approach to product development.
* Develop team capabilities in product ideation, product development, supplier innovation, value engineering, and strategic sourcing.
* Build strong partnerships across Publishing, Editorial, Design, Category Management, Supply Chain, Finance, and senior leadership, positioning the organization as a strategic product-development partner.

**Key Measures of Success**

Success will be measured through product development and innovation, cost per unit and total landed-cost, speed to market, supplier innovation and diversification, quality and compliance, on-time performance.

**About Scholastic**

For more than 100 years, Scholastic Corporation (NASDAQ: SCHL) has been meeting children where they are – at school, at home and in their communities – by creating quality content and experiences, all beginning with literacy. Scholastic delivers stories, characters, and learning moments that empower all kids to become lifelong readers and learners through bestselling children’s books, literacy- and knowledge-building resources for schools including classroom magazines, and award-winning, entertaining children's media. As the world's largest publisher and distributor of children's books through school-based book clubs and book fairs, classroom libraries, school and public libraries, retail, and online, and with a global reach into more than 135 countries, Scholastic encourages the personal and intellectual growth of all children, while nurturing a lifelong relationship with reading, themselves, and the world around them. Learn more at www.scholastic.com.

Some benefits that we offer:

 

* Full suite of health and wellness benefits (including a $0 deductible Medical Plan)
* Retirement Savings Plan 401(k) with options for both Roth and Traditional Contributions
* Tuition-Free programs for undergraduate and graduate degrees
* Generous Parental Leave Program
* Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP) with opportunity for discounted stock at a 15% discount

Thank you for your consideration in choosing Scholastic.

HOW YOU CAN FIT **(Qualifications)**

A minimum of 10 years of experience as a valued member of a non-book/novelty/ merchandise development team. Proven track record working at a well established company representing a diverse product catalog consisting of products attractive to consumer interest and educationaly directed.

Comfort in travel globally and managing teams remotely and developing deep relationships with vendors in China and India along with others Asian regions.

Direct book experience and knowledge of the book publishing cycles and development timelines.

new_roles.title: Director, Global Supply Chain Center of Excellence – Chemical Manufacturing
new_roles.description:
**The Opportunity:**
--------------------

**Position purpose**

 
 

Lead the global Supply Chain Center of Excellence across three pillars: Planning Excellence & Governance; Analytics, Optimization & Value Improvement; and Data, Systems & Digital Enablement.

 
 

Strengthen supply chain performance by establishing consistent planning practices, delivering actionable analysis and measurable improvements, and enabling reliable data and effective planning technology. Partner with regional supply chain leaders to build capabilities and sustain improvements while regional teams retain operational supply and inventory accountability.

 
 

**How you will thrive and create an impact**

 

**Planning Excellence & Governance**

* Establish global planning standards, business rules, decision rights, and exception thresholds.
* Define planning horizons, freeze rules, and handoffs between master supply planning, site scheduling, materials planning, and regional supply planning.
* Own S&OE/S&OP process design, calendars, review standards, and escalation methods.
* Establish Plan for Every Part (PFEP) standards and review methods for finished goods, raw materials, and packaging.
* Assess planning-process adoption and effectiveness, identify gaps, and lead improvements with regional owners.
* Build planner capabilities through training, coaching, knowledge sharing, and continuous improvement.

**Analytics, Optimization & Value Improvement**

* Establish common KPIs, dashboards, and performance-analysis methods across regions.
* Lead capacity scenarios and inventory modeling to support supply, working-capital, and investment decisions.
* Develop inventory policies, safety-stock methods, and replenishment recommendations with regional teams.
* Partner with Manufacturing and regional planning teams to improve capacity utilization, campaign planning, and planning parameters.
* Identify and quantify value leakage, including excess inventory, expiry, write-offs, premium freight, and avoidable expediting.
* Develop prioritized improvement initiatives with clear business cases, accountable execution owners, and milestones.
* Track corrective actions and validate realized benefits with Finance, distinguishing recurring savings, cash release, and cost avoidance.

**Data, Systems & Digital Enablement**

* Establish master-data standards, business ownership, validation controls, and data-quality remediation processes.
* Prioritize SAP planning gaps and configuration issues and lead business resolution with IT.
* Lead the business workstream for planning system implementation and SAP integration, including requirements, data readiness, testing, and deployment readiness.
* Advance reporting and workflow automation to improve planning productivity and exception management.
* Develop AI-enabled reporting, exception insights, and commentary with appropriate validation and accountable business review.
* Lead planner training, system adoption, and post-implementation improvement.
* Maintain a technology roadmap aligned with planning needs and measurable business outcomes.

**Leadership and cross-functional alignment**

* Set a balanced CoE roadmap across the three pillars, prioritizing resources against business needs.
* Lead and develop the CoE team with clear responsibilities and performance expectations.
* Partner with regional supply chain leaders, Manufacturing, Sourcing, Quality, Finance, and IT to implement improvements.
* Communicate progress, risks, benefits, and decisions required to supply chain leadership.
 

 

**Measures of success**

 
 

**Planning excellence**

* Adoption and effectiveness of planning standards, PFEP reviews, and S&OE/S&OP processes.
* Improved planning discipline, handoffs, and planner capability.

**Analytics and improvement**

* Quality and use of analysis in business decisions.
* Inventory and capacity improvements delivered with regional teams.
* Reduction in value leakage and Finance-validated benefits.

**Data and digital enablement**

* Planning-data accuracy and closure of critical data issues.
* Delivery and adoption of SAP, Netstock, and automation improvements.
* Measurable improvements in planning productivity and decision support.
 

 

**What we're looking for**

 
 

**Required**

* Typically 10 or more years of progressive supply chain experience, including team leadership and cross-functional improvement.
* Strong knowledge of master planning, capacity planning, inventory management, PFEP, and S&OE/S&OP.
* Demonstrated experience establishing planning governance and delivering measurable operational improvements.
* Proven leadership of teams and large, complex transformation programs across multiple sites or regions.
* Strong track record leading planning-system implementations, organizational change, training, and sustained adoption.
* Deep SAP planning expertise, including master-data governance and configuration, sufficient to guide business design and challenge technical solutions.
* Strong analytical judgment, with experience directing BI reporting, dashboards, and optimization initiatives to improve business performance.
* Demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders, establish planning governance, and deliver measurable operational and financial results.

 

**Preferred**

* Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Operations, Engineering, Business, or equivalent relevant experience.
* Chemicals or batch/process manufacturing experience.
* Experience leading a global-scale CoE or planning transformation.
* SAP and Netstock or comparable planning-platform experience.
* ASCM/APICS certification, Lean Six Sigma qualification, or an advanced degree.

 

**Disclaimer:**

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by employees assigned to this classification. They are not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties and skills required of employees assigned to this position. Avantor is proud to be an equal opportunity employer.

**Why Avantor?**

**Dare to go further in your career.** Join our global team of 14,000+ associates whose passion for discovery and determination to overcome challenges relentlessly advances life-changing science.
 
 
**The work we do changes people's lives for the better.** It brings new patient treatments and therapies to market, giving a cancer survivor the chance to walk his daughter down the aisle. It enables medical devices that help a little boy hear his mom's voice for the first time. Outcomes such as these create unlimited opportunities for you to contribute your talents, learn new skills and grow your career at Avantor.
 
 
We are committed to helping you on this journey through our diverse, equitable and inclusive culture which includes learning experiences to support your career growth and success. At Avantor, dare to go further and see how the impact of your contributions set science in motion to create a better world. **Apply today!**

**Pay Transparency:**

The expected pre-tax pay for this position is

$139,500.00 - $235,175.00

Actual pay may differ depending on relevant factors such as prior experience and geographic location.

**EEO Statement:**

We are an Equal Employment/Affirmative Action employer and VEVRAA Federal Contractor. We do not discriminate in hiring on the basis of sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religious creed, national origin, physical or mental disability, protected Veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state/province, or local law.

If you need a reasonable accommodation for any part of the employment process, please contact us by email at recruiting@avantorsciences.com and let us know the nature of your request and your contact information. Requests for accommodation will be considered on a case-by-case basis. Please note that only inquiries concerning a request for reasonable accommodation will be responded to from this email address.

For more information about equal employment opportunity protections, please view the Know Your Rights poster.

**Privacy Policy:**

We will use the personal information that you have submitted to us in order to consider your application for the relevant role.

Your privacy is important to us. Please click here for our Privacy Policy which explains the purposes for which we will use your personal information and the ways in which we will handle and retain your information. It also explains the rights you have in relation to your information, and how to contact us with any queries or requests.

**3rd Party Non-Solicitation Policy:**

By submitting candidates without having been formally assigned on and contracted for a specific job requisition by Avantor, or by failing to comply with the Avantor recruitment process, you forfeit any fee on the submitted candidates, regardless of your usual terms and conditions. Avantor works with a preferred supplier list and will take the initiative to engage with recruitment agencies based on its needs and will not be accepting any form of solicitation.

Avantor offers a comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, and vision coverage, wellness programs, health savings and flexible spending accounts, a 401(k) plan with company match, and an employee stock purchase program. Employees also receive 11 paid holidays, accrue 18 PTO days annually, are eligible for volunteer time off and 6 weeks of 100% paid parental leave (except in states that offer paid family leave). These benefits may not apply to employees covered by a collective bargaining agreement or those subject to other eligibility rules.

new_roles.title: Senior Director, Manufacturing Operations
new_roles.description:
* Team:Industrial Operations & Product Supply
* Location:Saratoga Springs
* Req ID:R53229
* Contract:Full time
* Work Pattern:Onsite

**The role**
------------

**Build our future together:**

At Regeneron, we use science and innovation to develop life-changing medicines for people with serious diseases. We’re hiring a Sr. Director/ Executive Director of Manufacturing Operations for our new highly automated bulk/ drug substance manufacturing plant, supporting 20–30 tech transfers a year alongside commercial delivery responsibility. GMP production will run concurrently with construction and CQV for 3–5 years. This role requires both building and operating.

 
 

This site operates on a foundation of strategy, execution, and rigor. Every function at the site owns a pyramid of metrics derived from annual goal planning that connects the site’s strategic goals to the factory floor, with performance measured back up to leadership to monitor, track, and mitigate against contingencies quantified using SMART goals in days and dollars.

 
 

The Sr. Director/ Executive Director of Manufacturing Operations owns cross-suite production performance across upstream and downstream operations in both single-use and stainless-steel suites. As the site scales to six suites, this leader is accountable for delivery of the site production plan, manufacturing cost performance, and workforce strategy, drives daily operational discipline through MDI and lean standard work, and represents manufacturing on the site Leadership Team.

 
 

**When & where:**

* Location: Saratoga Springs, New York, United States

* Work model: Monday-Friday, 8am-4:30pm
 

 

**Discover your role:**

* Own cross-suite production performance and site-wide annual batch plan attainment across all operating suites

* Lead fully integrated, operations-focused suite teams, with upstream, downstream, and support activities managed within each suite, and clear day-to-day accountability for execution, staffing, and scheduling

* Oversee these functions OpEx and CapEx budget and roadmap

* Serve as the primary responsible party for this function's alignment with the Global Center of Excellence (COE), connecting site execution back to the business-level function

* Ensure this function's metrics flow up and down through the MDI structure, connecting into the site's S&OP, AOP, and long-range planning cycles

* Champion adoption of lean principles across manufacturing including standardized work, visual controls, and a culture of continuous improvement (kaizen) as the site scales to six suites

* Lead the production plan across all suites, working with supply chain to align the supply plan to the production schedule through the site S&OP process

* Drive the site's daily MFG MDI process at the suite level surfacing, escalating, and resolving issues in real time across all shifts

* Serve as the manufacturing process and cost owner, driving cost-per-batch performance and contributing to the site Annual Operating Plan (AOP) and budget

* Manage workforce strategy and ramp for the manufacturing organization, including multi-shift staffing, hiring, training, and qualification of operators as new suites come online

* Ensure cGMP compliance, right-first-time execution, and inspection readiness on the manufacturing floor, partnering closely with Quality on deviations and batch record performance

* Champion a zero-harm EHS culture and drive manufacturing safety performance across all shifts

* Lead manufacturing operational readiness for suites entering service, partnering with Technical Services on tech transfer, process readiness, and PPQ execution

* Build and maintain a lean, scalable manufacturing organization, including area management and round-the-clock shift coverage within each suite

new_roles.description:
Job Description
 
 
The Executive Director, Organization & Talent Partner (OTP), Manufacturing Division, reports to the Vice President, Human Resources, Manufacturing Division and serves as the senior strategic organization and talent advisor to senior leaders and their leadership teams within the Global Biologics Operating Unit and the Global Science Engineering and Commercialization organization.
 
 
Operating with a divisional as well as an enterprise mindset, the leader architects the long-term view that connects priorities and business needs into organizational capability planning solutions that help ensure these organizations have the structures, capabilities, leadership, talent pipelines and ways of working needed to deliver their priorities.
 
 
The role operates across complex scientific, pipeline, workforce, geographic and organizational priorities; co-creates strategy; frames organization and workforce choices; and establishes governance and ways of working across multiple leadership interfaces.
 
 
The Executive Director leads a team of two Organization & Talent Partners. Operating with an enterprise mindset, the role connects priorities across Manufacturing, partnering with Talent Enablement and commissioning the right expertise from Centers of Excellence (COEs), Enterprise Team HR (ETHR) and HR Solutions & Operations to bring strategy into execution. As a people leader, the role is accountable for the direction, development, performance and effective deployment of a direct and indirect team of HR professionals.
 
 
**Primary Responsibilities:** 
Shape the agenda
 
 

* Understand, anticipate and translate business strategy into the long-term organization and talent agenda​
* Lead organization capability planning so structures, roles and capabilities are ready for where the business is going​
* Drive strategic workforce planning linked to business direction and transformation
* Bring an enterprise perspective to leadership and business planning, connecting organization, workforce and talent implications across leadership teams and the broader enterprise.

Develop the organization and its leaders
 
 

* Enable talent development strategy, including succession and leadership development for critical populations​
* Coach senior leaders to improve organizational effectiveness, leadership impact and talent decisions​
* Support transformational efforts from an organization and talent perspective​
* Act as steward in organizational effectiveness, driving stronger collaboration across functions and clarity in interfaces, so priorities connect rather than compete

Leverage the HR operating model to bring strategy into execution
 
 

* Be accountable for the strategy and execution of macro-level organizational change and transformation and ensure the right partnerships are activated to deliver successful execution​.
* Engage with TELs, COEs, ETHR, HR Solutions & Operations and other partners to deliver the highest-value business priorities, leveraging expertise and capacity where they reside. Across these partnerships, provide context on business priorities and dynamics, connect organization and talent priorities across divisions and countries
* Seek to understand local nuances and considerations when defining organization and talent strategy and execution plans​

​
 
 
**Experience, capabilities and leadership characteristics:** 
The successful candidate will bring deep strategic HR experience in a large, complex organization and a record of shaping outcomes through influence. The role requires the following capabilities and leadership characteristics:
 
 

* Business savviness: bring the depth of advanced business understanding needed to build differentiated talent strategies and workforce plans leaders will trust​.
* Organization development and effectiveness: diagnose how well the organization is working and take action to close the gaps and strengthen effectiveness, using the OCP playbook and OD team resources​.
* Talent growth and senior-leader coaching: anticipate talent and capability gaps in critical populations well before they become urgent, and shape the succession and development plans that close them​.
* Influence and executive communication: effectively frame and communicate complex or sensitive issues clearly and confidently to stakeholders and partners to ensure effective action is taken, ​and align senior stakeholders without relying on formal authority.
* Change catalyst leadership: drive the organizational and cultural shifts your strategy requires, championing new approaches and helping people move through resistance to get there​.
* Networking, partnerships: effectively navigate the organization, delivering through trusted partnerships across the HR Operating Model.
* People leadership: ​Demonstrated success as a people leader, ability to build an inclusive, high-performing OTP team with clear direction and shared accountability.
* Systems Thinking: see the organization as a connected system — deep understanding of he interdependencies between businesses, functions and regions, and read data and signals across them to find the patterns that shape the org and talent agenda​.

**Education:** 

* Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business or a related discipline required

**Required Experience and Skills:** 

* Minimum of twelve (12) years of progressive HR or closely related business experience, including significant strategic HR partnership experience in a complex, global environment.
* Demonstrated experience advising and coaching senior executives and leadership teams.
* Demonstrated broad-reaching experience in strategic workforce planning, organization capability planning, organization design and development, talent and succession.
* Experience supporting a pharmaceutical, life sciences, manufacturing, or other science-based organization.
* Proven ability to influence senior leaders, manage high-risk and sensitive matters, and coordinate outcomes across organizational boundaries. Ability to commission work through a networked operating model. Broad global perspective and the ability to lead with cultural sensitivity across a matrixed, global organization
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, business judgment and analytical capability.
* Demonstrated people leadership experience, including leading, coaching and developing experienced HR professionals and building a high-performing, inclusive team.

**Required Skills:** 
Change Management, Executive Coaching, Organizational Capability, Organizational Design, Strategic Human Resources Leadership, Strategic Workforce Planning, Succession Planning
 
 
**Preferred Skills:** 
Commercialization, Manufacturing

new_roles.title: Plant Manager
new_roles.description:
**PLANT OPERATIONS CAREERS**

Plant Manager

Lead a healthcare laundry plant.

**Where** [City, ST]

**Reports to** General Manager / Regional Vice President

As Plant Manager, you'll lead the full plant (production, maintenance, quality, and logistics) with accountability for safety, budget, and the healthcare customers who depend on clean, safe linen every day.

Why you'll like it here

**Own the plant**

Daily operations, people, budget, and results.

**Lean in action**

Drive improvement with Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma.

**Lead leaders**

Develop supervisors, maintenance staff, and production Associates.

**Healthcare standards**

Run an operation held to OSHA and HLAC requirements.

What you'll own

* Lead and manage the Safety & Health Program within the production environment.
* Lead, motivate, and develop a team of supervisors, maintenance staff, and production associates.
* Oversee daily plant operations, including production scheduling, labor forecasting, staffing, and workflow optimization.
* Drive process improvements using Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma methodologies.
* Manage plant budget, including labor, maintenance, and operational expenses.
* Oversee inventory management to ensure consistent material supply and stock levels.

What you need

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, or Business Administration required.
* 5–7 years of leadership experience in a manufacturing or industrial environment.
* Strong end-to-end understanding of plant operations, including safety, quality, maintenance, and compliance.
* Proven experience managing P&L, budgeting, payroll, and cost controls.
* Strong problem-solving, analytical, and strategic thinking skills.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, PowerPoint, Word) and ERP systems.
* Excellent leadership, communication, and organizational skills.

**Physical requirements**

* Ability to stand, walk, and move throughout a manufacturing facility for extended periods.
* Ability to occasionally lift up-to fifty (50) pounds.
* Comfortable working in a plant/production environment.
* Ability to push and pull carts of linen regularly.
* Ability to use required personal protective equipment (PPE), including safety glasses, hearing protection, and work boots.

**Bonus points**

* Experience with Lean Manufacturing and/or Six Sigma methodologies preferred.
* PMP (Project Management Professional) certification.
* Willing to relocate- GOE flexibility.
* Prior military leadership experience (e.g., Sergeant or above) a plus.
* Familiarity with ISO 14001 / ISO 9001 and GMP standards.
* Experience with manufacturing systems and reporting tools

**We'll teach you:** Our plant network, operating standards, and the support of a national organization.

How we work

Every ImageFIRST Associate lives our four Core Values. These are our required competencies.

**Be Respectful**

Value all we come in contact with.

**Be Remarkable**

Create a positive moment with every interaction.

**Be Safe**

Keep ourselves and those around us safe.

**Be Honest**

Be guided by truthfulness in all we do.

Great work gets noticed

**Everyday recognition**

Coworkers nominate each other for going above and beyond, and those nominations go up in the office for everyone to see.

**All Stars & Council of Excellence**

Each year, Associates who live our values are nominated as All-Stars and earn a certificate and a cash award. Top winners join the Council of Excellence with an additional reward.

Benefits

Weekly pay

Medical, Dental, Vision

Pet, Legal, and Hospital Indemnity Insurance

401(k) with company match

Paid Time Off package

Paid Parental Leave

Tuition Reimbursement

Referral Program

Great company culture

Collaborative team environment

 

**MILITARY & VETERANS**

Served? Your skills fit here.

Officers and senior NCOs who led maintenance, logistics, or production operations: command a plant. Whether you're transitioning out, serving in the Guard or Reserve, or a veteran, we want to hear from you.

* Leading a unit leading supervisors, maintenance, and production
* Readiness and inspections safety, quality, and compliance
* Resource stewardship plant budget and cost control

Guard and Reserve members: we support your service commitments. Tell us your branch and specialty when you apply.

 

Who we are

ImageFIRST is the nation's largest medical-focused linen and laundry provider, serving health systems, hospitals, and outpatient facilities since 1967. We run more HLAC-accredited facilities than anyone else, and 97% of our customers stay with us.

Our mission: improving the lives of our associates, our customers, and the patients they serve.

**If you're ready to own a plant's results, apply today.**

 

**Equal Opportunity Employer / Drug-Free Workplace**

We maintain a drug-free workplace in compliance with state and federal law. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religion, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, age, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. new_roles.title: Plant Manager
new_roles.description:
Chalk Point Generating Station, situated in Aquasco, Maryland, is a key power generation facility with a total capacity of approximately 1,618 MW. The station features a diverse lineup of nine generating units, including seven gas turbines and two steam turbines. This strategic configuration enhances efficiency and reliability, ensuring the station effectively meets regional energy demands.

**Opportunity Summary**

As the Plant Manager at Chalk Point Generating Station, you will oversee plant operations, maintenance, engineering, safety, environmental compliance, and administration to ensure safe, reliable, and cost-effective performance. Responsibilities include leading a union-represented workforce, managing budgets and contractual obligations, maintaining regulatory compliance, and driving operational improvements. Serving as the primary liaison between NAES and the Owner, you will also coordinate with regulatory agencies and community stakeholders to support facility objectives and maintain positive relationships.

***Your scope of responsibility as Plant Manager includes the following primary functions:***

* Direct plant operations, maintenance, safety, administrative, training, chemistry, NERC compliance, and environmental programs to ensure safe, efficient, and reliable performance while meeting operational targets.
* Oversee planned and forced outages, long-term maintenance planning, and asset reliability initiatives, optimizing schedules, resources, and contractor activities to minimize downtime and costs.
* Administer O&M, energy supply, service, and interconnection agreements while overseeing vendor performance and ensuring contractual compliance.
* Establish staffing, training, and qualification programs that support operational requirements, employee development, and facility objectives.
* Promote a strong safety culture through hazard identification, safe work practices, emergency preparedness, employee accountability, and adherence to established safety standards.
* Ensure environmental and regulatory compliance, including permits, landowner agreements, Management of Change (MOC) processes, and timely submission of required reports.
* Manage plant expenditures, operating and capital budgets, forecasting, procurement, and cost controls to achieve financial objectives and meet O&M Agreement requirements.
* Serve as the primary liaison with the Owner, regulatory agencies, and community stakeholders, maintaining positive relationships and supporting community engagement.
* Monitor plant performance, reliability, and operating KPIs while supporting equipment troubleshooting, root cause analysis, and corrective actions to improve operational efficiency.
* Lead union-represented and management personnel through performance management, collective bargaining agreement administration, labor relations, and continuous improvement initiatives that enhance operational and workforce effectiveness.
* Maintain reliable attendance and availability to support facility operations and management responsibilities.

* Carry out and complete additional special projects and tasks as needed.

**NAES Safe**

Safety is a core value at NAES, and as a condition of employment, all employees are expected to remain mentally alert and work safely at all times. All NAES managers and supervisors have a direct and important role in ensuring that all work is performed in a healthy and safe manner. Effectiveness in carrying out this responsibility is part of the evaluation of each Supervisor’s performance.

**Working Relationships**

The Plant Manager reports to the Operations Director and supervises the managers, technicians, and Plant Administrator. The Plant Manager is the single point of contact between NAES and the Owner on all matters pertaining to the operation, maintenance, and commercial management of the plant.

**Physical Requirements and Working Conditions**

Physical requirements include standing for extended periods of time, climbing stairs and ladders, working from elevated platforms and walkways at varying heights, and routinely lifting up to 50 pounds.

Power plant environment that may involve entering confined spaces, crawling through narrow areas, and handling hazardous materials, with exposure to fumes, extreme temperatures, and noise. Work may include high heat near equipment and varying outdoor weather conditions.

Some duties may require the use of protective equipment, which can include hard hats, safety glasses, and eye protection, air masks/respirators, ear protection, chemical suits, flame-resistant clothing (FRC), hot gloves, high-voltage protective gear, and fall protection. Fit testing for respirators may be required. Strict smoking restrictions apply in and around the facility.

**Fitness for Duty**

All employees will participate in the Fitness for Duty Program. This program includes a post-offer physical examination and drug screening and post-employment random drug screening.

**Work Schedule**

The Plant Manager works a standard Monday to Friday day-shift schedule. This position will require extended hours, flexible shifts, weekends, and holidays as needed to support plant operations and business needs and may also require callout availability. Depending on the position, on-call status may or may not apply.

Some travel may be involved to participate in Manager, Owner, User Group, or other offsite meetings.

**Compensation**

This position offers an annual base salary ranging from $214,000 to $250,000 and includes eligibility for an annual performance bonus.

**Professional Experience and Leadership Competencies**

* A Bachelor of Science degree in engineering or equivalent is desired, providing a strong foundation for understanding the technical aspects of power plant operations and management.

* Previous Plant Manager experience at a gas- or oil-fired power generation facility, or comparable leadership experience overseeing similar industrial operations, is preferred.
* Proven experience supervising technical, supervisory, and union-represented personnel, including collective bargaining agreement administration, grievance resolution, and labor relations.
* Extensive knowledge of power generation operations, independent power producer business practices, commercial agreements, and contractual requirements.
* Demonstrated proficiency in environmental and regulatory compliance, including applicable NERC requirements, operating and capital budgets, financial controls, and contract administration.
* Strong technical understanding of gas and steam turbine operations, outage management, equipment reliability, root cause analysis, and long-term maintenance planning.
* Effective leadership, communication, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to engage employees, senior management, Owners, regulatory agencies, and external stakeholders.
* Results-oriented approach to problem-solving, workforce development, emergency preparedness, change management, and continuous improvement across operational and financial functions.
* Must possess a valid, unrestricted U.S. driver’s license and ensure it remains in good standing at all times.

**About NAES**

NAES Corporation is a leading provider of operations, maintenance, and engineering services for energy facilities. We serve clients across the power generation, oil and gas, and renewable energy sectors throughout North America and internationally, supporting the full life cycle of power generation and other industrial facilities.

NAES is committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace. Employment decisions are based on merit and qualifications, without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, disability, military status, USERRA-protected status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

#### **Experience**

Preferred

* A Bachelor of Science degree in engineering or equivalent is desired, providing a strong foundation for understanding the technical aspects of power plant operations and management.
* Previous Plant Manager experience at a gas- or oil-fired power generation facility, or comparable leadership experience overseeing similar industrial operations, is preferred.
* Proven experience supervising technical, supervisory, and union-represented personnel, including collective bargaining agreement administration, grievance resolution, and labor relations.
* Extensive knowledge of power generation operations, independent power producer business practices, commercial agreements, and contractual requirements.
* Demonstrated proficiency in environmental and regulatory compliance, including applicable NERC requirements, operating and capital budgets, financial controls, and contract administration.
* Strong technical understanding of gas and steam turbine operations, outage management, equipment reliability, root cause analysis, and long-term maintenance planning.
* Effective leadership, communication, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to engage employees, senior management, Owners, regulatory agencies, and external stakeholders.
* Results-oriented approach to problem-solving, workforce development, emergency preparedness, change management, and continuous improvement across operational and financial functions.

#### **Education**

Preferred

* Bachelors or better in Engineering or related field

#### **Licenses & Certifications**

Required

* Driver's License

Preferred

* TWIC Trans Wrkr ID

#### **Skills**

Preferred

* Power Generation
* Budgeting
* Leadership
* Safety Policies and Procedures Management
* Gas Turbine O&M
* Team Leadership
* Combined Cycle
* Operations Management
* Maintenance Management
* Performance Optimization
* Outage Management
* NERC Reliability Standards Compliance
* Environmental Compliance and Reporting
* Contract Management
* MOC - Management of Change

* Vendor Management
* Cost Control

new_roles.title: Director of Operations
new_roles.description:
At Curaleaf, we're redefining the cannabis industry with a strong commitment to quality, expertise, and innovation. As a leading global cannabis provider, our brands—including Curaleaf, Select, and Grassroots—offer premium products and services in both medical and adult-use markets.

Join us at Curaleaf to be part of a high-growth, purpose-driven company that champions corporate social responsibility through our *Rooted in Good* initiative, supporting community outreach and positive change. Here, you'll have the opportunity to make a meaningful impact, drive innovation, and help shape the future of cannabis.

 

**Title:** Director of Operations 
**Location:** Webster, MA 
**Job Type:** Full Time | Exempt

**Who You Are:**

You're a strategic, hands-on operations leader who knows how to run complex, multi-site supply-side operations from end to end. You bring structure, accountability, and calm to fast-moving environments, with a deep understanding of what it takes to make and deliver at scale—safely, compliantly, and efficiently.

You have a proven ability to lead and coach field operations teams across cultivation, processing, manufacturing, logistics, supply chain, and facilities, while balancing day-to-day execution with long-term operational strategy. You're comfortable owning results and making decisions that directly impact revenue, cost, quality, and team performance.

You partner naturally across the business, working closely with Retail, Wholesale, Marketing, Finance, People & Culture, and Compliance to align priorities and execute against shared goals. You're detail-driven but not rigid, data-informed but people-first, and you continuously look for smarter, more efficient ways to operate.

Above all, you set the standard. You lead with safety, compliance, and quality at the forefront, drive continuous improvement, and build high-performing teams that deliver results while maintaining strong engagement and morale.

**What You'll Do:**

As a Director of Operations, you will lead and oversee all supply-side operations across cultivation, manufacturing, logistics, and facilities, ensuring safe, compliant, and efficient execution of the end-to-end make and deliver process while driving performance, quality, and profitability.

* Lead all day-to-day cultivation, manufacturing, and supply-side operations, planning and monitoring execution to ensure uninterrupted, efficient production
* Lead, develop, and coach site operations leadership teams, setting clear priorities, cascading goals, and driving accountability across all Make and Deliver functions
* Own metrics-based OKRs and drive operational excellence through continuous improvement, including Lean Six Sigma initiatives
* Maintain a strong field presence to support leaders and teams while fostering safe, compliant, and brand-appropriate manufacturing environments
* Oversee production planning, scheduling, logistics, and inventory flow from raw materials through finished goods
* Partner with Commercial, Retail, and Wholesale teams to translate demand, growth, and trends into accurate manufacturing forecasts and execution plans
* Collaborate with regional and national shared services to commercialize new products in the local market
* Ensure controlled substance inventory accuracy, variance resolution, SOX compliance, and adherence to all local, state, and national SOPs
* Maintain quality, safety, and compliance standards to reduce NOEs and non-conformances and ensure cost-effective operations in a GAP and cGMP environment
* Lead training, development, and recurring compliance initiatives across field operations
* Manage vendor and contractor relationships, bills of materials, standard costing, and ERP-related operational processes
* Lead capital improvement projects and oversee commissioning and maintenance of capital equipment
* Own site P&L, OPEX, labor standards, and org structures to control costs, reduce COGS, and improve operating margins

**What You'll Bring:**

* 10+ years of experience in manufacturing and logistics, with leadership experience in FDA-regulated, SQF, or cGMP production environments
* Experience supervising 25+ associates, with a proven ability to build, develop, and retain high-performing teams
* A hands-on, visible leadership style that earns credibility quickly and inspires trust across all levels of the organization
* A demonstrated track record of driving operational efficiencies, improving performance, and leading teams through change
* Strong people leadership, organizational, and collaboration skills, with the ability to build consensus through open dialogue
* The ability to work proactively and independently, bringing innovation, urgency, and ownership to both strategic and tactical goals
* Exceptional communication and negotiation skills, both internally and externally
* High School diploma required

**Even Better If:**

* Bachelor's degree in Business, Supply Chain, or a related field
* Experience in the cannabis industry
* Working knowledge of Lean manufacturing or Six Sigma principles, with practical application experience
* Start-up or high-growth environment experience

**What We Offer:**

* Career Growth Opportunities
* Competitive Pay and Benefits
* Generous PTO and Parental Leave
* 401(K) Retirement Plan
* Life/ Disability Insurance
* Community Involvement
* Referral Bonuses and Product Discounts

*Benefits vary by state, role type, and eligibility.*

**Follow us on Social Media:** 
Instagram: @curaleaf.usa 
Twitter: @Curaleaf\_Inc 
LinkedIn: Curaleaf LinkedIn

Curaleaf Holdings, Inc. (TSX: CURA) (OTCQX: CURLF) ("Curaleaf") is a leading international provider of consumer products in cannabis with a mission to enhance lives by cultivating, sharing, and celebrating the power of the plant. As a high-growth cannabis company known for quality, expertise and reliability, the Company, and its brands, including Curaleaf, Select, Grassroots, Find, and Anthem provide industry-leading service, product selection and accessibility across the medical and adult-use markets. Curaleaf International is powered by a strong presence in all stages of the supply chain. Its unique distribution network throughout Europe, Canada and Australasia brings together pioneering science and research with cutting-edge cultivation, extraction and production. Home | Curaleaf | Cannabis with Confidence

**Our Vision:** To be the world's leading cannabis company by consistently delivering superior products and services and driving the global acceptance of cannabis.

**Our Values:**

* Lead and Inspire.
* Commit to Win.
* ONE Curaleaf.
* Driven to Deliver Excellence.

Curaleaf is an equal opportunity employer. Curaleaf recruits, employs, trains, compensates, and promotes regardless of race, religion, color, national origin, gender identity, sexual orientation, physical ability, age, veteran status, and other protected status as required by applicable law.

We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodation.

Individuals adversely impacted by the war on drugs are encouraged to apply.

*Current Curaleaf employees should apply for open positions through our Internal Job Board, which can be accessed via the link on The Leaf.*

**\*\*\*Please note that U.S. immigration rules and regulations are governed by federal law; not state law. Although Curaleaf operates in states that have legalized and decriminalized marijuana, it is still considered a controlled substance under federal regulations and thus illegal under federal law. For this reason, unless and until federal law changes, Curaleaf is prohibited from offering sponsorship for any non-immigrant or immigrant visas.**

**\*\*\*Please also note that while candidates who are Lawful Permanent Residents (such as those with Green Cards) are eligible for employment with, and are hired by Curaleaf, working for a company engaged in a business that grows and sells a product that is illegal under federal law might compromise the candidate's immigration status. Before a Lawful Permanent Resident accepts an offer of employment, Curaleaf recommends that the candidate seek the advice of an immigration lawyer.**
