new_roles.description:
**Job Details:**

At Tyson Foods, we believe that our team members are the heart of our success. Are you ready to take on a dynamic role where you can make a significant impact? Join Our Team in the Prepared Foods Division as a Plant Manager I!

 

**Setting the table for your success** :

At Tyson Foods, our team members’ health and wellness is very important to us. We believe in helping our team members thrive inside and outside of the workplace. That’s why we’re committed to providing a holistic benefits package that provides support for you and your family.

 

We invest in our team members and their success by providing resources like **BENEFITS ON DAY ONE OF EMPLOYMENT and FREE EDUCATION!**

 

Benefits include medical/Rx, dental, and vision coverage; 9 paid holidays; [4] weeks paid vacation upon hire, plus earned time off; 401(k) with employer match; stock purchase program; and product purchase program. We also offer **CAREER GROWTH** and much more!

 

Summary: This facility is part of our Prepared Foods business unit and manufactures cooked Philly Steak. Looking for a leader to fill the Plant Manager role for this well-established facility through significant changes to the overall business.

 

**RESPONSIBILITIES** :

* Leadership & Safety
* Be a safety leader at the plant, establishing and directing plant policies and procedures.
* Maintain a clean and safe working environment, ensuring compliance with all federal, state, and company regulations.
* Establish and foster a team environment, promoting a positive culture.
* Operations & Production Management
* Direct and coordinate all plant operations and maintenance, adhering to company policies and procedures.
* Oversee and achieve plant production goals.
* Establish production schedules across all shifts to meet demand.
* Quality & Customer Relations
* Ensure product quality standards are met and maintained.
* Work directly with customers and suppliers to meet expectations and support operational needs.
* Staffing & Development
* Select, train, and manage plant supervisory and operations staff.
* Conduct employee performance reviews and support career development.
* Schedule and lead regular plant meetings to support communication and planning.
* Cross-Departmental Coordination
* Collaborate with department heads to coordinate safety, purchasing, production, quality, HR, accounting, and shipping.
* Community & Corporate Engagement
* Establish and maintain positive relationships within the community.
* Attend scheduled corporate training and meetings.
Other Duties: Perform other duties as assigned. 

 

**REQUIREMENTS:**

* Education: Associate or bachelor’s degree required.
* Experience: At least four years of plant management experience required to include progressive levels of responsibility. Direction of plant operations and supply chain knowledge helpful. Lean experience is preferred. Capital project management experience is preferred.
* Computer Skills: Good computer skills including Microsoft Office Suite.
* Communication Skills: Good verbal and written skills. Bilingual is preferred.
* Supervisory: Yes.
* Travel: 3 - 6 trips per year domestic and possible international trips.

All professional team members are expected to demonstrate responsible use of approved AI tools, including safeguarding sensitive information, adhering to company policies, and validating AI-generated outputs. Individual Contributors should demonstrate the ability to integrate AI into daily work, improve efficiency through AI-enabled solutions, evaluate outputs critically, and apply professional judgment when using AI. People Leaders should demonstrate the ability to drive responsible AI adoption, enable effective use of approved solutions, identify opportunities to improve team performance through AI, and ensure accountability for the quality and accuracy of AI-supported outcomes.

**Relocation Assistance Eligible:**

Yes

**Work Shift:**

1ST SHIFT (United States of America)

**Pay Range/Rate:**

$129,000.00 - $215,000.00

**Incentives:**

Annual Incentive Plan:

Yes

Long-Term Incentive Plan:

No

Any listed amounts represent the base pay range. Additional compensation may be available for this position based on various factors such as shift differentials, standby/on-call, overtime, premiums, extra shift incentives, or bonuses. Pay is just one part of Tyson’s total compensation package.

 
 

***Tyson will develop an offer based on a candidate's or team member’s relevant skills and capabilities, the market data for the role described in this requisition, internal equity, and other information relevant to the candidate and role.***

 

Hourly Applicants ONLY -You must complete the task after submitting your application to provide additional information to be considered for employment.

 
 

The successful candidate(s) must be willing and able to perform the physical requirements of the job with or without a reasonable accommodation.

 
 

Tyson is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will be considered without regard to race, national origin, color, religion, age, genetics, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability or veteran status.

new_roles.description:
Primo Brands is a leading branded beverage company in North America with a focus on healthy hydration. We are proud to offer an extensive and iconic portfolio of highly recognizable, sustainably sourced, and conveniently packaged branded beverages distributed across more than 150,000 retail outlets.

We are seeking a **Plant Manager**. Choose a career in Technical and Production and you'll be part of our Product Supply backbone and a crucial element of our success. Our factories are where our products start their journey to the customer. This area of Primo Brands offers you the chance to experience collaboration in its purest form as you work alongside a diverse range of highly motivated and passionate people in our factories spread across the nation. What you do will be fulfilling, impactful and meaningful - not least is you'll be helping to deliver healthy hydration to millions of thirsty customers. We'll make sure you have the strong leadership and clear direction you need to feel motivated and passionate about accomplishing great things. While you take pride in delivering an excellent performance, you'll see your contributions are recognized and rewarded with an outstanding level of support, training and benefits everything you need to grow and thrive in your career.

**Factory Location:** Lorton, VA 
**Compensation:** $144,380.40 - $176,284.80. This position is eligible for an annual bonus.

**Shift:**

**Health Benefits:** Medical, prescription, dental, vision, flexible spending account (FSA), dependent care flexible spending account (FSA), health savings account (HSA).

**Retirement/Investing:** 401K with a 5% match, Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP).

**Insurance:** Employee Life Insurance, short and long-term disability, critical illness, hospital indemnity, accident insurance, spouse/domestic partner/child life insurance, accidental death and dismemberment.

**Other great benefits:** Employee discounts, save on auto, home, and pet insurance, tuition reimbursement, paid vacation and sick time, 9 paid holidays and 3 paid floating holidays, paid leave for when you have a baby, adopt a child, or become a foster parent, legal services, identity theft protection, employee assistance program (EAP), adoption reimbursement benefit, FEDlogic, commuter benefits.

 

* Overall responsibility for total facility performance and metrics for this bottling and distribution facility.
* Spending time on the floor engaging with employees and overseeing plant operations.
* Responsible for P&L and customer satisfaction performance for the facility.
* Creating and maintaining a cohesive team of leaders and providing coaching and development.
* Serving as factory champion for national safety and quality programs and initiatives.
* Creating and maintaining a positive work environment for all employees.
* Leading and facilitating Primo Brands Continuous Excellence (BCE) and an upcoming Total Performance Management (TPM) implementation.
* Building effective relationships with other plant leaders and corporate team members.
* Ensuring compliance of operations with company policy and all Federal, State and local regulations.

 

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain or related field; Masters a plus.
* 10+ years of relevant experience in manufacturing, including career progression and cross functional assignments and 5 or more years. serving as a department manager to a team of leaders and employees.
* Consumer products goods industry experience required, prior food or beverage preferred.
* Technical knowledge of manufacturing operations, warehousing, and distribution.
* Experience with Manufacturing Excellence.
* In-depth understanding of production support functions including budgeting, planning, safety, quality and human resources.
* Strong computer skills, including experience with Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint and ERP systems such as SAP.
* Ability to inspire passion and commitment and lead and facilitate operational and cultural change initiatives.
* Demonstrated track record at building a cohesive team and creating a positive work environment.
* Prior experience leading, coaching and developing a team and delivering performance metrics through others.
* Continuous improvement experience, specifically Six Sigma, Lean or TPM.
* Exceptional communication, relationship building and formal presentation skills.
* Demonstrates and models a high degree of honesty, integrity and personal character.

**If you're ready to embark on an exciting journey with Primo Brands, apply now!**

**Salary Range Disclaimer:** 
The salary range provided for this position is an approximation based on market research, internal compensation data and the candidate’s qualifications and experience. Final salary offers are determined through a comprehensive evaluation of candidate qualifications and may vary depending on factors such as skills, experience, and geographic location of the position. Other components of the compensation package, including benefits and bonuses, will also be considered. We are committed to fair and equitable compensation practices, and we encourage open dialogue about compensation during the interview process.

Primo Brands’ established portfolio includes billion-dollar brands Poland Spring® and Pure Life®, premium brands like Saratoga® and Mountain Valley®, regional leaders such as Arrowhead®, Deer Park®, Ice Mountain® Ozarka®, and Zephyrhills®, purified brands, Primo Water® and Sparkletts®, and flavored and enhanced brands like Splash® and AC+ION®. Our extensive direct-to-consumer offerings and industry-leading line-up of innovative water dispensers create consumer connectivity through recurring water purchases across Water Direct, Water Exchange, and Water Refill.

At Primo Brands, our more than 11,000 associates are at the heart of what we do and deliver on our mission to provide healthy hydration to consumers wherever, however and whenever they want it. We believe in fostering a respectful culture, which values our associates who are deeply invested in quality hydration, our communities, and the sustainability of our packaging and water sources for generations to come.

Primo Brands is proud to be an Equal Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer, seeking to create a welcoming and diverse environment. We do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, transgender status, sexual stereotypes, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. We also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state, and local law.

Candidates must possess strong English language skills to effectively communicate with customers and provide exceptional service. Proficiency in English is essential for understanding customer needs, resolving inquiries, and collaborating with team members.

Overview:

**WHO WE ARE**

As the largest private-sector power producer in the world and the nation's largest producer of clean and reliable energy, Constellation is focused on our purpose: lighting the way to a brilliant tomorrow for all. We have been the leader in clean energy production for more than a decade, and we are cultivating a workplace where our employees can grow, thrive, and contribute. Now integrated with Calpine, our portfolio includes 55 gigawatts of capacity from nuclear, natural gas, geothermal, hydro, wind and solar facilities, with the generating capacity to power the equivalent of 27 million homes. 
 
Our culture and employee experience make it clear: We are powered by passion and purpose. Together, we're creating healthier communities and a cleaner planet, and our people are the driving force behind our success. At Constellation, you can build a fulfilling career with opportunities to learn, grow and make an impact. By doing our best work and meeting new challenges, we can accomplish great things. Join us in meeting the country's energy needs today and tomorrow.

**TOTAL REWARDS**

Constellation offers an extensive selection of benefits and rewards to help our employees thrive professionally and personally. We provide competitive compensation and a wide-range of benefits that support both employees and their families, helping them prepare for the future. In addition to highly competitive salaries, eligible employees are offered a bonus program, 401(k) with company match, employee stock purchase program; comprehensive medical, dental and vision benefits, including robust wellbeing programs; disability and life insurance benefits; paid time off for vacation, holidays, and sick days; and much more.

Expected salary range of $189,000 to $210,000, varies based on experience, along with comprehensive benefits package that includes bonus and 401(k).

Responsibilities:

**PRIMARY PURPOSE OF POSITION**

Manage and oversee the safe, efficient and reliable operation of fossil or hydro station(s). Ensure compliance with all federal, state and local regulatory requirements, applicable industry technical standards and company policies. Operate the plant(s) in a manner that minimizes the cost of generation and maximizes profitability while maintaining the long-term viability of the station assets.

 

**PRIMARY DUTIES AND ACCOUNTABILITIES**

* Ensure standards are established and implemented to provide a safe work environment.
* Effectively manage all resources to ensure generation of electricity in a timely and reliable manner at the direction of the Power Team.
* Maintain a positive work environment and good employee relations. Provide guidance for employee development opportunities and timely feedback regarding performance.
* Serve as a change agent for business initiatives, while assuring the human element is understood and considered
* Manage the station O&M and capital budgets to minimize costs and maximize profitability while ensuring the long-term viability of the assets.
* Ensure compliance with all federal, state and local regulatory requirements and maintain environmental stewardship.
* Maintain effective community relations to promote a positive image of the Company.
* Perform all other duties as assigned.

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

* BS in engineering or business
* Minimum of 10 years professional experience
* Minimum of 8 years power plant (or related) experience
* Minimum of 5 years supervisory/managerial experience
* Professional or technical level experience in a technical role at a power plant
* Operations
* At least 2 of the following: Corporate/Staff, Engineering, Maintenance, or Outage
* RHR Selection

Qualifications:

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**

* Master's Degree in engineering, business or related field
* Multi-site experience
* Multi-departmental experience
* Collective bargaining experience

new_roles.description:
**Company Description**

At **Link Snacks**, we show up hungry, roll up our sleeves, plaid or otherwise, and dive straight into the hard work. We don’t hide from challenges; we hunt them down. We push harder, move faster, and take the kinds of big swings that built this business in the North Woods of Wisconsin four decades ago.

We’re everyday people who deliver extraordinary results. Innovation, creativity, and urgency aren’t buzzwords, they’re expectations. And just like the real protein snacks we make across our global house of brands—Jack Link’s®*,* Lorissa’s Kitchen®*,* Golden Island®*,* BiFi®*, and* Peperami® *and* KOOEE!® to name a few—there’s nothing artificial about us. What you see is exactly what you get: humble, gritty, passionate people who show up every day ready to not just be a participate in the meat snack industry that the Link Family created, but to move faster, innovate harder and keep raising the bar so high, the rest of the world needs a ladder just to see it.

Dominating this space across the world takes a team. A team that runs together, succeeds together, and celebrates together. A team that’s full of relentless energy and spirit that can only be fueled by one thing: a fist full of our delicious meat snacks.

Real Meat Protein. Real People. Real Results. THAT is Link Snacks.

 **Job Description**

The Plant Manager directs overall plant operations and the retail store ensuring the achievement of production objectives at the lowest cost consistent with the company quality standards and customer delivery requirements.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

This list of duties and responsibilities is not all-inclusive and may be expanded to include other duties and responsibilities, as management may deem necessary from time to time.

1. Prioritize, schedule and delegate work assignments and directly supervise the plant staff to ensure the achievement of production objectives at the lowest cost consistent with company quality requirements.

2. Monitor suppliers to ensure that they efficiently and effectively provide needed goods or services within budgetary limits.

3. Direct or coordinate financial or budget activities to fund operations, maximize investments, or increase efficiency.

4. Evaluate, recommend, and implement improvements in methods and processes to increase productivity and quality.

5. Develop plans for the maximum utilization of materials, machines and employees.

6. Review production costs and product quality; modify production and inventory control programs to maintain and enhance profitable operation of division.

7. Ensure proper maintenance of equipment and building and establish plant housekeeping standards.

8. Develop and recommend plant capital and operating budgets to ensure conformance to budgets.

9. Develop policies and procedures to ensure compliance with OSHA, environmental and various regulatory agencies.

10. Enforce safety and work rules and company housekeeping standards.

11. Recommend locations for new facilities or oversee the remodeling or renovating of current facilities.

12. Ensure compliance with all quality, SQF, HACCP, safety, and sanitation regulations.

Supervisory Responsibilities

Manage supervisors who supervise employees in the manufacturing of company products. Is responsible for the overall direction, coordination, and evaluation of this unit. Carry out supervisory responsibilities in accordance with the organization's policies and applicable laws. Responsibilities include planning, assigning, and directing work; appraising performance; rewarding and disciplining employees; addressing complaints and resolving problems.

 **Qualifications**

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Education and/or Experience

Requires a bachelor's degree in production and operations management from a four-year college or university plus a minimum of five years progressively responsible related experience; or ten years progressively responsible related experience; or a combination of education and experience. Requires the ability to operate a computer and

standard office machines. Requires a general knowledge of company products and procedures. Requires a working knowledge of accounting methods and cost control procedures.

Language Skills

Ability to read, analyze, and interpret blueprints, customer specifications, general business periodicals, technical procedures, or governmental regulations. Ability to write reports and business correspondence. Ability to effectively present information and respond to questions from managers, customers, and other employees of the organization.

Mathematical Skills

Ability to work with mathematical concepts such as probability and statistical inference. Ability to apply concepts such as algebraic formulas, fractions, percentages, ratios, and proportions to practical situations.

Reasoning Ability

Ability to define problems, collect data, establish facts, and draw valid conclusions. Ability to interpret an extensive variety of technical instructions in mathematical or diagram form and deal with several abstract and concrete variables.

Physical Demands

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Wear required safety equipment when on shop floor. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to talk or hear. The employee frequently is required to stand. The employee is occasionally required to walk; sit; and use hands to finger, handle, or touch objects, tools, or controls. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision.

Work Environment

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is occasionally exposed to fumes or airborne particles. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate to loud.

 **Additional Information**

*The hiring range for this role is $135,000 - $145,000 yearly**. Actual wages will vary based on several factors, including but not limited to external market data, internal equity, location, and candidate skill set and experience. Base pay is just one component of Jack Link’s Total Rewards package for Team Members. Other rewards may include annual incentive and program-specific awards. Jack Link’s provides a variety of benefits to eligible Team Members, including medical, dental and vision benefits, life and disability insurance, 401k participation, paid holidays, and paid time off.*

**PHYSICAL DEMANDS**: 
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to be successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this job the employee is regularly required to stand, walk, use hands to finger, handle, or feel, lift and/or move up to 25 pounds, and talk or hear. The employee is occasionally required to sit, and reach with hands and arms. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision.

**WORK ENVIRONMENT**: 
The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. The work environment is a plant / office setting with varying degrees of temperatures and noise levels. Exposure to manufacturing equipment movement and wet / slippery floors. Travel may be required.

**EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER:** 
Jack Link’s provides equal employment opportunity (EEO) to all persons regardless of age, color, national origin, citizenship status, physical or mental disability, race, religion, creed, gender, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity and/or expression, genetic information, marital status, status with regard to public assistance, veteran status, or any other characteristic that is protected by federal, state or local law.

**E-VERIFY:** 
Jack Link’s is participant in the federal E-Verify program to confirm the identity and employment authorization of all newly hired employees. For information about the E-Verify program, please visit: http://www.uscis.gov/e-verify/employees

new_roles.description:
Cenveo is a leading North American manufacturer of envelopes with over 100 years of experience and approximately 30 billion envelopes manufactured annually. We are committed to safety, quality, and operational excellence.

We are hiring immediately for an experienced Plant Manager for its envelope manufacturing facility in Chicago, IL. The position will report into the Site-Leader/General Manager.

Headquartered in Stamford, Connecticut, Cenveo provides competitive pay and a comprehensive benefits package.

**Job Summary**

The Plant Manager directs the manufacturing, maintenance, warehousing and distribution operations of a facility to achieve business goals including safety, quality, and production (including efficiency and profitability). They ensure compliance with all government regulations and corporate policies. Additionally, the Plant Manager serves as a liaison between the manufacturing facility and its clients, the Sales department, and other groups.

**Key Responsibilities** (\*Essential Functions)

*These are functions a qualified incumbent or applicant must be able to perform with or without reasonable accommodation.*

* Through direct action and the management of others, ensure the safe, productive, and profitable daily operations of an envelope manufacturing facility.
* Effectively use financial, & other, reports to monitor and improve facility performance on a variety of business related metrics. Prepare similar reports as required.
* Select, train, and develop subordinates necessary to conduct facility operations.
* Direct the plant supervision team in the enforcement and consistent application of policies, and plant rules which may include the terms of a collective bargaining agreement.
* Monitor, train and communicate safety and quality programs and ensure compliance with company policies and government regulations.
* Ensure the efficient and effective purchasing and utilization of all materials and services.
* Collaborate with sales to improve or modify existing products as needed, and to aid in new product development.
* Visit customer facilities, or host customer visits to the Cenveo facility to aid in sales, customer relations, or the resolution of problem situations.
* Monitor new trends and developments in business and manufacturing.
* Represent the company and facility in community relations functions.
* Performs other duties as assigned.
* Perform other duties as assigned based on business needs.

**Pay / Other**

* Salaried Pay Range: $120,000 – 140,000 annually
* Schedule: Monday – Friday; Saturdays required during peak production/business needs.

**Other (Non-Essential) Functions**

Includes functions which are normally performed by persons holding this title. However, these functions may be reassigned to other employees as part of a "Reasonable Accommodation" under the ADA.

* Other duties and assignments as required.

**Job Requirements**

* Bachelor's degree preferred. Will consider experience in lieu of Bachelor's degree, emphasis on Manufacturing, Industrial Management, or similar preferred.
* Comprehensive experience in manufacturing, along with advanced knowledge in multiple related disciplines and processes is required.
* Experience in envelope, printing or packaging is highly preferred.
* Extensive experience Environmental, Health, & Safety.
* Six Sigma / Lean Manufacturing experience preferred.
* Managing teams or projects is preferred.
* Strong PC skills including Microsoft Office and internet research
* Strong interpersonal verbal and written communication
* Ability to work independently and with others, demonstrate analytical abilities, and be a strong and versatile leader.
* Must be a self-starter and thrive in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment.
* Ability to perform work, and resolve problems, that are complex and varied in nature.

**Physical Requirements & Environmental Conditions**

* Requires the ability to move throughout a manufacturing facility on a regular basis, including frequent walking of the production floor, climbing stairs, and navigating operational areas.
* Frequent exposure to manufacturing environment with one or more unpleasant or hazardous conditions including but not limited to dust, dirt, high noise levels, chemicals, etc.
* Ability to communicate effectively, hear, distinguish colors
* May occasionally reach, bend, grasp, carry, and lift and/or move objects weighing up to 50 pounds; manual dexterity as needed to perform job duties.
* Occasional travel may be required based on business needs.

**Employee Benefits**

* Comprehensive Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance
* 401(k) Retirement Plan
* Paid Holidays
* Vacation / Paid Sick Leave
* Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
* Employee Referral Bonus Program
* Other Company Sponsored Benefits

**CENVEO IS AN EEO EMPLOYER**

Requirements:

* The minimum education requirement is some college coursework or Associate's degree. Bachelor's degree is highly preferred.
* Typically possesses 10 years of related work experience, with at least 5 years' experience in managing teams or projects. Requires advanced technical and business knowledge in multiple disciplines and processes.
* Extensive experience Environmental, Health, & Safety experience.
* Comprehensive experience in manufacturing is required. Experience in envelope, printing or packaging is highly preferred.
* Experience in Six Sigma or Lean Manufacturing is preferred, but not required.
* Strong PC skills including Microsoft Office, Internet and Hagen.
* Excellent written/verbal communication skills.
* Excellent organizational skills.
* Must be able to work well with individuals at all levels within the organization.
* Must be a self-starter and must be able to thrive in a fast-paced, deadline driven environment.
* Proven ability to perform work that is complex and varied in nature. Defines and discerns key aspects of problem and develops an integrated solution within a broad technical and business context of significant impact. May provide guidance/training to more junior staff.
* This position requires contact with employees, management, sales, account teams, call center, production staff, customer and vendors.

new_roles.description:
**About the role:**
-------------------

As Plant Manager for Eaton’s Critical Power Solutions operations in Santa Ana, California, you’ll lead two facilities, 500+ employees, and approximately $280M in annual sales, delivering engineered-to-order critical power solutions for some of the world’s fastest-growing customers.

This is a **high-visibility business and operations leadership role** with the opportunity to make a significant impact. You’ll co-own the P&L, lead the full plant organization, and help scale the operation as demand continues to grow.

**We’re looking for a leader who can:**

* Build and develop high-performing, cross-functional teams.

new_roles.title: Director, NPI Program Management & Manufacturing Launch
new_roles.description:
If you’re looking for a special place to build or grow your career, you’ve found it. Whether you’re an experienced professional, a recent college graduate or somewhere in between, IDEX is a place where you can apply your existing skills and learn new ones in an environment where you can make an impact.

With interesting opportunities in engineering, marketing, sales, supply chain, operations, HR, finance, and more across more than 40 diverse businesses around the globe, chances are, we have something special for you.

**LOCATION:** Remote with Travel

US Valve is growing rapidly, driven by critical customer demand in data center and other high-growth markets, creating increasingly complex new product development programs with multiple manufacturing paths. The Director, NPI Program Management & Manufacturing Launch will build and lead the function responsible for taking these programs from business case through stable production, whether manufactured at US Valve, at sister IDEX business units, through external supply chain partners, or through a hybrid model. The role ensures that product design, manufacturing processes, suppliers, supply chain, quality systems, and commercial launch mature together against one integrated plan.

This leader is the single point of accountability for integrated NPI execution and owns end-to-end program results, including schedule, budget, quality, supplier readiness, manufacturing readiness, launch readiness, and ramp performance. The role organizes Product Management, Engineering, Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, Sourcing, Sales, Finance, BU partners, and external suppliers under one plan. The Director ensures APQP and launch deliverables, including PPAP, PFMEA, DFMEA, control plans, MSA, capability studies, and first article inspections, are completed on time and to standard. Success isn't design release; it is demonstrating that the full value stream can repeatedly meet customer demand with the required quality, cost, and delivery performance.

The right leader is a builder and results driver with the technical and operational credibility to walk the factory floor, challenge supplier capacity, identify manufacturing constraints, and lead cross-functional recovery. This person establishes the PMO, sets objective gate criteria and metrics, holds functional leaders and partners accountable without direct authority, challenges unrealistic plans, and leads recovery when programs fall behind. The leader will model IDEX values of trust, team, and excellence and build a high-performing team that scales with the business.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:**

***Build and Lead the Function***

* Build and lead the Program Management Office (PMO), including organizational structure, staffing plan, talent development, and succession for program and launch managers.
* Establish standard NPD governance—stage-gate/tollgate process, templates, operating cadence, and decision rights—aligned with the IDEX Operating Model.
* Define objective gate-exit criteria and recommend Go, Conditional Go, Hold, or Re-scope decisions based on demonstrated evidence.
* Own the NPD and launch portfolio; prioritize programs using 80/20 principles and align resources to the highest-value customer and growth opportunities.
* Lead executive-level business case, tollgate, and launch-readiness reviews, driving clear decisions on scope, investment, timing, and manufacturing path.

***IDEX Connected Growth and Cross-BU Leadership***

* Drive programs across multiple sister IDEX business units, leveraging IDEX connected growth strategies to share capacity, technology, capabilities, and supply chain.
* Organize and align BU partners, supply chain partners, and internal manufacturing teams into a single integrated execution plan for each program.
* Maintain one integrated critical path and one objective program status across product, supplier, tooling, manufacturing, quality, material, and customer workstreams.
* Lead make, buy, partner, intercompany, and contract manufacturing strategies, including location, capacity, Capex, tooling, staffing, and timing.
* Establish cross-BU agreements, roles, and communication cadences that ensure clear accountability for deliverables across sites and partners.
* Partner with Product Management, Engineering, Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, Sales, and Finance to align program strategy with BU and IDEX growth objectives.

***Quality Management and Launch Readiness Across Supply Chain Partners***

* Drive quality management across multiple supply chain partners, sister BUs, and internal sites to ensure consistent standards from development through production.
* Ensure APQP and product launch deliverables are completed on time and to standard, including PPAP, PFMEA, DFMEA, control plans, process flow diagrams, MSA, capability studies, and first article inspections.
* Partner with Quality and Supply Chain to qualify, develop, and audit suppliers and contract manufacturers, and drive corrective actions to closure.
* Lead launch-readiness and production-readiness gates, ensuring no program advances without required quality, validation, and capacity evidence.
* Separate product validation from production-rate validation; require evidence that the complete value stream can repeatedly achieve required volume, yield, quality, and delivery performance.
* Drive post-launch stabilization, ensuring yield, quality, and delivery targets are met before handoff to steady-state operations.

***Advanced Manufacturing and Capacity***

* Identify and drive advanced manufacturing processes, automation, and technologies needed to meet critical customer demand and scale production.
* Drive readiness of critical processes including welding and joining, filtration media and filter manufacturing, precision machining, assembly, automation, and production test.
* Lead capacity planning and implementation of new processes, including equipment selection, CapEx justification, facility changes, validation, and ramp plans.
* Partner with equipment providers, consultants, and IDEX sites to accelerate process development and transfer best practices.
* Champion design for manufacturability, lean, and continuous improvement in all new product introductions.
* Ensure process qualification, fixtures, tooling, controls, operator readiness, capacity, and rate trials are incorporated before design freeze and production release.

***Metrics, Visibility, and Results***

* Define and own program and launch KPIs, dashboards, and reporting that provide clear leadership visibility across BUs and partners.
* Identify risks early—schedule, resource, quality, sourcing, cost, capacity, and production readiness—and drive countermeasures and recovery plans.
* Challenge unrealistic timelines, resource assumptions, and commitments; escalate decisions and support needs to executive leadership.
* Deliver regular executive updates on portfolio status, risks, decisions, and results.
* Travel domestically and internationally up to 25% to support program execution, supplier engagement, site coordination, customer needs, and equipment-provider activities.
* Perform other related duties and support additional program, PMO, or business needs as assigned.

**KEY PERFORMANCE METRICS:**

* On-time milestone and launch attainment across the NPD portfolio.
* PPAP on-time completion and first-pass approval rate across internal sites, sister BUs, and supply chain partners.
* PFMEA, DFMEA, and control plan completion prior to required gates.
* Launch quality, including first-pass yield, PPM, and escapes at launch and 90 days post-launch.
* Ramp-to-rate performance, including time to target capacity and on-time delivery to customers.
* Critical manufacturing process readiness, including qualification and demonstrated capability for welding/joining, filtration manufacturing, machining, assembly, and test as applicable.
* Program budget, Capex, and product cost performance versus business case.
* Supplier and partner quality and delivery performance on launch programs.
* New product and IDEX-connected growth revenue enabled.
* PMO team capability, staffing, and retention.

**QUALIFICATIONS:**

* Proven leader who has built and scaled a PMO, NPD launch, or program management function in a manufacturing environment.
* undefined
* Deep experience with APQP and product launch deliverables, including PPAP, PFMEA, DFMEA, control plans, and production part qualification.
* Track record driving quality and launch execution across multiple supply chain partners, contract manufacturers, and internal sites.
* Experience identifying and implementing advanced manufacturing processes, automation, and capacity expansions to meet demanding customer ramps.
* undefined
* Demonstrated success leading across multiple business units in a matrixed organization; multi-BU or IDEX experience preferred.
* Strong business acumen in make-versus-buy, multi-site manufacturing, CapEx, tooling, cost, capacity, and risk decisions.
* Builds metrics, dashboards, and operating cadence that drive accountability and measurable results.
* Influential leader able to align executives, BU partners, and suppliers, and hold owners accountable without direct authority.
* Strong executive communicator who turns complex program information into clear decisions and actions.
* Experience with welding/joining, filtration, pneumatics, fluid handling, pumps, compressors, blowers, valves, electromechanical products, precision manufacturing, data center, thermal management, or engineered industrial components preferred.
* Lean, Six Sigma, or PMP certification preferred; working knowledge of the IDEX Operating Model and 80/20 a plus.
* Proficient with project management tools, dashboards, and Microsoft Office applications.

**EDUCATION AND/OR EXPERIENCE:**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, business, operations, supply chain, or a related field required; MBA or advanced degree preferred.
* 10+ years of program management, NPD, manufacturing launch, quality, or operations experience, including 5+ years leading teams, with experience in industrialization, supplier development, site transfers, and multi-site manufacturing.

**PHYSICAL DEMANDS:**

* While performing the duties of the job, the employee is required to move around and be still, use hands to finger, handle or feel objects, tools, or controls; reach with hands and arms; talk and hear.
* Employee will occasionally lift up to 35 lbs.
* Specific vision abilities required by the job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.

new_roles.title: Senior Manager Operational Excellence Initiatives
new_roles.description:
We’re building a world of health around every individual — shaping a more connected, convenient and compassionate health experience. At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. Join us and be part of something bigger – helping to simplify health care one person, one family and one community at a time.

**Position Summary**

CVS is seeking a Senior Manager to own the end-to-end process and technology strategy for stocking and picking across CVS Distribution. This role sits within the Operational Excellence (OpEx) Initiatives team, reporting to the Executive Director of Operational Excellence Initiatives (whose peers lead the OpEx Regional and OpEx Analytics organizations), alongside three other Senior Managers and a team of Managers/Senior Analysts. This role has two direct reports. Where peer Senior Managers on the team own the inbound-through-machine-replenishment and inbound/outbound value streams, this role owns the network's stocking and picking processes – the highest-volume and most labor-intensive processes in our network. This individual will also serve as the process-side subject matter expert on Warehouse Management System (WMS) configuration within owned value streams, to ensure system and process are in alignment. The role requires approximately 30–50% travel, often in stretches on an every-other-week cadence.

Responsibilities:

* **Technology Deployment (50%) —** Own the 3-year technology roadmap for stocking, picking, and module support, including code updates to existing processes, new process rollouts, and major enhancements, to improve colleague experience, quality, and productivity.
* + **Success Measures** — Deliver measurable improvements in inventory accuracy, stocking and picking quality defects, and throughput, specific to each enhancement or process change.
* **Process Optimization (15%) —** Own the process and technology, and advise on WMS configuration needs within your value streams, working with the other subject matter experts on the team who consult on and implement WMS changes, to tune system settings, improve operations, and keep WMS, technology, and process aligned across stocking and picking:
* + **Stocking —** Own the process and core technology for replenishing split-case picking modules
* + **Picking —** Own the process and core technology for picking across multiple picking methods, including split case and full case, in both active pick slots and reserve storage locations
* **Project & Change Management (25%) —** Plan and execute multiple concurrent projects (typically 4–5 programs in parallel, with a rollout roughly every other week across approximately 2,000 associates), applying strong project management skills — managing risk, critical path, dependencies, and budget — to meet project goals on time. Larger programs are led by the network Center of Excellence (COE); on others, this role provides oversight while the site leads. Build the financial business case and project plan for new opportunities, and ensure robust follow-through on changes to sustain results.
* **Mentorship/Training (10%)—** Grow and shape the organization's lean capability, developing training content and standard work that enhances the continuous improvement culture across the network. Lead, coach, and develop direct reports.

This is a work-from-home role with travel; relocation is not offered. The ideal candidate is located near one of the following distribution centers: La Habra (CA), Patterson (CA), Conroe (TX), Lumberton (NJ), Woonsocket (RI), Chemung (NY), Novi (DT), Kansas City (MO), Indianapolis (IN), Orlando (FL), North Augusta (SC), Fredericksburg (VA), or Knoxville (TN).

**Required Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's degree in Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or related engineering/science field or additional 4 years of experience in the requirements below
* 6+ years' experience in a manufacturing or distribution center environment
* 4+ years of demonstrated success and experience in Lean Manufacturing, Continuous Improvement, or Operational Excellence in a manufacturing or warehouse operation
* 4+ years of demonstrated success in managing projects
* 4+ years of experience with WMS, ERP, MES, or LMS systems and database structure

* 2+ years of experience with SQL
* Proven ability to influence and partner with operations, IT, and finance leaders; strong written and verbal communication; self-motivated and effective at managing multiple priorities 
 
 **Preferred Qualifications**
* 9+ years' experience in a manufacturing or distribution center environment
* 6+ years as continuous improvement, industrial engineering, or process engineering
* 2+ years of experience with Microsoft Azure Snowflake semantic modeling and Power BI
* 2+ years running operations (plant manager, senior operations manager, etc.)
* Certified in standards-based time and motion study systems such as MOST and MTM
* APICS CPIM, CSCP, or CLTD Certified
* PMP Certified
* Six Sigma Black Belt Certified

**Pay Range**

The typical pay range for this role is:

$82,940.00 - $182,549.00

This pay range represents the base hourly rate or base annual full-time salary for all positions in the job grade within which this position falls. The actual base salary offer will depend on a variety of factors including experience, education, geography and other relevant factors. This position is eligible for a CVS Health bonus, commission or short-term incentive program in addition to the base pay range listed above. This position also includes an award target in the company’s equity award program.

Our people fuel our future. Our teams reflect the customers, patients, members and communities we serve and we are committed to fostering a workplace where every colleague feels valued and that they belong.

**Great benefits for great people**

We take pride in offering a comprehensive and competitive mix of pay and benefits that reflects our commitment to our colleagues and their families.

 
This full‑time position is eligible for a comprehensive benefits package designed to support the physical, emotional, and financial well‑being of colleagues and their families. The benefits for this position include medical, dental, and vision coverage, paid time off, retirement savings options, wellness programs, and other resources, based on eligibility.

Additional details about available benefits are provided during the application process and on Benefits Moments.

 
We anticipate the application window for this opening will close on: 12/14/2026

Qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment in accordance with all federal, state and local laws.

new_roles.title: Sr. Manager, External Manufacturing Operations
new_roles.description:
At Solventum, we improve lives by helping healthcare professionals do their best work. Join a team using innovation and insight to make a real impact on the future of healthcare. All roles listed are with Solventum, and we’re committed to protecting your personal information—learn more in our Privacy Policy

**Job Description:**

**Sr. Manager, External Manufacturing Operations**

**3M Health Care is now Solventum**

**At Solventum, we enable better, smarter, safer healthcare to improve lives. As a new company with a long legacy of creating breakthrough solutions for our customers’ toughest challenges, we pioneer game-changing innovations at the intersection of health, material and data science that change patients' lives for the better while enabling healthcare professionals to perform at their best. Because people, and their wellbeing, are at the heart of every scientific advancement we pursue.**

**We partner closely with the brightest minds in healthcare to ensure that every solution we create melds the latest technology with compassion and empathy. Because at Solventum, we never stop solving for you.**

**The Impact You’ll Make in this Role**

As a **Sr, Manager of External Manufacturing Operations**, you will have the opportunity to tap into your curiosity and collaborate with some of the most innovative and diverse people around the world. Here, you will make an impact by:

* Owning the operational performance and strategic relationship of the external manufacturing partners supporting Brookings.
* Maintaining direct accountability for the continuity and availability of externally supplied materials and products required for Brookings manufacturing.
* Ensuring materials are available when needed, meet established specifications, and do not disrupt the manufacturing process.
* Establishing clear expectations for Contract Manufacturing Organization (CMO) performance across quality, delivery, capacity, cost, responsiveness, compliance, and supply continuity.
* Maintaining visibility to supplier production plans, materials, inventory, logistics, capacity, and constraints.
* Leading rapid response and escalation when supplier quality, capacity, production, logistics, technical, or operational issues threaten Brookings manufacturing.
* Driving containment, recovery, root cause, corrective action, and prevention to ensure issues are sustainably resolved.
* Establishing a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and operational excellence across the CMO network.

**Your Skills and Expertise**

To set you up for success in this role from day one, Solventum requires (at a minimum) the following qualifications:

 

* Bachelor's degree or higher in (completed and verified prior to start) AND twelve (12) years of combined experience in manufacturing, operations, external manufacturing, supply chain, quality, engineering, planning, and/or procurement

In addition to the above requirements, the following are also required:

 

* Experience managing contract manufacturing organizations (CMOs), contract manufacturers, and/or strategic manufacturing suppliers
* Experience supporting medical device manufacturing within a regulated manufacturing environment
* Experience managing supply continuity, CMO capacity, production planning, supplier quality, asset strategy, and/or operational risk

Additional qualifications that could help you succeed even further in this role include:

 

* Experience applying medical device quality systems and applicable regulatory requirements.
* Experience applying GMP, supplier quality, change control, specifications, CAPA, SCARs, Quality Agreements, and/or regulatory compliance requirements.
* Experience developing and executing CMO risk mitigation and business continuity strategies.
* Experience establishing supplier KPI dashboards, scorecards, and executive performance reviews.
* Experience supporting CMO contracts, Quality Agreements, commercial negotiations, and supplier performance management.
* Experience supporting budgeting, forecasting, capital expenditure (CapEx) planning, and business case development.
* Experience leading complex cross-functional initiatives involving Manufacturing, Engineering, Supplier Quality, Value Stream Management, Supply Chain, Procurement, Quality, Regulatory, Finance, and/or external partners.
* Experience communicating, negotiating, and presenting recommendations to cross-functional stakeholders and senior leaders.

**Work location:**

* **Hybrid Eligible (Job Duties allow for some remote work but require travel to Brookings and other sites, including suppliers and other Solventum locations)** 
 **OR**
* **Remote in United States**

**Travel: May include up to 70% domestic/international**

**Relocation Assistance: May be authorized**

**Must be legally authorized to work in country of employment without sponsorship for employment visa status (e.g., H1B status).**

**Supporting Your Well-being**

Solventum offers many programs to help you live your best life – both physically and financially. To ensure competitive pay and benefits, Solventum regularly benchmarks with other companies that are comparable in size and scope.

new_roles.title: Senior Manager, US Quality Operations
new_roles.description:
Xona is the navigational intelligence company bringing real-time, centimeter-level certainty to any device, anywhere on Earth.

With Pulsar – the world’s most advanced PNT satellite infrastructure in Low Earth Orbit – Xona will offer a future-proof, backwards-compatible global positioning system optimized for absolute precision, superior power, and robust protection.

As production grows, we need clear evidence that each spacecraft meets its requirements and a quality system that helps teams find and resolve risks early.

We are looking for a **Senior Manager, Quality Operations** to lead US quality for satellite buses and payloads from incoming material through building, test and acceptance. You will build a pragmatic system and lead engineers and inspectors close to the floor. You have independent authority to hold work or withhold readiness concurrence and to escalate unresolved mission risk. This is a hands-on leadership role in a fast-moving, dynamic environment.

**What you will do:**
=====================

* Lead US quality engineers and inspectors across supplier, receiving, production and test coverage. Set training, inspection points and delegated authority.
* Own fit-for-stage quality controls for document and configuration records, serial and lot traceability, calibration, nonconformances, corrective action and acceptance packages.
* Define risk-based controls for critical characteristics and supplier parts. Work with Supply Chain on qualifications, escapes, containment and verified corrective action.
* Make quality status visible through yield, repeat defects, escapes, NCR aging and acceptance-record completeness. Use trends to improve controls with Manufacturing and Engineering.
* Own the quality hold and escalation process. Engineering owns technical disposition; Quality evaluates controls and evidence and concurs on release.
* Concur independently on quality evidence at acceptance and flight readiness reviews. Escalate residual risk despite schedule pressure; partner with Engineering on reliability and mission risk.
* Align common requirements with the Canada Quality Lead and feed ground defects and on-orbit anomalies into later builds.

**What we are looking for**
===========================

* 8+ years in quality engineering or quality management for aerospace, defense or similarly complex hardware, including 3+ years directly leading engineers, inspectors or specialists through production and test.
* Experience building a usable QMS and leading teams through supplier escapes, nonconformances, root cause and corrective action.
* Independent judgment, strong technical communication and the ability to separate Engineering disposition from Quality release concurrence.
* Working knowledge of configuration control, risk-based inspection, process capability and cross-functional investigations.
* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, materials science, physics or a related technical field, or equivalent quality leadership experience in complex hardware.

**For U.S. Roles:** To comply with U.S. Government space technology export regulations, applicant must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the United States (i.e. Green Card holder), or other protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3).

**For U.K. Roles:** To comply with U.K. regulations, this role requires Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) checks, and successful candidates must be eligible to obtain UK Security Clearance (SC).

**For Canada Roles:** Successful candidates must obtain and hold a security clearance at the reliability status level, and pass security assessment for the Canadian Controlled Goods Program (CGP) and ITAR.

We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or veteran status.

Compensation Range: $180K - $230K

new_roles.title: Manufacturing Technical Services Senior Manager - Spray Dried Dispersion (SDD)
new_roles.description:
**Job Description**

**General Summary**
-------------------

The Manufacturing Technical Services Senior Manager provides technical leadership for commercial manufacturing operations for Spray Dried Dispersion (SDD) at external manufacturing partners. The role is accountable for overseeing technical services activities across the commercial manufacturing lifecycle, including manufacturing readiness, process performance, technical investigations, change management, process improvement, and supply-risk mitigation.

The Senior Manager partners with Manufacturing Operations, MS&T, Quality, Supply Chain, Engineering, Regulatory Affairs, and CDMOs/CMOs to ensure manufacturing processes are robust, compliant, reliable, and capable of supporting product supply. The role leads complex cross-functional technical workstreams and develops technical talent within the Manufacturing Technical Services organization.

**Key Duties and Responsibilities**
-----------------------------------

* Lead Manufacturing Technical Services support for assigned commercial manufacturing programs and external manufacturing partners.
* Establish technical plans and priorities to support manufacturing readiness, commercial production campaigns, product supply, and lifecycle-management objectives.
* Provide technical oversight during manufacturing execution; lead escalation and resolution of complex process, equipment, yield, and manufacturing-performance issues.
* Lead technical investigations of significant manufacturing deviations, process excursions, yield loss, equipment failures, and product-quality events; ensure root cause, technical impact, and sustainable corrective actions are clearly defined.
* Oversee manufacturing, process, analytical, and batch-performance trending to identify emerging risks, assess process robustness, and prioritize improvement opportunities.
* Lead technical assessment and approval of change controls, risk assessments, comparability assessments, process updates, and related manufacturing documentation.
* Partner with Manufacturing Operations and Supply Chain to assess technical constraints, manage manufacturing and supply risks, and develop recovery or mitigation plans.
* Lead technical governance with CDMOs/CMOs, including performance review, issue escalation, technical decision-making, data review, and follow-up of technical deliverables.
* Collaborate with MS&T, Quality, Engineering, and Regulatory Affairs to ensure technical strategies align with process-validation requirements, cGMP expectations, regulatory commitments, and product lifecycle plans.
* Lead continuous-improvement initiatives that enhance process robustness, product quality, yield, manufacturing efficiency, and supply reliability.
* Develop, mentor, and provide technical directions to Manufacturing Technical Services staff and matrixed technical teams.
* Travel to support on-site manufacturing activities, CDMO/CMO operations, audits, inspections, and business needs as required (10-20% travel expected)

**Knowledge and Skills**
------------------------

* Deep understanding of pharmaceutical manufacturing processes, testing, controls, and commercial manufacturing operations for Spray Dried Dispersion (SDD)
* Strong knowledge of current Good Manufacturing Practices, pharmaceutical quality systems, and controlled-documentation requirements.
* Demonstrated experience with commercial manufacturing support, technical services, process monitoring, product lifecycle management, and external manufacturing oversight.
* Advanced experience leading complex technical investigations, root-cause analysis, corrective and preventive actions, change controls, risk assessments, and process-improvement initiatives.
* Ability to interpret manufacturing, process, and analytical data; identify process-performance trends; assess technical risks; and recommend practical, sustainable solutions.
* Understanding of manufacturing operations, maintenance, engineering, equipment performance, capacity constraints, and supply-continuity planning.
* Experience leading CDMO/CMO technical relationships, including governance, performance management, technical issue resolution, and escalation.
* Strong cross-functional leadership and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to influence decisions without direct authority.
* Excellent written, verbal, presentation, strategic-thinking, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook, and relevant manufacturing or business systems.

**Education and Experience**
----------------------------

* Bachelor’s degree in Biological Sciences, Chemical Engineering, Chemistry, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Materials Science, or a related scientific or technical discipline.
* Typically requires 8+ years of experience in biotechnology, pharmaceutical, chemical, or another regulated manufacturing environment, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
* Significant experience supporting commercial manufacturing operations, technical services, MS&T, process development, engineering, quality, or external manufacturing.
* Demonstrated experience leading technical programs, manufacturing workstreams, complex investigations, process improvements, or cross-functional teams.
* Experience working in a cGMP environment and supporting controlled manufacturing documentation is required.
Demonstrate people leadership, matrix leadership, or technical leadership experience is required.

new_roles.title: Manager/Senior Manager, Global Quality Systems
new_roles.description:
***Who We Are:***

Xenon Pharmaceuticals (NASDAQ:XENE) is a neuroscience-focused biopharmaceutical company dedicated to drug discovery, clinical development, and commercialization of life-changing therapeutics for patients in need. We are looking for great people who thrive in a respectful, collaborative, inclusive, and productive culture to join the Xenon team.

***What We Do:***

We are advancing an exciting product pipeline to address indications with high unmet medical need, including epilepsy, depression and pain. Our late-stage azetukalner program represents the most advanced, clinically validated potassium channel modulator in late-stage clinical development for multiple indications. In March 2026, we announced positive topline data from our Phase 3 X-TOLE2 study of azetukalner in focal seizures (FS), and we submitted a New Drug Application to the Food and Drug Administration in the third quarter of 2026. Our Phase 3 epilepsy program also includes a second FS study, X-TOLE3, which would support regulatory submissions outside the U.S., and the X-ACKT study in primary generalized tonic-clonic seizures, which would support regulatory submissions for an additional epilepsy indication. We also are investigating azetukalner in major depressive disorder (MDD) and bipolar depression (BPD), based on topline data from our Phase 2 X-NOVA clinical trial. In addition, we continue to advance an early-stage pipeline of novel ion channel candidates, including studies of XEN1701 and XEN1720 (targeting Nav1.7) and XEN1120 (targeting Kv7), which are being developed for pain. Backed by a strong balance sheet to support our growth plans, we continue to build a fully integrated, premier neuroscience company with strong discovery, clinical development, corporate, and commercial operations.

***About the Role:***

We are seeking a **Manager/Senior Manager, Global Quality Systems,** who will provide leadership and oversight across key Quality Management System (QMS) processes, including quality events, investigations, root cause analysis, CAPA, and change control. This role will serve as a key quality partner across GxP functions, helping to identify systemic issues, strengthen investigation practices, and drive sustainable, risk-based improvements that support compliance, inspection readiness, and operational excellence. The role will work closely with internal teams and external service providers across Xenon’s outsourced operating model to ensure the QMS remains effective, compliant, and inspection ready.

The ideal candidate will bring strong Quality Systems experience, broad GxP knowledge, and sound business judgment, with the ability to effectively challenge investigations, facilitate meaningful root cause analysis, and influence stakeholders across functions. The role will also support quality governance, QMS metrics and trending, change control review, and the continued optimization of electronic quality systems.

This position reports to the Associate Director, Quality Assurance, Systems and will be based out of Boston, MA, USA in our Needham office. This role is a hybrid position, requiring a minimum of two onsite days per week. The level of the position will be commensurate with the candidate’s education and industry experience.

**RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* **Quality Systems & Governance**

 + Manage the oversight, lifecycle management, and continuous improvement of GxP Quality Systems, including quality events, investigations, CAPA, change control, and associated governance processes.
 + Ensure consistent, risk-based practices for investigation, root cause analysis, CAPA, and change management, including review and approval of records and escalation of significant quality or compliance risks.
 + Monitor QMS performance through metrics, trending, CAPA effectiveness, and Quality Management Review reporting to identify systemic risks and drive continuous improvement.
* **Compliance, Inspection Readiness & eQMS**

 + Assess QMS processes and proposed changes for GxP, regulatory, validation, training, documentation, and data integrity considerations, maintaining alignment with applicable regulatory requirements and industry expectations.
 + Support the administration, optimization, validation, upgrades, and continuous improvement of the eQMS and associated procedures, guidance, and training.
 + Support regulatory inspections and internal and external audits, including inspection readiness and responses to observations and findings.
* **Quality Leadership & Cross-Functional Partnership**

 + Provide Quality Systems expertise, guidance, coaching, and training to promote consistent, inspection-ready, and risk-based quality practices across the organization.
 + Partner with GxP functions and external service providers to establish quality expectations, resolve quality issues, implement compliant changes and CAPAs, and drive cross-functional quality improvement initiatives.
 + Promote a strong quality culture through effective stakeholder engagement, sound judgment, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
* **General Responsibilities**

 + Act in accordance with Company policies, including the Code of Business Conduct and Ethics, and ensure applicable policies are understood and followed by direct reports, if any.
 + Other duties as assigned.

**QUALIFICATIONS:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Life Sciences, Health Sciences, Pharmacy, or a related discipline; advanced degree preferred.
* 5–8+ years of relevant experience, or an equivalent combination of education and experience, within the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical device, or other regulated industry, with demonstrated experience in Quality Systems, Quality Assurance, or compliance.
* Demonstrated experience with quality event management, including complex investigations, root cause analysis, CAPA, and change control.
* Strong working knowledge of QMS requirements, quality risk management principles, and applicable GxP regulations, including GMP and familiarity with GCP, GVP, and GLP.
* Experience with electronic Quality Management Systems such as Veeva Quality, MasterControl, or equivalent, including supporting system implementation, optimization, or maintenance.
* Experience developing, reviewing, and maintaining quality procedures, SOPs, metrics, and trending to support risk-based decision-making and continuous improvement.
* Experience supporting quality governance activities, regulatory inspections, internal or external audits, and inspection readiness.
* Demonstrated ability to work cross-functionally and influence stakeholders while effectively navigating ambiguity and driving quality initiatives to completion.
* Strong critical thinking and problem-solving skills, with the ability to balance strategic judgment with a hands-on approach to execution.
* Excellent organizational, written, and verbal communication skills.

Our Total Rewards program includes base salary, target bonus, and stock options, as well as a full range of benefits including medical, dental, vision, short-& long-term disability, accidental death & dismemberment, and life insurance programs, Employee Assistance Program, travel insurance, and retirement savings programs with company matching contributions.

Xenon encourages time to rest and re-charge through vacation, personal days, sick days, and an end-of-year company shutdown. Xenon highly values employee development and has an expanding Training, Learning & Development program, including a Tuition Assistance program for advanced degrees.

Compensation Range: $131.3K - $173.3K

new_roles.title: Senior Manager, Operations - Quality
new_roles.description:
**About the role:**
===================

This is a hands-on role with both strategic and executional scope. You will build and lead quality assurance and quality control standards across Operations, set the sampling, validation, and escalation practices the organization runs on, and partner closely with the Senior Manager, Operations - Payer Ops, the Human-in-the-Loop Operations leader, Product, and Engineering. You will report to the Head of Operations and help define the company's AI/Human QA strategy as Adonis scales.

**What you'll do:**
===================

**Own the Quality Program across Operations**
---------------------------------------------

* Define and own QA/QC standards, sampling methodologies, audit practices, and validation processes across AI agent outputs, human-executed work, and vendor-delivered operations.
* Develop & present quarterly plans and operating metrics; communicate progress and trade-offs; surface risks early + Work closely with the Head of Operations on strategic projects
* Lead quality assurance for payer workflows and agent outcomes, including new payer activations on the voice channel.
* Lead the development and implementation of a near-real-time QA Dashboard to provide visibility into quality, identify performance gaps, and track improvement over time.
* Partner with the operations team and external vendors to ensure work consistently meets Adonis's accuracy, operational, and compliance standards.
* Partner closely with the operations team to align on quality standards, remediation priorities, and operational performance.
* Collaborate with Product, Engineering, vendors, and cross-functional stakeholders to address quality gaps, improve workflows, and support strategic initiatives.
* Serve as the quality subject matter expert across Operations, ensuring quality considerations are incorporated into new workflows, product launches, and operational changes.

**Turn quality findings into operational and product improvements**
-------------------------------------------------------------------

* Translate and present quality trends and findings into actionable recommendations for Product, Engineering, and Operations, driving improvements from identification through implementation and validation.
* Leverage AI, automation, and internal tooling to increase the efficiency, accuracy, and scalability of QA/QC processes.
* Establish quality thresholds and escalation criteria for uncertain, complex, or high-impact outcomes.

**Build and lead a high-performing quality function**
-----------------------------------------------------

* Build and scale the Quality function, establishing clear goals, ownership, processes, and performance metrics.
* Lead, coach, and develop onshore and offshore team members, as the function grows.
* Develop and maintain SOPs, playbooks, training materials, and quality guidelines to support operational consistency and continuous improvement.

**Who you are:**
================

* 6+ years of experience
* Experience in healthcare revenue cycle management (RCM) is required, with practical understanding of payer, claims, or related revenue-cycle workflows.
* Experience building or leading quality assurance, quality control, or quality programs in a technology-enabled operations environment.
* Experience coaching a team and creating clarity across multiple workstreams.
* Experience defining operating standards, evaluating results, investigating failures, and ensuring corrective actions are effective.
* Strong cross-functional communication skills, with the ability to work effectively with Product, Engineering, customer-facing teams, and operational partners.
* Comfort moving between strategic planning and hands-on operational detail in a fast-changing environment.
* An AI-forward mindset and practical experience applying AI, automation, or intelligent tooling to improve quality and operational performance, with sound judgment about when human review is needed.

The base salary range for this position is $140,000 to $180,000. Base pay offered may vary depending on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. In addition to base salary, we also offer competitive equity and benefits packages.

**About Adonis**
================

Adonis is the leading AI orchestration platform for healthcare revenue cycle management (RCM), purpose-built for healthcare organizations seeking to transform their revenue operations. Traditional RCM processes often struggle with inefficiencies, costing providers up to 15% or more of their potential revenue. Through advanced automation, data science, and AI Agents, Adonis helps revenue teams detect vulnerabilities, optimize workflows, and deploy precise solutions that drive reliable and scalable financial outcomes.

Adonis is headquartered in New York City and has raised over $95M in funding, including a recent $40M Series C round led by Quadrille Capital with continued support from existing investors such as General Catalyst and Bling Capital. This funding supports our mission to restore sanity to RCM and equip provider groups and health systems with AI-driven revenue cycle operations at scale.

**Compensation Philosophy**
===========================

Actual base pay will depend on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Adonis determines compensation based on each candidate’s experience and qualifications relative to peers, and most new hires fall near the middle of the range. In addition to base salary, you’ll receive meaningful equity and great benefits.

**Perks at Adonis**
===================

* Competitive equity packages
* Employer-paid medical insurance
* Employer-paid dental insurance
* Employer-paid vision insurance
* Employer-funded HSA
* Parental leave
* Commuter benefits
* Office lunches every day
* Office snacks
* Generous PTO
* Located in 3 World Trade Center with easy access to all trains and the PATH, and amazing views of the city

Adonis is proud to be an equal-opportunity employer. We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive culture that celebrates authenticity to win as one. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, protected veteran status, citizenship or immigration status, or any other legally protected characteristics.

At Adonis, we fully comply with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). We are dedicated to embracing challenges and creating an accessible, inclusive workplace for all individuals.

Compensation Range: $140K - $180K
