new_roles.title: Director of Operations Support & Program Management (Remote w/travel required)
new_roles.description:
Overview:

**At Anne Arundel Dermatology we give exceptional care - to our patients and to eachother.**
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Patient First | Caring | Accountability | Trust | One Team | Growth

Founded 50+ years ago with a mission to provide the highest quality and full spectrum of medical, surgical, and esthetic skin care services to each and every one of its patients, Anne Arundel Dermatology has assembled the finest group of dermatologists in the Mid-Atlantic and Southeastern states. With 250+ clinicians and 110+ locations in 7 states, we’re thriving, growing, and looking to add talented individuals to our team!

**Why join Anne Arundel Dermatology?**

We are committed to continual training and education for our physicians and staff. We are on top of the latest developments in dermatology including ongoing research, emerging treatments, new medications and prevention methods. You can find more than just a job with Anne Arundel Dermatology. We believe in providing our new associates with intensive hands on training and long-term career growth opportunities from within.

If you are looking for a career with a busy, fast paced medical office, then joining the Anne Arundel Dermatology’s Surgery Center team is for you! We are looking for highly motivated, self-starting individuals, who work efficiently and are detail oriented, to join our team. You will not only be working alongside a large administrative team, but also with some of the top Moh’s Surgeons in the area. This is a great opportunity to be a part of our vast growing practice or an essential stepping stone for anyone looking to advance their career in the administrative side of the medical field.

**DIRECTOR OF OPERATIONS SUPPORT & PROGRAM MANAGEMENT**

***Job Summary:***

The **Director of Operations Support & Program Management** provides strategic and operational leadership for enterprise operations support, project management, technology optimization, process improvement, and training. Serving as the central link between Operations, IT, Revenue Cycle Management (RCM), Clinical, Aesthetics, Marketing, and vendors, the Director removes operational barriers, translates operational needs into effective systems, workflows, and training, and ensures enterprise initiatives are implemented, adopted, and sustained.

Salary range of 140,000-160,000 annually, plus 20% bonus opportunity.

Responsibilities:

***Duties/Responsibilities:***

**Operations Support & Operational Excellence**

* Lead the Operations Support function and serve as the escalation point for complex operational and cross-functional issues.
* Establish and maintain standardized SOPs, workflows, and operational processes across the organization.
* Use process-analysis reporting to identify operational barriers and implement solutions that improve efficiency, consistency, and communication.
* Support provider onboarding and operational readiness, site moves, and other organizational changes.
* Maintain regular communication cadences with support functions, including Aesthetics and Marketing, to surface and resolve issues proactively.

**Enterprise Program & Project Management**

* Lead or oversee major cross-functional initiatives (e.g., telephony transformation, Assist Tracking/LIS transition, Medsender and AI Scribe implementations, and aesthetic online scheduling).
* Own the initiative portfolio, managing intake, prioritization, and sequencing of requests against team and field capacity.
* Establish project priorities, timelines, ownership, and deliverables using a consistent methodology (charters, stage gates, go-live readiness, hypercare, post-implementation reviews); identify risks, dependencies, resource needs, and operational impacts.
* Coordinate stakeholders across Operations, IT, clinical teams, RCM, and vendors from planning through adoption and stabilization, and manage vendor statements of work, timelines, and project budgets.
* Provide leadership with regular reporting on project progress, risks, and outcomes, including delivery measures such as on-time go-lives and adoption.

**Software Management & Digital Innovation**

* Provide strategic oversight of the operational software ecosystem (e.g., ModMed, Relatient, Klara, HubSpot, Medsender, Brevium, Birdeye, Zocdoc, and self-scheduling tools), including interface and workflow monitoring.
* Partner with IT to define system requirements, identify gaps, and implement workflow solutions; manage vendor relationships and enhancement priorities.
* Evaluate automation, integration, and digital innovation opportunities that improve the patient and provider experience.
* Establish governance for ongoing system optimization and ensure system changes are supported by sustainable workflows, training, and adoption.

**Training & Continuous Process Improvement**

* Oversee standardized training for Time of Service, new hires, providers, aesthetic processes and discounts, clinical documentation, and system or workflow changes.
* Partner with RCM and clinical leadership to address documentation deficiencies; monitor compliance and performance indicators to identify retraining needs.
* Keep training materials aligned with current SOPs and technology, and lead a culture in which process changes are implemented, measured, and refined.

**MIPS & Regulatory/Performance Initiatives**

* Lead operational coordination of MIPS activities, partnering with clinical, operational, and RCM stakeholders to operationalize requirements.
* Monitor progress, address barriers, and integrate MIPS requirements into workflows, training, documentation, and reporting.

Qualifications:

***Required Skills/Abilities:***

* Change management
* Project leadership, strategic thinking and data-driven decision making
* Process improvement and technology enablement
* Executive communication, cross-functional relationship management, accountability and follow-through

Licensure/Certifications/Education:

***Education and Experience:***

* Bachelor's degree in healthcare administration, business administration, operations, information systems, or related field, **or** 10+ years of relevant experience.
* Progressive leadership experience in healthcare operations, practice management, operational transformation, or project management.
* Demonstrated success leading cross-functional technology implementations, system optimization, integrations, and workflow redesign.
* Strong knowledge of SOP development, change management, and staff and provider training.
* Ability to manage multiple enterprise-level priorities and translate complex operational or technical issues into practical solutions.
* Experience working effectively with executive leadership, physicians/providers, vendors, and cross-functional teams.

***Physical Requirements:***

* Regularly required to sit for extended periods.
* Regular use of hands and fingers to operate a keyboard, mouse, and telephone.
* Occasionally required to stand and walk.
* Talking and listening in person and on the telephone.
* Occasionally lifting and carrying up to 25 pounds.
* 25% travel required, possibly up to 50%

**Full time employees (defined as regularly working at least 30 hours per week) are eligible for the following benefits:**

* Medical, Dental & Vision insurance – effective 1st of the month after date of start
* Short-term and long-term disability, Voluntary life (employee, spouse, and child), Critical Illness, and Hospital Indemnity – Effective the 1st of the month following date of hire
* Company provided Basic Life/AD&D insurance
* Paid time off
* Paid holidays
* Retirement Savings account
* Employee discount on cosmetic services and products

new_roles.title: Senior Director of Oncology Operations
new_roles.description:
**Job Summary**

The Sr. Director of Oncology Operations at Arizona Center for Cancer Care (AZCCC) provides operational leadership and oversight for outpatient oncology operations across AZCCC and its health system partner’s integrated cancer care network. This role oversees strategy, operations, and continuous improvement for infusion centers, physician practices, and outpatient clinics, as well as leadership of the oncology research and clinical trials program. The Director partners with physicians, clinical teams, and research leaders to optimize access, quality, and patient outcomes.

**Duties and responsibilities**

* Provides executive leadership and oversight for all outpatient oncology operations across AZCCC and its health system partner’s integrated cancer care network, including infusion centers, physician practices, and hospital outpatient department (HOPD) clinics.
* Drives the strategic alignment and execution of oncology services to ensure high-quality, efficient, and patient-centered care.
* Oversees the oncology research and clinical trials program, including compliance with NCI guidelines, Good Clinical Practice (GCP), and all applicable regulatory requirements.
* Collaborates with physician leadership and the Executive Medical Oncology Committee to develop and implement operational strategies that improve access, outcomes, and overall performance.
* Partners with physician investigators and research teams to integrate clinical research with patient care, supporting innovation and advancement in oncology treatments.
* Provides direct supervision and mentorship to clinic operations leaders, including practice administrators and department managers, ensuring operational goals are met across all sites.
* Monitors financial performance, develops annual budgets, and implements cost-control measures while maintaining high standards of quality and service.
* Ensures compliance with AZCCC policies, state and federal regulations, and accreditation standards across all outpatient oncology programs.
* Fosters a collaborative and accountable culture by promoting communication, transparency, and professional growth across interdisciplinary teams.
* Leads initiatives to optimize workflows, staffing models, and patient flow to achieve operational excellence and improve the patient experience.
* Serves as the primary liaison between senior leadership, physicians, and partner organizations, ensuring alignment of goals and strategies across entities.
* Uses data-driven insights to evaluate program performance and identify opportunities for growth, efficiency, and innovation
* Represents AZCCC and performs other related duties as assigned to support organizational goals and promote best practices in oncology care delivery.

**Licensure and Certifications**

* NA

**Direct Reports**

* Regional Practice Administrators

**Qualifications/Education Requirements**

* Master’s degree in health administration, business administration, or a related field required.
* Equivalent combination of education and progressive leadership experience in outpatient medical oncology operations preferred.
* Ability to demonstrate knowledge of oncology operations, including infusion services, physician practice management, HOPD operations, and compliance with NCI guidelines and GCP standards.
* Minimum of 5 years of progressive leadership experience in outpatient medical oncology operations.

**Working conditions**

* Works in an office or clinical setting.
* Exposed to moderate noise levels.
* Emphasizes collaboration with various stakeholders.
* Necessitates effective communication and teamwork.
* Functions in a fast-paced environment.
* May require flexibility in working hours.
* Requires adherence to safety protocols and compliance with healthcare regulations.
* Valid driver’s license and reliable transportation for travel between locations.

**Physical requirements**

* Must be able to lift 25 lbs.
* Must be able to sit, stand and walk for extended periods of time
* Must be able to bend, kneel, crawl and twist as needed
* Must be able to see, hear, type, and speak
* Must be able to reach and pull

**EEO Statement**

Arizona Center for Cancer Care provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws.

This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation and training.

new_roles.title: Program Operations Director - Epidemiology
new_roles.description:
Overview:

Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center is an independent, nonprofit organization providing adult cancer treatment and groundbreaking research focused on cancer and infectious diseases. Based in Seattle, Fred Hutch is the only National Cancer Institute-designated cancer center in Washington.

With a track record of global leadership in bone marrow transplantation, HIV/AIDS prevention, immunotherapy and COVID-19 vaccines, Fred Hutch has earned a reputation as one of the world’s leading cancer, infectious disease and biomedical research centers. Fred Hutch operates eight clinical care sites that provide medical oncology, infusion, radiation, proton therapy and related services, and network affiliations with hospitals in five states. Together, our fully integrated research and clinical care teams seek to discover new cures to the world’s deadliest diseases and make life beyond cancer a reality.

At Fred Hutch we value collaboration, compassion, determination, excellence, innovation, integrity and respect. Our mission is directly tied to the humanity, dignity and inherent value of each employee, patient, community member and supporter. Our commitment to learning across our differences and similarities make us stronger. We seek employees who bring different and innovative ways of seeing the world and solving problems.

The Cancer Epidemiology Program, as one of five scientific programs within the Public Health Sciences Division, is focused on reducing cancer incidence, progression, mortality, and sequalae through the identification of risk (or protective) factors, the elucidation of underlying biologic mechanisms, and the translation of discoveries into prevention strategies. The program includes more than a dozen core faculty based at Fred Hutch, plus affiliated faculty from the University of Washington, as well as a large number of research staff, ranging from program assistants, interviewers, medical record abstractors, project coordinators, study managers, and statistical research associates.

The **Program Operations Director** is responsible for the overall program activities and administrative operations including strategy, financial, personnel, grants and contracts, regulatory and administrative functions for a broad program comprised of multiple research groups. This position requires an understanding of sponsored research, regulatory requirements, performance management, administrative systems, program management and broad experience with business functions and systems, including program leadership, strategic planning, budgeting, fiscal analysis, human resources management and communication. This position reports to the Epidemiology Program Head.

Responsibilities:

This position works with overarching guidance from program leadership, Principal Investigators (PIs) and the Division’s Associate Vice President to independently plan and oversee administrative operations for the program research portfolio. The Program Operation Director manages the administrative team and oversees all day-to-day operational and administrative responsibilities for the program, sets functional strategies and objectives on operational plans that align with overall Division and organizational strategies, and provides input to Division-level strategic planning.

General Program Operations and Administration:

* Lead the program administration team.
* Support the Program Head in developing the program strategic plan and annual reporting requirements, planning and attending faculty meetings, workshops and retreats.
* Work in partnership with Center and Division administrative teams to ensure successful implementation and integration of programs and center-wide initiatives; foster cross-functional collaboration.
* Participate in Center and Division-led meetings, committees and special projects.
* Direct and provide leadership to the Epidemiology Program study managers, including ensuring there are regular research staff meetings, where information on new policies and practices relevant to the Program can be communicated, disseminated, and implemented.
* Manage space usage and allocation including planning for future uses and adapting to changing faculty/research needs.
* Partner with Communications Team to develop and maintain website and content development.

Financial and Data Management:

* Oversee general financial operations for the program including forecasting, management, reporting, reconciliations, purchasing and vendor contract management for sponsored, non-sponsored and foundation funded projects.
* Oversee the preparation, management, and monitoring of the Program's annual budget and faculty funding needs. Perform cost analysis and obtain data needed for requests. Justify and advocate for budget requests directly with Division senior leadership, Finance, and Compensation departments.
* In collaboration with the Senior Research Administration Manager, oversee grant activities including grant preparation, budget development/management, forecasting, reporting and report tools development.

Faculty Support:

* Coordinate faculty recruiting activities for the program and support the Division office in administration and faculty promotions
* Identify opportunities and assist faculty in cultivating and managing relationships within and outside Fred Hutch.
* Assist the Fred Hutch Philanthropy and Marketing departments in cooperation with the Division to ensure all achievements and donor relationships are appropriately highlighted and managed
* Manage and maintain the faculty grant library, program documentation, policy materials and support recurring reporting needs.
* Seek new funding opportunities for the program as appropriate

HR Management:

* Facilitate the annual staff performance management and merit review process.
* Assist the Program Head and Division with faculty HR matters including promotions, appointment changes, onboarding, offboarding and the annual merit review process.
* Advise and assist faculty and study managers in developing study team structures, submissions of employment requisitions and personnel actions, classification review, disciplinary actions, trainee and graduate student inquiries and staff training and development planning.

Qualifications:

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:**

* Bachelor’s degree in business, public administration or a related field.
* Minimum of 8-10 years of federal research administration management experience.
* Minimum of 3-5 years of supervisory and leadership experience.
* Demonstrated success managing and engaging diverse stakeholders across a complex research portfolio.
* Experience with translating science into strategy in creating and executing strategic plans.
* Strong communication and budgetary skills.

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:**

* Master's degree.
* 3-5 years of experience in supporting faculty in an academic environment.
* Experience in identifying areas for process improvement and implementing associated change management strategies to successfully rollout and sustain initiatives.
* Robust budget management and forecasting skills.
* Experience in leading a diverse team, thinking creatively and globally, projecting future needs, and being attuned to the day-to-day program operations.
* Flexible and comfortable working in a fast-paced environment with shifting priorities.
* Exemplary organizational skills, attention to detail and service orientation.
* Demonstrated ability to successfully operate in and lead a complex, matrixed, and high-performing organization.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
* Strong background in data analytics and visualization.
* Advanced experience with Microsoft suite (e.g., Excel, PowerPoint, SharePoint).
* Ability to create a positive work culture.
* Flexibility and adaptability.
* Ability to multi-task in a fast-paced environment.
* Outstanding interpersonal skills.
* Positive attitude and sense of humor.

The annual base salary range for this position is from $123,968 to $195,915, and pay offered will be based on experience and qualifications. 
 
Although Fred Hutch is not sponsoring most H-1B visas at this time, candidates who already hold an H-1B sponsored by another organization and are currently in the U.S. may be eligible for this position. 
 
Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center offers employees a comprehensive benefits package designed to enhance health, well-being, and financial security. Benefits include medical/vision, dental, flexible spending accounts, life, disability, retirement, family life support, employee assistance program, onsite health clinic, tuition reimbursement, paid vacation (12-22 days per year), paid sick leave (12-25 days per year), paid holidays (13 days per year), and paid parental leave (up to 4 weeks).

We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, creed, ancestry, national origin, sex, age, disability (physical or mental), marital or veteran status, genetic information, sexual orientation, gender identity, political ideology, or membership in any other legally protected class. We desire priority referrals of protected veterans. If due to a disability you need assistance/and or a reasonable accommodation during the application or recruiting process, please send a request to Human Resources at hrops@fredhutch.org or by calling 206-667-4700.

new_roles.title: Director, Faculty Practice Operations
new_roles.description:
The University of Nevada, Reno (UNR) appreciates your interest in employment at our growing institution. We want your application process to go smoothly and quickly. Final applications must be submitted prior to the close of the recruitment.

 

If you need assistance or have questions regarding the application process, please contact our recruitment helpline at (775) 784-1495 or jobs@unr.edu .

**Job Description**

The Orvis School of Nursing at the University of Nevada, Reno is recruiting for a Director of Faculty Practice Operations within the Office of Strategic Partnerships and Practice (OSPP). The Director of Faculty Practice Operations provides senior-level operational, managerial, and partnership execution leadership for the Office of Strategic Partnerships and Practice (OSPP). This role is responsible for the day-to-day operations and growth of all OSPP practice sites and initiatives, ensuring efficient, compliant, and sustainable operations in alignment with strategic priorities established by the Associate Dean for Strategic Partnerships and Practice (ADSPP). The Director brings strong business and financial acumen, practice management experience, grants and contracts experience, and expertise in community-based partnerships. This position will possess a working knowledge of healthcare reimbursement, medical billing and coding, revenue cycle management, and payer contracting processes in insurance-reimbursed clinical environments. The Director operationalizes strategy through strong infrastructure, systems, partnerships, and team leadership and assumes operational accountability for the financial, compliance, and reputational risk associated with OSPP practice sites, partnerships, and funded initiatives.

 

**Required Qualifications**

Bachelor’s degree and four (4) years of related professional work experience; **OR**

Master’s degree and two (2) years of related professional work experience.

**Related Experience** : Progressively responsible experience in practice management, operations, partnerships, or related leadership roles; experience in healthcare reimbursement, medical billing, coding, and revenue cycle processes, including the ability to work effectively with payer contracts, compliance requirements, and practice finance operations; experience working in a practice environment with evolving priorities and operational needs; people management and team leadership experience or a related field.

 

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Master of Business Administration (MBA) or Master of Healthcare Administration (MHA)
* Eligible for RN licensure in Nevada
* Experience in academic health sciences, higher education, or community-based organizations
* Experience supporting faculty practice, community-engaged scholarship, or interprofessional initiatives
A demonstrated commitment to equity, community engagement, and collaboration 

 

**Schedule and Travel Requirements**

* Variable work schedule
Occasional travel may be required 

**Compensation Grade**

Administrative Faculty – C

To view the salary schedule for this position, please visit: Salary Schedules and select Administrative Faculty by Grade. Salary is competitive and commensurate with related education and experience.

**Remarkable Retirement**

Our retirement plan is beyond compare. Your 19.25% contribution is generously matched by the University. With the faculty retirement plan, you are 100% vested your first day. Sit back and watch your retirement dollars grow! All permanent employees on an annual "A" or "B" contract who are employed at least 50% full-time are eligible to participate in the NSHE retirement program unless they are members of PERS of Nevada.

**Perks of Working at UNR**

* Health insurance options including dental and vision - Health Insurance
* Generous annual, sick leave, long term disability and life insurance – Faculty Benefits
* E. L. Wiegand Fitness Center offers annual or semester memberships and spouse/domestic partner membership options. E.L. Wiegand Fitness Center

* Reno is proud to be a University town! Many local businesses offer discounts to WolfCard holders
* Mountain EAP supports employees (and eligible dependents) through life's difficult moments. Mountain EAP is located in Reno and specializes in counseling and advising services for personal or interpersonal issues.
* Faculty Senate is the principal representing body for faculty. Its membership includes representatives from each academic and administrative major unit of the University. Faculty Senate
No state income tax! 

 

**Grants-in-Aid for Faculty Employees**

The University is proud to provide a reduced-rate tuition benefit to faculty and qualified dependents. Faculty can take up to six credits per semester at a reduced rate. Dependents of faculty have unlimited credits, but in order to be eligible children must be unmarried and under the age of 24 and must receive at least 50% of their financial support from the employee and/or employee’s spouse or domestic partner. Faculty Grants-in-Aid

 

**Faculty Dual Career Assistance Program**

The University of Nevada, Reno recognizes the importance of addressing dual-career couples’ professional needs. We offer a dual career assistance program to newly hired faculty spouses/partners that provides resources and assists them to identify career opportunities in Northern Nevada. Dual Career Assistance Program

 

**Department Information**

https://www.unr.edu/nursing

**Exempt**

Yes

**Full-Time Equivalent**

100.0%

**Required Attachment(s)**

Please note, once you submit your application the only attachment/s viewable to you will be the attachment/s to the resume/CV section of the application. Any additional required attachment/s to the cover letter, references, additional documents sections of the application, will not be viewable to you after you submit your application. All uploaded attachment/s will be on the application for the committee to review. To request updates to attachments, prior to the committee review of applications, please contact the candidate helpdesk at jobs@unr.edu .

**Please attach the following documents to your application**

1) Resume/CV

2) Cover Letter

3) Contact Information for three professional references

**This posting is open until filled**

Qualified individuals are encouraged to apply immediately. This search will close without notice when a sufficient number of applications are received, or a hiring decision has been made.

**Posting Close Date**

Note to Applicant

A background check will be conducted on the candidate(s) selected for hire.

HR will attempt to verify academic credentials upon receipt of hiring documents. If the academic credentials cannot be verified, HR will notify the faculty member that an official transcript of their highest degree must be submitted within thirty days of the faculty member’s first day of employment.

References will be contacted at the appropriate phase of the recruitment process.

Applicants hired on a federal contract may be subject to E-Verify.

As part of the hiring process, applicants for positions in the Nevada System of Higher Education may be required to demonstrate the ability to perform job-related tasks.

For positions that require driving, evidence of a valid driver's license will be required at the time of employment and as a condition of continued employment.

Schedules are subject to change based on organizational needs.

The University of Nevada, Reno is committed to providing a place of work and learning free of discrimination on the basis of a person’s age (40 or older), disability, whether actual or perceived by others (including service-connected disabilities), gender (including pregnancy related conditions), military status or military obligations, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, genetic information, national origin, race (including hair texture and protected hairstyles such as natural hairstyles, afros, bantu knots, curls, braids, locks and twists), color, or religion (protected classes).

**About Us**

The University of Nevada, Reno is a leading public research university committed to the promise of a future powered by knowledge. Founded in 1874 as Nevada’s original land-grant university, the University serves more than 23,000 undergraduate and graduate students from all 50 states and 63 countries.

Classified by the Carnegie® Classification of Institutions of Higher Education as an R1 (“Very High Research”) university, it is also recognized in the Carnegie® Community Engagement classification. The University is also ranked by U.S. News & World Report among the “Best National Universities” and “Best National Public Universities.” It also ranks in the top tier of the WSJ/Times Higher Education World University Rankings and the New York Times’ “Top Colleges for Economic Diversity.”

Since 2009, nearly $1 billion has been has invested in advanced labs, facilities, and residence halls on the main campus. The University is home to Nevada’s first medical school – the University of Nevada, Reno School of Medicine and the Wayne L. Prim Campus at Lake Tahoe, where education, research, and creative work thrive in a stunning mountain setting. The University delivers on its original land-grant mission with outreach across the state through the University of Nevada, Reno Extension, Nevada Agricultural Experiment Station, Nevada Bureau of Mines and Geology, Nevada Small Business Development Center, the Nevada Seismological Laboratory, and Wolf Pack Athletics.

The main campus is in Reno, Nevada, a burgeoning global technology hub with a vibrant midtown and downtown. Found where the high desert of the Great Basin meets the High Sierra and Lake Tahoe, the beautiful, 290-acre main campus is also a Nevada State Arboretum. The University’s physical infrastructure is expanding with ongoing construction of the newly named John Tullock Business Building, set to open in fall 2025. Groundbreaking is also planned for a new State Public Health Laboratory Building on campus, alongside the recent acquisition of 16 parcels near campus, known as “University Village,” to provide affordable housing for graduate students and early career faculty.

Collaborating with world-renowned organizations, the University fosters innovation through initiatives such as the Digital Wolf Pack partnership with Apple, which ensures equitable access to technology for students, providing new incoming freshman or transfer students with an iPad Air and accessories. Google’s TechWise initiate is an 18-month program that fully supports undergraduate students in becoming entry-level software engineers by graduation.

In 2023, the U.S. Department of Commerce’s Economic Development Administration (EDA) announced that Nevada – led by the University of Nevada, Reno – was named one of the inaugural 31 Regional Technology and Innovation Hubs (TechHubs). Nevada was selected from a competitive pool of 489 applicants from across the United States and its territories. Nevada’s Tech Hub will strengthen America’s lithium batteries, critical elements and other electric vehicle materials industry sectors within the state.

Through its commitment to high-impact education, world-improving research and creative activity, and outreach that’s transforming Nevada’s communities and businesses, the University continues its 150-year tradition of benefitting our state, nation and world.

The University recognizes that diversity promotes excellence in education and research. The inclusive and engaged community on campus recognizes the added value that students, faculty, and staff from different backgrounds bring to the educational experience.

Today, the University delivers on its original land-grant mission of access to education and knowledge by investing in the academics, facilities, support, engagement and vibrant campus life that promote our diverse students’ cognitive growth and academic achievement – all while remaining one of the best values in American higher education.

For more information, please visit the University’s website .

**University of Nevada, Reno**
------------------------------

new_roles.title: Director of Operations
new_roles.description:
**Join Our Team as the Director of Operations at ARRO Water Services!**

This position is responsible for providing strategic leadership and oversight of water and wastewater operations across multiple facilities and service areas. The Director of Operations ensures the safe, reliable, and efficient delivery of services while maintaining regulatory compliance, operational excellence, and client satisfaction.

The Director of Operations works closely with executive leadership, operations management, regulatory agencies, and clients to support organizational growth, financial performance, and long-term operational planning.

This role is instrumental in developing high-performing teams and fostering a culture of safety, accountability, and continuous improvement.

**Essential Job Responsibilities**

* Provide strategic leadership and oversight of water and wastewater operations across multiple facilities and service areas.
* Oversee treatment facilities, pumping stations, distribution systems, and collection systems.
* Ensure compliance with applicable local, state, and federal environmental, safety, and public health regulations.
* Lead, mentor, and develop operations management teams while supporting workforce planning and succession development.
* Develop and implement operational strategies, policies, procedures, and performance standards.
* Oversee operating and capital budgets, financial performance, and resource allocation.
* Monitor operational performance and identify opportunities to improve efficiency, reliability, and service delivery.
* Establish and maintain strong relationships with clients, regulatory agencies, and key stakeholders.
* Provide leadership during emergencies, system failures, and regulatory incidents.
* Collaborate with internal teams to support infrastructure improvements, asset management, and long-term planning.
* Promote a strong safety culture and ensure compliance with organizational safety policies and OSHA requirements.
* Support business development, client retention, and organizational growth initiatives.
* Perform other duties as assigned.

**Qualifications**

* High school diploma or equivalent required.
* Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Engineering, Public Administration, or a related field strongly preferred.
* Equivalent combinations of education, certifications, and relevant industry experience may be considered.
* 10–15 years of progressive water and/or wastewater operations experience, including significant leadership experience.
* Pennsylvania Water and/or Wastewater Operator Certification of the appropriate class and subclass required; advanced certifications preferred.
* Valid Pennsylvania driver’s license required.
* Extensive knowledge of water and wastewater treatment processes, PA DEP regulations, and environmental compliance requirements.
* Demonstrated experience managing teams, budgets, and complex operational activities.
* Strong leadership, communication, strategic planning, and problem-solving skills.
* Knowledge of SCADA systems, asset management, and operational technologies.
* Ability to travel regularly between facilities and respond to operational emergencies as needed.

**Benefits**

ARRO Water Services offers a competitive compensation and benefits package, including medical, dental, and vision insurance, a 401(k) retirement plan with company match, paid time off, paid holidays, life and disability insurance, and opportunities for professional development, training, and career advancement.

**Daily Work Location/Hours**

This is a full-time, salaried exempt position responsible for overseeing water and wastewater operations across multiple facilities and service areas. Work is performed in both office and field environments, with regular travel to operational facilities, client locations, and meetings.

Standard working hours are during normal business hours; however, flexibility may be required to accommodate operational needs, including evenings, weekends, holidays, and after-hours emergency situations.

**Pay Range:**

$53.07 - $79.60

A successful candidate's actual pay rate will be based on several factors including relevant experience, skills, training, certifications and education.

Hospital Sisters Health System (HSHS) is seeking an Executive Director-Mission Outreach Operations to join our team. Provides oversight and leadership within assigned areas of responsibility; is responsible for more than one area of service. Manages the overall operational, budgetary, and financial responsibilities and activities. Plans and implements systems that accomplish work objectives and fulfill the mission and goals efficiently and effectively. Plans and allocates resources to effectively staff department and meet productivity and quality goals. Plans, evaluates, and improves the efficiency of processes and procedures to enhance speed, quality, efficiency, and output. Formulates business decisions that are financially responsible, accountable, justifiable, and defensible in accordance with organization policies and procedures. Establishes and maintains relevant controls and feedback systems to monitor the operation of all areas of responsibility. Reviews performance data that may include quality, satisfaction, engagement, and financial reports. Monitors and measures productivity, goal achievement, and overall effectiveness. Participates in the preparation and maintenance of reports necessary to carry out the functions of the area of responsibility. Prepares periodic reports for management to track goal accomplishment.
 
 
Leads colleagues using performance management and development process. Plans and directs the activities of the service areas to ensure timely and accurate information to management and external parties. 
 
Oversees areas of responsibility operations and exercises discretion and independent judgment. Evaluates performance and professional development of staff. Supervisory authority includes authority to hire, transfer, suspend, layoff, recall, promote, discharge, assign, reward, discipline, responsibly direct or adjust grievances. 
 
Position Specifics:
 
o Department: Mission Outreach
 
o Core Function: Leadership
 
o Schedule: Full Time
 
o Facility: Mission Outreach 
o Location: Springfield, IL
 
o Compensation that aligns with your experience 
**Education Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in business or a related field is required.
* Master’s degree in business or a related field is preferred.

**Experience Qualifications**

* 5 years of healthcare, medical missions or supply chain experience is required.
* 5 years of progressively more responsible leadership experience is preferred.

**Certifications, Licenses and Registrations**

* N/A

Job Description

Scheduled Weekly Hours:

40

Throughout communities in Illinois and Wisconsin, 13 hospitals, numerous community-based health centers and clinics, our 13,000+ colleagues have built a culture based on our solid core values of respect, care, competence, and joy. These are the ideals we believe in, work by, and live each day.

Built upon more than 145 years of service to the communities we serve, we now look to the future and our place in it as a healthcare system that strives to continually improve processes, procedures, and outcomes with the latest and most advanced technologies and treatments.

Regardless of how far our passion for excellence carries us, our focus will always remain on the most important person in our entire organization: The patient.

**Benefits:** HSHS provides a benefits package designed to support the overall well-being of our colleagues including their physical, emotional, financial, spiritual, and work health. **Colleagues budgeted to work at least 48 hours per pay period are eligible for HSHS benefits.**

* Comprehensive and affordable health coverage includes medical, prescription, dental and vision coverage for full-time and part-time colleagues.
* Paid Time Off (PTO) combines vacation, sick, and personal days into one balance to allow you the flexibility to use your time off as you need.
* Retirement benefits including HSHS 
 contributions.
* Education Assistance benefits include up to $5,250 of educational assistance each calendar year and tuition discounts to select colleges with no waiting period.
* Adoption Assistance provides financial support up to $7,500 for colleagues growing their families through adoption to reimburse application and legal fees, transportation, and more!
* Other benefits include: Wellness program with incentives, employer-paid life insurance and short-term and long-term disability coverage, flexible spending accounts, employee assistance program, ID theft coverage, colleague rewards and recognition program, discount program, and more!

Benefits

new_roles.title: Director of Operations
new_roles.description:
**Salary:** 140,000-180,000

**Other Forms of Compensation:**

Our Passion is Food! 
 
At Bon Appetit Management Company we are committed to two things, great food and outstanding service! At Bon Appetit you won't find our managers referring to a corporate recipe book or our chefs microwaving the lunch special. We do not have standardized recipes or central commissaries, instead, our chefs and managers are expected to stay abreast of current culinary trends and bring cutting edge food into their cafes. We are a restaurant company that operates in contract food service. That means you will have the freedom to be creative, take risks, and truly shine. We are committed to our staff growing, trying new things, and learning all that they can. Our rapid growth and breadth of accounts translates into exciting opportunities for our people!

**Job Summary**
---------------

The Director of Operations serves as the senior on-site leader and primary client partner for a premier workplace hospitality program designed to deliver an exceptional employee experience through intentional service, elevated culinary offerings, and world-class hospitality. This highly visible leadership role is responsible for building the operation from the ground up, establishing a culture of excellence, and ensuring every aspect of the program reflects the standards of leading workplace environments.

As the face of the account, the Director of Operations will oversee all dining, hospitality, catering, retail, and workplace experience initiatives while serving as the trusted advisor to the client. This leader will drive operational performance, financial stewardship, team development, and strategic growth while ensuring a seamless experience across breakfast, lunch, dinner, micro-kitchens, and a robust catering program. The ideal candidate brings extensive experience in premium corporate dining, luxury hospitality, fine dining, or high-end food service environments and possesses the executive presence, emotional intelligence, and business acumen necessary to lead a rapidly growing operation.

Responsibilities

 

* Serve as the primary client-facing leader and strategic partner, building trusted relationships through exceptional communication, responsiveness, and operational execution.
* Lead the overall account strategy and daily operations, ensuring alignment with client goals, employee expectations, and company objectives.
* Launch and scale a premium workplace hospitality program designed to support significant organizational growth.
* Oversee multiple service platforms, including cafés, catering, workplace hospitality, executive events, micro-kitchens, and employee engagement initiatives.
* Provide leadership and direction to Café Managers, culinary leadership, catering teams, and hospitality staff while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and service excellence.
* Establish and maintain hospitality standards that deliver a highly personalized, white-glove guest experience.
* Drive a culture of intentional hospitality where every interaction enhances the employee and guest experience.
* Partner closely with the Senior Executive Chef to develop innovative dining experiences, culinary programming, and hospitality activations.
* Oversee a significant catering operation, ensuring flawless execution of meetings, executive functions, company events, and VIP hospitality experiences.
* Manage all financial aspects of the account, including budgeting, forecasting, P&L performance, labor management, cost controls, and financial reporting.
* Analyze operational and financial performance metrics to identify trends, opportunities, and continuous improvement initiatives.
* Lead recruitment, succession planning, employee engagement, and talent development efforts across the operation.
* Conduct regular business reviews with client stakeholders and provide strategic recommendations to enhance service offerings and overall program performance.
* Establish operational systems, policies, procedures, and service standards that support long-term scalability.
* Ensure compliance with all company policies, client requirements, food safety programs, workplace safety standards, and applicable regulations.
* Champion innovation through hospitality programming, employee activations, wellness initiatives, and unique dining experiences.
* Create a highly engaged, service-focused culture that attracts, develops, and retains top hospitality talent.
* Collaborate with regional and corporate leadership to support account growth, business objectives, and long-term client retention.

**Qualifications**
------------------

* Bachelor's degree in Hospitality Management, Business Administration, Hotel Management, Culinary Management, or related field preferred; equivalent professional experience will be considered.
* 8-12+ years of progressive leadership experience in premium corporate dining, luxury hospitality, upscale restaurants, hotels, workplace experience, or high-end food service environments.
* Proven success leading large-scale food service, hospitality, or workplace dining operations with significant client interaction and operational complexity.
* Strong financial acumen with extensive experience managing P&Ls, budgets, forecasting, labor models, and operational performance metrics.
* Demonstrated ability to build and grow high-performing teams through leadership, coaching, mentoring, and succession planning.
* Experience opening new operations, launching hospitality programs, or leading rapidly growing business environments.
* Strong background managing catering operations, executive dining programs, VIP events, and hospitality-driven service models.
* Exceptional client relationship management skills with a track record of building trusted partnerships and delivering measurable business results.
* High emotional intelligence with the ability to navigate complex situations, influence stakeholders, and lead through change.
* Experience working within highly visible client-facing environments where service expectations and attention to detail are exceptionally high.
* Demonstrated ability to balance strategic planning with hands-on operational leadership.
* Strong understanding of workplace hospitality trends, guest engagement strategies, and premium employee experience programs.
* Knowledge of food service operations, culinary programs, labor management, purchasing, inventory controls, and hospitality best practices.
* Proven ability to analyze business performance and develop operational strategies that drive growth, efficiency, and guest satisfaction.
* Excellent communication, presentation, and executive-level relationship-building skills.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, financial reporting tools, and operational management systems.
* Demonstrated professionalism, executive presence, business maturity, and leadership credibility.
* Passion for hospitality, service excellence, innovation, and creating extraordinary workplace experiences.

new_roles.description:
Description:

Position: Director of Operations

Company: GlobalMed Logistix (GMLx)

**Position Summary**

GMLx seeks a Director of Operations with a strong foundation in leadership, analytical problem-solving, and execution in complex, time-sensitive environments. This leader will oversee medical-device logistics, product, and customer service across multiple facilities and service lines, ensuring reliable surgical support while developing people, improving processes, and building capacity for growth.

The ideal candidate is a collaborative, customer-oriented leader who has led teams through demanding situations, translated ambiguous objectives into practical operating plans, and delivered measurable improvements. Prior medical-device industry experience is not required; the ability to learn quickly, exercise sound judgment, and lead effectively is essential.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead operations: Direct daily execution across assigned facilities and service lines, including surgical case fulfillment, inventory movement, customer service, and transportation coordination.
* Develop people and teams: Lead managers, supervisors, and frontline employees. Establish clear expectations, coach emerging leaders, and build a culture of accountability and continuous improvement.
* Translate strategy into execution: Turn business priorities into operating plans with defined responsibilities, resource requirements, milestones, and measurable outcomes.
* Improve operational performance: Identify constraints, redesign workflows, and implement sustainable improvements in service reliability, productivity, quality, and cost.
* Plan resources and capacity: Develop staffing models, capacity forecasts, and budget recommendations that balance current demands with future growth.
* Use data to drive decisions: Establish meaningful performance measures, investigate underlying causes of problems, and communicate findings and recommendations to executive leadership.
* Lead technology initiatives: Translate operational needs into business requirements. Partner with technical teams and vendors to test, implement, and improve systems that support execution and visibility.
* Manage customer and partner relationships: Build productive relationships with manufacturers, sales organizations, transportation providers, and internal stakeholders. Resolve escalations, support customer business reviews, contribute

operational insight to new-business pursuits, and align expectations with operational capabilities.

* Lead through disruptions: Make timely decisions under pressure, coordinate responses across teams, and maintain continuity of service when conditions change.
* Support business expansion: Develop the processes, staffing, training, and infrastructure required to onboard customers and launch new services.
* Establish operating discipline: Create clear procedures, strengthen communication and handoffs, and ensure corrective actions address the causes of recurring problems.

**What Success Looks Like**

Success means dependable service, capable and accountable teams, measurable gains in efficiency, and operations that can support continued growth. This leader learns the business quickly, builds credibility with employees and customers, and consistently turns priorities into results.

Requirements:

**Qualifications**

* Progressive leadership experience with responsibility for teams, operational execution, and measurable results.
* Experience working in environments where timing, coordination, accuracy, and sound judgment are critical.
* Demonstrated success improving processes, solving complex problems, and leading organizational change.
* Strong analytical capabilities, including experience using data to evaluate performance, allocate resources, and support decisions.
* Ability to lead cross-functional teams and earn the trust of specialists whose technical expertise may exceed their own.
* Collaborative interpersonal style, with a track record of building trust and alignment across Operations, Commercial, Quality, Finance, and IT.
* Customer-facing experience, including managing customer relationships, service reviews, and escalations.
* Experience managing competing priorities and making decisions with incomplete information.
* Clear written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present recommendations to senior leadership.
* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, business, operations, supply chain, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience.

**Preferred Background**

* Internal sales, business development, or account management experience, including supporting new-business pursuits, solution design, or account growth.
* Strong leadership, process improvement background, industrial or systems engineering, manufacturing, logistics, or another field requiring disciplined execution and coordination.
* Experience leading managers or multiple operational teams.
* Experience owning technology implementation, process transformation, or other complex cross-functional initiatives.
* MBA or other advanced education relevant to business and operational leadership.

identity_held_roles.description:
**Vice President Quality**

**Global Product Distribution Quality**

**The Opportunity**

Our client is a leading global medical technology company looking to appoint a hands-on VP Global Product Distribution Quality. Reporting directly to the SVP of Corporate Quality, you will be responsible for developing and implementing business strategies to effectively manage all global product distribution quality. In this role, you will lead the global product distribution quality organization and processes, holding quality management accountability for all captive and outsourced distribution centres across every entity worldwide.

This is a genuine turnaround and organizational design mandate, rather than a caretaker or step-up role. You will step in to stabilize day-to-day operations, manage significant FDA and global regulatory scrutiny, and reshape the commercial quality infrastructure into a world-class function. For a seasoned executive who enjoys building progressive systems at scale, there is a clear path to expanded enterprise responsibility within 6 to 20 months.

**Key Responsibilities**

* **Global Distribution Governance:**
 Own quality management systems/compliance performance across captive/3PL distribution centres globally - alongside full P&L, budget, and headcount accountability for the function.
* **Turnaround & Future-State Design:**
 Audit current teams, workflows, and systems to close compliance gaps, restructuring the global commercial quality organization into a streamlined, best-in-class model.
* **FDA & Global Regulatory Execution:**
 Act as the single accountable global executive for all distribution-related regulatory inspections, audit responses, and direct agency communications, including intensive FDA engagement.
* **Quality Systems & Digital Traceability:**
 Direct the IT partnership to optimize warehouse management systems (WMS), end-to-end product traceability, inventory controls, and nonconforming product containment.
* **Enterprise Leadership:**
 Serve as the global subject matter expert for distribution quality and contribute to enterprise-wide quality strategy as a senior member of the Global Corporate Quality leadership team.

**Candidate Profile**

* **Sitting or Recent Med-Tech VP:**
 Minimum 10 years of global organizational leadership at the Vice President level within medical devices, capital equipment, or adjacent life sciences—ready to deliver impact from day one.
* **Post-Manufacturing & 3PL Mastery:**
 Deep operational expertise in commercial, supply chain, and global distribution quality across multi-site networks (upstream supplier quality into manufacturing is out of scope).
* **Proven Remediation Track Record:**
 Demonstrated success leading quality turnarounds, organizational redesigns, and systemic remediation under active FDA scrutiny.
* **Global Trade & Customs Compliance:**
 Hands-on command of international medical device regulations, import/export laws, embargoes, import bans, and regional market-entry barriers.
* **Academic Foundation:**
 Bachelor of Science in a medical or applied science discipline

**What Sets You Apart**

You lead from the front with high energy and a clear appetite for complex turnarounds. You combine sharp analytical rigor with executive presence, enabling you to influence across commercial, supply chain, and regulatory stakeholders while building high-performing global teams.

identity_held_roles.description:
**Job Type**
: Full-Time, Exempt
 
 
**Duration of role**
: Permanent
 
 
**Number of Position**
: 1
 
 
**Reporting to**
: Global Head of Compliance, Health & Safety and Quality
 
 
**Location**
: Columbia, MD
 
 
**About Us**
Tate Americas is a key business within Kingspan Data Solutions and is at the forefront of delivering integrated solutions to the rapidly expanding data centre market. We combine engineering expertise, advanced manufacturing and operational excellence to deliver complex, mission-critical projects for some of the world’s largest technology companies.
 
 
With significant investment and ambitious growth plans, Tate is evolving beyond traditional manufacturing to become a fully integrated solutions provider, offering customers a seamless delivery model from design and manufacturing through installation, commissioning and final handover.
 
 
**About The Role**
The US Head of Quality provides strategic leadership of the quality management function across all US manufacturing sites, ensuring products manufactured for data-centre applications consistently meet customer specifications, regulatory standards and internal quality benchmarks. This role is accountable for the deployment and governance of the Quality Management System (ISO 9001) across US operations, the development of Site Quality Managers, the integrity of supplier quality, and the effective close-out of quality non-conformances. Working closely with the US Head of Compliance, Site General Managers, Engineering and Supply Chain, the role holder will drive a culture of Zero Defects, First-Time-Right, and continuous improvement through Lean and Six Sigma methodologies. The role is a key member of the Global Quality, Compliance & Health & Safety leadership team and supports the delivery of the Quality & Compliance Pyramid across all US sites.
 
 
**What You’ll Do**
**Quality Management System Leadership**

* Own and continually improve the US Quality Management System aligned to ISO 9001 and customer-specific requirements.
* Ensure consistent deployment of quality procedures, work instructions, Inspection & Test Plans and control plans across all US sites.
* Provide quarterly reporting on QMS maturity, system performance and external audit readiness.
* Act as the principal quality signatory for US operations at Management Review.
* Ensure calibration programs, nonconforming material controls and change-control processes operate effectively across all sites.

**Site Quality Leadership & People Development**

* Lead, coach and develop Site Quality Managers, Quality Engineers and Quality Supervisors across US sites.
* Establish clear objectives, capability frameworks and development plans for the US quality community.
* Drive a culture of accountability, cross-site collaboration and high performance within the quality function.
* Own succession planning and technical competence development including AWS CWI, AWS CWS, AMPP, Six Sigma and internal auditor certifications.
* Champion a Zero Defects mindset and psychological safety for raising quality concerns.

**Supplier Quality & Incoming Material Control**

* Govern the supplier quality program across US operations, including supplier qualification, PPAP / First Article Inspection, supplier audits and Supplier Corrective Action Requests.
* Ensure robust incoming goods inspection, control of externally provided processes, and supplier performance reporting.
* Drive measurable reduction in supplier-driven non-conformances, line stops and rework cost.
* Partner with Supply Chain leadership to align supplier strategy, approved vendor lists and commercial terms with quality expectations.

**Welding, Fabrication & Coating Process Quality**

* Own the welding qualification program (WPS, PQR, WPQ) to AWS D1.1 / D1.3 and applicable customer standards for structural steel and hot aisle containment products.
* Own the coating qualification program to AMPP (NACE/SSPC) requirements, including surface preparation, DFT, adhesion and cure.
* Establish in-process inspection regimes (VT, DFT, dimensional) and statistical process control across fabrication, welding and paint processes.
* Ensure capable, calibrated inspection equipment, traceable measurement systems and robust Measurement System Analysis.

**Non-Conformance, CAPA & Continuous Improvement**

* Govern the US non-conformance and CAPA program, ensuring root cause rigor, effectiveness verification and closure discipline.
* Drive Lean, 5S and Six Sigma improvement activities focused on defect prevention and reduction of Cost of Poor Quality.
* Establish and track regional quality KPIs and performance dashboards: DPPM, first-pass yield, customer complaints, scrap and rework cost, audit score.
* Lead quality improvement initiatives linked to the Quality & Compliance Pyramid Action Plan.

**Customer Quality & External Audit Face-off**

* Serve as senior quality representative for hyperscale customer audits, Factory Acceptance Tests and customer site visits.
* Manage customer quality escalations, 8D responses and corrective-action delivery with rigor and pace.
* Ensure customer-specific requirements are captured in quality plans, control plans and inspection regimes at site level.
* Partner with Sales, Commercial and Estimating teams on quality-related tender qualification and customer onboarding.

**Governance & Reporting**

* Provide monthly quality performance reports to the Global Head of Quality, Compliance & Health & Safety.
* Support Management Reviews, internal audits and external ISO 9001 surveillance and recertification audits.
* Ensure quality risks are identified, quantified and escalated appropriately within the US operation.
* Maintain regional ownership of Management of Change impacting product quality, process qualification or inspection regimes.

*Additional Expectations*

* Remain compliant with the Code of Conduct and Policies which includes the Kingspan Group Compliance Policy.
* Ensure that all duties related to product compliance are adhered to in accordance with the Product Compliance Policy, Laws, Regulations, and market demands.
* Responsible for all tasks to achieve compliance goals and demands of the Compliance Management System.
* Must raise concerns related to the Compliance Management System to their supervisor, manager, or any member of the Leadership Team, or through the confidential whistle blower service.

**What You’ll Bring**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Quality Management or related technical discipline; advanced degree preferred.
* Minimum 10 years of progressive quality experience in a manufacturing environment, including at least 5 years leading multi-site operations.
* Proven leadership of Quality Managers or equivalent senior roles across multiple sites.
* Lead auditor qualification in ISO 9001 required; additional qualification in ISO 37301 or ISO 14001 desirable.
* Deep experience of welded and fabricated product quality; AWS QC1 Certified Welding Inspector certification preferred.
* Practical experience with coating qualification to AMPP (NACE/SSPC) standards desirable.
* Certified Six Sigma Black Belt or equivalent continuous improvement qualification.
* Strong working knowledge of PPAP, APQP, control plans, PFMEA, SPC and Measurement System Analysis.
* Experience managing quality for hyperscale data-center customers, OEMs or comparable demanding clients.
* Exceptional leadership, communication, stakeholder management and decision-making skills.
* Willingness and ability to travel regularly to US manufacturing sites.

**What You’ll Get**

* This role is eligible for a discretionary bonus.
* Career Scope and Advancement: As we grow, new positions and career opportunities arise, offering accelerated paths for the right candidates, locally and globally.
* World of Wellness Philosophy: We empower you to take charge of your health and well-being. You’ll have access to a wide range of medical, dental, and vision benefits, along with personalized guidance from a “Health Advocate.” We also offer other supplemental options, including 401k, legal, disability, and theft insurance, to ensure your financial wellness.
* Corporate Social Responsibility: Through Planet Passionate we are determined to reduce our manufacturing carbon (CO2e) emissions to as close to zero as technically possible, together with halving carbon intensity in our primary supply chain. We are very involved in our community, and you will have ample opportunities to support us in creating a better world.
* Skills Development: Given the dynamic pace of our business and a strong collaborative environment, your new role will be diverse and multifaceted – allowing you to be more versatile and develop a broader skill set.
* Mentorship and development: At Tate, we don’t believe in hierarchy; we work together as one team for one common goal. You will have access and exposure to our senior leaders and experts for learning in your role, and additional mentorship for the future.
* Culture: We have a great team of culture, highly collaborative, supportive, and social skills. Together we innovate, collaborate, take ownership, and strive for excellence.

Stay connected with us on LinkedIn for insights into life at Tate. Join us in our mission to make a difference through exceptional solutions.
 
 
Tate Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to legally protected characteristics. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities. Employment is contingent upon the successful completion of post-offer requirements, including a background check and drug screening, in accordance with company policy and applicable laws.

Innovative engineered products business unit, part of a global industry serving OEM markets. New role reporting to GM due to growth in product ingenuity, expanding customer base, and increasing demand. Partner with Engineering, Supply Chain, Quality, Finance, and Business Development on strategy and tactical initiatives. Looking for a “lead by example” director with a process improvement mentality. Key responsibilities and opportunities to make a difference:

* Develop and implement manufacturing strategies that align with the overall goals and objectives
* Lead, mentor and develop a manufacturing team of over 100 employees
* Identify and address bottlenecks and rework in a metal working manufacturing and assembly process with 50 to 100 production steps and a strong backlog
* Develop and implement production forecasts, demand planning, and replenishment systems
* Monitor and analyze manufacturing data and KPI performance to make informed decisions about production and inventory management
* Evaluate supplier performance and material management

***REQUIREMENTS:***
BS required; Six Sigma certification a plus. Musthave 12+ years of manufacturing experience with 5+ years leading manufacturing operations within an ISO or AS9100 setting. Ideal candidates might have been employed by engineered products manufacturers for aerospace, automotive, or capital equipment OEMs. Must be on-site Monday through Friday.

***REWARD***
: $200,000 to $230,000 DOE plus bonus, stock/RSUs, and excellent benefits; relocation assistance offered.

identity_held_roles.title: Director, Production Operations
identity_held_roles.description:
**Sierra Space Careers:**
At Sierra Space, we build the missions and systems that keep our world secure in the domain above Earth.
 
 
Sierra Space team members share a spirit of innovation and collaboration and a belief that we can deliver on the boldest missions in space today. Together with our customers, we aim to safeguard our nation, sustain human presence in space, and secure the freedom of operations in low Earth orbit and beyond.
 
 
Our success is measured by the trust of those who rely on what we build and deliver, and our technologies keep the United States and its allies mission-ready throughout space.
 
 
We are mission-driven, and together, we are an extraordinary team.
 
 
**About The Role**
Sierra Space is scaling from development programs into high-rate, repeatable production across a diversified portfolio of military and commercial systems, including satellites and spacecraft, propulsion systems, solar power systems, and the Dream Chaser spaceplane. As Director, Production Operations based in Madison, Wisconsin, you will play a critical role in executing the production strategy for propulsion development and manufacturing, building the operational systems required to deliver hardware at pace, at quality, and at cost.
 
 
This is an execution-focused leadership role for a proven operations professional with expertise in propulsion systems. Reporting to the Vice President, Production, you will lead manufacturing and assembly operations for propulsion product lines and additional enterprise products within Sierra Space's Madison facility. You will drive standardization of production processes, implement data-driven manufacturing systems, and build high-performing teams capable of scaling propulsion output while maintaining quality and efficiency. You will partner closely with Engineering, Supply Chain, Quality, and Program Management to ensure production readiness and on-time delivery of critical propulsion systems for space and defense applications.
 
 
**About You**
Our mission is driven by an unyielding commitment to advancing space-based technology in service of our customers and safeguarding national security. We seek individuals who are passionate about innovating beyond boundaries and relentlessly pursuing solutions that protect, preserve and empower – to join us in this critical mission.
 
 
We’re looking for team members who align with our values, mission and goals – while also meeting the minimum qualifications below. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.
 
 
**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead manufacturing and assembly operations for propulsion product lines, including day-to-day oversight of production floor activities, scheduling, and workflow management at the Madison, WI facility.
* Execute production strategy to scale propulsion manufacturing from development programs into repeatable, high-rate production with a focus on throughput, yield, and cost efficiency.
* Standardize propulsion production processes and workflows to create consistent, repeatable, high-quality build operations aligned with enterprise-wide best practices.
* Support capacity planning and facility buildout efforts for propulsion manufacturing, including layout optimization, equipment installation, and production line commissioning.
* Drive vertical integration initiatives by standing up and maturing internal propulsion manufacturing capabilities, including additive manufacturing, machining, assembly, and test operations for propulsion components and systems.
* Implement and mature manufacturing execution systems (MES) and production data infrastructure to enable traceability, repeatability, and real-time visibility into propulsion manufacturing performance.
* Establish and maintain production operating rhythm through KPIs, dashboards, and review cadences focused on cycle time, yield, throughput, labor efficiency, on-time delivery, and cost for propulsion production.
* Apply lean manufacturing and continuous improvement methodologies (Lean, Six Sigma) to identify and eliminate production inefficiencies, reduce waste, and improve quality in propulsion operations.
* Collaborate with Propulsion Engineering and Product Assurance to drive design-for-manufacturing (DFM) and design-for-test (DFT) into propulsion product development and support new product introduction (NPI) activities.
* Partner across Supply Chain, Engineering, Quality, Facilities, Security, and Program Management to ensure aligned production readiness, material availability, and execution against propulsion program schedules.
* Manage production budgets for propulsion operations and analyze manufacturing costs to implement cost-saving measures that maintain quality standards and support financial goals.
* Lead and develop production management teams at the Madison facility, including supervisors, engineers, and technicians, fostering collaboration and accountability while upholding company values and a culture of operational excellence.
* Ensure compliance with industry-specific production standards, safety regulations, and quality management systems (ISO, AS9100, GMP, etc.) applicable to aerospace and propulsion manufacturing operations.
* Represent propulsion production operations in cross-functional forums and communicate status, risks, and mitigation plans to executive leadership and external stakeholders, including customers and regulatory bodies.

**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in engineering, manufacturing, operations, or a related technical field (or equivalent work experience in lieu of degree).
* 10+ years of experience in manufacturing, production, or operations roles in complex technical industries, with a significant portion in leadership positions.
* The ability to obtain and maintain a Top Secret U.S. Security Clearance is required
* Proven track record of successfully managing large teams and complex production projects in high-rate manufacturing environments.
* Strong background in manufacturing processes, assembly & integration, and operational execution for complex electromechanical or aerospace systems, with emphasis on propulsion systems preferred.
* Demonstrated experience implementing and scaling production operations, including process standardization, workflow optimization, and capacity planning.
* Experience with data-driven manufacturing systems, MES, and production management processes, including OKR development and performance tracking.
* Knowledge of design-for-manufacturing (DFM) principles and ability to collaborate with engineering teams to optimize product designs for production.
* Proven ability to lead multidisciplinary teams and drive operational excellence in fast-paced, highly technical environments.
* Expertise in continuous improvement methodologies (Lean, Six Sigma) with proven ability to identify and eliminate production inefficiencies.
* Strong financial acumen with demonstrated ability to manage production budgets, analyze manufacturing costs, and implement cost-saving measures.
* In-depth knowledge of industry-specific production standards, safety regulations, and quality management systems (ISO, AS9100, GMP, etc.).
