identity_held_roles.title: Director of Manufacturing
identity_held_roles.description:
***Custom Fabrication & Assembly Manufacturing | Southeast Alabama***
**Location:**
Dothan, AL (Onsite).
*Relocation assistance is available.*
**Compensation:**
$165,000 to $180,000 base, plus 10% annual bonus
 
 
**Reports to:**
President, Signage Division
 
 
**Team:**
Top leader on site for a custom manufacturing facility with approximately 125 employees across welding, metal fabrication, CNC, forming, electrical, and assembly
 
 
**Required**

* 7+ years of hands-on manufacturing leadership experience with direct responsibility for plant-level performance, whether as a Director of Manufacturing, Plant Manager, Operations Manager, or similar role
* Experience leading a labor-intensive, high-mix, low-volume operation such as a job shop, fabrication, or build-to-order environment. Broad manufacturing judgment matters more than deep expertise in any single process
* A track record of improving throughput, labor efficiency, quality, and on-time delivery through steady, practical improvements while keeping production running
* Working knowledge of manufacturing cost, including labor standards, earned hours or standard costing, and how floor performance shows up in a plant P&L
* Strong floor presence and the ability to earn trust with a long-tenured workforce, build real buy-in, and hold people accountable when the reasons for falling short do not add up
* Experience building repeatable systems and a leadership structure that keep a plant running dependably without relying on any one person
* Resourcefulness and comfort delivering results in a lean environment without large corporate engineering or support teams behind you
* Clear, professional communication with executive and finance leadership, including regular reporting on plant performance
* Bachelor's degree in engineering, operations, business, or a related field preferred; equivalent hands-on manufacturing experience will be considered
* Genuine comfort relocating to and leading in a small Southern community

**Nice to Have**

* Background in custom fabricated products such as signage, store fixtures, displays, architectural metals, or electrical closures
* Industrial engineering training or a similarly technical, process-focused background
* Experience in a private equity-backed or recently acquired manufacturing business
* Lean, Six Sigma, or similar continuous improvement experience applied in a practical, hands-on way
* Experience scaling production capacity, including adding shifts or growing output in a constrained labor market

**The Opportunity**
Our client is a private equity-backed national company that designs, builds, and installs branded products for well-known multi-site businesses across North America. This role leads their primary manufacturing facility in Southeast Alabama, a custom, build-to-order operation where a skilled team works hands-on with aluminum, steel, and electrical components, producing a wide variety of products in small lots.
 
 
The plant has made steady progress in recent years, with lower costs, better quality, and more reliable delivery. The next step is a strong, hands-on leader who can keep that momentum going and take the operation further. This is not a turnaround and not a maintenance role. It is a long-term opportunity to increase output, keep improving cost and efficiency, and build an operation that runs dependably every day.
 
 
**What You'll Do**

* Own plant performance: Lead every aspect of the facility, including safety, quality, throughput, delivery, and cost, with accountability for the plant P&L.
* Lead from the floor: Spend a good part of every day in production, getting to know the people, understanding what drives them, and building the trust that makes change stick.
* Find early wins: In the first 90 days, learn how the factory runs, stabilize performance, and identify practical process changes that make work easier for the people on the floor.
* Drive throughput and cost: Partner with the division President and finance leadership on a multi-year plan to increase output and reduce manufacturing cost, then deliver against it.
* Build repeatable systems: Put processes, metrics, and a leadership structure in place that let the plant run reliably without intensive oversight or dependence on any single person.
* Develop the team: Coach and grow the existing leadership group, including long-tenured leaders who know the product inside and out, and shape the structure the plant needs going forward.
* Hold the line on accountability: Understand the work well enough to see past excuses, set clear expectations, and follow through consistently.

**Why This Role Is Different**
This is the top leadership seat on site. The division President is based in another state, so this person will have real ownership and autonomy over how the plant runs, along with a leadership team that is invested in their success and has done this job before.
 
 
You will not be starting from scratch. The plant has a solid foundation, a clear direction, and the backing of a growing national platform and patient, long-term ownership. The opportunity is to take what has been built and make it better, with room to put your own mark on the operation.
 
 
**The Culture**
The plant has a loyal, tenured workforce that wants to do good work and takes pride in what it builds. The right person brings both process discipline and genuine people skills, someone who can hold the team to a high standard while building the relationships that earn real buy-in. Leadership is not looking for someone to shut things down and start over. They want a steady, visible leader who can find improvements while the work keeps moving, and who will feel at home in a close-knit, small-town Southern community.

identity_held_roles.description:
Job ID: 530933

Ash Grove is a CRH company with a legacy dating back to 1882. We combine technical expertise, safety and customer-focused solutions to deliver reliable performance for our customers. We manufacture and supply high-performance, advanced cementitious materials for the most demanding construction and infrastructure needs. With more than 2,000 people across 60 locations in the United States and Canada, we support a wide range of applications, from major infrastructure projects to the development and refurbishment of residential and non-residential buildings that support everyday life, from highways and bridges to schools and commercial buildings.

To learn more about us go to www.ashgrove.com

**Job Summary**

The Plant Manager plans, coordinates, and supervises the production operations, hazardous waste fuel program, maintenance activities, quality and safety programs, and other related functions involved in plant operations. This position incorporates directives provided by corporate management into policies and procedures to maintain standards and schedules. The position exercises direct or indirect supervision over a large number of employees.

**Job Location**

* This role will work out of our plant in Louisville, NE.

**Job Responsibilities**

* Promote and follow all plant safety guidelines.
* Conducts meetings with plant staff personnel to communicate, coordinate and discuss plant operations.
* Monitors, inspects, and reviews all plant activities.
* Ensures production schedule corresponds with sales forecasts.
* Assists in investigating customer and quality problems and concerns.
* Meets with government agencies and community groups concerning plant activities to ensure compliance with environmental regulations, policies, and standards.
* Prepares regular reports regarding plant production operations.
* Attends Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA) training for waste-derived fuel activities.
* Promotes effective job performance through motivation, goals, and providing feedback.
* Promotes the safety program, compliance with safety standards, and participates in safety meetings.
* Establishes plant standards, short-term goals, and long-term strategic plans for production, maintenance, and improvements.
* Discusses new products, equipment, and ideas with staff and vendors.
* Analyzes plant costs and explore methods to improve productivity cost-effectively.
* Uses technology to develop a continuous improvement plan for the plant.
* Troubleshoots various problems and performance barriers.

**Job Requirements**

* Ability to read, write, and understand warning labels, instructions, signs, etc.
* Minimum 4 Year - Bachelors Degree in engineering, chemistry, natural sciences, business administration, or closely related field.
* Professional Engineer (PE) preferred
* Ability to develop and deliver effective presentations
* Ability to make decisions and solve problems with high attention to detail and accuracy
* Ability to make sound independent judgments regularly
* Ability to effectively coach and deliver constructive feedback
* Ability to inspire and develop staff
* Proficient in effective negotiation skills in business and construction contracts
* Proficient in Microsoft Office365
* Ability to effectively use computers for general word processing, spreadsheets, presentations, e-mail, internet, and customized company programs.
* Ability to communicate the company's vision into actionable goals and contributions for plant personnel.
* Ability to network with industry professionals, consultants, vendors, suppliers, regulators, and the community.
* Knowledge of safety and environmental health regulations.
* Knowledge of cement chemistry, physical testing, and concrete performance.
* Knowledge of various systems for cement manufacturing (crushing, grinding, pyro processing, chemistry).
* Ability to work from general policies and procedures.
* Ability to refer to supervisor when clarification or interpretation of the organizational policy

identity_held_roles.title: Site Process & Manufacturing Engineering Director
identity_held_roles.description:
At Alstom, we build what millions depend on daily - rail transportation systems that can't afford to fail. We're more than 85,000 people worldwide creating the industry's most diverse portfolio: high-speed trains, metros, trams, maintenance services and integrated systems.

**More Than a Job: A Mission**

We seek a visionary leader to drive process and manufacturing excellence, designing and implementing advanced solutions that elevate operational performance. Join dedicated teams committed to transforming rail mobility, where your leadership shapes the future and leaves a lasting legacy.

**Your Role, Your Impact**

* Lead scalable process improvements to optimize manufacturing efficiency and support growth.
* Foster cross-functional collaboration between engineering, production, and quality teams.
* Ensure reliability and compliance in manufacturing operations through robust systems.
* Champion innovation by introducing new technologies and methodologies.
* Promote knowledge sharing and continuous improvement across the site.

You'll work with sharp, committed teams solving complex challenges that shape the future of mobility, ensuring seamless integration of business and technology.

**What You Bring**

* **Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Engineering or related field**
 .
* **Extensive manufacturing (industrial) engineering experience (ideally minimum 8-10 years), including proven leadership responsibilities**
 .
* Experience in working with an ERP (such as SAP) for Bill of Materials, Routings, Configuration follow-up.
* Working knowledge of Quality and Health & Safety standards and systems.
* Expertise in lean manufacturing, process optimization, and industrial automation.
* Strong understanding of quality systems, regulatory standards, and operational excellence.
* Proven leadership, strategic thinking, and ability to inspire high-performing teams.

**How Success Is Measured**

* Achievement of delivery timelines and strategic manufacturing goals.
* Effective collaboration and leadership across multidisciplinary teams.
* Reduction in defects, increased efficiency, and proactive troubleshooting.

**Alstom, A Great Place to Grow**

* Work with cutting-edge technology and drive strategic vision.
* Make a global impact from our West Mifflin office.
* Advance your career through continuous learning and development.

Here, progress isn't always easy but the impact is real. Because the scale is massive, the tasks are complex when the system runs, the train moves, and the city connects that feeling stays with you. And the legacy lasts.

our LinkedIn page!
 
 
 
Job details:
 
**Strong engineering leader needed with extensive PCB & SMT experience / Relocation assistance available**
This Jobot Job is hosted by: Christine McNamara
 
Are you a fit? Easy Apply now by clicking the "Easy Apply" button
 
and sending us your resume.
 
Salary: $160,000 - $180,000 per year
 
 
 
**A bit about us:**
We are seeking a hands-on Engineering Operations Leader to drive performance, efficiency, and team development within a fast-paced SMT / PCB manufacturing environment. This role will lead engineering and operations initiatives focused on continuous improvement, process optimization, and operational excellence, while developing and scaling a high-performing technical team.
 
 
The ideal candidate brings a strong Lean Manufacturing mindset, deep experience in electronics contract manufacturing (SMT/PCB), and the ability to drive accountability and measurable results across the organization.
 
 
\*\*Relocation assistance available for those not local to the area
 
 
 
**Why join us?**
Medical, Dental, Vision coverage
 
401(k) with company match
 
Relocation assistance
 
Annual performance bonus
 
Generous PTO & sick leave
 
 
 
**Job Details**
Key Responsibilities:
 
 
Operations & Continuous Improvement
 

* Lead Lean Manufacturing initiatives to improve throughput, yield, and overall equipment effectiveness (OEE)
* Identify and drive process improvements across SMT lines, PCB assembly, and supporting operations
* Implement and sustain Lean tools (Kaizen, 5S, value stream mapping, standard work, etc.)
* Analyze production data to identify inefficiencies and drive corrective actions
* Reduce scrap, rework, and downtime through structured problem-solving methodologies

Engineering Leadership
 

* Oversee engineering activities related to process development, troubleshooting, and optimization
* Partner with production to resolve complex technical and process challenges
* Support new product introductions (NPI) and ensure smooth transition into production
* Drive best practices across SMT processes including soldering, reflow, pick-and-place, inspection, etc.

Team Development & Leadership
 

* Lead, mentor, and develop a team of engineers, technicians, and support staff
* Build a culture of accountability, ownership, and continuous improvement
* Establish clear KPIs and performance metrics for engineering and operations teams
* Identify skill gaps and implement training / development plans

Cross-Functional Collaboration
 

* Partner with quality, supply chain, and production leadership to align operational goals
* Drive collaboration between engineering and manufacturing teams to improve execution
* Support customer needs and ensure alignment with delivery and quality expectations

Qualifications:
 
 
Required:
 

* 7–10+ years of experience in electronics contract manufacturing (SMT / PCB environment required)
* Proven leadership experience managing and developing technical teams (engineering or maintenance)
* Strong background in Lean Manufacturing / Continuous Improvement
* Hands-on experience with SMT processes (pick-and-place, reflow, inspection, etc.)
* Demonstrated success driving operational efficiency, process improvements, and accountability
* ITAR eligibility required; experience working in an ITAR-regulated environment is a strong plus
* Individual must be a US Citizen due to ITAR regulations

Preferred:
 

* IPC certification (IPC-A-610, IPC-7711/7721, etc.)
* Experience with high-mix, low-volume or high-speed production environments
* Exposure to automation, process engineering, or advanced manufacturing technologies

Interested in hearing more? Easy Apply now by clicking the "Easy Apply" button.

Jobot also prohibits harassment of applicants or employees based on any of these protected categories. identity_held_roles.description:
**Company Overview**

American Photonics, a portfolio company of BlueRock Global, is a precision optical manufacturer serving the aerospace, defense, industrial, medical, scientific, and commercial markets.

We are strengthening our manufacturing capabilities, investing in operational improvements, and expanding into higher-value precision optics and infrared applications.

We operate in a technically demanding manufacturing environment where quality, precision, accountability, and reliable execution are essential. Our focus is on building a stronger, more capable manufacturing business positioned for sustainable, profitable growth.

**Job Overview**

American Photonics is seeking an accomplished General Manager to lead overall business performance, manufacturing operations, and organizational development.

This is the senior on-site executive position, with direct responsibility for operating P&L performance and leadership across Manufacturing, Engineering, Quality, Sales, Supply Chain, and supporting business functions.

The ideal candidate has successfully led a technically complex manufacturing business, improved financial and operational results, developed accountable leadership teams, and executed meaningful business improvements.

We are looking for a decisive, hands-on leader who understands both the financial and operational sides of manufacturing. This individual must be equally comfortable reviewing business performance, resolving production challenges, developing customer relationships, and working directly with employees on the manufacturing floor.

Reporting to ownership, the General Manager will have responsibility for translating strategic objectives into achievable operating plans, establishing clear accountability, and delivering measurable results. The position will work closely with BlueRock's corporate resources while maintaining ownership of day-to-day business execution.

**Duties**

* Assume accountability for operating P&L performance, including revenue, gross margin, EBITDA, operating expenses, working capital, and achievement of financial objectives.
* Develop and execute annual operating plans, budgets, forecasts, workforce plans, and capital investment priorities aligned with business objectives.
* Lead Manufacturing, Engineering, Quality, Sales, Supply Chain, and business operations to ensure coordinated execution and achievement of company objectives.
* Improve manufacturing performance through effective production planning, scheduling, labor utilization, material readiness, equipment effectiveness, and capacity management.
* Identify and resolve operational inefficiencies, production bottlenecks, excess costs, scrap, rework, quality issues, and sources of margin erosion.
* Establish clear departmental objectives, performance metrics, reporting standards, and management accountability for results.
* Strengthen job costing, pricing discipline, inventory control, purchasing practices, and financial visibility to support profitable decision-making.
* Lead and develop department managers, establish clear responsibilities and decision-making authority, address performance gaps, and build a capable, accountable leadership team.
* Partner with Sales and Engineering to evaluate customer opportunities, improve quoting accuracy, assess technical and manufacturing feasibility, and support profitable business growth.
* Build and maintain effective relationships with key customers, suppliers, strategic partners, and other business stakeholders.
* Improve ERP utilization, operational reporting, inventory accuracy, manufacturing documentation, and process controls to support efficient and scalable operations.
* Evaluate manufacturing capabilities, equipment investments, facility requirements, and process improvements based on operational needs, financial returns, and long-term business value.
* Maintain effective quality management systems, product traceability, corrective action processes, workplace safety standards, and compliance with applicable customer and regulatory requirements.
* Provide ownership with timely, accurate reporting on financial performance, operational results, business risks, and progress against established priorities.
* Lead organizational and operational changes with sound judgment, clear communication, and a consistent focus on employee engagement, accountability, and execution.

**Qualifications**

**Required**

* Minimum 10 years of progressive leadership experience in precision, high-tolerance, or technically complex manufacturing environments.
* At least five years in a senior manufacturing leadership role, such as General Manager, Business Unit Leader, President, VP of Operations, or equivalent, with substantial financial and operational accountability.
* Demonstrated responsibility for a manufacturing business or business-unit P&L, including budgets, profitability, cost management, and operating performance.
* Proven success improving manufacturing profitability, productivity, operational efficiency, delivery performance, or organizational effectiveness, supported by measurable results.
* Experience leading cross-functional manufacturing teams, including Operations, Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, and related business functions.
* Demonstrated ability to develop managers, establish performance expectations, manage organizational change, and hold teams accountable.
* Experience managing manufacturing operations involving complex processes, demanding quality standards, and customer-specific requirements.
* Strong business judgment, financial acumen, and the ability to make timely decisions based on operational and financial information.
* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, Business, or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant executive manufacturing experience.
* Ability to work full-time, on-site in Sarasota, Florida.

**Preferred**

* Leadership experience in precision optics, infrared optics, photonics, optical components, precision machining, aerospace, or defense manufacturing.
* Experience improving or scaling a small to mid-sized manufacturing business, particularly within an entrepreneurial or private-equity-backed environment.
* Experience with ERP implementation, systems modernization, manufacturing cost accounting, or operational restructuring.
* Experience leading manufacturing capacity expansion, capital equipment investment, new product introduction, or business improvement initiatives.
* Familiarity with ISO 9001 quality management systems, ITAR/export-control requirements, and regulated manufacturing environments.

**Compensation** will be determined based on the candidate’s relevant experience, qualifications, demonstrated capabilities, and the responsibilities of the position.

**Equal Employment Opportunity**

American Photonics is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to providing a workplace free from discrimination and harassment. All employment decisions are made based on qualifications, experience, performance, and business needs, without regard to any status protected by applicable federal, state, or local laws.

Join us to lead innovative manufacturing processes that make a difference! We value energetic leaders who thrive on strategic growth, operational excellence, and inspiring teams to achieve their best every day.

Pay: From $1.00 per year

Application Question(s):

* Describe your experience leading precision, engineered, regulated, or technically complex manufacturing.
* This is an on-site in-person position, would commute be an issue?
* What is your earliest available start date?
* Describe the most recent manufacturing company you led, including its products, approximate revenue, employee count, and functions reporting to you.
* Describe the scope of your direct P&L responsibility, including the financial results and capital decisions you owned.
* Provide one example of a manufacturing business, market, customer base, or product line you helped grow. What actions did you lead, and what measurable results followed?
* Compensation is based on experience, demonstrated results, and capabilities. What are your salary expectations for this role?

Work Location: In person

identity_held_roles.title: Global Director of Manufacturing Engineering Services
identity_held_roles.description:
It's fun to work in a company where people truly BELIEVE in what they're doing!

We're committed to bringing passion and customer focus to the business.

Creation Technologies is seeking a Director of Manufacturing Engineering Services to shape the future of engineering across our global manufacturing operations. This is an exciting opportunity to make an enterprise-wide impact by driving engineering strategy, advancing manufacturing capabilities, championing continuous improvement, and delivering innovative solutions within the dynamic Electronics Manufacturing Services (EMS) industry. This position offers the flexibility to work remotely while collaborating with talented engineering and operational teams across our global footprint. 
 
In this role, you will lead a diverse network of engineering leaders and technical professionals, transforming strategic vision into measurable business results. From advancing New Product Introduction (NPI) and Design for Excellence (DfX) initiatives to leveraging advanced analytics, emerging technologies, and best-in-class manufacturing practices, you will play a pivotal role in strengthening Creation’s engineering capabilities and delivering exceptional customer outcomes. If you thrive in a fast-paced, collaborative environment and are energized by solving complex challenges, building technical excellence, and driving meaningful organizational change, we want to hear from you!

**Responsibilities Include:**

 

* Provide global leadership for the Manufacturing Engineering Leaders and teams in development and execution of technology roadmaps
* Ownership and continuous improvement of global business processes including Configuration Management and Engineering Change Orders
* DfM capabilities including Valor DfM analysis, DfM Guidelines development, and best practices for the enterprise
* SMT, PTH, and Box Build/System Integration Routing Definitions, Assembly documents, and Work Instructions processes and tools 
 Procurement Specifications developed in conjunction with Customer and Supply Chain team members
* Product Lifecycle Management processes and tools
* Manage Product Environmental Compliance capabilities and requirements in conjunction with Customer and Quality Assurance team members
* Management of global supplier relationships with various Engineering service and software providers including related negotiations
* Manages the engineering software validation process for PLM, MES, DfX, NPI, Component Data Intelligence and other key applications 
 Works with all site and regional technical and business teams to develop, share, and implement best practices
* Represents the needs from the Manufacturing Engineering team to executive strategic, tactical, and operational

**QUALIFICATIONS**

**Education and Required Experience:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering (Electrical, Electronics, Computer, or Computer Science) is required
* Minimum of 15 years of related experience in a senior leadership and multi-site responsibility role
* Advanced degree in Engineering Management or Business Administration preferred
* Minimum of 10+ years’ experience in Electronics manufacturing of high-reliability PCBA sub-assemblies, assemblies, and system level products

**Skills Required:**

 

* Extensive applied manufacturing experience in Aerospace & Defense, Medical, and Tech Industrial products manufacturing (Highly preferred)
* Familiar with the product life development cycle for NPIs including Planning, Prototype, Qualification, and Ramp to sustaining volume production (Highly preferred)
* Proven analytical, problem-solving skills, and use of advanced statistical tools
* Strong technical acumen, attention to detail, and the ability to solve problems and clearly communicate topics of high technical content across various audiences including customers
* Demonstrated ability to identify & implement best practices
* Proven leadership and project management experience
* Excellent presentation skills and experience in customer relations
* Strategic thinker with a strong learning mindset and passion to support and grow a unique culture
* Thrives on the challenges of continuous improvement
* Driven by a high degree of integrity, with cultural and core value alignment to Creation
* Effective communication to interact effectively with all levels of the organization
* Entrepreneurial, creative and high-energy team player with the proven ability to balance competing priorities
* Deep knowledge of ISO 9001, AS9100, ISO 13485, FDA GMP Regulations, and Nadcap Process Certification

**Requirements:**

 

* Strong understanding of differences between IPC Class 1, 2 and 3 product build requirements.
* Knowledge of advanced Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma principles, tools, and methodologies
* Certified Six Sigma Black Belt/Green Belt an asset 
 Engineering experience in printed circuit board or semiconductor manufacturing is a plus

In accordance with pay transparency regulations, the anticipated starting salary for this position ranges from $150k-$180k USD | CAD annually. Full-time employees are also eligible for performance-based bonuses and a range of benefits. Please note that this salary range is not guaranteed, and the final offer may vary based on experience, education, location, and shift. Additionally, the benefits and programs available may differ depending on the hire date, schedule type, and hours worked.

*If you like wild growth and working with happy, enthusiastic over-achievers, you'll enjoy your career with us!*

Creation Technologies is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, race, color, religion, national origin, disability, protected Veteran status, age, or any other characteristic protected by law.

If you require any accommodations to complete the application process or need the job posting in an alternative format, please email Accessibility@creationtech.com. You will be connected with our Talent Acquisition team.

If you are contacted regarding the position, please inform our Talent Acquisition team of any accommodations you may need during the recruiting process. All information related to accommodation requests will be handled confidentially.

identity_held_roles.description:
**About Monster Energy:**
-------------------------

Forget about blending in. That's not our style. We're the risk-takers, the trailblazers, the game-changers. We're not perfect, and we don't pretend to be. We're raw, unfiltered, and a bit unconventional. But our drive is unrivaled, just like our athletes. The power is in your hands to define what success looks like and where you want to take your career. It's not just about what we do, but about who we become along the way. We are much more than a brand here. We are a way of life, a mindset. Join us.

**A day in the life:**
----------------------

As the Director, SAP Supply Chain Planning & Manufacturing Systems, you will own the design, implementation, and optimization of Monster's end-to-end supply chain planning landscape within the SAP ecosystem. Your primary focus is SAP Integrated Business Planning (IBP) covering demand planning, supply planning, S&OP, inventory optimization, order based planning and the roadmap of S/4HANA.

You will also guide the connected Manufacturing and Quality solutions, including SAP PP, PP/DS, production execution, and SAP QM, so that planning decisions flow cleanly into the plant floor and quality processes. You will set global processes, solution architecture, and governance; lead a team of SAP IT professionals; and partner with Supply Chain, Operations, and Quality leaders to drive continuous improvement and innovation.

**The impact you'll make:**
---------------------------

***Supply Chain Planning (primary focus)***

* Own the global SAP planning solution, with SAP IBP and SAP APO (DP, SNP, PP/DS) as the core platforms, and define the target architecture and roadmap, including to S/4HANA.
* Lead solution design and configuration decisions across demand planning, supply planning, S&OP, inventory optimization, and response/deployment planning.
* Lead planning projects from inception to completion, including implementations, upgrades, enhancements, and migrations, delivered on time, in scope, and on budget.
* Establish planning master data standards, parameter governance, and integration between IBP/APO, S/4HANA, and connected systems (e.g., RTI, CPI).
* Serve as the point of contact on emerging trends in supply chain planning and evaluate solutions that improve forecast accuracy, service levels, and inventory performance.

***Manufacturing & Quality (supporting scope)***

* Oversee SAP production execution solutions so that plans translate into executable production schedules across plants and co-manufacturers.
* Guide SAP QM processes, including inspection planning, batch management, quality notifications, and release, in partnership with Quality and Regulatory teams.
* Ensure end-to-end integration across Planning, Manufacturing, and Quality so the business runs on one consistent process.

***Leadership & strategy***

* Analyze business requirements, prioritize based on cost/benefit, and present a clear implementation roadmap to IT and business leadership.
* Build, mentor, and lead a high-performing global team of SAP specialists and manage system integrator and partner relationships.
* Partner closely with end-to-end solution verticals to understand requirements, manage business risk, and deliver quality outcomes on budget and timeline.
* Engage operations leaders to identify problems suited to AI, automation, and advanced analytics, in line with the Digital Transformation (DT) roadmap and vision.

**Who you are:**
----------------

* Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Engineering, Information Technology, Business Administration, or a related field preferred.
* 10+ years of SAP supply chain experience working on the IT side, including hands-on process mapping, solution design, configuration, and customization.
* **7+ years of hands-on SAP IBP and/or SAP APO experience**, including at least one full-lifecycle implementation you led or owned. APO-to-IBP migration experience strongly preferred.
* Working experience with SAP PP, and production execution, and exposure to SAP QM. Depth here is valued but secondary to Planning.
* Experience with SAP S/4HANA and SAP SCM implementations as part of an IT team.
* Proven track record making solution design and roadmap decisions and leading SAP teams and system integrators.
* Experience aligning teams to a common business process and driving application adoption.

***Preferred***

* Certifications: SAP IBP, APICS (CPIM/CSCP), SAP Manufacturing, or SAP Quality.
* Experience in consumer packaged goods, beverage, or other high-volume manufacturing environments.
* Background with automation and analytics tools and platforms (e.g., RPA, workflow automation, process mining, AI/ML forecasting).
* Technical skills: SAP IBP, SAP APO (DP, SNP, PP/DS), S/4HANA, SAP PP, SAP QM, SAP Analytics Cloud, and Microsoft tools.

identity_held_roles.title: Sr. Director, Additive Manufacturing Systems Engineering
identity_held_roles.description:
**Hadrian - Manufacturing the Future**
======================================

Hadrian is building autonomous factories to reindustrialize America. By combining AI, advanced software, robotics, and full-stack manufacturing, we help aerospace and defense companies build rockets, satellites, aircraft, ships, and other mission-critical systems up to 10x faster and at significantly lower cost.

Following our $1.37B Series D at a $7.87B valuation, Hadrian is rapidly expanding our manufacturing footprint, launching new capabilities across welding, casting, forging, electronics, additive manufacturing, and more, while scaling our Factory-as-a-Service platform to transform how critical products are built.

Backed by leading investors including JPMorgan Chase, Valor Equity Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, 137 Ventures, Lux Capital, T. Rowe Price, and Morgan Stanley, we’re building the future of American manufacturing—and looking for exceptional people to help make it happen.

If you’re ready to take on the most challenging and rewarding work of your career while helping create American manufacturing jobs for generations to come, you’re exactly who we’re looking for.

**Why This Role Exists**
------------------------

Hadrian is building an additive manufacturing capability that runs as part of an autonomous factory, not as a room full of printers. The hard problem is not any single machine, material, or line of code. It is making all of them behave as one system. Systems engineering is the glue that holds that system together, and this role owns the glue.

The Senior Director leads three engineering functions, materials and process engineering, hardware engineering, and software engineering, and is accountable for the digital backbone that binds them to each other and to applications engineering: the architecture, interfaces, and data that connect Hadrian’s Opus platform to cutting-edge additive manufacturing equipment, add automation where it makes sense, fuse sensor data into the part record, and turn a collection of parts into a full, integrated digital manufacturing system built around additive.

The measure of success is not three strong teams. It is one manufacturing system that a customer part flows through, from design intent to qualified hardware, with every decision and every data point captured along the way.

**What You’ll Do**
------------------

* **Architect the system.** Define and control the end-to-end architecture for additive at Hadrian: requirements, interfaces, data model, and acceptance criteria that hold across multiple equipment platforms, modalities, and sites. Treat the factory as the product.
* **Build the digital backbone.** Connect additive equipment, peripherals, and inspection assets to Opus with the same discipline a semiconductor fab applies to connecting tools to the host: standardized state models, telemetry, event streams, and data contracts, with security and configuration control built in.
* **Fuse the sensors.** Bring in-situ monitoring, machine telemetry, environmental data, and downstream inspection into one correlated record per part, then move from monitoring to data-driven release and, where it is justified, closed-loop control.
* **Automate where it pays.** Lead automation across additive cells (material and powder handling, build changeover, part removal and depowdering, post-processing flow, robotics, controls, and safety) with a written case for each: safety, repeatability, and data capture first; labor second. Never automate an unstable process.
* **Lead the three functions as one.** Set standards, priorities, and cadence for materials and process, hardware, and software engineering. Resolve conflicts between them at the architecture level, not the escalation level.
* **Own the applications engineering interface.** With the Head of Applications Engineering, define what a production-ready hand-off looks like, publish the process capability and design-rule data applications engineers build to, and close the loop from floor results back into design guidance.
* **Industrialize the equipment.** Through the hardware engineering leader, own factory and site acceptance, commissioning, reliability (preventive maintenance, spares, MTBF/MTTR), and configuration-controlled modification and upgrade of additive systems, and lead the technical relationships with equipment partners that unlock deeper integration. The machine-level depth lives in that team; the standards and the outcomes live here.
* **Design for the factory.** Partner with Factory Development and Factory Automation on cell and site design: material flow, capacity, simulation, utilities, and the path to lights-out operation for additive.
* **Build quality in.** Make the system itself the evidence: traceability, data integrity, and process control that stand up to AS9100 audits and customer qualification without a separate paper trail.
* **Be the additive voice in Hadrian’s platform.** Carry additive requirements into Core Engineering and the Opus roadmap, and bring platform capability back to the floor.
* **Hire, develop, and retain.** Build a leadership bench under you, set a high technical bar, and make Hadrian the place the best additive systems engineers in the country want to work.

**What We’re Looking For**
--------------------------

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering or a physical science; an advanced degree is strongly preferred.
* 12+ years in advanced manufacturing, with real depth in at least three of these six domains: factory design and industrial automation; semiconductor or other high-reliability capital-equipment engineering; manufacturing software and data systems; materials science and process engineering; quality systems in regulated industries; sensing, process monitoring, and sensor fusion.
* 5+ years leading engineering teams, including leading through managers and building at least one function from the ground up.
* Production experience with metal laser powder bed fusion, as a user of the equipment, a developer of it, or both.
* Has led the integration of complex equipment into factory-level software (manufacturing execution, equipment host, or data platforms), including requirements, interface standards, and acceptance criteria.
* Has taken at least one production automation or capital-equipment program (robotic cells, material handling, or equipment with safety systems and controls) from concept through commissioning in a regulated environment (aerospace and defense, semiconductor, medical, or similar), and has owned the reliability of production equipment afterward.
* Fluent across the stack: can review a process flow, a data schema, a metallurgical cross-section, and a controls narrative in the same meeting, and knows which one is lying.
* Has worked as a true peer to a customer-facing or design function, with a record of building clean interfaces rather than absorbing the other team.
* Willing to travel up to 20%, including to Hadrian sites and international partners. Must meet the ITAR requirements below.

**What Will Set You Apart**
---------------------------

* Ph.D. in materials science, mechanical engineering, systems engineering or a related discipline.
* Semiconductor capital-equipment background: equipment-to-host integration, tool matching, fleet data, fault detection and statistical process control at scale.
* Equipment-maker experience developing or launching metal additive systems (new product introduction, cost-productivity trades, design reviews) in addition to user-side experience.
* In-situ monitoring and sensor fusion implemented in production, with data-driven release or closed-loop control.
* Factory design: material flow planning, discrete-event simulation, and highly automated or lights-out operations.
* AS9100 and customer qualification pathways; familiarity with AM specifications (ASTM F42, ISO/ASTM 529xx, SAE AMS 7xxx series).
* Budget or P&L ownership of a capital-intensive program, with a record of making the build-versus-buy and automate-versus-wait calls well.
* Modern software fluency: APIs, event streaming, OT/IT architecture, industrial interoperability standards (OPC UA, MTConnect), and cloud data platforms.

**Compensation**
----------------

For this role, the target salary range is $300,000 - $350,000 (actual range may vary based on experience).

This is the lowest to highest salary we reasonably and in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. We may ultimately pay more or less than the posted range, and the range may be modified in the future. An employee's pay position within the salary range will be based on several factors, including, but not limited to, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, geographic location, performance, and business or organizational needs.

**Benefits for Full-time Employees**
------------------------------------

* Medical, dental, vision, and life insurance plans for employees
 
 401k
* Relocation support may be provided for certain situations, based on business need.
* Flexible vacation policy
* Equity

**ITAR Requirements**
---------------------

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen or national, lawful permanent resident, protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

**Use of AI in hiring**
-----------------------

Hadrian uses AI-assisted tools in our recruiting and hiring processes to help our team work more efficiently. This may include tools that help organize and analyze recruiting data, as well as an AI-powered notetaker that can record and transcribe interviews and help coordinate feedback. These tools support our team and are not used to make hiring decisions. All candidate evaluations and hiring decisions are performed by humans. If an interview will be recorded, you will be notified in advance and may opt out at any time with no impact on your candidacy. Candidate data processed through these tools is subject to the same protections described in our Privacy Policy.

**Consideration of Criminal History**
-------------------------------------

Hadrian will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of all applicable laws. We do not ask about criminal history on our application, and we do not consider criminal history before making a conditional offer of employment.

**Hadrian Is An Equal Opportunity Employer**
--------------------------------------------

Hadrian does not unlawfully discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, marital status, mental status, physical disability or any other legally protected status. When necessary, the Company also makes reasonable accommodations for disabled candidates and employees, including for candidates or employees who are disabled by pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions.

Compensation Range: $300K - $350K

identity_held_roles.title: Senior Manager, Project Management - External Manufacturing
identity_held_roles.description:
Rezolute is a pre-commercial ultra-rare disease company focused on significantly improving outcomes for individuals with hypoglycemia caused by hyperinsulinism (HI). Our fully human monoclonal antibody therapy, RZ358 (ersodetug), is designed to treat all forms of HI and has shown substantial benefit in clinical trials and real-world use for the treatment of congenital hyperinsulinism (cHI) and tumor hyperinsulinism (tHI).

**Position Summary**

Rezolute is seeking a proactive, execution-focused project management professional to coordinate external manufacturing programs as the company advances toward commercial manufacturing.

The Senior Manager, Project Management - External Manufacturing will manage integrated plans, communications, and deliverables across technology transfer, GMP manufacturing, process characterization, process validation, and commercial readiness. Working with internal functional leads and contract development and manufacturing organizations (CDMOs), this individual will align schedules, supplier commitments, and cross-functional dependencies with Rezolute’s Plan of Record (POR), supply requirements, and business priorities.

This role owns project coordination and follow-through, not technical oversight. External Manufacturing Operations, Manufacturing Science and Technology (MSAT), Quality Assurance (QA), and designated functional experts retain responsibility for technical strategy, scientific assessments, manufacturing process decisions, and quality approvals.

### **Principal Duties and Responsibilities**

Integrated Project Planning and Execution

* Develop and maintain integrated project plans for external Drug Substance (DS) and Drug Product (DP) programs, defining scope, deliverables, owners, milestones, dependencies, and target dates.

* Align project baselines and supplier commitments with the POR, supply requirements, and approved priorities.

* Monitor critical-path activities and progress against plan; coordinate recovery actions for overdue or at-risk commitments with functional owners and suppliers.

* Assess scope, schedule, and resource changes with accountable stakeholders and route proposed changes through established approval processes.

Communications and Cross-Functional Coordination

* Serve as the project management point of contact between Rezolute teams and CDMOs, facilitating cross-functional coordination and timely communication of changes.

* Lead internal and supplier project meetings, using focused agendas to address progress, upcoming deliverables, dependencies, and decisions required.

* Maintain and distribute meeting records and action items with clear owners and due dates; drive follow-through to closure.

Workstream and Milestone Coordination

* Coordinate manufacturing and milestone readiness by tracking prerequisites, including material availability, documentation, internal reviews, and supplier deliverables.

* Integrate technical and quality review timelines into project schedules, including protocols, reports, and master or electronic batch records.

* Track schedule dependencies associated with change controls, deviations, investigations, and other quality-system activities in partnership with QA and technical owners.

* Coordinate handoffs from development and validation activities to routine commercial manufacturing, tracking agreed deliverables, receiving owners, and outstanding actions.

Risk, Issue, and Decision Management

* Maintain risk, issue, assumption, decision, and dependency logs, including accountable owners and required completion dates.

* Work with functional leads and suppliers to assess execution risks and track mitigation actions and residual risks.

* Facilitate issue resolution and escalate unresolved items or pending decisions, clearly communicating timing requirements and potential project impacts.

Reporting, Scope, and Project Controls

* Provide dashboards and leadership updates showing milestone performance, forecast completion dates, critical-path activities, risks, and decisions or intervention required.

* Partner with External Manufacturing leadership, Supplier Relationship Management (SRM), Business, and Procurement to define milestones, deliverables, assumptions, and timelines in supplier scopes of work.

* Support project-level financial tracking with budget owners, including planned work, supplier milestones, and the budget and schedule impacts of scope changes.

* Improve project management tools, reporting practices, and lessons-learned processes across the external manufacturing network.

### **Qualifications/Requirements:**

* Bachelor’s degree in a scientific, engineering, business, project management, or related discipline.

* Minimum of seven years of relevant biopharmaceutical industry experience, including responsibility for managing cross-functional projects involving CDMOs or other external manufacturing partners.

* Demonstrated ability to manage integrated schedules, critical-path activities, risks, and changing priorities across multiple workstreams.

* Experience coordinating technology transfer, GMP manufacturing, process characterization, process validation, or commercial manufacturing readiness activities.

* Working knowledge of biopharmaceutical manufacturing and cGMP requirements sufficient to understand project dependencies and engage effectively with technical and quality teams.

* Strong meeting facilitation, written communication, and stakeholder management skills, including communication with external partners and senior leadership.

* Ability to translate technical discussions into clear project actions, decisions, and schedule implications while respecting functional decision-making authority.

* Strong organization, attention to detail, and follow-through, with the ability to drive accountability and prioritize independently in a matrixed environment.

* Proficiency in Smartsheet or comparable project management software and Microsoft Teams, Excel, Word, and PowerPoint.

Preferred Qualifications:

* Experience supporting late-stage biologics programs transitioning to commercial manufacturing.

* Experience coordinating DS and/or DP manufacturing projects across multiple external partners.

* Experience working in a small to mid-sized biotechnology company.

* Experience tracking project budgets, supplier scopes of work, and change requests.

Core Competencies:

* Project Planning and Controls: Creates practical plans that connect workstreams and support timely delivery.

* Execution and Accountability: Establishes ownership and follows through on commitments.

* Communication and Collaboration: Builds productive relationships and keeps internal and external teams aligned.

* Risk and Issue Management: Anticipates challenges, coordinates mitigation, and escalates appropriately.

* Adaptability and Prioritization: Adjusts plans as circumstances change while maintaining focus on program objectives.

Rezolute (RZLT) currently anticipates the base salary for Senior Manager - Project Management External Manufacturing role could range from $165,000 to $180,000 and will depend, in part, on the successful candidate’s geographical location and their qualifications for the role, including education and experience. This position will also be eligible for an annual performance bonus in accordance with the terms of the applicable plan (depending, in part, on company and individual performance and at the Company’s discretion on an individual basis). The compensation described above is subject to change and could be higher or lower than the range described based on current market survey data and the qualifications, education, experience and geographical location of the selected candidate.

Qualifying employees are eligible to participate in benefit programs such as:

* Health Insurance (Medical / Dental / Vision)

* Disability, Life & Long-Term Care Insurance

* Holiday Pay

* Tracking Free Vacation Program

* 401(k) Plan Match

* Educational Assistance Benefit

* Fitness Center Reimbursement

We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. identity_held_roles.title: Senior Manager, Manufacturing Infrastructure
identity_held_roles.description:
Founded in 2015, Shield AI is a venture-backed deep-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include the V-BAT aircraft, Hivemind Enterprise, and the Hivemind Vision product lines. With nine offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and the Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit Shield Open . Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube.

### **Job Description**

Shield AI is seeking a Senior Manager, Manufacturing Infrastructure to lead the server and network infrastructure for our new 400,000 sq ft manufacturing facility in the Seattle-Tacoma area, home to our newest flagship product. You will own the systems and network engineering that keep the factory running, from build-out and commissioning through ramp to high-rate production, including compute, virtualization, storage, backup and recovery, IT and OT networks, wireless, and the infrastructure behind manufacturing systems such as MES and PLM. You will lead a site-based team of systems and network engineers and partner closely with Manufacturing Engineering, Operations, Facilities, Cybersecurity, Cloud Platform, Network Engineering, and Service Delivery.

This position is based on site in the Seattle, Tacoma, or surrounding SeaTac, WA area.

### **What You’ll Do**

* Own the infrastructure strategy, architecture, roadmap, and budget for the manufacturing facility.
* Lead technology readiness for the facility from design through construction, commissioning, and production ramp, working with Facilities, contractors, and Manufacturing Engineering.
* Build, lead, and develop an on-site team of systems and network engineers, including hiring, on-call coverage, and performance management.
* Own design and operation of the factory network, including core, access, wireless, IT/OT segmentation, and connectivity to Shield AI sites and cloud, in partnership with Network Engineering.
* Own server, virtualization, storage, backup, and disaster recovery infrastructure for manufacturing systems such as MES, ERP and PLM integrations (including Teamcenter), quality, and test systems.
* Provide management oversight for the servers, virtualization, storage, and network infrastructure that host and connect production systems and test and inspection equipment, partnering with Manufacturing Engineering, controls teams, and equipment vendors.
* Oversee site data center, MDF/IDF, and server room infrastructure, including capacity, power and cooling, cabling, and documentation, in coordination with Facilities.
* Partner with Cybersecurity to apply segmentation, patching, vulnerability management, and access controls aligned with NIST 800-171, CMMC, and ITAR requirements.
* Define uptime targets, change governance, and maintenance windows that fit production schedules; lead major incident response and root-cause analysis.
* Drive standardization, automation, and observability, and build repeatable site blueprints for future lines and facilities.
* Manage vendors, integrators, contracts, and budgets, and communicate site readiness, risks, and status to technical and executive stakeholders.

### **Required Qualifications**

* 10+ years of experience in enterprise infrastructure, network, or systems engineering, including 5+ years leading engineers, with direct experience supporting a manufacturing or production environment.
* Experience standing up or significantly expanding infrastructure for a new or large facility, from design through operations.
* Strong knowledge of enterprise networking, including switching, routing, wireless, segmentation, firewalls, and WAN connectivity.
* Experience designing and operating compute, virtualization, storage, backup, disaster recovery, and Windows and Linux server environments.
* Experience supporting manufacturing systems such as MES, ERP, PLM, or quality platforms, and familiarity with how production equipment connects to the network.
* Strong understanding of high availability, capacity planning, patching, and monitoring in an environment where downtime affects output.
* Strong people leadership skills, including hiring, coaching, and developing technical talent.
* Experience managing vendors, budgets, and capital projects, with clear written and verbal communication.
* Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
* Ability to participate in after-hours work and travel periodically to other Shield AI locations.
* This position may require access to export-controlled information, and employment may be contingent on U.S. person status or export authorization.

### **Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience in aerospace, defense, or other regulated manufacturing, including ITAR and CUI environments.
* Experience with high-rate production ramp and Siemens Teamcenter or other MES platforms.
* Experience with VMware, Hyper-V, NetApp, Cohesity, Active Directory, and Entra ID.
* Experience with automation and infrastructure as code (PowerShell, Python, Ansible, Terraform).
* Familiarity with OT security guidance such as IEC 62443 and industrial protocols such as OPC UA.
* Relevant networking, security, or infrastructure certifications (for example CCNP, CISSP, or ITIL).

Compensation Range: $200,240 - $300,360

existing_roles.description:
**Summary/Job Purpose**
The Vice President, Quality Assurance - GMP is accountable for leading the enterprise GMP Quality Assurance strategy and ensuring GMP QA activities are aligned with the enterprise Quality system across clinical and commercial operations.
  
  
This role serves as the final decision authority for product disposition while ensuring compliance with global regulatory requirements.
  
  
As a member of the PSC leadership team, the Vice President, Quality Assurance - GMP partners with clinical and commercial manufacturing, supply chain, logistics, third-party contractors, GCP QA and Quality Systems to ensure GMP requirements are supported, governed and escalated effectively.
  
  
**Essential Duties/Responsibilities**

* Lead and oversee the GMP Quality Assurance department
* Drive compliant execution across all GMP QA responsibilities in alignment with the enterprise GMP Quality Assurance strategy
* Lead organizational readiness for GMP inspections at Exelixis and third-party vendors, including regulatory inspections by the FDA and other agencies and audits or inspections by collaboration partners
* Lead Quality input into GMP quality agreements to ensure they support operational needs, compliance expectations and appropriate Quality oversight
* Oversee final review and disposition of clinical and commercial materials and products in compliance with global regulatory standards to ensure reliability, quality, efficacy and compliance
* Lead GMP Operations QA, Labeling QA, Audit and Inspection Readiness and associated Quality functions to ensure QA GMP operates at the highest standards
* Partner with the Head of Quality Systems to ensure GMP QA requirements are reflected in Quality systems, governance processes, and continuous improvement activities
* Oversee labeling governance for clinical and commercial products to support regulatory compliance and consistency
* Partner with PSC functions to establish effective GMP supplier quality and vendor audit programs
* Ensure independent Quality oversight of manufacturing, testing, distribution and external partners
* Ensure effective execution of investigations, root cause analysis, risk assessments, change controls and CAPAs at Exelixis and third-party contractors
* Ensure performance metrics for GMP QA are established, appropriate and regularly assessed
* Identify, evaluate and escalate product quality risks to senior leadership
* Represent GMP Quality in cross-functional governance forums and regulatory interactions
* Lead and develop organizational capability, including talent strategy and succession planning
* Performs other duties as assigned
* Complies with all policies and standards

**Supervisory Responsibilities**

**Hey! We're Huel, and we're pleased to meet you 👋**

Our culture thrives on high performance, and we set the bar high for new Hueligans who join us.

We invite you to read the advert below for our new
**Head of US Quality & Food Safety**
position to understand the role, and explore our 7 Huel values before applying to ensure we have the right working environment for you!

**The role**

As Head of US Quality & Food Safety, you’ll be accountable for driving our US QFS strategic plan across a complex, international manufacturing base (US/Canada). You’ll play a critical role in protecting our brand and our customers, while enabling Huel to scale safely across the region.
**This is a remote role, but we’re looking for someone who is based locally in Utah and can easily commute into Salt Lake City to meet regularly with the team**
. Here's a glimpse of what you can expect:

* Lead our US Quality & Food Safety (QFS) function, taking overall accountability for food safety and quality across all Huel products and sites, including raw materials and co-manufacturing (RTD, Powders, Hot & Savoury and other categories).
* Lead, coach and develop a high-performing US team of three direct reports (2 US Technical Managers and an Ingredient Quality Manager), providing clear direction, building capability and ensuring strong ownership across the team.
* Define and drive our US QFS strategy, delivering 'right first time' products and an outstanding consumer experience, while setting CPMU reduction targets and driving continuous improvement across all sites.
* Ensure compliance with US food safety regulations and standards (SQF, FSSC 22000, BRCGS, FDA, FSMA and cGMPs), owning and continually improving our Food Safety & Quality Management Systems (HACCP, VACCP, TACCP and GFSI standards).
* Lead regulatory and food safety risk assessments for contaminants, including heavy metals, pesticide residues and other chemical hazards, translating US regulatory requirements into effective risk-management and compliance actions.
* Oversee our US raw material suppliers and co-manufacturers, ensuring ingredients and products are safe, compliant and consistently meet Huel's standards, while working with HQ to establish robust material onboarding processes and building a resilient supply network.
* Take ownership of our end-to-end testing agenda for ingredients and finished products, ensuring timely analysis, monitoring trends and driving investigations and corrective actions where needed.
* Be the key escalation point for US food safety incidents and quality crises, leading decisive responses, clear stakeholder communication and escalation to the Technical Director and SLT when required.
* Work closely with Product Supply and our co-manufacturing partners to strengthen manufacturing controls, ensure consistency and deliver safe, high-quality products across the US.
* Champion continuous improvement and regulatory compliance across our US operations, maintaining accreditations, supporting FDA, FSMA, state-level, packaging, labelling and market registration requirements, and embedding food safety awareness across the business.

Not yet sure if this is the right role for you? Click
**HERE**
to read a more detailed job description.

**What we're looking for in you**

* A proven QFS leader with 10+ years' experience in the food industry (FMCG, manufacturing or retail), bringing deep knowledge of Food Safety & Quality systems across the US.
* A brilliant people leader who knows how to build, develop and inspire multi-disciplinary technical teams, providing clear direction and structure while empowering autonomy across three direct report functions.
* Strong technical knowledge of US food law, ingredients, nutrition and manufacturing processes, including FDA requirements for foods and dietary supplements, with the curiosity and foresight to spot emerging regulatory risks and opportunities and turn these into actionable guidance for the business.
* Hands-on experience working with products similar to Huel's range, including powders and dry ingredient mixes, RTD/aseptic bottling, canning and Hot & Savoury, within a US manufacturing environment.
* A confident communicator and natural relationship builder who can influence and collaborate across NPD, Supply Chain, Logistics, Procurement and Commercial/Marketing teams, while representing Huel credibly with regulators, accreditation bodies and co-manufacturing partners.
* A strong understanding of allergen controls, including the US 'Big 9' allergen labelling requirements, testing methodologies and limits, alongside experience working with third-party accreditation bodies to maintain high standards.
* A degree in Food Science, Microbiology, Food Technology or a related discipline. Advanced HACCP qualifications, PCQI, SQF Practitioner and BRCGS or other Lead Auditor certification would be a big plus!

And as always, we’re on the lookout for new Hueligans who love a fast-paced environment and are always striving to be their best. We want people who aren’t afraid to think differently and push boundaries. If you’re all about setting big goals and believe that amazing things happen through creativity and teamwork, you’ll fit right in at Huel!

**What do we offer in return?**

We know that at times, our teams face demanding pressures, and exceptional effort deserves meaningful rewards. That's why we've created a world-class perks and benefits program designed to support our Hueligans in achieving their best, both professionally and personally, while celebrating the global impact they're making!

💸 A competitive salary range of
**$175,000-$200,000**
per annum depending on your skills and experience

🕖 Flexible working hours

🌴 30 Paid Vacation Days PLUS Federal Holidays

🥤 Free Huel to keep you going

🏖️ 2 weeks a year to work remotely from anywhere!

💰 401K Plan

🚕 Commuter Benefits

🤰 Enhanced Family Leave

🐾 Dog friendly

🏋️ Monthly gym membership contribution plus we will also give you your own nutrition plan!

🧠 Free 1-on-1 therapy provided by
**BetterHelp**

🏥 Private Medical and Health insurance for you, including free life insurance

💸 Paid Employee Referral Scheme

🎉 Biannual events to celebrate success - Have you heard about Huelchella?

**We are Hueligans**

We know diversity isn’t just important... it’s essential. It makes us stronger, sharper, and better at what we do. At Huel, we’re about people, not just sustainable nutrition - real people with different backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives.

We celebrate what makes each of us unique and we actively bring together Hueligans from all walks of life. Because whilst we share the same
**7 values,**
it’s our differences that power our thinking, challenge our ideas, and help us build better products for a global community.

Belonging matters here. So does fairness. We want every Hueligan to have the opportunity to thrive, contribute, and be heard - no matter where they come from or what path they’ve taken to get here.

We don’t just welcome diversity of thought…we go looking for it!

Meet our teams
**here.**

**How will you make your impact?**
As the
**Head of Quality,**
you will leader to define, implement, and continuously improve the Quality Management System across the Americas. This role is responsible for ensuring quality is designed into every stage of project delivery, from engineering and procurement through construction, commissioning, and closeout. This is a highly visible leadership role with direct influence on project performance, supplier quality, operational discipline, customer satisfaction, and continuous improvement across the Americas.
  
  
The
**Head of Quality**
will establish and lead a quality organization that embeds quality into how projects are planned, executed, and continuously improved.
  
  
You will drive a preventive approach to quality by strengthening planning, supplier oversight, project controls, auditing, and lessons learned. You will create the frameworks that connect Engineering, Procurement, Construction, Project Delivery, and Quality into a single system focused on delivering projects right the first time. Success will be measured by reductions in rework and recurring issues, stronger supplier performance, improved audit outcomes, increased first-time-right execution, and the maturity of the quality culture across the organization.
  
  
**What will you do?**

* You will lead the development and continuous improvement of the Americas Quality Management System (QMS), ensuring consistent standards, governance, and accountability across the region.
* You will establish quality requirements and controls from tender through project closeout to ensure quality is built into project delivery from the outset.
* You will implement risk-based supplier qualification, surveillance, inspection, and release processes to improve supplier quality performance.
* You will ensure inspection and test plans align with engineering requirements, contract obligations, and construction execution strategies.
* You will lead audits, management reviews, quality assurance programs, and performance reporting across the project portfolio.
* You will drive root-cause analysis and corrective action processes that address systemic issues rather than isolated events.
* You will establish and lead continuous improvement initiatives focused on reducing defects, rework, and the Cost of Poor Quality.
* You will build and develop a high-performing Quality Assurance and Quality Control organization across the Americas.
* You will strengthen collaboration across Engineering, Procurement, PMO, Construction, and HSE to improve quality outcomes throughout the project lifecycle.
* You will develop quality capability, training programs, succession plans, and best practices that support long-term organizational growth.
* You will assess and strengthen the Americas Quality Management System, focusing resources on the highest-priority risks and improvement opportunities.
* You will establish clear quality governance, accountability, and performance reporting across the region.
* You will standardize project quality planning, supplier quality management, inspection requirements, and NCR governance practices.
* You will improve visibility into the Cost of Poor Quality, quality trends, and leading indicators across the project portfolio.
* You will reduce recurring quality issues, rework, and warranty exposure through stronger preventive controls and root-cause resolution.
* You will improve audit performance, supplier quality outcomes, and project readiness before execution begins.
* You will create a culture where quality is proactively planned, owned, measured, and continuously improved across functions.
* You will build a scalable quality organization capable of supporting Linxon's continued growth across the Americas.

**Who you are?**

* You are an experienced quality leader with 7-15+ years of experience in EPC, power, industrial, construction, manufacturing, or other complex project environments.
* You are proven in leading multi-project or regional Quality Management Systems and driving quality performance across diverse operations.
* You are knowledgeable in ISO 9001 principles, supplier quality management, project QA/QC, auditing practices, and root-cause methodologies.
* You are skilled at translating quality data and performance trends into preventive actions, operational discipline, and business improvements.
* You are experienced in developing quality organizations, improving governance, and building sustainable quality cultures.
* You hold a degree in engineering, quality, or a related technical field, and quality or auditing certifications are considered an asset.
* You are a leader who puts the mission, the customer, and the team ahead of individual recognition.
* You are comfortable making decisions with incomplete information and adjusting course as conditions change.
* You are committed to raising standards while fostering respect, inclusion, and psychological safety.
* You are passionate about developing people, sharing knowledge, and strengthening organizational capability.
* You are trusted because of your actions, credibility, and follow-through rather than your title.
* You are disciplined, data-driven, and focused on creating systems that prevent issues rather than simply react to them.
