existing_roles.description:
Shape the future of quality and patient trust. Join us as the Vice President, Global Quality Control and lead a world-class laboratory network that powers our clinical and commercial programs across the globe. Reporting to the Chief Quality Officer, you will set the enterprise strategy and build a unified, high-performing Quality Control organization that delivers reliable data, inspection-ready laboratories, and timely product release support—while advancing standardization, digital innovation, scientific excellence, and operational performance.
  
  
**Company Overview**
The work we do at FUJIFILM Biotechnologies has never been more important—and we are looking for talented candidates to join us. We are growing our locations, our capabilities, and our teams, and looking for passionate, mission-driven people like you who want to make a real difference in people’s lives.
  
  
Join FUJIFILM Biotechnologies and help make the next vaccine, cure, or gene therapy in partnership with some of the most innovative biopharma companies across the globe. We are proud to cultivate a culture that will fuel your passion, energy, and drive - what we call Genki.
  
  
Fujifilm is globally headquartered in Tokyo with over 70,000 employees across four key business segments of healthcare, electronics, business innovation, and imaging. We are guided and united by our Group Purpose of “giving our world more smiles.” Visit: https://www.fujifilm.com/us/en/about/region/careers
  
  
**Job Description**
Your impact In this enterprise role, your leadership will directly influence patient safety, product quality, inspection outcomes, batch disposition timelines, and continuity of supply across a diverse global portfolio. You will advise senior executives on investment, capacity, technology, organizational design, and regulatory strategy—shaping multi‑year business and quality plans. Your decisions will strengthen client trust, accelerate revenue recognition, reduce the cost of quality, and protect the company’s license to operate.
  
  
What you will do
  
  

* Define and execute a global Quality Control strategy, operating model, and multi‑year roadmap across sites, modalities, and development phases. Establish enterprise standards, clear decision rights, and governance forums that enable consistent, phase‑appropriate control while allowing justified site or platform differences.
* Provide executive oversight of end‑to‑end Quality Control operations, including analytical, biochemical, biological, microbiological, raw‑material, in‑process, release, and stability testing; as well as environmental and utility monitoring. Ensure capacity, prioritization, and flawless execution to meet program milestones, product disposition, client commitments, and uninterrupted supply.
* Govern the analytical method lifecycle from early development through transfer, qualification, validation, comparability, continued performance verification, and retirement. Ensure control strategies and specifications evolve appropriately through clinical development, process performance qualification, launch, and sustained commercial supply.
* Set global expectations for current good manufacturing practice, applicable good laboratory practice principles, data governance, principles that ensure data are attributable, legible, contemporaneous, original, accurate and complete, laboratory investigations, out of specification and out of trend management, corrective and preventive action effectiveness, change control, and audit readiness. Lead enterprise strategy and executive response for regulatory inspections and critical client audits.
* Build and deliver the digital and technology roadmap for laboratory information management systems, electronic laboratory notebooks, laboratory execution systems, chromatography data systems, laboratory automation, advanced analytics, and instrument connectivity. Sponsor validated deployment, master‑data governance, cybersecurity, and adoption that improve right‑first‑time outcomes and cycle time.
* Direct enterprise Quality Control capacity planning, capital prioritization, make‑versus‑buy decisions, laboratory footprint strategy, and governance of external testing partners. Align resources and contingency plans with demand forecasts, technology transfers, new product introductions, and network resiliency needs.
* Establish enterprise metrics and management review for on‑time testing and release support, lead time, invalid results, out of specification and out of trend rates, investigation cycle time, corrective and preventive action effectiveness, stability execution, method performance, cost, and productivity. Drive risk‑based priorities, Lean practices, and cross‑site learning to deliver sustainable improvement.
* Serve as the senior Quality Control liaison for strategic clients, regulatory authorities, and executive governance. Translate complex laboratory, method, and compliance risks into clear business implications, negotiate technically sound solutions, and ensure commitments are realistic, documented, and delivered.
* Build and lead a global organization through senior leaders. Define capabilities and succession plans, develop technical career paths and communities of practice, and cultivate a culture of scientific rigor, transparency, accountability, inclusion, and proactive risk management.
* Own escalation and coordinated response for significant Quality Control events, laboratory constraints, critical data‑integrity concerns, assay failures, method or specification issues, and testing disruptions. Make or recommend risk‑based decisions on testing strategy, product impact, remediation, and continuity of supply.
* Perform other duties in support of the broader Global Quality strategy and company objectives.

**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Chemistry, Biochemistry, Biology, Microbiology, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Engineering, or a related scientific discipline, with fifteen or more years of progressive experience in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or contract development and manufacturing organization Quality Control; or a Master’s degree with ten or more years.
* Ten or more years of people leadership, including five or more years leading senior leaders with accountability for multiple laboratories, sites, or functional areas.
* Demonstrated leadership of Quality Control across development and commercial stages, including method transfer, qualification and validation, release and stability testing, microbiology, and environmental and utility monitoring.
* Proven experience with global regulatory inspections and client audits, and with complex out of specification, out of trend, data‑integrity, and laboratory‑compliance matters.
* Experience managing budgets, capital portfolios, headcount, capacity, external laboratories, and enterprise transformation in a matrixed global organization.
* Executive‑level communication and client‑facing experience in a regulated, technically complex environment.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Advanced scientific degree and/or a Master of Business Administration.
* Global leadership within a contract development and manufacturing organization supporting biologics, vaccines, advanced therapies, or sterile manufacturing.
* Experience scaling Quality Control from clinical development through process performance qualification, launch, and sustained commercial supply.
* Working knowledge of the following: Food and Drug Administration; European Medicines Agency; Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency; Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency; International Council for Harmonisation guidelines Q2, Q5, Q6, Q9, Q10, and Q14; United States Pharmacopeia; European Pharmacopoeia; Japanese Pharmacopoeia; Title 21 of the Code of Federal Regulations Parts 210, 211, and 11; and European Union Good Manufacturing Practice Annexes 1 and 11; as well as applicable data‑integrity expectations.
* Experience deploying global laboratory information management systems and laboratory digitalization and automation.
* Credentials from the American Society for Quality, and training in Lean and Six Sigma or equivalent quality and operational excellence disciplines.

If you are a strategic, hands‑on executive who thrives at the intersection of science, operations, and leadership, we would love to hear from you. Apply today and help us raise the bar for quality worldwide.

**Description**

**Company & Job Overview:**

Diality is a medical device company focused on developing solutions to improve lives impacted by kidney disease. Diality offers the Moda-flx Hemodialysis System, a user-friendly, mobile, and connected hemodialysis system designed to maximize clinical flexibility and ease-of-use for both clinical and non-clinical users. The Moda-flx Hemodialysis system combines flow rate capabilities of conventional in-center dialysis devices with a fully integrated reverse osmosis (RO) water filtration system to provide a broad range of prescriptions and meet the needs of any professional dialysis care setting.

The Vice President of Manufacturing is a strategic executive responsible for leading the end-to-end operational strategy, including manufacturing, supply chain, procurement, and logistics. The ideal candidate will scale our production capabilities, optimize global supply chain resilience, and ensure uncompromising compliance with FDA, ISO 13485, and GMP regulations. This leader will bridge the gap between R&D, product development, and commercialization to deliver high-quality, cost-effective medical devices to the market

existing_roles.title: Director of Manufacturing and Quality
existing_roles.description:
Bolt Graphics is a semiconductor startup based in Sunnyvale, CA building the fastest and most efficient graphics processors. We pride ourselves on our first principles approach to solving problems. We are energized by our mission to reduce the barrier of entry for content creation and consumption. Our goal is to enable everyone to easily create, simulate and consume immersive experiences as vividly as they can imagine them.
  
  
****Our Values****

* Be Fearless: Unmute yourself. Test boundaries and get proven right.
* Remain Adaptable: Stay comfortable in a continuously changing world. If you’re wrong, concede and move on.
* Educate Your Ego: Selflessly collaborate towards our shared purpose.

**About The Role**
Reporting directly to the VP of Manufacturing Operations, the Director of Manufacturing and Quality will hold complete accountability for the global manufacturing strategy, production execution, and end-to-end quality management of Bolt’s hardware portfolio. This leadership role spans the entire product lifecycle—from early NPI (New Product Introduction) and design-for-manufacturability (DFM) reviews to high-volume mass production, factory consolidation, and field quality tracking.
  
  
The ideal candidate has a proven track record of unifying multi-site manufacturing footprints, establishing overseas extended factories (particularly in Asia), and scaling rigorous Quality Management Systems (QMS). You will lead a cross-functional team of manufacturing, test, and quality engineers to achieve world-class production yields and flawless execution.
  
  
**What You'll Do**
****Global Manufacturing Strategy & Execution****

* Production Footprint Optimization: Architect and execute the global manufacturing strategy, including the optimization of domestic facilities and the successful launch and stabilization of overseas extended factories.
* NPI to Mass Production Scaling: Drive the seamless operational handoff of complex hardware products from design engineering into high-volume manufacturing. Establish robust New Product Introduction (NPI) playbooks.
* Capacity & Efficiency Optimization: Drive line balancing, automation initiatives, and factory layout designs to optimize throughput, maximize capital expenditure efficiency, and reduce cycle times.
* Vendor & CM Operations: Manage technical execution at tier-1 Contract Manufacturers (CMs) and ODMs. Partner with Supply Chain to hold vendors accountable to strict operational SLAs.

****End-to-End Quality Engineering & Compliance****

* QMS Leadership: Own, scale, and continuous improve Bolt’s global Quality Management System (QMS) across all manufacturing sites and external partners, ensuring compliance with relevant international standards.
* Advanced Quality Planning: Embed Design for Manufacturability, Assembly, and Test (DFM/DFA/DFT) early in the product development cycle. Implement robust PFMEA (Process Failure Mode and Effects Analysis) and control plans at all factory levels.
* Yield & Reliability Maximization: Drive rigorous statistical process control (SPC) on the factory floor. Analyze complex test data to root-cause and eliminate component-level, PCBA-level, and system-level failures.
* Closed-Loop Corrective Action: Lead global failure analysis (FA) and Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) processes for manufacturing escapes and field returns, ensuring engineering feedback loops are closed instantly.

****Team Leadership & Executive Advisory****

* Organizational Scaling: Build, mentor, and lead a high-performing international team of Manufacturing, Test, and Supplier Quality Engineers.
* Executive Metrics Dashboard: Define, track, and regularly report on mission-critical operational metrics (First Pass Yield, Cost of Poor Quality, OEE, Scrap Rate, and Field Defect Rates) to the VP of Operations and the executive leadership team.

**Qualifications**

* 10+ years of progressive leadership experience in hardware manufacturing operations, NPI, and quality engineering within high-tech electronics, compute hardware, or complex electromechanical industries.

**Proven Delivery Track Record**

* Direct experience establishing and scaling overseas manufacturing facilities/extended factories (particularly in Taiwan, China, or Southeast Asia) and managing Tier-1 EMS/CM partners.

**Technical Depth**

* Deep understanding of both Electrical fabrication (SMT lines, PCBA testing, ICT/FCT fixtures, thermal management) and Mechanical processes (precision machining, die-casting, custom tooling, injection molding).

**Quality Methodologies**

* Expert knowledge of advanced quality tools (Six Sigma Black Belt preferred, Lean Manufacturing, SPC, 8D problem solving, FMEA, Gauge R&R).
* System Familiarity: Extensive experience utilizing PLM (e.g., Arena, Agile), ERP, and manufacturing execution systems (MES) to drive process discipline.

**Education**

* Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related technical discipline. An MS in Engineering or an MBA is highly desirable.

**Travel**

* Ability to travel globally (up to 30-40%) to domestic facilities and international manufacturing sites to lead factory bring-ups, line audits, and critical business reviews.
* Targeting cross-functional team scaling, standard setting, and unifying overseas extended factories.

**Unifying Global Quality Culture**

* "When scaling an operational footprint that includes both domestic facilities and overseas extended factories in Asia, a disconnect in quality culture often emerges. How do you instill a unified, proactive quality mindset across geographically separated teams so that local operators and remote contract manufacturers take joint ownership of quality standards rather than treating them as a checkbox exercise?"

**Developing & Mentoring Specialized Engineers**

* "Manufacturing, Test, and Supplier Quality Engineering require vastly different technical skillsets. How do you approach building out a career progression track and mentoring framework for these distinct functions? Can you give an example of how you coached a junior engineer to effectively stand their ground during an aggressive yield dispute with a tier-1 global ODM?"

**Managing Cross-Functional Friction (Engineering Vs. Operations)**

Please review the job details below.
  
  
Intuitive Machines - West is currently seeking a courageous, innovative, multi-skilled Director of High-Rate AIT Production to join our spacecraft production team in Palo Alto, CA.
  
  
**Life with Us**
Your Project: Intuitive Machines is a world leader in high-power spacecraft, having delivered some of the largest and highest-power spacecraft in the world. We are now looking to take this legacy of excellence to the next level, architecting a high-volume production line to build a large number of advanced spacecraft.
  
  
In this role, you will architect and implement a high-volume assembly, integration, and test (AIT) production line for these next-generation vehicles. You will be responsible for transforming our AIT operations from low-rate to high-rate production, establishing scalable processes and organizational capabilities to support our ambitious production targets. The scope includes complete spacecraft AIT from component receipt through final acceptance testing, encompassing electrical systems integration, solar array integration with the spacecraft bus, battery integration, advanced thermal solutions, and comprehensive environmental testing at production scale.
  
  
A critical aspect of this role is developing an efficient, right-sized test program—one that provides high confidence the vehicles will perform as designed while eliminating non-value-added test activities that add cost and schedule without commensurate risk reduction. You will apply rigorous engineering judgment to distinguish between essential verification activities and legacy testing practices that may not be necessary for production-rate vehicles.
  
  
We are looking for leaders to bravely challenge conventional AIT approaches and establish production-rate processes for these advanced systems. You will play an essential role in applying design-for-manufacturing/design-for-test (DFM/DFT) principles to develop AIT specifications and manufacturing plans suitable for volume production. Additionally, you will represent AIT capabilities during customer proposal efforts, providing technical credibility and instilling confidence in our ability to execute high-volume production of complex spacecraft.
  
  
Your Career: We're very serious about professional development and continuing education at Intuitive Machines - West. We offer our team members the opportunity to define their own career trajectory. You will work with your manager to set goals and design a development plan to advance your career. This unique opportunity is a high-visibility role critical to our company's leadership position in spacecraft manufacturing.
  
  
What We Offer: Time for dedicated professional development, conference attendance, industry training, peer group collaboration, as well as paid certifications and education reimbursement.
  
  
Who you will work with: You will report to the VP of Spacecraft Production and Operations and collaborate closely with Engineering, Quality, and Supply Chain teams. You will lead a team of AIT production engineers and technicians while partnering with design engineering to ensure producibility of our spacecraft systems. You will also engage directly with potential customers during proposal phases to communicate our production and test capabilities.

* Establish scalable AIT work instructions, process controls, and quality gates
* Lead development of an efficient, risk-informed test program that ensures vehicle performance confidence while eliminating non-value-added testing
* Oversee spacecraft-level integration of solar arrays, batteries, and other major subsystems with the spacecraft bus

**What We Look For In Team Members**
As a team member at Intuitive Machines - West, we expect you to demonstrate honesty, integrity, innovation, collaboration, and a commitment to excellence.
  
  
**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering or related technical field. Four additional years of experience may be substituted for a degree
* Minimum of 15 years related aerospace manufacturing/AIT experience
* Minimum of 7 years leadership experience in production or manufacturing engineering
* Experience working cross-functionally within a company and/or with external partners and contractors
* Proven track record scaling aerospace production operations

**Preferred Qualifications**

**Build Our Future Together**
At Regeneron, we use science and innovation to develop life-changing medicines for people with serious diseases. Regeneron is currently looking for a Director of Internal Fill Finish Manufacturing to join our Industrial Operations and Product Supply (IOPS) team. This leadership role is accountable for the aseptic filling operation for clinical and commercial drug products, including vials and syringes in both liquid and lyophilized formats. The Director owns the full filling value stream: materials management; preparation of equipment, format parts, and components; formulation of drug product and placebo; aseptic filling; and lyophilization. The Director also ensures a seamless handoff to downstream finishing operations (Visual Inspection, syringe safety systems and autoinjector assembly, packaging, labeling, and serialization) and oversees facility cleaning and contamination control for the filling suites.
  
  
This role focuses on the start-up and execution of compliant GMP aseptic operations, ensuring the facility is properly staffed and trained, and supporting a dynamic, flexible production planning process that meets the needs of Regenerons patients. The Director will work directly with Drug Substance and Finish manufacturing management to ensure production timelines are met and will be a key member of various management teams within IOPS.
  
  
This position offers the opportunity to contribute to a fast-growing, science-driven organization making a meaningful difference to patients worldwide.
  
  
**When & Where**
Location: Rensselaer, NY
  
  
Work model: Monday- Friday, 8am-4:30pm
  
  
**Discover Your Role**
Provides leadership, vision, and management to the Filling team and its supporting functions, and leads all aspects of Filling operations at the facility to manufacture commercial and clinical parenteral medicines according to approved protocols, regulations, and schedules
  
  
Directly oversees aseptic filling of drug product and placebo into vials and syringes, in liquid and lyophilized formats, including stoppering, capping, and crimping
  
  
Directly oversees formulation of bulk drug product and placebo, including solution preparation and sterile filtration
  
  
Directly oversees preparation of equipment, format parts, and components to support aseptic filling, including washing, depyrogenation, sterilization, and setup of filling lines
  
  
Directly oversees lyophilization operations, including loading, cycle execution, and unloading, as well as the management of materials and components required to support filling operations
  
  
Directly oversees cleaning and sanitization of filling suites, including Graded space (Grade AD) and Controlled Non-Classified rooms (iCNC), and supports the site contamination control strategy, environmental monitoring, and aseptic process simulations (media fills)
  
  
Ensures a smooth, timely handoff of filled product to downstream finishing operations (Visual Inspection, assembly, packaging, and labeling) in partnership with the leaders of those areas
  
  
Troubleshoots and resolves issues impeding filling deliverables, including equipment performance, line interventions, and yield; provides technical input to resolve filling and aseptic process challenges
  
  
Partners with department Directors and Project Management to implement new filling processes, including new formats, PFS and vial filling lines, formulation, aseptic filling, and lyophilization
  
  
Manages department metrics and goals, monitors performance to objectives, and drives continuous improvement initiatives essential to meeting patient and business needs
  
  
Leads the annual merit performance review process, builds departmental structure, and develops long-term staffing plans, including aseptic gowning qualification and training programs
  
  
Collaborates with department Directors to support development of the annual budget, and rapidly and accurately communicates issues to department Directors
  
  
Writes, reviews, and/or approves Standard Operating Procedures, specifications, regulatory filings, or other controlled documents as needed
  
  
Executes Quality Management System assignments (CAPA, Deviation, Investigation, Change Control, etc.)

Oversees, supports, and participates in cGMP audits of all filling areas within the facility; maintains site inspection readiness and represents the filling operation during regulatory and client audits

BS in any of the physical or biological sciences or chemical engineering, with biopharmaceutical/biotech experience in a GMP drug product production facility, including aseptic filling experience, or an equivalent combination of education and experienceDirector: 12+ years of experience

This role serves as the primary architect of operational excellence moving the organization toward more data-driven decisions. The Director standardizes processes, drives toward modern manufacturing systems (KPIs, OEE, ERP), ensures food safety, and champions the successful implementation and optimization of our core cheesecake production lines.

---

**Primary Duties & Responsibilities**

**1. Change Management & Professionalization**

· Standardize Operations: Develop, implement, and enforce standard operating procedures (SOPs) across both plants to ensure consistency in quality, safety, and efficiency.

· Cultivate Leadership: Mentor, coach, and upskill plant managers and front-line supervisors, shifting the culture from firefighting to proactive, structured problem-solving.

· Data-Driven Culture: Introduce and track rigorous key performance indicators (KPIs) and Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) metrics to guide daily, weekly, and monthly business reviews.

**2. Core Product Implementation & Optimization (Cheesecake Operations)**

· Product Optimization: Partner with the Senior Production Manager to evaluate all new cheesecake formulas, sizes, and configurations introduced into production.

· Constraint Assessment: Review new product introductions to assess potential issues or constraints affecting quality performance, labor efficiency, run rates, and operating costs.

· Executional Direction: Provide hands-on, "feet-on-the-floor" leadership to the operations team during major line optimizations, ERP system changes, and plant renovations.

**3. Food Safety, Quality & Compliance**

· Regulatory & Legality: Ensure both facilities strictly adhere to FDA, USDA, OSHA, and local regulations, taking ultimate responsibility for the safety and legality of all food products.

· Audit Readiness: Maintain "always audit-ready" standards for SQF, BRC, or other GFSI-benchmarked certifications and retail customer audits.

· Safety Culture: Champion a zero-injury safety culture through robust Hazard Identification, training, and behavioral safety programs.

4. Financial & Strategic Management

· CAPEX Planning: Identify, justify, and execute capital expenditure (CAPEX) projects aimed at automation, capacity expansion, and facility modernization.

---

· Experience: 10+ years of progressive food production operations management experience, with at least 5+ years in a multi-plant or regional leadership role.

· Scale & Product Expertise: Proven track record of managing a large workforce (500–1,000+ employees) in high-volume environments, with deep knowledge of automated bakery or cheesecake production processes.

· Education: Bachelor’s degree in Food Science, Engineering, Business Administration, or a related technical field. An MBA or advanced degree is preferred.

· Certifications: Lean/Six Sigma Green or Black Belt highly desirable. Full understanding of SQF/BRC and HACCP systems.

---

This is a key senior leadership position responsible for ensuring the successful manufacturing, assembly, integration, and delivery of ASI's advanced simulation and military training device hardware.
  
  
Based in Tampa, Florida, and reporting directly to the Chief Operating Officer (COO), the Director of Production will oversee Production Control, Material Control, and Manufacturing through functional managers and department leads. The position will also provide executive oversight of Facility Management and Workplace Safety through the Facilities Manager.
  
  
The successful candidate will bring demonstrated experience leading complex manufacturing operations, developing high-performing teams, managing production capacity and resources, and delivering technical products in demanding, schedule-driven environments.
  
  
This individual will play an important role in supporting ASI's Department of Defense, U.S. military, government agency, and defense industry programs while ensuring the organization is positioned to support new business opportunities and long-term growth.

* Establish production priorities, performance expectations, resource requirements, and organizational objectives.
* Lead through functional managers, promoting accountability, operational discipline, and effective execution.
* Ensure production operations consistently meet contractual commitments, customer requirements, program milestones, and delivery schedules.
* Partner with executive leadership to develop operational strategies supporting current programs and future business growth.
* Establish and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) to measure organizational effectiveness and drive improvement.

*Production Planning & Program Execution*

* Ensure production readiness, including personnel, materials, equipment, facilities, documentation, and approved manufacturing processes.
* Identify and mitigate production risks that could impact cost, schedule, quality, or customer delivery.
* Support program reviews, production readiness assessments, customer meetings, and government inspections.

* Support the integration of major simulation hardware components, including visual display systems, motion platforms, and associated subsystems.
* Ensure manufacturing activities follow approved engineering drawings, Bills of Materials (BOMs), configuration requirements, and engineering change processes.

* Develop staffing and workforce plans to support current and anticipated production requirements.
* Identify workforce development needs and implement appropriate training and cross-training initiatives.
* Build organizational depth through succession planning, leadership development, and employee engagement.
* Foster a culture centered on safety, quality, teamwork, accountability, and continuous improvement.

*Materials Management & Supply Chain Coordination*

* Monitor material shortages, supplier performance, inventory levels, and long-lead procurement requirements.
* Establish appropriate material priorities based on program schedules and contractual commitments.

*Quality & Regulatory Compliance*

. Are you ready to move the world forward? Apply now.
  
  
**A Brief Summary Of This Position**
The Plant Manager is accountable for end-to-end operations of the Elkhart plant and for achieving Safety, Quality, Delivery, and Cost (SQDC) objectives. The incumbent provides leadership, direction, planning, and control across manufacturing, materials/purchasing, production scheduling, and shipping to ensure products are produced safely, meet customer and regulatory requirements, and are delivered complete and on time. This role drives continuous improvement and operational excellence, develops and coaches leaders, and manages budgets and cost controls to optimize productivity, quality performance, and overall plant profitability.
  
  
**Essential Functions**

* Ensure that all administrative, supervisory and hourly positions are staffed with the best qualified personnel available.
* Drive team engagement through regular coaching, feedback and involvement in day-to-day operations.
* Foster an environment of open communication.
* Maintain required professional competencies; assess staffing levels and capability; and develop direct reports through training and development opportunities.
* Empower all employees to seek and recommend work methods, tools and procedures to improve safety, quality, delivery and cost functions.
* Develop, coach, and hold leaders and teams accountable through clear expectations, training, and performance management.
* Enforce company policies and procedures in partnership with HR, the Site Controller and operational leadership.
* Lead and sustain a continuous improvement culture across all departments.
* Own site performance to Safety, Quality, Delivery, and Cost (SQDC) targets by setting expectations, reviewing results, and driving corrective actions with the Production and Materials team, including:

+ Safety: OSHA recordable incident rate (TRIR) and VSI leading indicators
+ Quality: CoPQ: Internal (scrap and rework) and External (customer defects/complaints)
+ Delivery: SCOT (Ship Complete On Time)
+ Cost: labor and overhead (burden) performance vs. budget/standard
+ Cost: operating profit / plant financial performance
+ Cost/Working Capital: inventory turns and inventory accuracy
+ Cost: manufacturing expense per earned hour / pcs (TME)

* Ensure equipment, processes, and behaviors comply with safety requirements.
* Maintain product quality standards and lead ongoing continuous improvement efforts related to quality.
* Ensure that production and shipment of product meets or exceeds the conformance and delivery expectations of product users and customers.
* Lead cross-functional alignment across sales/marketing, engineering, manufacturing, production control, and off-site operations to achieve SQDC commitments.
* Review daily/weekly SQDC performance and implement countermeasures to protect on-time shipment and cost targets.
* Communicate plant priorities, performance, and changes to hourly and salaried employees.
* Manage inventory to support SCOT while minimizing working capital and obsolescence.
* Oversee preventative maintenance systems in an effort to maintain and protect physical corporate assets.
* Ensure strong systems are in place and functioning to drive asset reliability.
* Lead site-level control activities by communicating expectations and ensuring alignment through a strong partnership with the site Controller.
* Recommend improvements to controls, monitor compliance, and provide accountability to senior management.

**Required Qualifications of Every Candidate (Education, Experience, Knowledge, Skills and Abilities):**

* Preferred Bachelors with 7+ years relevant experience or Associates Degree with 9+ years relevant experience or 11+ years of relevant experience
* Seven or more years of progressive management experience in a manufacturing environment
* Extensive experience with budget and cost management
* Working knowledge of all areas of production from material procurement, transformation, through to shipment
* Experience using MS Office (PowerPoint, Word, Excel, Outlook)
* Ability to travel up to 10%, including overnights

**Highly Qualified Candidates Will Also Possess These Qualifications**

* B.S. in Manufacturing, Business, Technology, or related field is preferred
* Master’s Degree
* Prior experience as a Plant Manager of a manufacturing facility

Work is typically performed in a manufacturing plant environment and the incumbent needs to be able to move about the office and production environments. There is often exposure to conditions such as dust, dirt, heat, fumes, and cold as well as noise levels above 80 decibels. Many aspects of this role are physical and the incumbent has to be able to lift up to 50 lbs. The employee is regularly required to reach with hands and arms. The incumbent is frequently required to stand, walk, sit, use hands to finger, handle, feel, as well as balance, stoop, kneel, crouch, talk, and hear. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, and depth perception.

Valmont offers employees and their families a comprehensive Total Wellbeing benefit package to ensure their individual and family’s overall wellness needs are met. Some offerings are dependent upon the role, work schedule, or location and can include the following:
  
  

* Healthcare (medical, prescription drugs, dental and vision)

* Employer paid life insurance
* Employer paid short-term and long-term disability including maternity leave
* Work Life Support

Georgia-Pacific is currently seeking a Plant Manager at the Gurdon, AR Plywood location.  This key leadership role provides strategic leadership and coaching to employees across the operation, driving transformation and continuous improvement in proactive EH&S leadership, process reliability, product quality, and operating costs by leveraging Principled Based Management (PBM®).
  
  
The successful candidate will be a principled, results-driven leader who creates value by developing people, improving systems, and leading sustainable change.
  
  
**What You Will Do**

* Develop, lead, and mentor Principled Entrepreneurs to drive engagement, accountability, and long-term value creation through a Principle-Based Management (PBM®) culture.

+ Lead the overall operation of the facility, from receipt of raw materials through the shipment of finished plywood to market.
+ Demonstrate personal ownership of Environmental, Health & Safety (EHS) performance by building systems, leadership behaviors, and organizational capability that drive an injury-free and environmentally compliant workplace.
+ Advance disciplined operations to exceed expectations for production scheduling, inventory control, operating rate, fiber recovery, quality, and financial performance.
+ Lead and sustain transformational change initiatives that improve safety, reliability, quality, and cost competitiveness.
+ Lead profitable change initiatives that strengthen operational performance and deliver long-term business value.
+ Own facility financial performance, including operating expense management, capital investment decisions, and financial trade-offs aligned with business objectives.
+ Formulate and execute business improvement strategies that deliver measurable operational and financial results.
+ Provide clear direction and priorities to ensure successful execution of workflow processes across the facility.
+ Build advantaged talent position by selecting, developing, and leading a high-performing leadership team that works collaboratively to achieve facility objectives.
+ Maintain strong working relationships with peers across operations, procurement, sales, accounting, HR, engineering, and other support capabilities.
+ Ensure the facility complies with all applicable company policies and state, federal, and local regulations.

**Who You Are (Basic Qualifications)**

* Three (3) or more years of experience leading manufacturing operations, including ownership of safety, production, maintenance, reliability, and continuous improvement in a complex operating environment.

+ Experience leading and managing direct reports, including identifying talent gaps, coaching and development, performance feedback, and incentive alignment.
+ Working knowledge of Environmental, Health & Safety (EHS) management systems, risk assessment and mitigation, and project planning and execution.
+ Ability and commitment to work safely while promoting and enforcing safe work practices.

**What Will Put You Ahead**

* Three (3) or more years of progressive leadership experience in a wood products manufacturing facility in one or more of the following roles: Plant Manager, Operations Manager, Production Manager, Plant Superintendent, Reliability or Maintenance Manager, or equivalent leadership position.

+ Bachelor’s degree or higher in Engineering or Wood Science.
+ Experience in leading or supporting large capital engineering or management projects.

*At Koch companies, we are entrepreneurs. This means we openly challenge the status quo, find new ways to create value and get rewarded for our individual contributions. Any compensation range provided for a role is an estimate determined by available market data. The actual amount may be higher or lower than the range provided considering each candidate's knowledge, skills, abilities, and geographic location. If you have questions, please speak to your recruiter about the flexibility and detail of our compensation philosophy.*

All Koch companies value diversity of thought, perspectives, aptitudes, experiences, and backgrounds. We are Military Ready and Second Chance employers. Learn more about our hiring philosophy here.
  
  
**Who We Are**
As a Koch company and a leading manufacturer of bath tissue, paper towels, paper-based packaging, cellulose, specialty fibers, building products and much more, Georgia-Pacific works to meet evolving needs of customers worldwide with quality products. In addition to the products we make, we operate one of the largest recycling businesses. Our more than 30,000 employees in over 150 locations are empowered to innovate every day – to make everyday products even better.
  
  
At Koch, employees are empowered to do what they do best to make life better. Learn how our business philosophy helps employees unleash their potential while creating value for themselves and the company.
  
  
**Our Benefits**
Our goal is for each employee, and their families, to live fulfilling and healthy lives. Specific eligibility criteria is set by the applicable Summary Plan Description, policy or guideline and benefits may vary by geographic region. Additionally, everyone has individual work and personal needs. We seek to enable the best work environment that helps you and the business work together to produce superior results.

Job ID: 530933
  
  
Ash Grove is a CRH company with a legacy dating back to 1882. We combine technical expertise, safety and customer-focused solutions to deliver reliable performance for our customers. We manufacture and supply high-performance, advanced cementitious materials for the most demanding construction and infrastructure needs. With more than 2,000 people across 60 locations in the United States and Canada, we support a wide range of applications, from major infrastructure projects to the development and refurbishment of residential and non-residential buildings that support everyday life, from highways and bridges to schools and commercial buildings.
  
  
To learn more about us go to www.ashgrove.com
  
  
**Job Summary**
The Plant Manager plans, coordinates, and supervises the production operations, hazardous waste fuel program, maintenance activities, quality and safety programs, and other related functions involved in plant operations. This position incorporates directives provided by corporate management into policies and procedures to maintain standards and schedules. The position exercises direct or indirect supervision over a large number of employees.
  
  
**Job Location**

* This role will work out of our plant in Louisville, NE.

**Job Responsibilities**

* Promote and follow all plant safety guidelines.
* Conducts meetings with plant staff personnel to communicate, coordinate and discuss plant operations.
* Monitors, inspects, and reviews all plant activities.
* Ensures production schedule corresponds with sales forecasts.
* Assists in investigating customer and quality problems and concerns.
* Meets with government agencies and community groups concerning plant activities to ensure compliance with environmental regulations, policies, and standards.
* Prepares regular reports regarding plant production operations.
* Attends Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA) training for waste-derived fuel activities.
* Promotes effective job performance through motivation, goals, and providing feedback.
* Promotes the safety program, compliance with safety standards, and participates in safety meetings.
* Establishes plant standards, short-term goals, and long-term strategic plans for production, maintenance, and improvements.
* Discusses new products, equipment, and ideas with staff and vendors.
* Analyzes plant costs and explore methods to improve productivity cost-effectively.
* Uses technology to develop a continuous improvement plan for the plant.
* Troubleshoots various problems and performance barriers.

**Job Requirements**

* Ability to read, write, and understand warning labels, instructions, signs, etc.
* Minimum 4 Year - Bachelors Degree in engineering, chemistry, natural sciences, business administration, or closely related field.
* Professional Engineer (PE) preferred
* Ability to develop and deliver effective presentations
* Ability to make decisions and solve problems with high attention to detail and accuracy
* Ability to make sound independent judgments regularly
* Ability to effectively coach and deliver constructive feedback
* Ability to inspire and develop staff
* Proficient in effective negotiation skills in business and construction contracts
* Proficient in Microsoft Office365
* Ability to effectively use computers for general word processing, spreadsheets, presentations, e-mail, internet, and customized company programs.
* Ability to communicate the company's vision into actionable goals and contributions for plant personnel.
* Ability to network with industry professionals, consultants, vendors, suppliers, regulators, and the community.
* Knowledge of safety and environmental health regulations.
* Knowledge of cement chemistry, physical testing, and concrete performance.
* Knowledge of various systems for cement manufacturing (crushing, grinding, pyro processing, chemistry).
* Ability to work from general policies and procedures.
* Ability to refer to supervisor when clarification or interpretation of the organizational policy

**What CRH Offers You**

* Highly competitive base pay
* Comprehensive medical, dental and disability benefits programs
* Group retirement savings program
* Health and wellness programs
* An inclusive culture that values opportunity for growth, development, and internal promotion

**About CRH**
CRH has a long and proud heritage. We are a collection of hundreds of family businesses, regional companies and large enterprises that together form the CRH family. CRH operates in a decentralized, diversified structure that allows you to work in a small company environment while having the career opportunities of a large international organization.
  
  
If you’re up for a rewarding challenge, we invite you to take the first step and apply today! Once you click apply now, you will be brought to our official employment application. Please complete your online profile and it will be sent to the hiring manager. Our system allows you to view and track your status 24 hours a day. Thank you for your interest!
  
  
Ash Grove Cement, a CRH Company, is an Affirmative Action and Equal Opportunity Employer.
  
  
EOE/Vet/Disability
  
  
CRH is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, status as a protected veteran or any other characteristic protected under applicable federal, state, or local law.

existing_roles.description:
Your Contribution
  
  
The Head of Plant Production Engineering is responsible for leading all Production Engineering activities associated with customer projects, product acquisitions, new product launches, industrialization, and production readiness within the plant. This position serves as the plant's primary owner for Production Engineering processes, ensuring successful execution of the Product Development Process (PDP) from acquisition through Start of Production (SOP) and ramp-up. The role provides leadership to Production Engineers, drives standardization and deployment of manufacturing concepts, ensures manufacturability of product designs, manages capital investments, and represents Operations within project core teams. The Plant Head of Production Engineering ensures project launches meet safety, quality, delivery, cost, and operational performance objectives.
  
  

* Lead, develop, coach, & manage the plant Production Engineering organization.
* Build organizational capability to support current and future product launches.
* Own industrialization activities for all customer projects within the plant. Ensure successful execution of product launches from acquisition and business transfer through SOP and stabilization.
* Lead development of manufacturing concepts, production processes, line layouts, and assembly strategies.
* Ensure product designs are manufacturable and meet operational standards.
* Coordinate launch readiness across Manufacturing Engineering, Tooling Engineering, Quality, Logistics, Purchasing, and Operations Support acquisition reviews and participate in PAC, PRC, and pre-development activities.
* Ensure implementation of Design-for-Manufacturing principles throughout project development. Ensure compliance with MAHLE PDP milestones, gates, deliverables, and timing requirements. Oversee completion of all Production Engineering deliverables throughout all quality gates.
* Monitor project status, risks, cost performance, capacity requirements, and launch readiness. Lead escalation activities when project risks threaten timing, quality, or cost objectives. Review project dashboards and launch metrics with plant leadership and program teams.
* Approve and govern: Manufacturing concepts, Process flows, Plant layouts, Assembly concepts, Material flow strategies, Value stream integration.
* Ensure application of Lean Manufacturing and Manufacturing Optimization Process (MOP) methodologies in alignment with Operations Excellence Manager.
* Drive takt-time analysis, line balancing, ergonomic studies, and capacity planning. Validate cycle times using MTM or equivalent engineering methods. Ensure implementation of standardized manufacturing processes across the region.
* Ensure development, completion, and approval of Process FMEA (P-FMEA), Control Plans, Special Characteristics, Process Capability Studies, Validation Plans. Support flawless launch activities and manufacturing risk reduction. Lead readiness reviews for installation checks, internal process approval, internal run at rate, customer run at rate, PPAP readiness. Ensure production systems consistently achieve quality and operational KPI’s.
* Lead capital expenditure planning and approval activities. Validate business cases and investment requirements. Ensure optimal utilization of existing equipment before requesting new capital. Support supplier selection through PDC and SDC processes. Approve manufacturing equipment specifications. Participate in procurement and acceptance of production equipment, tooling, fixtures, and test systems.
* Chair Production Engineering project meetings, and lead the plant Production Engineering Extended Team, ensuring effective communication between Project Core Teams and Plant Extended Teams.

**Your Experience & Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s Degree required, B.S. in Engineering, or related technical discipline required. Master’s Degree preferred.
* 8+ years’ experience in manufacturing, launch, industrialization, or production engineering.
* 5+ years’ progressive leadership responsibility regarding engineering or manufacturing operations.
* Demonstrated success in leading complex product launches and PDP projects.
* Experience in an automotive manufacturing facility required; high volume, medium to large campus experience preferred.
* Demonstrated knowledge in IATF16949, ISO14001 and 45001 Audits and processes.
* Excellent diagnostic abilities / root cause analysis required; Lean Six Sigma and Black Belt certification strongly preferred.

Our Offer
  
  
We will provide a collaborative environment working on exciting assignments, along with ongoing personal & career development opportunities. We encourage you to apply even if you don't meet every single requirement. You may just be the right candidate for this or other roles! After receiving your online application, the interview process will typically be, a screening call followed by Personal Interview(s).
  
  
For more information about MAHLE and what a career with us looks like for you, click here. and to learn more about our foundation owned technology group click here.
  
  
#DiversityMatters with our inclusive culture, we welcome applications from all social, religious & ethnical backgrounds, disabilities both mental and physical, identities (gender) and neurodivergent people.

existing_roles.title: Kerr Director, Manufacturing Process Development (Pomona, CA)
existing_roles.description:
**Job Summary**
The
**Director, Manufacturing Process Development**
will develop, characterize, scale, validate, transfer, and optimize manufacturing processes for dental consumables globally. This role translates product, chemistry, material, quality, and customer requirements into robust, compliant, cost-effective manufacturing processes within an FDA- and ISO-regulated environment.
  
  
Reporting to the VP, Innovation & R&D, this leader bridges R&D Engineering, Manufacturing, Regulatory Affairs, Supply Chain, and Procurement, driving manufacturing readiness, technical risk management, and process ownership. The role leads a team of engineers and requires strong influence, relationship-building, and cross-functional navigation skills.
  
  
*Candidate must reside within a commutable distance to Pomona, CA. This is not a hybrid or remote opportunity and requires onsite presence 4 days per week.*
**Primary Duties & Responsibilities**

* Develop process development strategy and roadmaps aligned to business and portfolio priorities, setting standards, governance, and resourcing for development, scale-up, validation, and lifecycle support.
* Lead, coach, and develop a process engineering team, building technical depth, accountability, and succession planning.
* Develop scalable manufacturing platforms, standards, and reusable process technologies to accelerate future product introductions and operational excellence.
* Drive development and adoption of innovative manufacturing technologies and automation solutions to improve scalability, quality, efficiency, and competitive advantage.
* Partner with product development teams to embed design-for-manufacturability principles early in product and formulation development.
* Own process development from feasibility through validation and transfer for adhesives, composites, cements, endodontic, and other dental consumable platforms, defining process specifications, critical parameters, and controls.
* In collaboration with Chemistry team, characterize material and process behavior (e.g., rheology, mixing, variability, hold times) to build scientific understanding linking materials, equipment, and finished-product performance.
* Apply Design of Experiments (DOE), statistical analysis, and risk-based tools to define process design spaces, control strategies, and acceptance criteria.
* Identify, assess, and mitigate manufacturing, scale-up, and commercialization risks throughout the product lifecycle.
* Lead pilot builds, scale-up, qualification, validation, and manufacturing transfer, ensuring readiness criteria, documentation, and training are in place.
* Provide process development leadership on New Product Development (NPD), commercialization, and lifecycle teams, aligning scope, risk, resources, and timelines across functions.
* Serve as the key technical liaison between Manufacturing and R&D, building trust and alignment across functions without relying on positional authority.
* Partner with Operations and Engineering to optimize processes, troubleshoot issues, and improve capability across the product lifecycle, clarifying handoffs from development to routine manufacturing.
* Collaborate on investigations into nonconformances, deviations, and quality events using root-cause analysis and statistical methods to drive effective CAPAs.

existing_roles.description:
**About Rivian**
Rivian is on a mission to keep the world adventurous forever. This goes for the emissions-free Electric Adventure Vehicles we build, and the curious, courageous souls we seek to attract.
  
  
As a company, we constantly challenge what’s possible, never simply accepting what has always been done. We reframe old problems, seek new solutions and operate comfortably in areas that are unknown. Our backgrounds are diverse, but our team shares a love of the outdoors and a desire to protect it for future generations.
  
  
**Role Summary**
As a leader of a multi-disciplinary team of manufacturing engineers, you will be instrumental in launching new products and capacities at Rivian, transforming innovative ideas into tangible realities. This role sits at the intersection of product design, validation, factory design, and launch, ultimately delivering Rivian's best ideas into the hands of our customers. You will be responsible for leading and developing a motivated team of manufacturing SMEs in supporting all Rivian vehicle products and factories. This position is located at our Plymouth, MI headquarters or Georgia facility and will require significant travel to our manufacturing facilities in Normal, IL, and future locations. This role reports directly to the Director of Manufacturing Engineering in General Assembly.
  
  
**Responsibilities**

* Lead a team of manufacturing engineers responsible for designing and executing workstation design aligned with lean manufacturing principles. Workstation design supports overall plant metrics of 90 - 95% utilization and greater than 50 value added elements. Start to finish ownership of workstation design from virtual build through launch.
* Support Rivian manufacturing lines and sites and cover factory layout, manufacturing technology selection, equipment design, process design, etc.
* A special focus of this team will be advancing Rivian’s manufacturing technology and innovation roadmap
* Conduct virtual builds, support design validation builds of next generation products and provide Design for Manufacturing and Assembly feedback, collaborating with vehicle architecture, design, software, and other upstream partners
* Define and execute launch and ramp strategies, collaborating with launch, operations, RPS, quality and design responsible teams
* Deliver production documentation such as JES, PFMEA, Control Plans etc.
* Develop and implement processes, standards and workflows to improve team efficiency
* Actively mentor and grow manufacturing engineers and managers through technical leadership, translate vision into action, inspiring from ideation to execution
* Actively engage in value engineering, challenge assumptions and break the status quo

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in engineering or similar technical field.
* 10+ years of experience in an engineering role related to manufacturing engineering, DFMA, product optimization, manufacturing process or equipment development
* Expertise in manufacturing and industrial engineering principles (OEE, cycle time analysis, DVA, Cp/Cpk, GR&R, ergonomics, DOE, quality control, equipment selection, ROI, error proofing, supply chain & logistics)
* Demonstrated ability to solve complex technical problems using first principles, challenge assumptions and biased towards action
* Proven technical leader that can lead and influence cross-functional teams launching new products, lean manufacturing workstations and material flow processes
* Exceptional verbal and written communication skills, ability to concisely summarize and escalate complex topics
* Experienced working within 2D & 3D CAD environments, simulation tools and other digital tools in the field of engineering

**Pay Disclosure**
The salary range for this role is $161,000-$201,200 for Georgia and Michigan based applicants. This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An employee’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, geographic location, shift, and organizational needs.
  
  
The successful candidate may be eligible for annual performance bonus and equity awards.
  
  
We offer a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and part-time employees, their spouse or domestic partner, and children up to age 26, including but not limited to paid vacation, paid sick leave, and a competitive portfolio of insurance benefits including life, medical, dental, vision, short-term disability insurance, and long-term disability insurance to eligible employees. You may also have the opportunity to participate in Rivian’s 401(k) Plan and Employee Stock Purchase Program if you meet certain eligibility requirements. Full-time employee coverage is effective on their first day of employment. Part-time employee coverage is effective the first of the month following 90 days of employment. More information about benefits is available at rivianbenefits.com.
  
  
You can apply for this role through careers.rivian.com (or through internal-careers-rivian.icims.com if you are a current employee). This job is not expected to be closed any sooner than 1/1/2027.
  
  
**Interview Integrity & AI Policy**
Our interview process is designed to evaluate your personal technical foundation, real-time problem-solving logic, and structured capabilities. Therefore,
**the use of assistive generative AI tools to formulate or deliver your solutions during live interview sessions is not permitted**
. We care most about how you think — how you make sense of unclear requirements, weigh trade-offs, and explain why you chose one approach over another. We value your unique human perspective, your authenticity, and the journey it takes to reach a solution.
  
  
**Equal Opportunity**
Rivian is an equal opportunity employer and complies with all applicable federal, state, and local fair employment practices laws. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender expression, gender identity, genetic information or characteristics, physical or mental disability, marital/domestic partner status, age, military/veteran status, medical condition, or any other characteristic protected by law.
  
  
Rivian is committed to ensuring that our hiring process is accessible for persons with disabilities. If you have a disability or limitation, such as those covered by the Americans with Disabilities Act, that requires accommodations to assist you in the search and application process, please email us at candidateaccommodations@rivian.com.
  
  
**Candidate Data Privacy and Technology**
Rivian may collect, use and disclose your personal information or personal data (within the meaning of the applicable data protection laws) when you apply for employment and/or participate in our recruitment processes (“Candidate Personal Data”). This data includes contact, demographic, communications, educational, professional, employment, social media/website, network/device, recruiting system usage/interaction, security and preference information. Rivian may use your Candidate Personal Data for the purposes of (i) tracking interactions with our recruiting system; (ii) carrying out, analyzing and improving our application and recruitment process, including assessing you and your application and conducting employment, background and reference checks; (iii) establishing an employment relationship or entering into an employment contract with you; (iv) complying with our legal, regulatory and corporate governance obligations; (v) recordkeeping; (vi) ensuring network and information security and preventing fraud; and (vii) as otherwise required or permitted by applicable law.
  
  
Rivian may share your Candidate Personal Data with (i) internal personnel who have a need to know such information in order to perform their duties, including individuals on our People Team, Finance, Legal, and the team(s) with the position(s) for which you are applying; (ii) Rivian affiliates; and (iii) Rivian’s service providers, including providers of background checks, staffing services, and cloud services.
  
  
Rivian may transfer or store internationally your Candidate Personal Data, including to or in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, and the European Union and in the cloud, and this data may be subject to the laws and accessible to the courts, law enforcement and national security authorities of such jurisdictions.
  
  
How We Use AI in Our Hiring Process: To ensure transparency, we want candidates to know that Rivian uses iCIMS Talent Cloud Artificial Intelligence (TCAI) and AI-enabled tools to assist with screening, reviewing, organizing and highlighting profiles and applications that match the key requirements for each role.
  
  
AI does not make hiring decisions: Qualified candidate applications are reviewed by a member of our team, and all decisions throughout the process are made by humans. We use AI to support efficiency and consistency, not to replace human judgment. We are committed to a fair, thoughtful, and equitable experience for every candidate.
  
  
Participation in AI profile matching is entirely voluntary. If you prefer that your profile not be used in this process, you can opt out at any time. Opting out means your profile will be excluded from automated matching and will not be surfaced for additional roles through this system. Your current application remains active and will not be affected in any way.
  
  
**Please note that we are currently not accepting applications from third party application services.**

We're committed to bringing safety, quality, and customer focus to the business of advanced ceramics manufacturing.
  
  
**Job Title**
Sr Manager Manufacturing Operations
  
  
As the Senior Manager, Manufacturing Operations you will be the senior production leader for the Oak Ridge Plant manufacturing execution, responsible for translating site priorities and customer requirements into safe, reliable manufacturing results. You will lead all production operations through a period of significant growth and increasing customer demand, with accountability for safety, quality, delivery, productivity, capacity utilization, and workforce performance.
  
  
As a leader, you will create and drives urgency, clarity, and accountability across the manufacturing organization. You will lead through production managers and supervisors, partners across functions to remove barriers, and represents the plant on customer calls related to production performance, capacity, delivery, and recovery plans. Overall site strategy, P&L ownership, capital allocation, and leadership of non-production functions remain with senior plant/regional leadership.
  
  
**Roles & Responsibilities:**

* Lead production execution across the Oak Ridge manufacturing operation, establishing clear priorities and delivering safety, quality, output, delivery, productivity, and workforce objectives.
* Lead, coach, and develop production managers, supervisors, and frontline teams; set clear expectations, reinforce accountability, and build leadership capability for continued growth.
* Create a visible and engaging leadership presence on the manufacturing floor, connecting employees to customer commitments, business priorities, and daily performance expectations.
* Establish disciplined daily management systems, operating rhythms, performance metrics, and escalation processes that enable teams to identify issues early and respond with urgency.
* Identify and remove constraints across labor, equipment, process flow, materials, maintenance, quality, and manufacturing systems to improve throughput and capacity utilization.
* Partner with Planning, Supply Chain, Engineering, Maintenance, Quality, Human Resources, Finance, and Commercial teams to align resources, resolve barriers, and deliver production commitments.
* Represent the plant on customer calls and internal operating reviews, partnering with Commercial, Planning, Quality, and other teams to communicate production status, risks, recovery actions, and commitments.
* Lead the manufacturing response to customer-impacting issues, ensuring timely containment, clear communication, root-cause analysis, corrective action, and sustainable resolution.
* Use production, labor, maintenance, yield, quality, capacity, and delivery data to identify trends, prioritize actions, and drive measurable improvement.
* Champion Lean, Theory of Constraints, structured problem solving, and continuous improvement to reduce waste and variation, improve flow, and strengthen operational capability.
* Support approved equipment installations, capacity expansions, and manufacturing-readiness activities required to meet current and future demand.
* Ensure production activities comply with safety, environmental, quality, regulatory, and company requirements, reinforcing that safety and quality are never compromised.

**Job Requirements:**
**Education & Experience:**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, Business, or a related field; equivalent relevant manufacturing leadership experience may be considered.
* At least 7 years of progressive manufacturing or operations experience, including significant responsibility for leading managers, supervisors, or large production teams.
* Demonstrated success leading manufacturing through growth, capacity expansion, operational transformation, or substantial increases in customer demand.
* Proven results improving throughput, delivery, productivity, quality, capacity utilization, and operational stability.
* Experience applying Lean, Theory of Constraints, Six Sigma, or other structured continuous improvement and problem-solving methods.
* Experience in complex, high-precision manufacturing such as advanced materials, ceramics, semiconductor, electronics, aerospace, or medical devices is preferred.

**Functional/Technical Knowledge, Skills & Abilities:**

* Visible, decisive leadership style that creates alignment, urgency, engagement, and accountability.
* Ability to lead through other leaders and strengthen the performance of a multi-layer manufacturing organization.
* Strong understanding of production planning, capacity management, equipment utilization, labor productivity, yield, quality, delivery, and manufacturing cost.
* Ability to influence across functions and resolve complex operational barriers without direct authority over partner teams.

We have signed contracts with leading electric utilities across the United States and production of our iron-air batteries is underway at our first high-volume manufacturing facility in West Virginia.
  
  
Working for Form Energy is more than just a job, it’s a chance to be part of something extraordinary. And now - right as we significantly scale up battery manufacturing - might be the most exciting moment in the company’s history to join. We are assembling a team of highly talented and driven individuals across the country. Driven by our core values of humanity, excellence, and creativity, our team is determined to deliver on our mission and transform the energy landscape for the better.

Role Description
  
  
As the Senior Manager of Assembly Manufacturing Engineering, you will serve as the primary architect of the production lifecycle, bridging the gap between research prototypes and high-volume factory operations. You will lead a multidisciplinary team of engineers to develop and internalize robust manufacturing processes for both battery enclosures and module/pack assembly—including robotic joining, sealing, electrolyte filling, and leak testing. By owning the full equipment lifecycle, from defining detailed user requirements through to factory testing and final site commissioning, you ensure that production lines are world-class, delivering a "machine that builds the machine" with precision and technical rigor.
  
  
Strategically, your objective is to drive operational scale by ensuring products are designed specifically for ease of manufacturing and assembly during the earliest development phases. You will champion a data-driven culture that utilizes failure mode analysis and advanced root-cause investigation to reduce production risks and achieve aggressive targets for quality, output rate, and equipment uptime. By fostering collaboration between Product Design, Quality, and Supply Chain, you will manage the critical transition from initial design to full-scale production, ensuring that every process is statistically validated to guarantee long-term reliability and cost-effectiveness.
  
  
**What You'll Do**

* Lead the development and optimization of battery manufacturing processes for battery assembly manufacturing.
* Ensure highly capable processes are identified and demonstrated for our production facilities ahead of detailed equipment design.
* Oversee the design and implementation of manufacturing processes such as: manual and robotic assembly, joining, sealing, system leak testing, and quality checks to achieve optimal performance and reliability.
* Collaborate with product design team, R&D, quality, and supply chain, to translate product requirements into a battery design and manufacturing process that achieve our company targets.
* Collaborate cross functionally to develop and maintain PFMEA, process specifications, measurement systems GR&R, control plan, and quality inspection methods (incoming, outgoing, and in-process).
* Lead troubleshooting efforts to identify root causes of manufacturing issues and implement corrective actions to prevent recurrence.
* Internalize responsibility for delivery of equipment and processes that enable the operations team to achieve factory production metrics (quality, yield, rate, and availability).
* Identify trends/correlations, and make data-driven decisions for process optimization.

**What You'll Bring**

* Hands-on experience in a high-volume manufacturing organization.
* Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical engineering, Chemical Engineering, Electrical Engineering.
* 10 years of experience in engineering roles within battery manufacturing or a related industry, with expertise in complex assembly processes. 4+ leading technical teams.
* Demonstrated experience in manufacturing equipment procurement, setup, and commissioning, including a clear understanding of equipment qualification and validation protocols.
* Strong understanding of lean manufacturing principles and their application in a high-volume production environment.
* Proven track record of successfully leading cross-functional teams in the development and optimization of manufacturing processes for electrochemical systems.
* Proficiency in process engineering principles, statistical analysis, and quality management systems for process optimization and improvement.
* Strong communication skills with the ability to collaborate effectively with multidisciplinary teams and convey technical concepts to diverse stakeholders.
* Leadership and mentoring abilities with a commitment to fostering a culture of continuous learning and accelerated innovation through quick iteration.
* Experience working in a fast-paced startup environment is a plus.

*This opportunity is based out of Form Factory 1 – Form Energy’s 550,000-square-foot, state-of-the-art manufacturing facility located in Weirton, WV, a commutable distance from Pittsburgh. Purpose-built for high-volume, advanced battery production, Form Factory 1 is a hub of fast-moving, collaborative work driving a new era of large-scale American energy manufacturing in the heart of the Rust Belt.*
*Relocation assistance is available.*
*Humanity is a cornerstone of Form Energy’s culture, and we make sure our compensation and benefits reflect that. Form Energy offers competitive salaries, stock options, and a holistic benefits package to ensure all employees have what they need to thrive while working here.*
*When it comes to you and your family’s health, we cover 100% of medical, dental, and vision premiums for full-time employees - and 80% of healthcare premiums for dependents. This starts from day one. We also offer at least 12 weeks of paid leave for new parents (up to 20 weeks for birthing parents), and generous vacation policies to give employees time to recharge when needed.*
